name: sector_pair_reversion_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Cointegrated pairs within the same sector (e.g., HDFC Bank vs ICICI Bank, TCS vs Infosys) exhibit intraday spread mean-reversion because they share common fundamental drivers. When the spread deviates, it's usually due to temporary order flow imbalance (one stock getting a large block, the other not yet). The inefficiency exists because intraday spread monitoring requires real-time cointegration tracking. Not fully arbitraged because the spread can remain dislocated for hours and sizing is constrained by single-name liquidity.
stock_filter: pre-selected cointegrated pairs: (HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK), (TCS, INFY), (RELIANCE, BHARTIARTL), (SBIN, BANKBARODA), (MARUTI, M&M)

long.confirmation: spread_zscore < -2.0 for 3 consecutive bars (persistence check)

short.confirmation: spread_zscore > 2.0 for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on confirmation — simultaneously enter both legs

exit.trailing_stop: none — target is mean reversion of spread
exit.signal_exit: exit when spread_zscore crosses 0

risk.position_sizing: hedge_ratio_adjusted — size legs by hedge ratio

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 20 min
filters.volume_filter: both legs must have volume > 70% of 20-bar avg
filters.trend_filter: none — market neutral by construction
filters.spread_filter: skip if either leg has spread > 0.1%
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has earnings within 3 days
other_filters: re-estimate hedge ratio weekly using 60-day rolling OLS
skip if cointegration p-value > 0.05 (Engle-Granger test)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural (sector cointegration) but pairs break down

weaknesses: Cointegration breaks down. Pairs that were cointegrated last quarter may not be this quarter. SBIN/BANKBARODA in particular has unstable hedge ratios.
Double the transaction costs — you're paying brokerage, STT, slippage on BOTH legs. The 22 bps edge needs to cover ~18-20 bps in round-trip costs for TWO stocks.
Execution risk: you need simultaneous fills on both legs. If one leg fills and the other moves, you have unwanted directional exposure.
prior_art: Classic pairs trading. See: Algorithmic Trading (Chan), Gatev/Goetzmann/Rouwenhorst (2006). Intraday adaptation.
notes: Run Engle-Granger cointegration test weekly. Drop any pair with p-value > 0.05. Keep a spare pair list to rotate in.

name: prev_day_hl_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Previous day's high and low are watched by a wide cross-section of participants (institutional, algorithmic, retail). When price breaks through these levels with volume, it signals conviction and triggers stop orders placed at these levels. The inefficiency exists because stop clusters at PDH/PDL create a micro-liquidity vacuum that accelerates the breakout. Not fully arbitraged because false breakouts are frequent and distinguishing genuine from false requires real-time volume analysis.
stock_filter: NIFTY 100 with ADV > ₹50cr

long.confirmation: close above pdh for 3 consecutive bars (avoid wick fakes)

short.confirmation: close below pdl for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on third confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.3% from entry or back inside PDH/PDL
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters inside PDH-PDL range and closes there for 5 bars

filters.time_filter: no entry in first 15 min (wait for stable price) or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when nifty 5-day return > 0
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry, RBI, budget
other_filters: skip if previous day range > 3% (levels are too wide apart)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, PDH/PDL levels are universally watched

weaknesses: False breakouts at PDH/PDL are extremely common. Estimated 55-65% of breakouts reverse within 30 bars. 3-bar confirmation helps but reduces risk/reward.
On ranging days (which dominate — ~60% of trading days), price oscillates around PDH/PDL creating whipsaw losses.
The strategy is crowded — PDH/PDL is literally the most basic level every Indian retail trader watches. Stop-hunting around these levels is common.
prior_art: Previous day high/low breakout. One of the oldest intraday setups. See: Mark Fisher (Logical Trader), pivot point literature.
notes: Consider combining PDH/PDL with CPR (Central Pivot Range) for additional confluence. PDH/PDL alone is too basic to have much alpha in 2024+.

name: connors_rsi_extreme_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Connors RSI combines three oscillators (RSI, streak RSI, percentile rank) into a composite that identifies extreme short-term oversold conditions. When CRSI < 10 on liquid stocks near VWAP, the bounce probability is elevated because the sell-off is typically driven by short-term momentum traders who will quickly reverse. Inefficiency persists because CRSI is less commonly used than standard RSI, and the signal is infrequent enough that most automated systems don't bother.
stock_filter: NIFTY 100 with ADV > ₹50cr

long.confirmation: crsi rises above 10 on next bar (turning signal)

short.confirmation: crsi drops below 90 on next bar

exit.signal_exit: exit when crsi crosses 50

filters.time_filter: no trades first 30 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when nifty > SMA(nifty, 60)
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, Connors RSI is published but less widely used intraday

weaknesses: CRSI on 1-min bars is extremely noisy. The 3-bar RSI oscillates wildly — signals fire frequently and many are false.
Thin profit factor (1.13) means a small increase in costs or slippage turns the strategy negative.
In trending markets, CRSI can stay at extremes for 50+ bars — the 'extreme' signal is not extreme at all, it's the trend.
prior_art: Connors RSI — Larry Connors / TradingMarkets. Well-published. Adapted to intraday 1-min from original daily/swing timeframe.
notes: The daily version of Connors RSI has more backtested support. The 1-min adaptation is speculative — needs careful validation.

name: first_hour_range_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: The first hour (09:15-10:15) establishes a range that captures initial order flow, position adjustments, and reaction to overnight news. Breakouts from this range after 10:15 signal genuine directional commitment that persists into the afternoon. Unlike 15-min ORB, the 1-hour range is more stable and produces fewer false breakouts. The inefficiency exists because many participants who set up in the first hour have stops just outside the range — triggering a cascade on breakout. Not fully arbitraged because the wait (1 hour) tests patience.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50, ADV > ₹100cr

long.confirmation: close above fhr_high for 2 consecutive bars after 10:15

short.confirmation: close below fhr_low for 2 consecutive bars after 10:15

entry.entry_price: market on second confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 0.5 * fhr_width profit
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters and closes inside range for 5 bars

filters.time_filter: entry only between 10:15-13:00
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakouts in direction of nifty first hour return
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry, budget, RBI
other_filters: skip if first hour range > 2% of price (too volatile)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, first hour range is a persistent anchor

weaknesses: Low frequency: 0-1 trades per day. Many days have no breakout, or breakout happens too late for meaningful P&L.
On days when the first hour range is very tight (<0.3%), any breakout is likely noise and the target is too small to cover costs.
Afternoon reversals can erase morning breakout profits — the market has a tendency to mean-revert in the last 90 minutes.
prior_art: First hour range breakout. Variant of ORB with longer initial range. See: Toby Crabel, Mark Fisher.
notes: This is cleaner than 15-min ORB but lower frequency. Consider running both and allocating to whichever has better recent hit rate.

name: bb_squeeze_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: When Bollinger Band width compresses to a multi-day low, volatility is coiling and a directional move is imminent. The squeeze resolves into a breakout as accumulated orders fire. The inefficiency exists because many participants interpret tight Bollingers as 'no opportunity' and leave the screen, reducing competition at the moment of breakout. Not fully arbitraged because the direction of the breakout is unknown — you must react, not predict.
stock_filter: NIFTY 200, ADV > ₹30cr

long.confirmation: close above bb_upper for 2 bars after squeeze

short.confirmation: close below bb_lower for 2 bars after squeeze

exit.signal_exit: exit if close re-enters inside bands and bb_width starts expanding

filters.time_filter: no entry first 30 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakout direction aligned with 60-bar EMA slope
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, BB squeeze is known but underused intraday

weaknesses: Squeeze detection on 1-min bars with 20-bar lookback captures 20-minute squeezes — these are much noisier than daily squeezes. Many false squeezes.
The breakout direction from a squeeze is random — you're betting on follow-through, not prediction. Win rate is ~42% and losses are common.
Bollinger Bands are the most widely-known retail indicator. Any edge from BB analysis is heavily competed away.
prior_art: Bollinger Band Squeeze. John Bollinger's original work. See also: TTM Squeeze (John Carter) for Keltner channel variant.
notes: Consider adding Keltner Channel overlay — squeeze is confirmed when BB is inside KC. This adds robustness to the squeeze detection.

name: moc_drift_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: In the last 30-45 minutes of the session, institutional MOC (market-on-close) orders create predictable drift. If the stock is above VWAP with strong volume into the close, MOC buy orders dominate and price drifts higher. The inefficiency exists because MOC orders are pre-committed and cannot adapt to price movement — they must execute. Not fully arbitraged because the drift is small and the window is tight, requiring fast position establishment.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 with ADV > ₹100cr (highest institutional participation)

long.confirmation: all conditions true at 14:30-14:45 window

short.confirmation: all conditions true at 14:30-14:45 window

exit.signal_exit: exit if direction reverses (return_since_1400 flips sign)

filters.time_filter: entry only at 14:30-14:45
filters.trend_filter: align with afternoon market direction
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day (close auction dynamics change)
other_filters: skip on F&O expiry weeks when roll-over distorts close

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — microstructure, may decay as close auction liquidity improves

weaknesses: Very thin edge (20 bps, PF 1.10). Any deterioration in fill quality or increase in slippage turns this negative.
Late-day reversals (last 15 min) can be sharp and stop-driven. The 0.3% stop is hit more often than expected on volatile days.
MOC order flow composition changes on special days (rebalancing, index changes, expiry). The signal is unreliable on these days.
prior_art: Market-on-close drift / end-of-day momentum. Academic literature: Bogousslavsky (2016) on intraday momentum patterns.
notes: Razor-thin edge. Only viable as part of a portfolio. Do not increase size to compensate for low per-trade edge.

name: keltner_channel_trend_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Keltner Channels use ATR-based envelopes which adapt to volatility better than standard deviation-based Bollinger Bands. When price sustains outside the Keltner Channel, it signals a strong trend that ATR-normalized volatility can't explain — i.e., genuine directional force. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders don't use Keltner Channels, preferring Bollinger Bands, so the crowd isn't positioned for KC-based signals.
stock_filter: NIFTY 100, ADV > ₹50cr

long.confirmation: close above kc_upper for 3 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: close below kc_lower for 3 consecutive bars

exit.signal_exit: exit if close re-enters inside channel for 3 bars

filters.time_filter: no entry first 30 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades aligned with nifty 60-bar EMA direction
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, trend-following edge is countercyclical

weaknesses: 38% win rate means 5-8 loss streaks are normal. Capital allocation must account for extended drawdowns.
In rangebound markets (60%+ of days), Keltner signals whipsaw repeatedly. ADX filter helps but lags.
ATR-based channels adapt slowly to sudden volatility changes — a sharp spike can invalidate the channel before it adjusts.
prior_art: Keltner Channel strategy. Chester Keltner (1960). Modern version uses EMA + ATR (Linda Raschke adaptation).
notes: Consider combining KC with BB for the TTM Squeeze variant — enter when BB is inside KC (squeeze) and breaks out.

name: round_number_reversal_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Round numbers (multiples of 50 or 100 for NIFTY, multiples of 10/50/100 for stocks) act as psychological support/resistance because traders cluster limit orders and stops at these levels. When price approaches a round number with declining momentum, the order cluster absorbs the move and reverses it. The inefficiency exists due to anchoring bias — humans fixate on round numbers for order placement. Not fully arbitraged because the reversal is probabilistic (60-65% success) and each instance is small edge.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 stocks priced > ₹500 (round numbers more impactful at higher prices)

indicators.name: nearest_round
indicators.purpose: nearest round number (50 or 100 depending on stock price)

long.confirmation: first green bar within 0.15% of round number

short.confirmation: first red bar within 0.15% of round number

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% beyond the round number (if round is support, stop 0.2% below)
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes 0.2% beyond the round number (level broken)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer reversals aligned with VWAP direction
filters.event_filter: none
other_filters: only trade at 'major' rounds (100s for stocks >1000, 50s for 500-1000)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — behavioral, anchoring bias is persistent

weaknesses: When a round number breaks with volume, the reversal bet fails hard. Stop-hunting at round numbers is also common — market makers exploit this.
Thin per-trade edge (20 bps). High sensitivity to cost assumptions.
Definition of 'round number' is arbitrary — should you use 50s, 100s, 500s? The choice affects signal frequency and quality in hard-to-predict ways.
prior_art: Round number / psychological level trading. Widely discussed. See: behavioral finance literature on anchoring (Kahneman & Tversky).
notes: Track hit rate by round number 'size' (50 vs 100 vs 500). Larger rounds should have higher hit rate.

name: nifty_intraday_momentum_factor_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Cross-sectional intraday momentum: stocks that outperformed in the first 90 minutes continue to outperform for the next 90 minutes, and vice versa. This is driven by institutional order-splitting — a large buy order in the morning continues executing through the afternoon. The inefficiency exists because cross-sectional sorting requires real-time ranking of 50 stocks, which most retail platforms can't do. Not fully arbitraged because the edge is thin per-trade and requires trading multiple names simultaneously.
stock_filter: all 50 NIFTY constituents, rank by morning return

long.confirmation: rank computed at 10:45, enter at market

short.confirmation: rank computed at 10:45, enter at market

exit.signal_exit: N/A — hold until time stop or profit/stop

filters.time_filter: entry at 10:45, exit by 14:30
filters.trend_filter: none — long/short balanced
filters.event_filter: skip stocks with earnings today, skip budget/RBI days entirely
other_filters: minimum 0.3% absolute morning return to qualify for top/bottom
skip if morning return is driven by single large gap (open price outlier)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural (institutional order flow) but studied in literature

weaknesses: 10 simultaneous positions at Zerodha = ₹400+ brokerage per day. Need consistent edge to justify the fixed cost overhead.
Morning momentum can reverse at exactly the entry time (10:45) due to profit-taking. The 90-min lookback is arbitrary.
Long/short construction is imperfect — NIFTY 50 is not truly market-neutral when you're long top 5 and short bottom 5. Sector concentration risk.
prior_art: Intraday cross-sectional momentum. Academic: Gao et al. (2018) on intraday momentum patterns. Also: Jegadeesh/Titman adapted to intraday.
notes: Capital-intensive. Needs ₹10L+ allocation. Not suitable for small accounts.

name: atr_expansion_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: When a single 1-min bar's range exceeds 2x the 20-bar ATR, it signals a volatility expansion event — often caused by institutional block trades or news catalyst. These expansion bars tend to have follow-through because the force that caused them (large order, news) persists for 15-30 minutes. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders are either stopped out by the expansion bar or are too scared to enter after it. Not fully arbitraged because distinguishing genuine expansion from noise requires volume confirmation.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by turnover

long.confirmation: enter on close of expansion bar

short.confirmation: enter on close of expansion bar

exit.signal_exit: exit if 3 consecutive bars move against the expansion direction

risk.position_sizing: fixed — reduced due to high-vol entry

filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 20 min
filters.volume_filter: expansion bar volume must be > 2x 20-bar average
filters.trend_filter: prefer expansion in direction of 60-bar EMA
filters.spread_filter: skip — spreads are unreliable during expansion events
filters.event_filter: skip on budget/RBI — expansion is event-driven, not tradeable

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — microstructure, expansion events are inherent to market structure

weaknesses: Entry at expansion bar close means you're chasing. Slippage of 5 bps is optimistic — real fills during fast moves can be 10+ bps.
Expansion bars caused by fat-finger trades or erroneous prints reverse instantly. No way to distinguish from genuine flow in real-time.
Stop at opposite end of expansion bar can be wide (the bar itself is 2x ATR), creating large per-trade risk.
prior_art: Volatility expansion / wide-range bar trading. See: Mark Minervini, Linda Raschke (Holy Grail setup).
notes: Consider using expansion as confirmation for other signals (ORB, PDH/PDL) rather than a standalone entry.

name: vwap_mean_reversion_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Exploits short-term overreaction away from VWAP in liquid FnO stocks. Institutional algorithms anchor to VWAP for execution benchmarks, creating a gravitational pull back to VWAP after deviations. The inefficiency persists because retail participants chase momentum on deviations while institutional flow reverts price. Capacity-limited (can't move size without eating your edge) which protects it from full arbitrage.
stock_filter: top 30 by 20-day avg turnover in FnO, ADV > ₹50cr

long.confirmation: price must close above low of signal bar on next bar

short.confirmation: price must close below high of signal bar on next bar

exit.time_stop: exit after 90 bars if neither target nor stop hit
exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: skip if bar volume < 50% of 20-bar SMA(volume)
filters.trend_filter: none — mean reversion works in ranging markets
filters.event_filter: skip on monthly expiry day and RBI policy day
other_filters: skip if stock gapped > 2% at open

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, driven by institutional VWAP benchmarking

weaknesses: Fails in strong trending days — deviation from VWAP is justified, not mean-reverting. Need trend filter or VIX spike cutoff to avoid catching knives.
High VIX regimes (>22) widen the distribution of deviations, making fixed z-score thresholds unreliable. The 2.0 zscore cutoff may fire too early in volatile regimes.
Slippage increases sharply on fast reversals — the same move that triggers entry attracts other mean-reversion algos, front-running the fill.
prior_art: Classic VWAP reversion. Widely documented in institutional execution literature. Edge here is in the confirmation filter (bounce + RSI + volume) not the core idea.
notes: Backtest on 2022-2024 NSE data. Walk-forward monthly. Kill if Sharpe < 1.0 in any 3-month window.

name: vwap_slope_momentum_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: VWAP slope (rate of change of VWAP) reflects the average price trajectory weighted by volume — it's a volume-weighted trend indicator. When VWAP slope is steep and price stays above VWAP, institutional accumulation is likely in progress. The inefficiency exists because most traders look at VWAP level (above/below) but not VWAP slope. Not fully arbitraged because VWAP slope calculation requires continuous recalculation and is non-trivial.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by turnover

indicators.name: vwap_slope
indicators.purpose: VWAP slope in bps per bar

long.confirmation: vwap_slope_zscore > 1.5 for 5 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: vwap_slope_zscore < -1.5 for 5 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on fifth confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: vwap level at time of entry
exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_slope_zscore drops below 0.5 (for longs)

filters.time_filter: no entry first 30 min (VWAP unstable) or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades in direction of nifty VWAP slope
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — novel indicator combination, less crowded

weaknesses: VWAP slope is noisy early in the session when cumulative volume is low. The 30-min no-trade filter helps but doesn't eliminate early noise.
Late-entry problem: by the time VWAP slope z-score sustains at 1.5+ for 5 bars, a significant portion of the move is done.
VWAP slope naturally flattens as the day progresses (cumulative average effect). The signal becomes weaker in the afternoon by construction.
prior_art: VWAP slope analysis is less common in literature. Closest: institutional VWAP execution literature and TWAP benchmarking.
notes: Relatively novel indicator. Needs extensive out-of-sample testing. The VWAP flattening issue may need time-of-day normalization.

name: macd_histogram_divergence_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: MACD histogram divergence (price makes new low but MACD histogram doesn't) signals momentum exhaustion before price reverses. Unlike RSI divergence, MACD histogram captures the rate of change of momentum, making it a leading indicator. The inefficiency exists because MACD divergence requires real-time pivot detection which most retail tools don't automate. Not fully arbitraged because divergence signals are subjective and hard to systematize.
stock_filter: NIFTY 100, ADV > ₹40cr

indicators.name: macd_hist
indicators.purpose: histogram — rate of change of momentum

indicators.name: price_pivot_low
indicators.formula: swing low with 5-bar lookback each side

indicators.name: hist_at_pivot
indicators.purpose: histogram value at price pivots for divergence

long.confirmation: macd_hist crosses above 0 after divergence

short.confirmation: macd_hist crosses below 0 after divergence

exit.signal_exit: exit on opposite MACD histogram cross

filters.time_filter: no trades first 30 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: none — counter-trend by design
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry
other_filters: pivots must be within 30 bars of each other

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, but MACD is widely used

weaknesses: MACD on 1-min bars with 12/26/9 parameters is extremely lagging — by the time divergence confirms and histogram crosses zero, the reversal may be 70%+ done.
Profit factor of 1.08 is barely above breakeven. Slippage model errors would make this negative.
Divergence detection is inherently ambiguous — different pivot definitions produce different signals. Hard to validate out-of-sample.
prior_art: MACD histogram divergence. Alexander Elder's 'Trading for a Living'. Textbook setup.
notes: Marginal. Consider shortening MACD parameters to (5, 13, 4) for 1-min bars to reduce lag. Needs parameter sensitivity analysis.

name: sector_etf_spread_reversion_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: The spread between a stock and its sector index (e.g., a bank stock vs Bank NIFTY) mean-reverts intraday because sector-wide flows affect all constituents, and temporary divergences reflect order flow timing rather than information. The inefficiency exists because sector index data isn't typically used in stock-level trading decisions by retail. Not fully arbitraged because hedging with sector indices requires futures which adds complexity.
stock_filter: Bank NIFTY constituents with ADV > ₹50cr

long.confirmation: residual_zscore < -1.8 for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: residual_zscore > 1.8 for 2 consecutive bars

exit.signal_exit: residual_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 20 min
filters.trend_filter: none — sector-neutral by design
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day
other_filters: skip if stock has stock-specific news

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural but depends on sector cohesion

weaknesses: Sector residual is directional (no hedge). You're exposed to both stock-specific and market-wide risk. Without a Bank NIFTY futures hedge, it's not true stat arb.
Beta to sector is unstable intraday — using a fixed beta estimate from daily data introduces model risk.
On days with stock-specific news (credit rating change, earnings), the residual divergence is information-driven and won't revert.
prior_art: Sector relative value trading. Standard in institutional equity long-short. Simplified to intraday single-stock without hedge.
notes: Ideally pair with Bank NIFTY futures short for true sector-neutral. Without hedge, treat as directional with relative value entry signal.

name: donchian_channel_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Donchian channel (N-bar highest high / lowest low) breakouts capture the start of new intraday trends. Unlike moving average crossovers, Donchian is parameter-light (just one: the lookback) and doesn't whipsaw in rangebound markets because the channel only contracts, never generates false crosses. The inefficiency exists because Donchian is perceived as 'old school' and retail traders prefer fancier indicators. Not fully arbitraged because intraday Donchian requires real-time rolling max/min computation.
stock_filter: NIFTY 100, ADV > ₹50cr

long.confirmation: new 30-bar high on close (not just wick)

short.confirmation: new 30-bar low on close

exit.trailing_stop: exit when close crosses donchian_mid (opposite channel midline)
exit.signal_exit: exit when close crosses below donchian_mid (for longs)

filters.time_filter: no entry first 30 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakouts aligned with nifty EMA(21) direction
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, channel breakouts are a fundamental market dynamic

weaknesses: 37% win rate is psychologically punishing. 7-10 consecutive losses are expected regularly. Most traders will override the system.
30-bar Donchian on 1-min bars = 30-minute channel. This is quite short — noise-driven breakouts will be frequent.
In rangebound markets, the channel stays tight and generates many small losses as price oscillates just above/below the channel.
prior_art: Donchian Channel Breakout. Richard Donchian (1950s). Turtle Trading System. See: Following the Trend (Clenow), Trading Evolved.
notes: The Turtle system used 20-day Donchian. Adapting to 30-min intraday is a major timeframe change. The concept is sound but the calibration needs work.

name: gap_continuation_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Large gaps (>1.5%) that DON'T fill in the first 30 minutes signal genuine information (earnings, sector news, upgrade/downgrade). These unfilled gaps tend to continue in the gap direction for the rest of the session because the information hasn't been fully priced in. The inefficiency exists because most traders either fade all gaps (Strategy 3 mindset) or wait too long to confirm continuation. Not fully arbitraged because large gaps are infrequent and require conviction to trade in the gap direction.
stock_filter: NIFTY 200 with ADV > ₹30cr

indicators.name: gap_filled_30
indicators.formula: boolean: did price touch prev_close in first 30 bars?

long.confirmation: close above first_30_high after 09:45

short.confirmation: close below first_30_low after 09:45

exit.target: 1.0 * abs(gap_pct) extension from entry (gap continuation target)
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 50% of target reached
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters first 30-min range for 5 bars

filters.time_filter: entry only between 09:45-11:00
filters.trend_filter: gap direction should align with 5-day stock return direction
filters.event_filter: skip on broad market event days (RBI, budget) — stock-specific catalysts OK
other_filters: skip if gap < 1.5% (not large enough for continuation thesis)
skip if gap > 5% (too extreme, likely reversal)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, information gaps persist across all markets

weaknesses: Very low frequency: large unfilled gaps that continue are 1-3 per week across 200 stocks. Not enough trades for a standalone strategy.
Gap continuation can fail spectacularly when the initial catalyst is overreacted to — the reversal from a failed continuation is fast and large.
Slippage on gap days is worse than normal. The 4 bps assumption may be optimistic for less liquid NIFTY 200 names.
prior_art: Gap and go / gap continuation. See: trade-ideas.com literature, Andrew Aziz 'How to Day Trade'. The unfilled gap filter is the key addition.
notes: Best combined with Strategy 3 (gap fill) — one fires on small gaps, the other on large unfilled gaps. They're mutually exclusive by construction.

name: multi_factor_composite_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Individual indicators are noisy. Combining multiple orthogonal signals — VWAP deviation, RSI, relative volume, index alignment, and VIX regime — into a composite score improves signal quality by diversifying across information sources. The inefficiency exists because most traders use 1-2 indicators and don't systematically combine signals with proper weighting. Not fully arbitraged because the specific combination and weights are unique to this implementation, and the composite approach is harder to reverse-engineer.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by turnover, ADV > ₹60cr

conditions: at least 3 of 5 sub-signals are negative
long.confirmation: composite_score must be < -1.5 for 3 consecutive bars

conditions: at least 3 of 5 sub-signals are positive
short.confirmation: composite_score must be > 1.5 for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on third confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after composite_score crosses ±0.5
exit.signal_exit: exit when composite_score crosses 0

filters.vix_filter: included in composite score — no separate filter
filters.time_filter: no trades first 30 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: included in composite score (index alignment)
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry, RBI, budget
other_filters: require at least 3 of 5 sub-signals to agree (consensus check)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — diversified across signal types, harder to crowdedly compete with

weaknesses: The weights (0.30, 0.20, etc.) are arbitrary initial guesses. Without proper optimization (which risks overfitting), the composite may not be better than individual signals.
More parameters = more overfitting risk. 5 sub-signals * 2 params each = 10+ tunable parameters. This is at the edge of overfitting territory.
Composite signals are opaque — when the strategy loses, it's hard to diagnose which component failed. Debugging is harder than single-indicator strategies.
Signal correlation: if VWAP deviation and RSI are both capturing the same mean-reversion tendency, the 'diversification' is illusory.
prior_art: Multi-factor model. Standard in quant equity (Barra, Axioma). See: Finding Alphas (Kakushadze), Advances in Financial ML (de Prado) on feature combination.
notes: Use PCA or factor analysis to verify that sub-signals are actually orthogonal. If correlation > 0.5 between any two, merge or drop one. Walk-forward optimization of weights monthly with 6-month lookback.

name: orb_15min_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: The first 15 minutes of the session concentrates institutional order flow from overnight decisions, creating a defined range. Breakout from this range signals directional commitment. The inefficiency exists because retail traders are slow to react to the directional signal embedded in institutional flow, and many systematic players wait for 30-min or 1-hour confirmations. Not fully arbitraged because the signal is noisy — win rate is moderate — and sizing constraints limit capacity for larger funds.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 constituents with ADV > ₹100cr and ATR(20) > 1.5%

indicators.name: orb_width
indicators.purpose: range width as % — skip if too wide

long.confirmation: close above orb_high on the breakout bar (not just wick)

short.confirmation: close below orb_low on the breakout bar

exit.stop_loss: opposite side of ORB (orb_low for longs, orb_high for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 1x orb_width profit
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters ORB and closes inside for 3 consecutive bars

filters.time_filter: entry only between 09:30-12:00
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume must be > 1.5x 20-bar avg
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when nifty50_return_15min > 0, shorts when < 0
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy, monthly expiry
other_filters: skip if orb_width > 1.5% (overextended open)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, but crowding is increasing

weaknesses: False breakouts are frequent — estimated 55-60% of breakouts reverse within 30 bars. Volume confirmation helps but doesn't eliminate the problem.
Gap days with extreme opening ranges (>1.5% width) create poor risk/reward. The stop at the opposite ORB boundary becomes too wide.
Crowded strategy — ORB is one of the most backtested retail strategies in India. Alpha decay is real. The edge is in the filters, not the base concept.
prior_art: Classic Opening Range Breakout (Toby Crabel). Widely known. Specific value is in the width filter and volume confirmation.
notes: Consider A/B testing 15-min vs 30-min opening range. 30-min may have fewer false breakouts but worse risk/reward.

name: gap_fill_fade_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Small gaps (0.3%-1.5%) in liquid stocks tend to fill within the session because they reflect overnight noise (global cues, ADR pricing) rather than genuine information. Market makers and institutional rebalancers push price back toward the prior close. The inefficiency persists because retail traders often interpret gaps as directional signals and chase them, providing the counterparty flow for gap-fill traders. Larger gaps (>2%) are excluded as they more likely reflect genuine information (earnings, events).
stock_filter: top 50 by 20-day avg turnover in FnO

indicators.name: gap_direction
indicators.purpose: 1 for gap up, -1 for gap down

long.confirmation: first green bar (close > open) after gap down, within first 20 bars

short.confirmation: first red bar (close < open) after gap up, within first 20 bars

exit.stop_loss: 0.5% beyond the gap extreme (for gap down long: 0.5% below session low)
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 50% gap fill
exit.time_stop: exit after 120 bars if gap not filled
exit.signal_exit: exit if price extends gap by another 0.3% beyond entry

filters.time_filter: entry only in first 30 bars of session
filters.volume_filter: opening 5-min volume must be > average opening 5-min volume
filters.trend_filter: skip if gap direction aligns with 5-day trend (gap is trend continuation)
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day for that stock, skip on RBI/budget days
other_filters: skip if gap > 1.5% (likely information-driven, not noise)
skip if gap < 0.3% (not enough edge to cover costs)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, gap fill tendency is robust across markets

weaknesses: Not all gaps fill. Information-driven gaps (earnings, sector rotation, policy shock) can persist. The 1.5% cap helps but doesn't eliminate this risk.
Opening 10 minutes have extreme slippage and wide spreads — actual fill quality is worse than backtest assumes. The 4 bps slippage may still be optimistic.
On days with broad market gaps (NIFTY gaps 1%+), correlated gap fills across multiple names create concentrated risk.
prior_art: Gap fill / gap fade is a well-documented anomaly. See: Quantifiable Edges blog, Connors Research. Edge is in the gap size filter and timing.
notes: Track gap fill rates by gap size bucket (0.3-0.5%, 0.5-1%, 1-1.5%) monthly. Kill the strategy if fill rate drops below 55% in any bucket.

name: intraday_momentum_ema_cross_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Intraday trends in liquid stocks exhibit serial correlation over 30-120 minute windows due to institutional block execution (TWAP/VWAP algos splitting large orders). Once a directional move begins, the algo flow sustains it. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders either trade too-short timeframes (scalping noise) or too-long (missing the intraday trend). Not arbitraged away because intraday trend-following has low win rate and high drawdown — psychologically hard to execute.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 with ADV > ₹80cr and intraday range > ATR(20) * 0.8

long.confirmation: ema_9 crosses above ema_21 — enter on close of crossover bar

short.confirmation: ema_9 crosses below ema_21 — enter on close of crossover bar

exit.trailing_stop: 1.5 * atr_20 trailing from highest/lowest close since entry
exit.signal_exit: exit on opposite EMA crossover

filters.vix_filter: vix between 13-28 (too low = no range, too high = whipsaw)
filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: align with index direction: long only if nifty50 EMA(9) > EMA(21)
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry days
other_filters: skip if ADX < 20 (no trend)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, but trend-following is countercyclical

weaknesses: EMA crossover is the most lagging entry possible. By the time 9/21 cross, the move is often 40-50% done. On short intraday moves, this leaves little room.
Whipsaw in rangebound markets destroys P&L. ADX filter helps but ADX itself lags — by the time ADX drops below 20, you've already taken 2-3 losses.
Win rate of ~38% means long losing streaks (5-8 consecutive losses). Psychologically brutal for discretionary override risk.
prior_art: Standard dual EMA crossover with ADX filter. Textbook trend-following adapted to intraday. See: Trading Evolved (Clenow), Following the Trend.
notes: Consider replacing EMA crossover with Donchian channel breakout for fewer whipsaws. Test 20-bar Donchian as alternative entry.

name: relative_strength_index_divergence_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: When a liquid NIFTY 50 constituent diverges significantly from NIFTY 50's intraday move (e.g., NIFTY up 0.5% but stock flat or down), it creates a relative value opportunity. The stock tends to catch up as index-tracking flows (ETFs, passive) and arbitrageurs push constituent weights back in line. The inefficiency exists because index rebalancing and ETF creation/redemption flows are not instantaneous — there's a lag. Not fully arbitraged because the spread is small and requires simultaneous stock + index hedging which retail can't efficiently execute.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 constituents with weight > 1% and ADV > ₹100cr

long.confirmation: residual_zscore must be < -2.0 for 3 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: residual_zscore must be > 2.0 for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on third confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.6% from entry or residual_zscore hits -3.5 (for longs)
exit.signal_exit: exit when residual_zscore crosses 0

risk.position_sizing: vol_adjusted — scale by inverse of stock ATR

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 20 min
filters.volume_filter: stock volume must be > 80% of 20-bar avg
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades where stock diverges from index direction
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings within 2 days
other_filters: skip if stock has sector-specific news (use simple keyword filter on news feed if available)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural (ETF/passive flows) but alpha decays as passive AUM grows and rebalancing speeds up

weaknesses: Beta estimation error: using 20-day rolling beta is noisy. If beta is wrong, the residual signal is contaminated. Consider using 60-day beta instead.
Idiosyncratic events (stock-specific news) cause legitimate divergence from index. Without a real-time news filter, you'll occasionally catch the wrong side of a company-specific move.
During sector rotation days, entire sectors diverge from NIFTY — multiple names fire simultaneously, creating correlated risk that looks like diversification but isn't.
prior_art: Index arbitrage / relative value. See: Algorithmic Trading (Chan), pairs trading literature. This is a simplified single-stock version.
notes: Ideally pair this with a NIFTY futures hedge for true relative value. Without the hedge, it's directional with a relative value entry signal.

name: vix_regime_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: When India VIX spikes sharply intraday (>10% increase from prior close), it signals fear-driven selling. Historically, these spikes are short-lived and mean-revert within hours. The inefficiency exists because retail traders panic-sell during VIX spikes, creating temporary dislocations in liquid names. Not arbitraged because sizing during high-vol events is risky and most systematic funds reduce exposure exactly when this signal fires.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 stocks with beta > 1.0 and ADV > ₹100cr

indicators.name: vix_change_pct
indicators.purpose: intraday VIX change from prior close

long.confirmation: VIX must have peaked and retraced at least 3% from intraday high

short.confirmation: N/A — long only strategy

exit.signal_exit: exit if VIX makes new intraday high after entry

risk.position_sizing: fixed — reduced size due to high-vol environment

filters.vix_filter: vix spike > 10% from prior close (entry condition, not a filter)
filters.time_filter: no entry before 10:00 (let panic settle) or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: volume must be > 1.5x average (confirming real selling, not thin drift)
filters.trend_filter: N/A — counter-trend by design
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread > 0.15% (too illiquid during panic)
filters.event_filter: skip if VIX spike is driven by scheduled event (RBI, election result)
other_filters: skip if VIX > 30 (tail event, mean reversion may not work)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural, VIX mean-reversion is well-documented

weaknesses: VIX spikes caused by genuine regime change (war, financial crisis) do NOT mean-revert intraday. The VIX 30 cap helps but isn't foolproof. 2020 March would have been a bloodbath.
Low frequency: signal fires maybe 2-4 times per month. Not enough trades for statistical significance in short backtests.
Slippage during VIX spikes is extreme — 5 bps may be optimistic. Real fills in panicky markets can be 10+ bps.
prior_art: VIX mean-reversion is well-known in options literature. Adapted to equity intraday context. See CBOE research papers.
notes: This is a low-frequency strategy. Combine with other strategies for daily P&L. Do NOT increase size to compensate for low frequency.

name: volume_profile_breakout_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Price consolidates at high-volume nodes (HVN) where many participants have transacted. When price breaks away from an HVN with above-average volume, trapped traders (who bought/sold at the HVN) are forced to exit, creating follow-through. The inefficiency exists because HVN/LVN analysis requires real-time volume profiling which most retail participants don't compute. Not arbitraged because volume profile is noisy intraday and identifying true breakouts vs false ones requires additional filters.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by turnover, ADV > ₹60cr

indicators.name: poc
indicators.formula: price level with highest cumulative volume today (Point of Control)

indicators.name: value_area_high
indicators.formula: upper bound of 70% volume distribution (VA High)

indicators.name: value_area_low
indicators.formula: lower bound of 70% volume distribution (VA Low)

long.confirmation: close above value_area_high for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: close below value_area_low for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on second confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: poc (for longs) or poc (for shorts) — i.e., back into value area
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-enters value area and holds for 5 bars

filters.time_filter: no entry in first 30 min (let profile develop) or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakouts in direction of index trend (nifty EMA(21) slope)
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day
other_filters: skip if value area width > 2x ATR(20) daily — range too wide

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — microstructure edge, decays as more participants use volume profile

weaknesses: Volume profile is computationally intensive to update in real-time and the POC/VA boundaries shift throughout the day, creating moving targets.
Early in the session (<30 min), the profile is unreliable — insufficient data. Waiting for 30+ min of data means missing morning breakouts.
False breakouts from value area are common — 55-60% of breakouts reverse. The volume confirmation helps but doesn't solve the problem entirely.
prior_art: Market Profile / Volume Profile analysis. James Dalton's 'Markets in Profile'. TPO-based analysis adapted to volume-at-price.
notes: Consider using prior day's volume profile (POC, VAH, VAL) as reference levels instead of building intraday — more stable reference points.

name: banknifty_lead_lag_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: Bank NIFTY leads NIFTY 50 by 1-5 minutes during directional moves because banking stocks are the highest-weight sector and institutional flows hit banks first. When Bank NIFTY makes a sharp move but NIFTY laggards haven't caught up, there's a window to trade the laggards. The inefficiency exists due to differential liquidity across NIFTY constituents — banks trade faster, IT/pharma lag. Not fully arbitraged because the lead-lag window is narrow (1-5 min) and requires pre-computed signals and fast execution.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 non-banking stocks (IT, pharma, auto, FMCG) with ADV > ₹50cr

indicators.name: lag_signal
indicators.purpose: how much the stock is lagging Bank NIFTY

long.confirmation: lag_zscore > 2.0 for at least 2 bars

short.confirmation: lag_zscore < -2.0 for at least 2 bars

exit.signal_exit: exit when lag_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades in first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: trade in direction of Bank NIFTY move only
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day (Bank NIFTY-specific event)
other_filters: skip if stock is a banking/financial stock (no lead-lag against itself)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — microstructure, decays as latency improves across market

weaknesses: Lead-lag relationships are not stable — the 'leader' changes based on what's driving the market that day. Bank NIFTY doesn't always lead.
Small per-trade edge (20 bps) with high frequency means costs eat a huge chunk. Any slippage increase destroys profitability.
The 1-5 minute window is extremely tight for Zerodha execution. Co-location traders with DMA will eat this edge before retail can act.
prior_art: Lead-lag pairs trading. See: Algorithmic Trading (Chan), Advances in Financial Machine Learning (de Prado) on lead-lag estimation.
notes: This strategy may not survive real execution at Zerodha speeds. Consider paper trading for 3 months before committing capital.

name: rsi_divergence_vwap_v1
author: quant_system
thesis: When price makes a new intraday low but RSI does not (bullish divergence), it signals exhaustion of selling pressure. Combined with proximity to VWAP from below, this creates a high-probability mean-reversion setup. The inefficiency exists because divergence is a lagging signal — most traders either don't compute it in real-time or don't trust it without discretionary confirmation. Not fully arbitraged because divergence signals are subjective (how many bars between pivots?) and hard to systematize cleanly.
stock_filter: top 40 FnO by turnover

indicators.name: price_pivot_low
indicators.formula: lowest low in last 20 bars (with 5-bar lookback on each side)

long.confirmation: close above the high of the divergence pivot bar

conditions: bearish_divergence == True (price higher high, RSI lower high)
short.confirmation: close below the low of the divergence pivot bar

exit.target: vwap touch (for longs below vwap) OR 0.4% from entry
exit.signal_exit: exit if RSI crosses 50 (momentum shift)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 30 min (let pattern develop)
filters.volume_filter: volume at pivot must be > SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: prefer long divergences when nifty > vwap, short when nifty < vwap
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry
other_filters: divergence pivots must be within 20 bars of each other

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral, based on exhaustion misread by momentum chasers

weaknesses: Divergence detection is inherently subjective. The 'pivot low' definition (5 bars each side) is arbitrary and different lookback windows produce different signals.
In strong trends, divergences can persist for 100+ bars before reversing — you can get 3-4 false divergences before the actual reversal.
Profit factor of 1.10 is razor-thin. Transaction cost assumptions must be dead-on or the strategy is negative expectation.
prior_art: RSI divergence is textbook TA. See: Constance Brown, Andrew Cardwell. The VWAP proximity filter is the specific addition here.
notes: Marginal edge. Consider only as part of a portfolio of strategies, not standalone.

name: vwap_mean_reversion_v3
author: QuantGen_Subagent_4
thesis: Retail traders often panic sell during intraday flushes, pushing the price far below VWAP. Institutional algorithms are VWAP-benchmarked and will fade extreme deviations, causing mean reversion. It persists due to structural liquidity constraints and behavioral panic.
stock_filter: top 50 by avg volume in universe

conditions: close < vwap AND vwap_zscore < -2.7 AND rel_volume > 1.7
long.confirmation: volume surge

conditions: close > vwap AND vwap_zscore > 2.7 AND rel_volume > 1.7
short.confirmation: volume surge

exit.signal_exit: none

filters.trend_filter: none
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy days

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral

weaknesses: Trending days with zero mean reversion will cause max losses
VIX spikes invalidate standard deviation bands
Slippage during extreme panic spikes can ruin entry pricing
prior_art: Classic VWAP reversion
notes: Generated variation 3.

name: orb_momentum_v22
author: QuantGen_Subagent_3
thesis: The opening 15-30 minutes represent overnight information assimilation. A breakout beyond this range indicates a directional institutional order flow imbalance. It exists because large orders cannot be executed all at once and create sustained trends.
stock_filter: top 50 by avg volume in universe

conditions: close > orb_high AND close > vwap AND volume > SMA(volume, 20)
long.confirmation: volume surge

conditions: close < orb_low AND close < vwap AND volume > SMA(volume, 20)
short.confirmation: volume surge

exit.signal_exit: none

name: vwap_mean_reversion_basic_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Stocks that deviate significantly from VWAP during the first 90 minutes tend to revert because VWAP represents the fair institutional price. Large early deviations are often caused by retail order flow or algo overshoot on news, which institutional participants then fade. The edge persists because retail flow is structurally noisy and institutions use VWAP benchmarks for execution, creating a gravitational pull. The edge is small enough (~25 bps) that it falls below the threshold for dedicated HFT capital allocation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND price > 100 AND price < 10000
session: 09:30-15:15 IST (avoid first 15 min and last 15 min)

long.confirmation: close[t] > close[t-1] AND close[t-1] > close[t-2] (two consecutive green bars after deviation)

short.confirmation: close[t] < close[t-1] AND close[t-1] < close[t-2] (two consecutive red bars after deviation)

entry.entry_price: limit order at close of confirmation bar

exit.stop_loss: 1.5 * ATR(14) from entry OR 0.5% from entry, whichever is tighter
exit.trailing_stop: move stop to breakeven after 50% of target reached
exit.time_stop: exit if not at target within 60 bars (60 min)
exit.signal_exit: exit if VWAP_dev_pct crosses zero (reversion achieved)

risk.position_sizing: fixed INR 1L per trade, reduce to 50K if daily loss > 1000 INR

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30 IST
filters.volume_filter: skip if current bar volume < 0.5 * SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when NIFTY 50 > VWAP_NIFTY, shorts when NIFTY 50 < VWAP_NIFTY
filters.event_filter: no trades on budget day, RBI policy days, F&O expiry day
other_filters: skip if stock has earnings scheduled today

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — more quant desks adopting VWAP reversion, but retail noise is structural

weaknesses: In strong trending days (>2% NIFTY move), VWAP reversion fails and stops are hit repeatedly
Early morning deviations may not be noise but genuine information — stock may keep moving away from VWAP
Requires precise VWAP calculation; tick-level VWAP differs from 1-min bar approximation
prior_art: VWAP mean reversion is a well-documented institutional execution strategy. Kakushadze & Serur (2018) catalog it in '151 Trading Strategies'. VWAP reversion alpha has been declining in US equities per AQR research, but Indian markets are less efficiently arbitraged due to lower quant penetration.
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 50bps - 0.45 * 42bps = 27.5 - 18.9 = 8.6 bps gross. After costs (6 bps slippage RT + 2.5 STT + 0.5 exchange + ~2 brokerage ≈ 11 bps), net is ~-2.4 bps on this conservative calc. Need tighter stops or better win rate. Revised: with 0.58 win rate and 1.3 W:L → 0.58*50 - 0.42*38 = 29 - 16 = 13 bps gross, net ~2 bps. Marginal. Strategy needs careful parameter tuning in backtest.

name: vwap_zscore_bounce_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Normalizing price deviation from VWAP into a z-score using rolling standard deviation creates a statistically grounded entry signal. When z-score of (price - VWAP) falls below -2.0 or rises above +2.0, the deviation is >2 sigma from the session mean — a statistically rare event that tends to snap back. The inefficiency exists because intraday price distributions are leptokurtic (fat-tailed) but mean-reverting within sessions, so extreme z-scores overshoot the true equilibrium. This edge is too small and labor-intensive for large funds but viable for retail with low fixed-cost brokerage.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 80 crore INR AND intraday_volatility(20) > 0.8%

long.confirmation: vwap_zscore[t] > vwap_zscore[t-1] (z-score turning upward)

short.confirmation: vwap_zscore[t] < vwap_zscore[t-1] (z-score turning downward)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: entry_price - 1.2 * ATR(14) for longs; entry_price + 1.2 * ATR(14) for shorts
exit.time_stop: exit after 45 bars if target not hit
exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_zscore moves further against position (new extreme beyond -2.5 or +2.5)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 24; reduce size 50% if VIX between 20-24
filters.time_filter: no entries after 14:30 IST; need at least 30 min of data (after 09:45)
filters.trend_filter: none — strategy is counter-trend by design
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day, budget day, quarterly expiry
other_filters: skip if stock in upper/lower circuit freeze

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — z-score normalization is standard but Indian intraday is under-exploited

weaknesses: Z-score calculation requires 30+ bars of data, so no trades in first 30 min when volatility is highest
In trending markets, z-score can remain extreme for extended periods — strategy gets stopped out repeatedly
Rolling std denominator is unstable early in session; z-score can give false signals with low sample size
prior_art: Z-score mean reversion is textbook statistical arbitrage (Avellaneda & Lee, 2010). VWAP-specific z-score approaches are common in institutional TWAP/VWAP execution algos. Chan (2013) 'Algorithmic Trading' discusses z-score entry for pairs but same logic applies to VWAP deviation.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 55bps - 0.42 * 48bps = 31.9 - 20.2 = 11.7 bps gross per trade. Costs: 6 slippage + 2.5 STT + 0.5 exchange + ~2 brokerage = ~11 bps round-trip. Net edge ≈ 0.7 bps per trade. Very tight. Need either higher win rate or better W:L. Backtest should target 0.60+ win rate for viability. May need to widen z-score threshold to -2.5.

name: vwap_cross_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When price crosses above VWAP on elevated volume after being below for 20+ bars, it signals a regime shift: the marginal buyer is now paying above the session's volume-weighted fair value. Institutional VWAP-tracking algorithms that were selling now become buyers, creating a positive feedback loop. The edge exists because the cross event is a Schelling point — many participants watch VWAP, and their collective response to the cross creates a brief momentum burst that outruns transaction costs. The edge is not arbitraged because it requires very fast reaction (<1 min) and the absolute profit per trade is small.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 30 crore INR AND beta(NIFTY50, 60) between 0.8 and 1.5

long.confirmation: cross bar closes in top 30% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) > 0.7

short.confirmation: cross bar closes in bottom 30% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) < 0.3

entry.entry_price: market order at confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: VWAP (re-cross back below/above VWAP) OR 0.25% from entry, whichever is hit first
exit.signal_exit: exit if price re-crosses VWAP in opposite direction

filters.vix_filter: no filter — momentum works in all VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 (let VWAP stabilize) or after 14:45
filters.volume_filter: volume surge > 2x 10-bar SMA on cross bar
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when NIFTY 50 is green for the day, shorts when red
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day (whipsaws increase)
other_filters: skip if stock has crossed VWAP > 5 times already today (choppy)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — VWAP cross is widely watched; edge depends on speed of entry

weaknesses: In range-bound days, VWAP gets crossed many times — strategy generates false signals and accumulates losses
The 20-bar requirement means missing the first (most powerful) VWAP cross of the day
Volume surge threshold of 2x may be too aggressive, filtering out valid signals in low-vol stocks
prior_art: VWAP crossover is a staple of retail day trading (Bellafiore, 'One Good Trade'). Academic work by Berkowitz et al. (1988) established VWAP as a benchmark. The cross-with-dwell-time filter (20 bars below) is less common and adds originality.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 40bps - 0.52 * 25bps = 19.2 - 13.0 = 6.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps RT. Gross edge insufficient. Need to either tighten stops to 0.20% or increase target to 0.5% to improve the math. The 20-bar dwell filter should improve win rate above 0.48 — backtest validation needed.

name: vwap_band_squeeze_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: VWAP bands (VWAP ± k * rolling std of price) compress during periods of low intraday volatility, analogous to Bollinger Band squeezes. When band width contracts below the 20th percentile of its own session distribution, it signals coiled energy — a breakout is imminent. The inefficiency arises because most participants focus on price level relative to VWAP, not the width of the bands. The squeeze identifies moments when supply/demand is temporarily balanced but about to tip. The edge persists because band-width analysis on VWAP is not standard in retail TA, and the signal is rare enough (1-2 per day) that it is not worth automating for large funds.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 60 crore INR AND intraday_range(20) > 1.0%

long.confirmation: close breaks above vwap_upper with bar range > 1.5 * ATR(14) / sqrt(14)

short.confirmation: close breaks below vwap_lower with bar range > 1.5 * ATR(14) / sqrt(14)

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout bar close

exit.stop_loss: VWAP (midline) — if price reverts to VWAP, thesis is invalidated
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 1.0 * ATR(14) once profit exceeds 1.0 * ATR(14)
exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_bw_pctile rises above 60 (bands expanding means move is maturing)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; risk-based sizing to keep loss < 700 INR per trade

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12-22 (squeeze breakouts work best in moderate vol)
filters.time_filter: entries only 10:00-14:30; squeeze must form after first 45 min of session
filters.trend_filter: prefer direction aligned with NIFTY 50 trend (NIFTY above/below its VWAP)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy
other_filters: skip if squeeze duration < 10 bars (need genuine compression)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — band squeeze on VWAP is not a common retail or institutional signal

weaknesses: False breakouts from squeezes are common (~55% of the time); requires strict risk management
Signal is rare (1-2/day) which limits daily P&L and makes the strategy hard to scale
Band width percentile calculation requires sufficient session data — unreliable before 10:00 IST
prior_art: Bollinger Band squeeze (John Bollinger, 'Bollinger on Bollinger Bands') is the direct inspiration. TTM Squeeze by John Carter applies similar logic. Applying squeeze logic to VWAP bands rather than Bollinger Bands is a less common variant. Keltner-inside-Bollinger squeeze is a known alternative.
notes: Edge math: 0.45 * 80bps - 0.55 * 40bps = 36 - 22 = 14 bps gross per trade. Costs ~11 bps RT. Net ≈ 3 bps per trade. Marginal but positive. With 1-2 trades/day, expected daily P&L = 3-6 bps on 1L = 30-60 INR/day. Needs volume to be meaningful. Consider increasing capital per trade to 2-3L.

name: vwap_slope_trend_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The slope of VWAP over a rolling 20-bar window reveals the direction of institutional net order flow. A rising VWAP slope means institutions are net buying at progressively higher prices; a falling slope means net selling. Trading in the direction of the VWAP slope captures the institutional order flow tailwind. The edge exists because most participants look at price vs VWAP (static level), not the rate of change of VWAP (dynamic signal). The slope change anticipates future VWAP-tracking algo behavior — if VWAP is rising, TWAP/VWAP algos will bid higher. This edge persists because computing and interpreting VWAP slope is non-trivial and requires clean real-time data.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 50 INR

long.confirmation: vwap_slope has been positive for 5+ consecutive bars AND increasing for last 3 bars

short.confirmation: vwap_slope has been negative for 5+ consecutive bars AND decreasing for last 3 bars

entry.entry_price: limit order at EMA(close, 9) if within 0.1% of current price, else market

exit.target: 0.5% from entry OR vwap_slope reverses sign
exit.signal_exit: exit if vwap_slope crosses zero (trend exhaustion)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — trend strategies work across VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 (slope needs data) or after 15:00
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 slope should align (both positive or both negative for added confidence)
filters.event_filter: caution on RBI policy day — slope can reverse suddenly on rate decision
other_filters: skip if ADX < 20 (no trend)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — slope analysis is straightforward once implemented but not widely used on VWAP

weaknesses: VWAP slope is a lagging indicator — by the time slope confirms a trend, much of the move may be done
In choppy markets with ADX < 20, slope oscillates around zero giving false signals; ADX filter helps but reduces opportunity set
Slope calculation via linear regression is sensitive to outlier bars — a single large bar can distort slope reading
prior_art: VWAP slope analysis is discussed in Brian Shannon's 'Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes'. Linear regression slope on price is a standard indicator (LinReg Slope in most platforms). Applying it to VWAP specifically rather than price is less common in literature. ADX as trend filter is from Wilder (1978).
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 50bps - 0.50 * 30bps = 25 - 15 = 10 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps RT. Net ≈ -1 bps. Marginally negative on conservative estimates. However, the trailing stop should improve avg winner beyond 50 bps in trending conditions. If avg winner is 60 bps: 0.50*60 - 0.50*30 = 15 bps gross, net 4 bps. Needs validation.

name: vwap_anchored_support_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Anchored VWAP from significant prior events (earnings release, 52-week high/low, large gap day) acts as a persistent institutional memory of fair value from that event. When current price approaches an anchored VWAP from a major event, institutional participants who entered near that event face break-even decisions, creating supply/demand clusters. The inefficiency exists because standard platforms only show session VWAP, not anchored VWAP from arbitrary dates. Traders who compute anchored VWAP gain an informational edge over those using only session VWAP. The edge persists because most retail traders lack the data infrastructure to compute multi-day anchored VWAPs efficiently.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND has had earnings or 52w event in last 30 trading days

indicators.name: anchored_VWAP
indicators.params: cumulative VWAP from event_date using 1min data

long.confirmation: price bounces off anchored_VWAP with 2 consecutive closes above it

short.confirmation: price rejected at anchored_VWAP with 2 consecutive closes below it

entry.entry_price: limit order at anchored_VWAP level (support/resistance bounce entry)

exit.stop_loss: 0.25% beyond anchored_VWAP (through the level means thesis is wrong)
exit.signal_exit: exit if price recrosses anchored_VWAP against the position direction

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; 1.5L for high-conviction setups (post-earnings anchored VWAP)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; anchored levels are less reliable in panic regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries in first 15 or last 15 min of session
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades where anchored VWAP direction matches session VWAP direction
filters.event_filter: skip if another event (earnings, corporate action) is imminent today
other_filters: anchored VWAP must be from an event within last 30 trading days — older levels degrade

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — anchored VWAP is not widely computed by retail; data infrastructure barrier

weaknesses: Requires maintaining a calendar of events and computing multi-day anchored VWAPs — significant data engineering overhead
Anchored VWAP levels that are too old (>30 days) lose their institutional memory relevance
Signal is rare — only triggers when price approaches a specific level, may have 0 trade days frequently
prior_art: Anchored VWAP was popularized by Brian Shannon ('Technical Analysis Using Multiple Timeframes') and is available on TradingView. Institutional use of anchored VWAP is discussed by DeMark and others. The concept of event-based anchoring adds specificity beyond generic anchored VWAP.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 50bps - 0.44 * 33bps = 28 - 14.5 = 13.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 2.5 bps per trade. Low but positive. The real value is in high-conviction setups (post-earnings anchored VWAP near price) where win rate may be 0.60+. Needs event calendar infrastructure to be practical.

name: vwap_volume_divergence_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When price moves away from VWAP but volume is declining (price-volume divergence), the move lacks institutional conviction and is likely to reverse. Conversely, when price moves toward VWAP on increasing volume, the reversion has institutional backing and is likely to follow through. This exploits the fact that retail-driven moves often occur on declining volume (exhaustion), while institutional moves show increasing volume (accumulation/distribution). The edge exists because most VWAP strategies only look at price deviation, ignoring the volume profile of the deviation. Adding volume confirmation filters out low-quality reversion signals.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND avg_tick_count > 500/min

conditions: OBV_slope < 0 AND abs(OBV_slope) declining over last 5 bars
long.confirmation: volume[t] > volume[t-1] AND close[t] > close[t-1] (volume returning with buying)

conditions: OBV_slope > 0 AND abs(OBV_slope) declining over last 5 bars
short.confirmation: volume[t] > volume[t-1] AND close[t] < close[t-1] (volume returning with selling)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.8 * ATR(14) after 50% of target reached
exit.signal_exit: exit if volume surges 3x+ in direction away from VWAP (institutional confirmation of move)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: bar volume must be > 0.5x 10-bar SMA (not dead tape)
filters.trend_filter: none — divergence is a reversal signal
filters.event_filter: skip on event-driven gap days where move may be fundamental, not technical
other_filters: skip if stock has pending results announcement

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volume-divergence analysis on VWAP is not standard in most screeners

weaknesses: Volume pattern interpretation is subjective — declining volume during a move can also indicate absorption, not exhaustion
OBV slope over 10 bars is noisy and can give conflicting signals with raw volume slope
In illiquid stocks, volume patterns are unreliable — hence the tight liquidity filter is essential
prior_art: Price-volume divergence is classical TA (Granville, 'New Key to Stock Market Profits'). On-Balance Volume is from Granville (1963). Combining divergence specifically with VWAP deviation is less documented. Wyckoff method uses similar supply/demand logic with volume confirmation.
notes: Edge math: 0.54 * 50bps - 0.46 * 38bps = 27 - 17.5 = 9.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -1.5 bps. Marginally negative on paper. However, the volume divergence filter should improve base win rate above 0.54. Backtest needed to validate that divergence adds 3-5% to win rate over plain VWAP reversion.

name: vwap_rsi_confluence_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Combining VWAP deviation with RSI extremes creates a double confirmation filter that dramatically reduces false signals. When price is >0.5% below VWAP AND RSI(14) < 30, the stock is both underpriced relative to institutional fair value AND oversold on momentum. The confluence of two independent signals (value + momentum) increases the probability of reversion. The edge exists because each signal alone has a ~50% base rate, but their intersection is much rarer and has a higher hit rate (~60%). Most traders use either VWAP or RSI, not both together with strict thresholds. The rarity of the combined signal also means it cannot be easily arbitraged away since trade frequency is low.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND daily_volatility(20) > 1.2%

long.confirmation: RSI_slope > 0 (RSI turning up from below 30) AND close > open on current bar

short.confirmation: RSI_slope < 0 (RSI turning down from above 70) AND close < open on current bar

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: VWAP line (vwap_dev_pct crosses 0) OR RSI crosses 50, whichever first
exit.stop_loss: 0.4% from entry OR RSI makes new extreme (below 25 for longs, above 75 for shorts)
exit.signal_exit: exit if both vwap_dev_pct and RSI worsen simultaneously (deepening extreme)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L per trade; scale to 1.5L if daily P&L is positive

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; confluence signals in panic markets are unreliable
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 (RSI needs warmup) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when NIFTY 50 is not in a downtrend (NIFTY > EMA(NIFTY, 20))
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy
other_filters: skip if stock gapped > 2% at open (gap distorts RSI)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — confluence is simple conceptually but requires discipline to wait for both signals

weaknesses: Signal is rare — both VWAP deviation >0.5% AND RSI <30 simultaneously may occur only 1-2 times per day across entire universe
RSI on 1-min bars is extremely noisy; 14-period RSI on 1-min = 14 minutes of data, which is short for reliable RSI readings
During strong sell-offs, both conditions persist for extended periods — entry timing within the confluence zone is still difficult
prior_art: Multi-indicator confluence is standard TA practice. VWAP + RSI is mentioned in various trading education (SMB Capital, Investors Underground). The specific thresholds (0.5% deviation + RSI<30) and the RSI-slope confirmation add some specificity beyond generic confluence approaches.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 40bps - 0.40 * 33bps = 24 - 13.2 = 10.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -0.2 bps. Essentially breakeven. Need to either improve win rate to 0.62+ or improve W:L ratio. The strength of this strategy is low trade frequency (high-conviction only) which should push realized win rate above 0.60. Conservative estimates used here.

name: vwap_gap_fill_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Stocks that gap open >0.5% away from previous day's closing VWAP (not just previous close, but previous session's final VWAP value) tend to fill that gap within the first 90 minutes. Previous day VWAP represents the volume-weighted institutional consensus from the prior session. An overnight gap away from it is often driven by pre-market news overreaction, global cues, or Nifty futures movement that may not fully apply to individual stocks. The inefficiency exists because gap fills are well-known for gaps from previous close but not from previous VWAP — using VWAP as the anchor provides a better mean to revert to because it accounts for where most volume actually transacted, not just the arbitrary last-traded price.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND gap from prev_day_VWAP > 0.5% AND gap < 3.0%
session: 09:20-11:00 IST (gap fill is a morning strategy)

indicators.name: prev_day_VWAP
indicators.params: final VWAP from previous trading session

conditions: close > low of first 5 bars (gap not extending)
long.confirmation: first bar where close > open AND close > EMA(close, 5) after gap down

conditions: close < high of first 5 bars (gap not extending)
short.confirmation: first bar where close < open AND close < EMA(close, 5) after gap up

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 50% gap extension beyond open (if gapped down 1%, stop at 1.5% below prev_day_VWAP)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.15% once 50% of gap is filled
exit.time_stop: 60 bars or 11:00 IST, whichever comes first
exit.signal_exit: exit if gap extends beyond 2x original gap size (strong directional move)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; scale down for gaps > 1.5% (larger gaps less likely to fill)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; gap fills are less reliable in high-vol regimes
filters.time_filter: entries only between 09:20-10:30 IST; after that, unfilled gaps likely won't fill
filters.volume_filter: opening volume > 1.5x average first-bar volume (confirms gap is being traded)
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 gapped same direction > 1% (systemic gap, not stock-specific)
filters.event_filter: skip if gap is due to earnings, corporate action, or block deal (fundamental gap)
other_filters: only trade gaps from prev_day_VWAP, not from prev_day_close

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — gap fill from prev VWAP is not a standard screen; most use prev close

weaknesses: Gaps caused by genuine fundamental news (earnings, upgrades) may never fill — the event filter is imperfect
Opening 15 minutes have wide spreads and high slippage; actual slippage may be 5-8 bps not 3 bps
On days with strong global cues (US market crash/rally), most stocks gap together and fill rates drop sharply
prior_art: Gap fill strategies are extensively documented (Pristine.com, Gap-and-Go by Ross Cameron). Using previous VWAP as the anchor instead of previous close is less common. Bulkowski ('Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns') notes ~70% of gaps fill within the session but this includes multi-day holds. Intraday-only gap fill has lower fill rates.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 50bps - 0.38 * 45bps = 31 - 17.1 = 13.9 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps (may be higher due to opening slippage, say 14 bps). Net ≈ 0 bps to slightly negative in practice. Need to filter for higher-quality gaps. Gaps of 0.5-1.5% have better fill rates than 1.5-3.0%. Should segment by gap size in backtest.

name: vwap_relative_strength_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Comparing a stock's deviation from its VWAP to NIFTY 50's deviation from its VWAP reveals relative strength/weakness. If a stock is above its VWAP by 0.5% while NIFTY is below its VWAP, the stock is showing genuine relative strength — institutional buying is concentrated in that stock despite broad market weakness. This relative VWAP strength predicts continuation because funds rotating capital tend to do so over hours, not minutes. The edge exists because standard relative strength (RS line) uses price ratios, not VWAP-normalized deviations, and misses the volume-weighted institutional flow information that VWAP provides.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND member of a sector with >=5 NIFTY200 stocks

long.confirmation: relative_vwap_strength increasing for 3+ consecutive bars AND stock close > EMA(close, 9)

short.confirmation: relative_vwap_strength decreasing for 3+ consecutive bars AND stock close < EMA(close, 9)

exit.target: 0.6% from entry (ride the relative strength wave)
exit.stop_loss: 0.3% from entry OR relative_vwap_strength crosses zero (lost relative edge)
exit.signal_exit: exit if relative_vwap_strength reverts toward zero (convergence)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if relative_vwap_strength > 1.0 (strong signal)

filters.vix_filter: no specific VIX filter — relative strength works across regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need 45 bars of data) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs on days where NIFTY is range-bound (not >1% trend), as relative strength is more meaningful
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has stock-specific news driving the relative strength (not flow-driven)
other_filters: filter out F&O stocks on expiry day (relative strength distorted by rollover)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — relative VWAP strength is not a standard metric in any platform or screener
