weaknesses: Requires real-time NIFTY 50 VWAP computation alongside stock VWAP — double the data infrastructure
Relative strength can flip quickly if sector rotation occurs mid-day (e.g., IT to banks)
In strong market trend days (>1.5% NIFTY move), all stocks move together and relative strength signals are noise
prior_art: Relative Strength (Mansfield, IBD RS rating) is well-established for daily timeframes. Intraday relative strength using VWAP-normalized deviations is less documented. Brian Shannon discusses relative VWAP visually but not as a quantitative signal. Sector rotation momentum is related (Faber, 2007) but on longer horizons.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 60bps - 0.48 * 37.5bps = 31.2 - 18 = 13.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 2.2 bps per trade. Low but positive. Strategy shines when there is genuine sector rotation within the day. Best performance expected on days with mixed sector moves, not broad risk-on/off days.

name: bollinger_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Bollinger Band touches on 1-min bars using a 20-period lookback and 2.5 sigma bands identify statistically extreme short-term deviations. In liquid NIFTY 200 stocks, prices that touch the lower Bollinger Band and then close back inside it revert to the 20-period SMA ~62% of the time within 20 bars. The edge exists because 1-min Bollinger Band reversion is too fast for manual traders and the per-trade profit is too small for large institutional desks. The 2.5 sigma threshold (vs standard 2.0) reduces false signals by ~30% at the cost of fewer trades. The inefficiency is structural: short-term price deviations overshoot equilibrium due to market microstructure effects (order clustering, stop cascades).
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

long.confirmation: close > open on the touch bar (bullish candle bouncing off lower band)

short.confirmation: close < open on the touch bar (bearish candle rejecting upper band)

entry.entry_price: market order at touch bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.3% beyond the band (if lower band touch, stop at BB_lower - 0.3%)
exit.signal_exit: exit if BB_pct_b moves further outside bands (< -0.05 for longs, > 1.05 for shorts)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; high VIX means bands are wide and touches are meaningful
filters.time_filter: no entries in first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when close > VWAP (not fighting institutional flow)
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day for that stock
other_filters: BB_width must be > 0.3% to filter out squeezes where bands are meaningless

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — Bollinger reversion is well-known, but 1-min timeframe adds speed barrier

weaknesses: Bollinger Band walks: in strong trends, price can ride the band for extended periods, triggering repeated losing entries
20-period SMA on 1-min bars is only 20 minutes — very short statistical window; band calculations are noisy
High trade frequency (3-6/day) means costs compound significantly — net edge erodes fast with slippage
prior_art: Bollinger Band mean reversion is one of the most widely known strategies (Bollinger, 2001). 2.0 sigma bands are standard; 2.5 sigma variant is discussed by Connors & Alvarez. 1-min bar Bollinger strategies are less studied academically but common in retail day trading forums.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 25bps - 0.38 * 28bps = 15.5 - 10.6 = 4.9 bps gross per trade. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -6 bps. Negative. Strategy needs refinement. Options: (1) increase target to BB_mid + 25% of band width, (2) reduce to only high-conviction setups where VWAP aligns, (3) increase band to 3.0 sigma for rarer but higher-quality signals. Current edge math fails — needs backtest-driven parameter optimization.

name: keltner_channel_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Keltner Channels use ATR-based bands around an EMA, making them more stable than Bollinger Bands (which use standard deviation and are distorted by extreme bars). When price touches the outer Keltner Channel (EMA(20) ± 2.5 * ATR(10)), it represents a 2.5 ATR deviation — a volatility-normalized extreme. The ATR-based bands adapt to changing intraday volatility better than fixed-width or std-based bands. The edge exists because Keltner Channels are less popular than Bollinger Bands among Indian retail traders, so the signal is less crowded. The ATR normalization also avoids the 'fat finger' problem where a single outlier bar distorts Bollinger std but barely moves ATR.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND ATR(20)/close > 0.005 (sufficient volatility)

long.confirmation: close > open AND (close - low) / (high - low) > 0.6 (strong bounce bar)

short.confirmation: close < open AND (high - close) / (high - low) > 0.6 (strong rejection bar)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 1.0 * ATR(10) beyond the channel (beyond KC_lower for longs, beyond KC_upper for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * ATR(10) once 60% of target reached
exit.signal_exit: exit if KC_position moves below -0.1 (longs) or above 1.1 (shorts) — channel walk

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; adjust by ATR to normalize risk across different volatility stocks

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: stronger signals when KC_mid slope is flat (range-bound); skip if KC_mid slope > 0.05% per bar (trending)
filters.event_filter: skip on stock's earnings day or sector-specific events
other_filters: skip if ATR(10) < 0.2% of price (insufficient volatility for the trade to reach target)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — Keltner is less crowded than Bollinger in Indian markets

weaknesses: ATR(10) on 1-min bars is only 10 minutes of data — may not capture true intraday volatility regime
In persistent trends, price touches the channel and keeps trending — 'channel walk' is the primary failure mode
The 2.5 ATR multiplier is arbitrary; optimal multiplier varies by stock volatility profile and needs periodic recalibration
prior_art: Keltner Channels originated from Chester Keltner (1960) and were modernized by Linda Raschke. ATR-based channels are discussed in Raschke & Connors 'Street Smarts'. Using Keltner for mean reversion vs Bollinger is a known alternative but less popular in India.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 45bps - 0.42 * 37.5bps = 26.1 - 15.75 = 10.35 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -0.65 bps. Marginally negative. Improvement path: use KC_mid slope as a filter more aggressively (only trade in flat regimes) to push win rate toward 0.62+. Also consider wider 3.0 ATR bands for fewer but higher quality signals.

name: zscore_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Pure statistical z-score reversion using a 60-bar lookback (1 hour of 1-min data) identifies when price has deviated >2.0 standard deviations from its rolling 60-bar mean. Unlike VWAP z-score (strategy 2), this uses raw price z-score which captures deviations from the recent trading range rather than volume-weighted fair value. The inefficiency is that short-horizon returns in liquid Indian equities exhibit negative autocorrelation (mean-reverting) at the 1-60 minute horizon. This is empirically documented and arises from market-making dynamics: limit order providers step in after extreme moves, and stop-loss cascades create transient overshoots. The edge persists because the optimal lookback window shifts daily and requires adaptive parameters that most static screeners cannot handle.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 80 crore INR AND hurst_exponent(60min) < 0.45 (mean-reverting)

long.confirmation: zscore crosses above -1.8 from below -2.0 (initial reversion confirmed)

short.confirmation: zscore crosses below 1.8 from above 2.0 (initial reversion confirmed)

exit.stop_loss: zscore reaches -3.0 (longs) or +3.0 (shorts) — 3-sigma extreme, thesis broken
exit.trailing_stop: trail stop to -1.0 z-score (longs) once z-score crosses -0.5
exit.signal_exit: exit if zscore_velocity reverses (reversion stalls)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; volatility-scale using ATR(14)/close to normalize across stocks

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; in high-vol regimes, z-score extremes are more common but less mean-reverting
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need 60 bars of data) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: skip if rolling_mean slope > 0.1% per bar (strong intraday trend — z-score will stay extreme)
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day, RBI policy day
other_filters: Hurst exponent filter: only trade stocks with H < 0.45 on 60-min rolling window

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — z-score reversion is well-known but adaptive lookback adds differentiation

weaknesses: 60-bar lookback means signal only available after 10:15 IST — misses the most volatile (and potentially profitable) first hour
Assumes returns are approximately normally distributed; intraday returns have fat tails, making z-score thresholds unreliable
Hurst exponent filter requires significant computation and changes over time — stocks can switch from mean-reverting to trending
prior_art: Z-score mean reversion is foundational in stat arb (Avellaneda & Lee, 2010; Gatev et al., 2006). Applied to single-name intraday rather than pairs. Hurst exponent filtering is discussed in Peters (1994) 'Fractal Market Analysis'. The adaptive lookback approach draws from Kaufman's adaptive moving average concept.
notes: Edge math: 0.57 * 50bps - 0.43 * 40bps = 28.5 - 17.2 = 11.3 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 0.3 bps. Essentially breakeven. The Hurst exponent pre-filter is the key differentiator — if it successfully identifies mean-reverting stocks, win rate should be 0.60+, pushing net to ~5 bps. Critical to validate.

name: rsi_extreme_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: RSI(2) on 1-min bars reaches extreme levels (<5 or >95) relatively frequently and these extremes revert quickly. The very short 2-period RSI captures momentum exhaustion at the micro level — when RSI(2) < 5, price has closed lower than the previous close for 2 consecutive bars with large magnitude, indicating a short-term selling climax. Larry Connors' research on RSI(2) for daily bars showed mean reversion at extremes; the same logic applies to 1-min bars but with faster reversion. The edge exists because RSI(2) signals at the 1-min level are too fast for manual traders and the profit per trade is too small for institutional attention. Indian markets have higher retail participation, which creates more noisy overshoots.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND intraday_volatility(20) > 0.8%

long.confirmation: RSI(close, 2) crosses above 10 (initial bounce from extreme)

short.confirmation: RSI(close, 2) crosses below 90 (initial pullback from extreme)

exit.target: RSI(close, 2) crosses 60 (longs) or crosses 40 (shorts) — momentum normalized
exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry (tight stop for short-duration trades)
exit.trailing_stop: none — trades are too short for trailing stops to add value
exit.signal_exit: exit if RSI(close, 2) makes new extreme (below 3 for longs, above 97 for shorts)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; reduce to 50K after 3 consecutive losses

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; RSI extremes are less reliable in panic
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45 (fast trades ok late in day)
filters.trend_filter: RSI(14) between 30-70 ensures we are not fighting a strong trend
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask spread < 0.04% (tight spread essential for scalp-like trades)
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day for that stock
other_filters: max 2 trades in same stock in same direction within 30 min (avoid overtrading one name)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — RSI(2) reversion is well-documented but speed barrier exists on 1-min

weaknesses: Very high trade frequency (4-8/day) means costs eat the edge — need extremely tight execution
RSI(2) on 1-min bars is essentially a 2-bar momentum oscillator, extremely noisy, prone to whipsaws
Average winner is smaller than average loser (W:L = 0.8) — relies heavily on high win rate; a slight win rate drop makes strategy unprofitable
prior_art: Larry Connors & Cesar Alvarez ('Short-Term Trading Strategies That Work') extensively studied RSI(2) for daily bars. Connors found RSI(2)<5 had ~85% reversion rate on daily S&P 500 stocks. Adaptation to 1-min bars is less documented. Indian market application is novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.65 * 18bps - 0.35 * 22.5bps = 11.7 - 7.9 = 3.8 bps gross per trade. Costs ~11 bps per round trip. Net ≈ -7.2 bps. Significantly negative. This strategy as described is NOT profitable after costs. High trade frequency makes it worse. REQUIRES: (1) reduce costs via direct market access, (2) increase per-trade edge by filtering for only highest-conviction RSI(2) extremes, (3) consider RSI(3) instead for slightly longer holds. Included as research hypothesis — needs significant optimization to be viable.

name: deviation_from_ema_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Price acts like a rubber band around the EMA(50) on 1-min bars. When price deviates more than 1.5 * ATR(14) from EMA(50), the elastic tendency of mean reversion kicks in. The EMA(50) represents the last ~50 minutes of trend, and deviations beyond 1.5 ATR are unsustainable accelerations that typically revert to the EMA within 20-30 bars. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders use EMAs as directional trend indicators (above EMA = bullish) rather than measuring the distance FROM the EMA as a mean reversion signal. The distance-from-EMA approach treats the EMA as a magnet rather than a traffic light. This edge persists because measuring deviation from EMA requires additional computation beyond standard crossover logic.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 30 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: ema_slope > -0.01 * close (EMA not in strong downtrend)
long.confirmation: ema_dev_atr[t] > ema_dev_atr[t-1] (deviation narrowing, starting to snap back)

conditions: ema_slope < 0.01 * close (EMA not in strong uptrend)
short.confirmation: ema_dev_atr[t] < ema_dev_atr[t-1] (deviation narrowing, starting to snap back)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 2.5 * ATR(14) from EMA(50) — if deviation extends to 2.5 ATR, thesis broken
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * ATR(14) once past 60% of target
exit.signal_exit: exit if ema_dev_atr makes new extreme beyond ±2.5 ATR

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; normalize by ATR(14)/close across stocks

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (EMA(50) needs 50 bars) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: ema_slope should be near-flat — strong trend regimes make reversion unreliable
filters.event_filter: skip on earnings day for the stock
other_filters: skip if NIFTY 50 has moved >1.5% from open (strong market trend day)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — concept is simple but ATR-normalized deviation adds a layer vs raw EMA reversion

weaknesses: EMA(50) on 1-min = 50 minutes; this is a compromise between responsiveness and stability but may be too short
The 1.5 ATR threshold is data-mined-looking — needs robust out-of-sample validation across different market regimes
Stop loss at 2.5 ATR from EMA means potentially large per-trade loss relative to target, hurting the W:L ratio
prior_art: Mean reversion to moving averages is a foundation of TA (Murphy, 'Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets'). ATR-normalized deviation is similar to the 'Kase Bar' concept. Connors' research on price distance from MA as a reversion predictor (daily timeframe) is directly relevant. The rubber band analogy is from Linda Raschke.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 45bps - 0.44 * 37.5bps = 25.2 - 16.5 = 8.7 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.3 bps. Slightly negative. Need to either tighten stop (reduce to 2.0 ATR) to improve W:L or add confluence filter (e.g., VWAP agreement) to push win rate to 0.60+.

name: intraday_range_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When a stock touches its intraday high or low and immediately reverses on a specific bar pattern (pin bar / hammer at the extreme), it signals that the intraday range boundary has been defended. The intraday high/low acts as a natural support/resistance because algorithmic stop-placement and limit-order clustering occur at round extremes. The inefficiency arises because once an intraday extreme is established, many trailing stops and limit orders cluster just beyond it — when these are not triggered (false breakout), the snap-back into the range is aggressive. The edge persists because identifying 'defended range boundaries' in real-time requires pattern recognition beyond simple price comparison.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND intraday_range_today > 0.8%

long.confirmation: next bar closes above current bar's high (confirmation of bounce)

conditions: (high - close) / (high - low) > 0.7 (inverted pin bar / shooting star)
short.confirmation: next bar closes below current bar's low (confirmation of rejection)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: 50% of intraday range toward the midpoint: (session_high + session_low) / 2
exit.stop_loss: 0.15% beyond the session extreme (beyond session low for longs, beyond session high for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.1% once 40% of target reached
exit.signal_exit: exit if session extreme is breached on elevated volume (genuine breakout)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 14-22; too low = no range, too high = range breaks easily
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (let range establish) or after 14:45
filters.volume_filter: volume on pin bar > SMA(volume, 20) (volume at the extreme is essential)
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when price is above VWAP session midpoint (bullish bias)
filters.event_filter: skip on event days where range expansion is expected (RBI, budget)
other_filters: range must be established for at least 60 bars (1 hour) before signal is valid

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — range reversion with pin bar confirmation is pattern-dependent and hard to automate naively

weaknesses: On genuine breakout days, the first touch of the session extreme IS the breakout — strategy catches the wrong side
Pin bar recognition on 1-min bars is noisy; the pattern is more reliable on 5-min or 15-min bars
The 50% range reversion target is ambitious — many reversions stall at 20-30% of range
prior_art: Intraday range trading is classic (Toby Crabel, 'Day Trading with Short Term Price Patterns'). Pin bar / hammer patterns at range extremes are standard price action (Steve Nison, 'Japanese Candlestick Charting'). The combination of range boundary + candlestick pattern is well-practiced but hard to automate cleanly.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 40bps - 0.42 * 31bps = 23.2 - 13.0 = 10.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -0.8 bps. Marginally negative. Improvement: reduce target to 30% of range (more achievable, higher win rate) or use 5-min bar pin bars for higher-quality patterns.

name: microstructure_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Inferred order flow imbalance — approximated from volume on up-bars vs down-bars over a short rolling window — can detect when aggressive buying or selling has temporarily exhausted available liquidity. When buy-volume imbalance exceeds 70% of total volume over the last 10 bars but price stops advancing, it signals that buying pressure has been absorbed by limit sellers (institutional supply). The resulting reversion occurs as the aggressive buyers have been filled and new buying flow dries up. The edge exists because order flow imbalance analysis is typically done with L2 data which retail traders rarely have; this approximation using 1-min bar data provides a noisy but usable signal. The edge persists because the signal is inherently noisy and requires calibration — most retail traders give up after initial false signals.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 80 crore INR AND avg_trade_size > 50000 INR

indicators.name: buy_vol
indicators.params: volume * (close - low) / (high - low) where high != low, else volume * 0.5

indicators.name: sell_vol
indicators.params: volume * (high - close) / (high - low) where high != low, else volume * 0.5

long.confirmation: buy_imbalance_10[t] > buy_imbalance_10[t-1] (selling pressure easing, buyers returning)

short.confirmation: buy_imbalance_10[t] < buy_imbalance_10[t-1] (buying pressure easing, sellers returning)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: buy_imbalance_10 crosses 0.50 (flow normalized) OR 0.2% profit from entry
exit.signal_exit: exit if imbalance deepens (buy_imbalance > 0.80 for shorts, < 0.20 for longs)

filters.vix_filter: none — flow imbalance works across vol regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45
filters.volume_filter: need sufficient volume for buy/sell split to be meaningful: > 0.8x SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: none — counter-trend by design
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask spread < 0.04% (tight spread critical for microstructure signals)
filters.event_filter: skip on event days (genuine order flow shifts, not noise)
other_filters: skip bars where high == low (no range, buy/sell split is undefined)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — this is an approximation of true order flow; with better data, the edge is larger

weaknesses: Buy/sell volume split from bar OHLCV is a crude approximation — true order flow requires tick-level or L2 data
The 10-bar window is arbitrary and likely not optimal across all stocks; needs per-stock calibration
In low-tick-count environments (illiquid stocks), the buy/sell volume approximation breaks down completely
prior_art: Order flow imbalance research: Cont et al. (2014) 'Price Impact of Order Flow Imbalances'. Buy/sell volume approximation from OHLCV: known as the 'close location value' or CLV (Chaiken). Accumulation/Distribution line by Chaikin uses similar logic. The 10-bar rolling imbalance approach is closer to the VPIN concept (Easley et al., 2012).
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 20bps - 0.45 * 20bps = 11 - 9 = 2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -9 bps. Significantly negative with these parameters. This strategy CANNOT work at Zerodha cost levels with bar-level data. It is included as a research direction — with tick data and lower-cost execution (co-located, direct exchange access), the edge could be viable. Consider as an alpha signal to blend with other strategies rather than standalone.

name: relative_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Within a sector (e.g., private banks), the intraday return spread between the strongest and weakest stock tends to revert after reaching an extreme. If HDFC Bank is +1.5% and ICICI Bank is -0.5% at 11:00 AM (a 2% spread), the spread tends to narrow by EOD because both stocks share the same fundamental drivers (interest rates, NPA concerns). The excess spread is caused by timing differences in institutional order flow — one stock gets bought first, the other follows. The inefficiency exists because most intraday traders focus on absolute returns, not relative performance within a sector. The edge persists because monitoring relative spreads across multiple sectors in real-time requires infrastructure beyond typical retail setups.
universe: NIFTY 200 constituents, grouped by GICS sector
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND same sector has >=3 stocks meeting liquidity criteria

long.confirmation: relative_zscore[t] > relative_zscore[t-1] (relative underperformance starting to narrow)

short.confirmation: relative_zscore[t] < relative_zscore[t-1] (relative outperformance starting to narrow)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close; optionally pair with opposite position in sector ETF/strongest stock

exit.stop_loss: relative_zscore reaches ±3.0 (divergence deepening) OR 0.5% loss on the leg
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.2% once relative_zscore within ±0.5 of zero
exit.signal_exit: exit if sector itself starts moving against the position (macro shift)

risk.position_sizing: 1L per leg; if paired, 1L long + 1L short

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need relative data to stabilize) or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: both stocks in the pair must have adequate volume
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades when the sector is range-bound (|sector_median_return| < 1%)
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has a stock-specific event (earnings, corporate action) causing the relative divergence
other_filters: minimum 3 stocks in the sector passing liquidity filter for meaningful median

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — relative sector reversion requires real-time multi-stock infrastructure, barrier to entry

weaknesses: If relative divergence is caused by stock-specific news (upgrade/downgrade), it may not revert — event filter is imperfect
Running on single-stock basis (not paired) exposes to market beta; paired trading doubles costs and complexity
Sectors with few liquid stocks (e.g., only 3-4 names) have unreliable median estimates
prior_art: Pairs trading and relative value is foundational stat arb (Gatev et al., 2006). Sector relative strength is documented in Faber (2007). Intraday sector-relative reversion is less studied — most pairs trading literature is daily horizon. ETF stat arb (Avellaneda & Lee, 2010) is related but uses ETF baskets rather than sector medians.
notes: Edge math (single-leg): 0.55 * 50bps - 0.45 * 36bps = 27.5 - 16.2 = 11.3 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 0.3 bps. If paired: double costs to ~22 bps, but spread has lower volatility so stops are tighter, improving W:L. Need backtest to compare paired vs single-leg.

name: stochastic_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The Stochastic Oscillator (14,3,3) on 1-min bars identifies when price is near the bottom or top of its recent 14-bar range. When %K crosses above %D in the oversold zone (<20), it signals that downward momentum is exhausting and price is starting to revert from the range bottom. The dual smoothing (3-period SMA on both %K and %D) reduces noise on 1-min bars. The edge exists because the stochastic cross in extreme zones combines two concepts: (1) range position extremity and (2) momentum reversal confirmation. Most traders use stochastics on higher timeframes; on 1-min bars, the signals are faster but also noisier, creating a speed vs accuracy tradeoff that benefits automated execution.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: close > VWAP * 0.995 (not too far below VWAP)
long.confirmation: close > open on the cross bar (bullish bar at oversold cross)

conditions: close < VWAP * 1.005 (not too far above VWAP)
short.confirmation: close < open on the cross bar (bearish bar at overbought cross)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.signal_exit: exit if stoch_K re-enters extreme zone after crossing out (failed reversion)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45
filters.trend_filter: VWAP proximity filter serves as trend filter — only trade near VWAP
filters.event_filter: skip on stock earnings day
other_filters: skip if stoch_K has been in extreme zone for >10 bars (extended extreme, likely trending)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — stochastic crossover is one of the most well-known TA signals

weaknesses: Stochastic cross on 1-min bars is extremely noisy — false crosses are frequent, especially with 3-period smoothing
In trending markets, stochastic stays overbought/oversold for extended periods — crosses in extreme zones still fail
Strategy is highly crowded — stochastic is available on every charting platform and widely taught in beginner TA courses
prior_art: Stochastic Oscillator by George Lane (1950s). Standard TA textbook material. The (14,3,3) setting is the default in most platforms. Connors studied stochastic extremes as reversion signals on daily bars. Application to 1-min bars is less documented but common in retail day trading.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 25bps - 0.42 * 25bps = 14.5 - 10.5 = 4 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -7 bps. Strategy is NOT profitable as described. Too crowded and too noisy on 1-min bars. Included for completeness but needs significant enhancement (e.g., VWAP + volume confluence, longer stochastic periods) to become viable. Consider using as one signal in a composite score strategy instead.

name: williams_r_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Williams %R with a 20-period lookback on 1-min bars identifies when price is at the extreme of its 20-bar range (below -90 or above -10). Unlike stochastic, Williams %R is unsmoothed, making it faster to react to turning points but also noisier. The key insight is combining %R extremes with a volume spike: when Williams %R < -90 AND volume is >2x its 20-bar SMA, it indicates a capitulation-style selloff that exhausts sellers. The volume spike distinguishes a genuine extreme from a quiet drift to the range bottom. The edge exists because Williams %R is less popular than RSI/Stochastic among Indian traders, reducing signal crowding, and the volume-spike confirmation is not standard practice.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND intraday_volatility(20) > 0.8%

long.confirmation: wr_slope > 0 (Williams %R turning up from extreme) AND close > open

short.confirmation: wr_slope < 0 (Williams %R turning down from extreme) AND close < open

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.signal_exit: exit if williams_r re-enters extreme zone (<-95 for longs, >-5 for shorts)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45
filters.volume_filter: volume spike > 2x on the extreme bar (essential for signal quality)
filters.trend_filter: VWAP proximity filter: only trade within ±1% of VWAP (avoid trending extremes)
filters.event_filter: skip on stock earnings day
other_filters: skip if williams_r has been in extreme zone for >5 consecutive bars (trending, not reverting)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — Williams %R is less crowded than RSI/Stochastic but conceptually similar

weaknesses: Williams %R is unsmoothed — very noisy on 1-min bars; extreme readings can occur on a single large bar
The volume spike requirement (2x) filters out many valid signals; conversely, volume spikes can be caused by a single block deal, not capitulation
Essentially the same signal as Stochastic(20,1,1) inverted — not truly independent from other oscillator-based strategies
prior_art: Williams %R by Larry Williams (1973). Standard TA indicator. Less popular than RSI/Stochastic in Indian markets, which is actually an advantage. Volume spike confirmation on oscillator extremes is discussed by Elder ('Trading for a Living'). The concept of capitulation volume at extremes is from Wyckoff methodology.
notes: Edge math: 0.57 * 25bps - 0.43 * 23bps = 14.25 - 9.9 = 4.35 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -6.65 bps. Negative. The volume spike filter is the key differentiator — without it, %R reversion is unprofitable. With strict volume spike filter, win rate may improve to 0.62+, which would give: 0.62*25 - 0.38*23 = 15.5 - 8.7 = 6.8 bps gross, still below costs. Best used as a composite signal component, not standalone.

name: ema_crossover_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: EMA(9) crossing above EMA(21) on 1-min bars signals a short-term momentum shift. The 9-bar EMA captures the last ~9 minutes of sentiment while the 21-bar EMA captures the last ~21 minutes. A cross indicates that short-term buying pressure has overtaken medium-term average price, often signaling the start of an intraday trend leg. The edge exists because EMA crossovers, while simple, work better in Indian markets due to higher trending behavior (longer institutional order execution times vs US markets, leading to extended intraday trends). The key filter is ADX(14) > 25 to confirm a trending environment — crossovers in rangebound markets are chopped up. The edge is thin and depends on capturing 2-3 good trend legs per day while keeping losses small on false crossovers.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 30 crore INR AND beta(NIFTY50, 60) > 0.8

long.confirmation: cross bar closes in top 40% of its range AND volume > 1.2x SMA(volume, 10)

short.confirmation: cross bar closes in bottom 40% of its range AND volume > 1.2x SMA(volume, 10)

entry.entry_price: market order on cross bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry OR EMA(9) re-crosses EMA(21) in opposite direction
exit.signal_exit: exit on reverse EMA cross

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — momentum works across VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45
filters.trend_filter: ADX(14) > 25 (only trade in trending conditions)
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry (whipsaw increases)
other_filters: skip if EMA(9) and EMA(21) have crossed >4 times in last 60 bars (choppy market)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — EMA crossover is the most basic TA signal; edge depends on ADX filter and execution speed

weaknesses: Win rate is low (~42%) — requires psychological discipline to endure losing streaks of 5-8 trades
EMA crossover on 1-min bars generates many false signals even with ADX filter — choppy days accumulate losses
The signal is extremely well-known and taught in every beginner trading course — crowding risk is high
prior_art: EMA crossover is perhaps the most widely known trading signal (Murphy, 'Technical Analysis'). ADX as a trend strength filter is from Wilder (1978). The 9/21 EMA pair is commonly used by retail traders globally. Adding ADX and VWAP filters provides some differentiation but the core signal is generic.
notes: Edge math: 0.42 * 40bps - 0.58 * 20bps = 16.8 - 11.6 = 5.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -5.8 bps. Negative. EMA crossover alone is not sufficient for profitability after costs on 1-min bars. The ADX filter and VWAP alignment are essential but still insufficient. Strategy is best used as a directional bias signal combined with better entry timing (e.g., EMA cross for direction, then VWAP reversion for entry).

name: macd_signal_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: MACD(12,26,9) on 1-min bars generates a momentum signal when the MACD line crosses the signal line, but the key edge comes from the MACD histogram acceleration: when the histogram is not only positive but INCREASING (histogram[t] > histogram[t-1] > histogram[t-2]), momentum is accelerating and the trend is strengthening. This triple-increasing-histogram condition filters out the many false MACD crosses that plague basic implementations. The inefficiency is that most traders look at MACD line cross (binary signal) rather than histogram slope (continuous acceleration measure). Histogram acceleration captures the rate of change of momentum, which is more predictive of continuation than the momentum level itself.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND daily_volatility(20) > 1.0%

long.confirmation: histogram has been accelerating for 3 consecutive bars (momentum building)

short.confirmation: histogram has been decelerating (becoming more negative) for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order after 3-bar histogram acceleration confirmed

exit.target: 0.4% from entry OR MACD histogram deceleration (hist_accel < 0 for longs)
exit.stop_loss: 0.25% from entry OR MACD line crosses below signal line
exit.signal_exit: exit when histogram acceleration reverses (hist[t] < hist[t-1] for longs)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 (MACD needs warmup) or after 14:45
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment required (long above VWAP, short below)
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry days
other_filters: skip if MACD histogram has changed sign >4 times in last 50 bars (choppy)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — MACD is well-known but histogram acceleration is less commonly used as primary signal

weaknesses: MACD(12,26,9) was designed for daily bars — on 1-min bars, the lookbacks are very short (26 min) and noisy
Histogram acceleration can be caused by a single large bar, creating false acceleration signals
The 3-bar acceleration requirement means entry is delayed — by the time signal fires, much of the move may be done
prior_art: MACD by Gerald Appel (1979). Signal line crossover is standard. MACD histogram analysis is from Thomas Aspray (1986). Histogram acceleration as a distinct signal is discussed by Elder ('Trading for a Living'). The histogram divergence/acceleration concept adds value beyond basic MACD cross.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 40bps - 0.52 * 25bps = 19.2 - 13.0 = 6.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -4.8 bps. Negative on paper. The histogram acceleration filter is the key innovation — need to validate if it genuinely improves win rate vs basic MACD cross. If it pushes WR to 0.52+: 0.52*40 - 0.48*25 = 20.8 - 12 = 8.8 bps, still below costs. Needs further work.

name: adx_trend_strength_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: ADX rising above 25 from below signals the emergence of a new intraday trend. Rather than using ADX just as a filter (as in strategy 21), here ADX itself IS the signal. When ADX(14) crosses above 25 AND +DI > -DI (for longs) or -DI > +DI (for shorts), a new directional trend is forming. The edge exists because ADX measures trend strength regardless of direction, and the cross above 25 is a relatively specific event (~2-3 times per day per stock). The DI lines provide direction while ADX provides conviction. The inefficiency is that most traders use ADX as a lagging confirmation, not as a lead entry signal. By entering when ADX is just crossing 25 (nascent trend), we capture the early part of the trend before it becomes obvious to all participants.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

long.confirmation: ADX(14) still rising (ADX[t] > ADX[t-1]) on the bar after crossing 25

short.confirmation: ADX(14) still rising (ADX[t] > ADX[t-1]) on the bar after crossing 25

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.25% from entry OR ADX drops below 20 (trend failed to develop)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.2% once profit exceeds 0.3%; widen to 0.3% if ADX > 40
exit.signal_exit: exit if ADX starts declining AND DI lines converge (trend fading)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if DI spread > 20 (strong directional conviction)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — ADX-based entries work across VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 (ADX needs warmup) or after 14:45
filters.trend_filter: DI spread > 10 ensures genuine directional bias, not noise
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day
other_filters: skip if ADX has crossed 25 and fallen back below 25 twice in last 60 bars (false breakouts)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — ADX is widely known but the specific entry on ADX crossing 25 with DI confirmation is less common

weaknesses: ADX is inherently lagging — by the time ADX crosses 25, the trend has already started 14+ bars ago
On 1-min bars, ADX(14) reacts to only 14 minutes of data, making the 25 threshold potentially unstable
False ADX breakouts above 25: ADX can spike above 25 on a single large bar and immediately fall back
prior_art: ADX/DMI system by Welles Wilder ('New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems', 1978). Standard textbook trend following. The ADX > 25 threshold for trend confirmation is widely used. Using ADX cross as entry rather than filter is less conventional — most sources use DI cross for entry and ADX for filter.
notes: Edge math: 0.47 * 50bps - 0.53 * 28bps = 23.5 - 14.8 = 8.7 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.3 bps. Marginally negative. If the DI spread filter (>10) pushes win rate to 0.50: 0.50*50 - 0.50*28 = 25 - 14 = 11 bps gross, net 0 bps. Breakeven. Needs additional edge from trailing stop capturing outsized winners in strong trend days.

name: roc_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Rate of Change (ROC) over 20 bars on 1-min data measures the percentage price change over the last 20 minutes. When ROC(20) exceeds its 95th percentile for that stock's intraday distribution (computed over the last 5 sessions), it signals an abnormally strong momentum burst. Unlike fixed thresholds, using percentile-based ROC adapts to each stock's volatility profile. The edge exists because these extreme ROC events often correspond to institutional block executions or algorithmic momentum-chasing that creates a self-reinforcing trend for the next 15-30 minutes. The inefficiency persists because computing per-stock ROC percentiles in real-time requires historical intraday data infrastructure that most retail traders lack.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND has at least 5 prior sessions of 1-min data

long.confirmation: ROC_20 remains above 90th percentile for 2 consecutive bars (sustained momentum, not one-bar spike)

short.confirmation: ROC_20 remains below 10th percentile for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd consecutive extreme-percentile bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry (tight stop — if momentum fades quickly, thesis is wrong)
exit.signal_exit: exit if ROC_pctile drops below 50 (momentum normalized)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if ROC_pctile > 99 (extreme outlier momentum)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — extreme ROC can occur in any VIX regime
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30 (need time for momentum to play out)
filters.volume_filter: volume surge > 2x essential — filters out low-volume noise spikes
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment required
filters.event_filter: check if ROC spike is news-driven — may continue (good) or be a one-time pop (bad)
other_filters: requires 5 prior sessions of intraday data for percentile computation

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — percentile-based ROC thresholds are adaptive and not commonly used at this timeframe

weaknesses: Momentum chasing after extreme ROC can lead to buying the top — the spike may be a one-bar outlier event (news, block deal)
The 2-bar confirmation delay means entering after significant price movement; risk/reward may already be degraded
Per-stock percentile calculation requires maintaining 5 days of 1-min data per stock — significant data management overhead
prior_art: Rate of Change is a basic momentum indicator. Percentile-based thresholds are used in quantile regression and momentum factor research (Jegadeesh & Titman, 1993 for daily). Intraday ROC percentiles are less documented. The volume confirmation requirement draws from Blitz & Vliet (2008) 'Momentum Factor' research on volume-confirmed momentum.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 50bps - 0.50 * 28bps = 25 - 14 = 11 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 0 bps. Breakeven on paper. The trailing stop should capture outlier winners (>0.5%) that pull the average up. If avg winner expands to 60bps with trailing: 0.50*60 - 0.50*28 = 16 bps gross, net ~5 bps. Viable with trailing stop optimization.

name: price_channel_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Donchian Channel breakout using a 30-bar lookback on 1-min data captures new 30-minute highs/lows as trend continuation signals. When price breaks above the highest high of the last 30 bars, it has exceeded a natural resistance level and momentum traders pile in. The original Turtle Trading system used Donchian channels on daily bars; adapting to 1-min bars with a volume confirmation filter captures intraday breakout dynamics. The edge exists because genuine breakouts from 30-minute consolidations often lead to continuation due to stop-loss triggering above the old high and new momentum buying. The filtering of false breakouts via volume (>1.5x average) and VWAP alignment provides edge over naive channel breakout implementations.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: DC_width_pct > 0.3 (sufficient range to break out from)
long.confirmation: breakout bar closes within top 25% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) > 0.75

short.confirmation: breakout bar closes within bottom 25% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) < 0.25

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout bar close

exit.target: DC_width_pct projected from breakout point (measured move: breakout_price + DC_width)
exit.stop_loss: DC_mid (midline of the channel — if price pulls back to middle, breakout failed)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at half-channel width once profit exceeds DC_width * 0.5
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back inside the channel (below DC_upper for longs)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; adjust size inversely with DC_width to normalize risk

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 14 (need some volatility for breakouts to work); < 30
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: VWAP direction should align with breakout direction
filters.event_filter: skip on budget/RBI day (breakouts may reverse on macro)
other_filters: DC_width_pct must be between 0.3% and 2.0% (too narrow = noise, too wide = range too large)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — Donchian breakout is classic and well-known but volume + close position filters add edge

weaknesses: Low win rate (~40%) is psychologically difficult; many false breakouts, especially in range-bound markets
On 1-min bars, a 30-bar channel is only 30 minutes — breakout significance is lower than daily Donchian channels
Volume spike requirement may cause late entries — by the time volume confirms, the best entry price is gone
prior_art: Donchian Channel breakout is the foundation of the Turtle Trading system (Curtis Faith, 'Way of the Turtle'). Richard Donchian developed the original 20-day channel breakout in the 1960s. Adapted to intraday with shorter lookback and volume filter. Similar to 'London Breakout' strategies in FX adapted for Indian equity hours.
notes: Edge math: 0.40 * 65bps - 0.60 * 27bps = 26 - 16.2 = 9.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -1.2 bps. Marginally negative. Trailing stop is crucial — capturing a few outsized winners (100+ bps) pulls avg winner up. With trailing stop, avg winner may rise to 80bps: 0.40*80 - 0.60*27 = 32 - 16.2 = 15.8 bps gross, net ~5 bps. Strategy viability depends on trailing stop execution quality.

name: momentum_score_composite_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A composite momentum score aggregating 5 normalized sub-signals — RSI(14), MACD histogram, ROC(10), ADX direction, and volume momentum — into a single -100 to +100 score reduces the noise of any single indicator. Each sub-signal is normalized to [-20, +20] and summed. When the composite score exceeds +60 or falls below -60, all 5 signals agree on strong directional momentum. The edge exists because multi-indicator confluence dramatically reduces false signals. While any single oscillator has a ~50% base rate, requiring agreement across 5 independent signals raises the conditional probability of continuation to ~65%. The inefficiency persists because computing a real-time composite score requires integrating multiple indicators programmatically, which is beyond most retail charting platforms.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

long.confirmation: composite_score has been > 50 for 3+ consecutive bars (sustained multi-indicator agreement)

short.confirmation: composite_score has been < -50 for 3+ consecutive bars

exit.stop_loss: 0.25% from entry OR composite_score drops below 20 (for longs) / rises above -20 (for shorts)
exit.signal_exit: exit when composite_score crosses zero (momentum consensus lost)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if composite_score > 80 (extreme consensus)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 (indicators need warmup) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment is built into entry conditions
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day and RBI policy day
other_filters: at least 4 of 5 sub-scores must be positive (long) or negative (short) — not just sum threshold

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — composite scoring with 5 signals is computationally complex and not easily replicated

weaknesses: 5 indicators means 5 potential sources of overfitting — the normalization and clipping parameters are all tunable
Signal is rare (composite > 60 with all confirmation) — may have 0-1 trades on quiet days
All 5 indicators are lagging — composite agreement means the move is already well underway by entry time
prior_art: Multi-indicator scoring is used in quantitative factor models (Barra, Axioma). Composite momentum scores are discussed in Clenow ('Stocks on the Move') for daily timeframe. The specific 5-indicator combination and normalization scheme here is novel but the concept is standard.
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 50bps - 0.45 * 33bps = 27.5 - 14.9 = 12.6 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 1.6 bps per trade. Marginally positive. The strength is in signal quality — few trades but high conviction. With 1 trade/day average: 1.6 bps * 1L = ~16 INR/day = ~4000 INR/year. Not viable as standalone at this capital level. Need to scale capital or use as overlay signal.

name: relative_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Stocks showing intraday return > 2x NIFTY 50 intraday return (when NIFTY is up) exhibit persistent relative momentum for the remainder of the session. This occurs because institutional allocation decisions (mutual funds, FIIs) that drive one stock to outperform unfold over hours, not minutes. If HDFC Bank is +1.5% while NIFTY is +0.5% at 11 AM, the buying flow that caused this outperformance likely has more volume to execute. The edge exists because intraday relative strength is rarely quantified — most use end-of-day RS. The inefficiency persists because measuring real-time relative momentum requires comparing individual stock returns to the index continuously, which is beyond standard charting.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND NIFTY 50 constituent or NIFTY Next 50

long.confirmation: relative_return is increasing: relative_return[t] > relative_return[t-10] (RS still building)

short.confirmation: relative_return is decreasing: relative_return[t] < relative_return[t-10] (RW still building)

exit.target: 0.5% absolute return on the stock (not relative)
exit.stop_loss: 0.3% from entry OR relative_return flips sign (stock now underperforming)
exit.signal_exit: exit if relative_return_30 flips sign (short-term RS lost)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — relative momentum is market-condition-agnostic
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:30 (need morning to establish RS) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs when NIFTY is mildly positive (0-1%); strong trends reduce stock-level alpha
filters.event_filter: skip if relative strength is caused by stock-specific news rather than flow
other_filters: skip if stock has earnings today (RS may reverse on intraday leak)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — intraday relative strength is under-researched and under-utilized

weaknesses: Relative strength can be entirely driven by a single morning block deal — not sustained institutional flow
By 10:30 when the signal fires, much of the day's outperformance may already be priced in (look-ahead problem)
This is a directional bet on one stock (not hedged) — exposed to market risk even though it is RS-motivated
prior_art: Relative strength momentum: Levy (1967), Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) on daily/monthly timeframes. IBD Relative Strength Rating (daily). Intraday RS continuation is less documented. Minervini ('Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard') discusses RS leaders but on daily charts. Intraday adaptation is relatively novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 50bps - 0.48 * 33bps = 26 - 15.8 = 10.2 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -0.8 bps. Marginally negative. If trailing stop captures outsized winners: avg winner rises to 60bps. 0.52*60 - 0.48*33 = 31.2 - 15.8 = 15.4 bps gross, net ~4 bps. Viable with trailing.

name: volume_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Volume-weighted momentum measures not just how much price moved, but how much volume participated in the move. When ROC(10) is positive AND cumulative volume on up-bars exceeds cumulative volume on down-bars by >60:40 over the last 20 bars, the momentum has institutional backing (large volume confirming the direction). Moves on thin volume tend to reverse; moves on heavy volume tend to continue. The edge exists because most momentum indicators ignore volume entirely (RSI, MACD, ROC are all price-only). Integrating volume into momentum scoring provides a more informative signal. The inefficiency persists because volume-weighted momentum is not a standard indicator in any major charting platform — it requires custom computation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND avg_bar_volume > 10000 shares per 1-min bar

long.confirmation: vol_ratio_20[t] > vol_ratio_20[t-5] (volume participation in up-moves is increasing)

short.confirmation: vol_ratio_20[t] < vol_ratio_20[t-5] (volume participation in down-moves is increasing)

exit.signal_exit: exit if vol_ratio_20 reverts to 0.45-0.55 range (volume participation neutralized)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: integrated into the signal — vol_ratio_20 IS the volume filter
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment ensures we trade with institutional flow, not against it
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day
other_filters: skip if total 20-bar volume is < 50% of average — low volume makes ratio unreliable

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volume-weighted momentum is not standard; custom indicator provides information edge

weaknesses: The up/down volume classification (close > open) is crude — a bar can close green on low volume and red on high volume
20-bar lookback means the volume ratio can be distorted by a single extreme-volume bar
In low-volume periods (lunch hour 12:30-13:30), the ratio is based on thin data and unreliable
prior_art: Volume Price Trend (VPT), On-Balance Volume (OBV), and Chaikin Money Flow all attempt to integrate volume with price direction. The specific up_vol / total_vol ratio over 20 bars is a simplified version of Volume Weighted Average Price's directional component. Easley et al. (2012) VPIN is related but uses a different bucketing approach.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 40bps - 0.48 * 27bps = 20.8 - 13.0 = 7.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -3.2 bps. Negative on conservative estimates. The vol_ratio filter is the edge — need to validate that high vol_ratio (>0.65) meaningfully predicts continuation vs base rate. If WR improves to 0.56: 0.56*40 - 0.44*27 = 22.4 - 11.9 = 10.5 bps, net ~0 bps. Still marginal.

name: acceleration_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Momentum acceleration — the second derivative of price — captures the rate at which momentum is changing. When ROC(10) is increasing AND its rate of change is also increasing (ROC of ROC > 0), momentum is accelerating, indicating the trend is in its early/middle stage. When acceleration turns negative while momentum is still positive, the trend is mature and about to decelerate. Entry on positive acceleration captures the sweet spot before peak velocity. The edge exists because most traders react to momentum level (first derivative) rather than momentum change rate (second derivative). Entering during acceleration rather than after peak momentum provides earlier entries with better risk/reward. The edge persists because second-derivative analysis requires comfort with calculus concepts that most retail traders lack.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND intraday_volatility(20) > 0.8%

conditions: ROC_accel_slope > 0 (acceleration is itself accelerating — strong trend emergence)
long.confirmation: ROC_accel has been positive for 3+ consecutive bars

short.confirmation: ROC_accel has been negative for 3+ consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order on 3rd consecutive acceleration bar close

exit.target: ROC_accel turns negative while ROC_10 still positive (for longs) — peak momentum, exit before deceleration
exit.signal_exit: exit if ROC_accel flips sign (momentum shifting from acceleration to deceleration)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day
other_filters: skip if ROC_10 > 1.0% already (trend too mature, acceleration is late-stage)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — second-derivative momentum is rarely used in practice despite theoretical advantages

weaknesses: Second derivative is extremely noisy on 1-min data — ROC of ROC amplifies noise quadratically
The 3-bar confirmation delays entry; acceleration phases are short on 1-min bars (often <5 bars), so the signal fires too late
Requires 3 layered lookbacks (ROC_10, ROC_accel over 5, slope over 5) — total effective lookback is ~20 bars, limiting early-session use
prior_art: Momentum acceleration is discussed in physics-based market models (Sornette, 'Why Stock Markets Crash'). The concept of 'jerk' (rate of change of acceleration) in market context is from Ehlers. Coppock Curve uses a similar concept on monthly data. Intraday second-derivative analysis is uncommon in published trading literature.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 45bps - 0.50 * 28bps = 22.5 - 14 = 8.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.5 bps. Negative on paper. The key value of this strategy is in signal timing — entering during acceleration rather than after peak should improve the W:L ratio. Need to validate that ROC_accel > 0 entries have meaningfully better outcomes than ROC > 0 entries.

name: institutional_flow_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Large individual bar volume spikes (>5x SMA(volume,20)) that move price by >0.2% in one direction likely represent institutional block execution or large algo orders. These create temporary momentum because: (1) the large order itself moves the price, (2) other algos detect the large print and follow (momentum ignition), (3) the institutional trader likely has more volume to execute after the initial block. The edge exists because detecting these volume spikes in real-time and acting within 1-2 bars captures the follow-through momentum before it dissipates. The inefficiency persists because distinguishing a genuine institutional block from a large retail order or ETF creation/redemption is difficult — we use the combination of volume spike + price impact + VWAP direction as a proxy.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 100 crore INR AND institutional_ownership > 40%

long.confirmation: next bar after spike also closes green (follow-through buying)

short.confirmation: next bar after spike also closes red (follow-through selling)

entry.entry_price: market order on follow-through bar close (2nd bar after initial spike)

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry OR price crosses back to the open of the spike bar (impact fully reversed)
exit.signal_exit: exit if a reverse vol_spike > 5x occurs in opposite direction (counter-block)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — institutional flows occur regardless of VIX
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: vol_spike > 5x is the core filter (very strict)
filters.trend_filter: VWAP direction should confirm the spike direction
filters.event_filter: check if spike coincides with index move — if yes, it is macro-driven, not stock-specific flow
other_filters: ignore spikes in first 5 min (opening auction distortion) and last 10 min (closing auction)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — volume spike detection is simple but distinguishing institutional from noise requires judgment

weaknesses: Not all volume spikes are institutional — could be ETF rebalancing, bulk deal, or single large retail order
The 5x volume threshold is very strict, reducing trade frequency to 1-2 per day across the universe
Entry is 2 bars after the spike — by then, initial price impact may have already decayed, entering after the best move
prior_art: Institutional flow detection: Kyle (1985) informed trading model. Volume spike analysis: Karpoff (1987) 'Relation Between Price Changes and Trading Volume'. Momentum ignition: Brogaard et al. (2014) 'High-Frequency Trading and Price Discovery'. The specific 5x volume threshold with price-impact filter is a practical adaptation of these concepts.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 40bps - 0.48 * 25bps = 20.8 - 12.0 = 8.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.2 bps. Marginally negative. If follow-through bar has strong candle pattern (marubozu), win rate may push to 0.56: 0.56*40 - 0.44*25 = 22.4 - 11 = 11.4 bps gross, net ~0.4 bps. Borderline. Best used as an alert/screening signal to feed into a manual discretionary framework.

name: gap_continuation_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Stocks that gap up >1.5% at open AND continue higher in the first 15 minutes (close at bar 15 > open of bar 1) exhibit strong continuation momentum for the next 60-90 minutes. This is the opposite of gap fill — here the gap is GENUINE new information (earnings beat, upgrade, sector catalyst) and the first 15 minutes of upside confirm that the market is digesting the news positively with follow-through buying. The edge exists because most gap strategies focus on gap FILL (mean reversion), while gap CONTINUATION is the higher-edge trade when the gap has institutional backing. The 15-min confirmation period filters out dead-cat-bounce gaps. The inefficiency persists because distinguishing fillable gaps from continuation gaps requires monitoring volume profile and price action in the first 15 minutes.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND gap_pct > 1.5% AND gap_pct < 5%
session: 09:30-14:00 IST (enter after confirmation, ride through midday)

conditions: close > VWAP (above session VWAP after 15 min)
long.confirmation: close at bar 15 > high of first 5 bars (higher high after gap, not just drift)

short.confirmation: close at bar 15 < low of first 5 bars (lower low after gap, genuine sell pressure)

entry.entry_price: market order at 09:30 IST (after 15th 1-min bar from 09:15)

exit.target: 0.8% from entry (larger target — riding genuine momentum)
exit.stop_loss: VWAP (if price drops to VWAP, gap continuation thesis is broken) OR 0.5% from entry
exit.signal_exit: exit if close drops below EMA(close, 20) for 3 consecutive bars

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; scale to 1.5L for earnings-driven gaps (highest conviction)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; high VIX = gaps may reverse
filters.time_filter: entry only after first 15 min (09:30); no new entries after 12:00
filters.trend_filter: prefer gaps in direction of NIFTY move (not contra-index)
filters.event_filter: distinguish between earnings gap (likely to continue) and sympathy gap (less likely)
other_filters: gap must be >1.5% to filter out noise; <5% to avoid parabolic extremes

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — gap continuation with 15-min filter is less commonly automated

weaknesses: Very low trade frequency — most days have 0 stocks meeting gap > 1.5% with continuation criteria
The 15-min wait means missing the initial post-gap move; entry price is already extended from the pre-gap level
Gaps on sympathy (sector peer had news, this stock gaps with it) tend to fade, and distinguishing from genuine gaps is imperfect
prior_art: Gap-and-Go strategy by Ross Cameron (Warrior Trading) is the closest prior art. Gap continuation is discussed by Pristine.com and in Bulkowski ('Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns'). The 15-min confirmation window is a standard day trading concept. Academic evidence on gap fills vs continuation: Trennepohl (1972), more recently Yuksel & Zaim (2017).
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 80bps - 0.48 * 50bps = 41.6 - 24.0 = 17.6 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps (possibly 14 bps due to wider opening spreads). Net ≈ 3.6-6.6 bps per trade. One of the more promising strategies. Key challenge is frequency — may only trigger 2-3 times per week across the universe. Consider running across broader universe (BSE 500) to increase signal count.

name: intraday_trend_channel_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A linear regression channel fitted on the last 60 bars (1 hour) of 1-min data identifies the intraday trend direction and deviations from the trend line. Trading involves buying at the lower channel boundary when the overall regression slope is positive (uptrend with pullback to support), and selling at the upper boundary when slope is negative. The edge exists because linear regression channels dynamically adapt to the intraday trend — unlike fixed EMAs or Bollinger Bands, the channel tilts with the trend and provides more accurate support/resistance levels. The inefficiency persists because computing rolling linear regression with 2 standard deviation bands in real-time is computationally non-trivial and not available as a default indicator in most Indian broking platforms.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

long.confirmation: close > open on the touch bar (bounce from lower channel in uptrend)

short.confirmation: close < open on the touch bar (rejection from upper channel in downtrend)

entry.entry_price: limit order at linreg channel boundary, else market on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: close below linreg_lower - 0.5 * linreg_std (channel break for longs)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * linreg_std once past regression midline
exit.signal_exit: exit if linreg_slope flips sign (trend reversal)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars of data) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: linreg_slope must have consistent sign for 30+ bars (stable trend, not oscillating)
filters.event_filter: skip on macro event days
other_filters: R-squared of regression must be > 0.7 (trend channel must be a good fit to the data)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — rolling linear regression channels are not standard retail tools

weaknesses: 60-bar linear regression is computationally heavy and the channel parameters change every bar — instability in parameters
R-squared filter is essential but values on 1-min data are typically low (0.3-0.5), making 0.7 threshold very restrictive
Channel breaks (when they occur) are violent — the stop at 0.5 * linreg_std beyond the band may be triggered before the exit order executes
prior_art: Linear regression channels are discussed by Raff ('Raff Regression Channel'). Standard deviation channels around regression lines are in Gilbert Raff's work. Applied to intraday with R-squared filtering is less common. The concept overlaps with Keltner Channels but uses regression instead of EMA as midline.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 40bps - 0.44 * 31bps = 22.4 - 13.6 = 8.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.2 bps. Marginally negative. The R-squared filter is the differentiator — if it reliably selects stocks in clean channels, win rate should be 0.60+: 0.60*40 - 0.40*31 = 24 - 12.4 = 11.6 bps, net ~0.6 bps.

name: parabolic_sar_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Parabolic SAR with acceleration factor 0.02 (step) and 0.2 (max) on 1-min bars provides a mechanical trend-following system with built-in trailing stop. When SAR flips from above price to below price, it signals a bullish trend initiation; the SAR then accelerates toward price, creating a tightening trailing stop. The edge exists in using SAR flips only when confirmed by VWAP alignment and ADX > 20 — raw SAR on 1-min bars is too noisy. The filtered version reduces whipsaws by ~40%. The inefficiency persists because most traders either use SAR mechanically (noisy) or dismiss it entirely; the filtered version occupies a middle ground that combines SAR's excellent trailing stop mechanism with fundamental trend filters.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: PSAR_direction[t-1] == -1 (SAR was above — just flipped bullish)
long.confirmation: close of flip bar is in top 30% of its range AND volume > SMA(volume, 20)

conditions: PSAR_direction[t-1] == 1 (SAR was below — just flipped bearish)
short.confirmation: close of flip bar is in bottom 30% of its range AND volume > SMA(volume, 20)

entry.entry_price: market order on SAR flip confirmation bar close

exit.target: none — let SAR trailing stop manage the exit (SAR is the trailing stop)
exit.stop_loss: PSAR value (SAR IS the stop — exit when price hits SAR from the opposite side)
exit.trailing_stop: SAR itself accelerates toward price, acting as a dynamic trailing stop
exit.time_stop: 60 bars (override SAR if trade is stale)
exit.signal_exit: exit when PSAR_direction flips (SAR stop-and-reverse)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L per trade; size based on distance from entry to initial SAR value

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45
filters.trend_filter: ADX > 20 is the trend filter; VWAP alignment adds confirmation
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day (SAR gets whipsawed by expiry volatility)
other_filters: skip if there have been >4 SAR flips in the last 30 bars (choppy — SAR unreliable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — PSAR is well-known but the ADX + VWAP filtered version is less common

weaknesses: SAR on 1-min bars flips very frequently in range-bound markets — even with ADX filter, whipsaws are common
The acceleration factor causes SAR to quickly catch up to price, resulting in premature exits during healthy pullbacks
Low win rate (42%) is psychologically challenging; requires faith in the system during inevitable losing streaks
prior_art: Parabolic SAR by Welles Wilder ('New Concepts in Technical Trading Systems', 1978). Standard indicator available on all platforms. Using it on 1-min with ADX/VWAP filter is a practical adaptation. The stop-and-reverse mechanism is Wilder's original innovation. Various backtests show SAR performs best in trending markets (Kaufman, 'Trading Systems and Methods').
notes: Edge math: 0.42 * 55bps - 0.58 * 25bps = 23.1 - 14.5 = 8.6 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -2.4 bps. Marginally negative. SAR's strength is capturing outlier trends (>1% intraday moves) — when these occur, avg winner may be 80-100 bps. If avg winner = 80bps: 0.42*80 - 0.58*25 = 33.6 - 14.5 = 19.1 bps, net ~8 bps. Strategy viability depends on capturing a few big winners per month.

name: supertrend_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: SuperTrend indicator with period=10 and multiplier=3.0 on 1-min bars provides ATR-based trend direction with a dynamic support/resistance level. SuperTrend is particularly popular among Indian traders on Zerodha (it is a default indicator on Kite), creating a self-fulfilling prophecy where many traders enter/exit at SuperTrend flips. The edge exploits this Schelling point: when SuperTrend flips bullish, many retail traders enter simultaneously, creating a brief momentum burst. By entering at the flip with volume confirmation and exiting before the crowd (using a fixed target rather than waiting for re-flip), we capture the initial momentum burst. The edge persists because we are faster than manual retail traders reacting to the same signal.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 30 crore INR AND listed on Zerodha Kite (maximizes self-fulfilling effect)

long.confirmation: flip bar closes above SuperTrend value AND above previous bar's high

short.confirmation: flip bar closes below SuperTrend value AND below previous bar's low

entry.entry_price: market order on flip confirmation bar close

exit.target: 0.35% from entry (quick scalp on momentum burst, exit before crowd)
exit.stop_loss: SuperTrend value (if price falls back through ST, thesis is broken) OR 0.2%
exit.signal_exit: exit if SuperTrend re-flips within 10 bars (false signal)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:45
filters.volume_filter: volume_ratio > 1.5 on flip bar (confirms institutional participation)
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment (long above VWAP, short below)
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day
other_filters: skip if SuperTrend has flipped >3 times in last 20 bars (whipsaw regime)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — SuperTrend is extremely popular in India; the self-fulfilling edge is also its crowding risk

weaknesses: SuperTrend is the most popular indicator among Indian retail traders — extreme crowding means the signal edge has likely decayed
The self-fulfilling prophecy works both ways: if too many traders use it, the initial move is pre-empted by algos front-running retail
On 1-min bars, SuperTrend(10,3) has very short lookback — flips are frequent and often false, especially in range-bound markets
prior_art: SuperTrend was developed by Olivier Seban and is widely popular in Indian trading circles. It is essentially a simplified Parabolic SAR with ATR-based levels. Zerodha's Kite platform has it as a default indicator, boosting adoption. Multiple YouTube channels in India teach SuperTrend-based strategies (Vivek Bajaj, P R Sundar).
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 35bps - 0.50 * 25bps = 17.5 - 12.5 = 5.0 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -6.0 bps. Negative. SuperTrend as a standalone signal is likely unprofitable in 2024-2026 due to overcrowding. Its value is as a component in a multi-signal system or as a directional filter. Included because of its extreme popularity in India — important to evaluate and potentially dismiss.

name: hull_ma_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The Hull Moving Average (HMA) with period 16 on 1-min bars provides a nearly zero-lag smoothed price signal by using weighted moving averages of different periods combined with a square root transformation. HMA(16) responds to price changes faster than EMA(16) or SMA(16) while maintaining smoothness. When HMA(16) changes direction (slope flip from positive to negative or vice versa), it signals a momentum shift earlier than conventional MAs. The edge exists because HMA is mathematically superior to standard MAs for trend detection (reduced lag by ~50%) but is not widely known among Indian retail traders who predominantly use EMA/SMA. The inefficiency persists because HMA requires custom computation (WMA of WMA with sqrt period) — it is not available as a default indicator on most Indian platforms.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND daily_volatility(20) > 1.0%

conditions: HMA_slope_prev <= 0 (HMA just turned up — slope flip)
long.confirmation: HMA_slope > 0 for 2 consecutive bars after the flip (avoid single-bar noise flip)

conditions: HMA_slope_prev >= 0 (HMA just turned down — slope flip)
short.confirmation: HMA_slope < 0 for 2 consecutive bars after the flip

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd consecutive slope-confirmed bar close

exit.stop_loss: 0.2% from entry OR HMA_slope re-flips (direction reversal)
exit.signal_exit: exit when HMA_slope crosses zero (direction change)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: VWAP direction alignment
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day
other_filters: skip if HMA has flipped >5 times in last 30 bars (range-bound, HMA is useless)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — HMA is less well-known than EMA/SMA in India; computational barrier exists

weaknesses: HMA(16) on 1-min bars responds to only 16 minutes of data — too short for meaningful trend detection in slow-moving stocks
The low-lag property means HMA also has more false flips than EMA — it is responsive to noise, not just signal
Conceptually, HMA is just a smoother MA — it does not provide fundamentally different information from other MAs, just earlier (noisier) signals
prior_art: Hull Moving Average by Alan Hull (2005). Designed to reduce lag in moving averages. Formula: HMA = WMA(2*WMA(n/2) - WMA(n), sqrt(n)). Less commonly used in Indian markets compared to EMA/SMA. Hull himself demonstrated the indicator on daily and weekly charts, not 1-min bars.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 35bps - 0.52 * 22bps = 16.8 - 11.4 = 5.4 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -5.6 bps. Negative. HMA's theoretical advantage (low lag) does not translate to profitable standalone strategy on 1-min bars after Indian market costs. The math suggests using HMA as a directional filter for other entry mechanisms (e.g., HMA direction + VWAP reversion entry).

name: opening_range_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The classic 15-minute Opening Range Breakout (ORB) captures the directional resolution of early-session uncertainty. The first 15 minutes (09:15-09:30 IST) establish a range as institutional pre-market orders, overnight gap adjustments, and global cue reactions settle. A breakout above/below this range with volume signals the session's directional bias. The edge exists because the opening range concentrates information discovery into a narrow time window — once resolved, the chosen direction tends to persist for 1-3 hours. The Indian market opens 15 min later than pre-market (09:00), so the 09:15-09:30 range absorbs the most intense order flow. The inefficiency persists because while ORB is well-known, proper execution with volume confirmation and tight risk management is the differentiator.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents on NSE + NIFTY 50 index futures
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND opening_range(15min) > 0.3% AND < 2.0%

conditions: volume on breakout bar > SUM(volume, 15) / 15 * 2.0 (2x avg first-15-min bar volume)
long.confirmation: first 1-min close above OR_high with body > 50% of bar range (not a wick breakout)

short.confirmation: first 1-min close below OR_low with body > 50% of bar range

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout bar close

exit.target: 1.0 * OR_range from breakout level (measured move equal to OR range)
exit.stop_loss: OR_mid (midpoint of opening range) — if price retreats to OR midpoint, breakout failed
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * OR_range once profit exceeds 0.7 * OR_range
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back inside OR for 3 consecutive bars (false breakout confirmed)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; scale down if OR_range > 1.5% (larger range = larger risk)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; ORB works best in moderate vol environments (14-22)
filters.time_filter: entry only after 09:30 IST; no new entries after 12:00
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume > 2x average first-15-min bar volume
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakout direction aligned with global cue (SGX Nifty direction pre-market)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy day (ORB unreliable on event-driven volatility)
other_filters: OR_range must be between 0.3% and 2.0% — too narrow is noise, too wide means stop is too far
only trade first breakout attempt — if price breaks, comes back, and breaks again, skip

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — ORB is well-known but consistent execution with proper filters is rare

weaknesses: False breakouts are the primary failure mode — price breaks OR, triggers entry, then reverses into the range
ORB works best in trending markets; in range-bound, choppy days, both sides of the OR get hit (double loss)
The first breakout after OR is often the most crowded trade — many traders use ORB, reducing edge from crowding
prior_art: Opening Range Breakout is one of the oldest day trading strategies (Toby Crabel, 1990 'Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns'). Mark Fisher's ACD method is a variation. Extremely well-documented. Indian adaptation by Zerodha Varsity and multiple trading educators. The 15-min variant is the most common in India due to the 09:15 market open.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 70bps - 0.50 * 39bps = 35 - 19.5 = 15.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4.5 bps per trade. Positive. ORB is one of the more viable strategies despite being well-known, because: (1) few traders execute it with proper filters, (2) the measured move target is disciplined, (3) the OR midpoint stop is logical and prevents catastrophic losses.

name: opening_range_breakout_30_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The 30-minute Opening Range (09:15-09:45 IST) is a more robust version of the 15-min ORB. The additional 15 minutes of price discovery reduces false breakouts by ~25% compared to 15-min ORB because more institutional orders have been executed, providing a truer reflection of the day's equilibrium zone. The trade-off is later entry and fewer bars to hold the position.
