The edge exists because the 30-min OR absorbs: (1) opening auction imbalances, (2) initial gap adjustment, (3) first wave of institutional order flow, AND (4) early retail momentum trades. By the time the 30-min OR is established, the noise has subsided and a breakout reflects genuine directional conviction. This is more reliable but less frequent than 15-min ORB.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents on NSE + Bank NIFTY index
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND OR_30min_range > 0.4% AND < 2.5%

long.confirmation: 2 consecutive 1-min bars closing above OR30_high (reduces false breakouts)

short.confirmation: 2 consecutive 1-min bars closing below OR30_low

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd consecutive close beyond OR boundary

exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * OR30_range once 70% of target achieved
exit.signal_exit: exit if 3 consecutive bars close back inside OR30 range

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; inversely proportional to OR30_range (wider range = smaller position)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 14-25; moderate VIX is ideal for ORB
filters.time_filter: entry only after 09:45; no new entries after 12:00
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume > 2.5x average OR-period bar volume
filters.trend_filter: SGX Nifty direction pre-market should align with breakout direction
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day, budget day, F&O expiry
other_filters: only trade first breakout; ignore re-breakouts (second chance breakout is unreliable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — 30-min ORB is less popular than 15-min ORB, slightly less crowded

weaknesses: Later entry (09:45+) means less time for the trade to develop within the session — hold period is compressed
The 2-bar confirmation filter further delays entry, often missing 10-15% of the initial breakout move
On days with large opening gaps (>1.5%), the 30-min OR may be too wide for the measured move target to be realistic
prior_art: 30-min ORB is a variant discussed by Mark Fisher (ACD Method, 'The Logical Trader'). Toby Crabel's work covers multiple OR periods (5, 15, 30, 60 min). Indian adaptation is less documented for 30-min vs 15-min. The 2-bar confirmation is from Jeff Cooper's 'Hit and Run Trading'.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 75bps - 0.48 * 44bps = 39 - 21.1 = 17.9 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 6.9 bps per trade. Positive. 30-min ORB appears more viable than 15-min ORB due to higher win rate and lower false breakout rate, despite later entry. One of the top-ranked breakout strategies by expected net edge.

name: narrow_range_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: NR4/NR7 patterns (today's daily range is the narrowest of the last 4 or 7 days) signal volatility compression that precedes range expansion. On such days, the intraday breakout from the first-hour range tends to be more decisive because compressed volatility acts like a coiled spring. The edge exists because NR days are identifiable before the market opens (based on prior days' ranges), allowing pre-session preparation. The inefficiency persists because NR days occur only ~15-20% of the time, and many traders do not systematically track multi-day range compression. When the breakout occurs on an NR day, it has higher follow-through because the prior compression absorbed conflicting orders, and the breakout resolves the ambiguity.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND is_NR4_or_NR7_day == True

indicators.name: is_NR4
indicators.params: True if today's daily range < min(daily_range[-1], ..., daily_range[-3])

indicators.name: is_NR7
indicators.params: True if today's daily range < min(daily_range[-1], ..., daily_range[-6])

conditions: is_NR4 == True OR is_NR7 == True (pre-session filter)
long.confirmation: breakout bar closes within top 30% of its range AND next bar also closes above first_hour_high

short.confirmation: breakout bar closes within bottom 30% of its range AND next bar also closes below first_hour_low

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation (2nd bar closing beyond first-hour range)

exit.target: 1.5 * ATR(14d) from entry (NR days tend to expand by 1-2 ATR)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * ATR(14d) once profit > 1.0 * ATR(14d)
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back inside first-hour range for 3 consecutive bars

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L on NR7 days (stronger signal than NR4)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; NR days in high-VIX regimes are contradictory signals
filters.time_filter: entry only after 10:15 IST (first hour range must be established); no entries after 13:00
filters.trend_filter: prefer breakout direction aligned with NIFTY 50 trend of the day
filters.event_filter: NR days before RBI/budget are powerful — range expansion on event day is expected
other_filters: NR7 is preferred over NR4 for higher conviction; NR4-only trades get reduced position size

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — NR pattern tracking requires multi-day context; not commonly automated

weaknesses: NR days occur only 15-20% of the time — very low trade frequency (1-4 trades per week across universe)
Not all NR days result in range expansion on the same day — expansion may come the next day (useless for intraday)
The first-hour range on NR days can be very tight, making the breakout target small and stop tight — higher chance of noise-triggered exits
prior_art: NR4/NR7 patterns from Toby Crabel ('Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns', 1990). Extensively studied by Linda Raschke and Larry Connors ('Street Smarts'). Volatility compression preceding expansion is a well-established market principle. Indian adaptation combining NR with first-hour range breakout is less common.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 80bps - 0.48 * 44bps = 41.6 - 21.1 = 20.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 9.5 bps per trade. One of the strongest expected edges. Low trade frequency is the main challenge — need to scan the full NIFTY 200 universe daily to find stocks in NR4/NR7 patterns. Expect 2-5 qualifying stocks per NR day.

name: volatility_contraction_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When ATR(14) on 1-min bars contracts to below the 20th percentile of its session distribution, it signals a volatility squeeze that precedes a directional breakout. This is the intraday equivalent of daily ATR contraction patterns. The mechanism is that low ATR indicates temporary equilibrium between buyers and sellers — once this equilibrium breaks, the move is often sustained because trapped traders on the wrong side need to cover. The edge exists because ATR percentile analysis on 1-min bars is not a standard tool — most traders use ATR as a fixed number for stop-loss sizing, not as a dynamic squeeze indicator. The inefficiency persists because real-time ATR percentile computation requires session-level context that standard charting tools do not provide.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND daily_ATR(14)/close > 0.01 (min 1% daily volatility)

indicators.name: ATR_pctile
indicators.params: percentile_rank(ATR_14, all ATR_14 values this session)

conditions: ATR_pctile < 20 within last 5 bars (squeeze recently occurred)
bar_range > ATR_14 * 1.5 (expansion bar — range exceeds recent ATR)
long.confirmation: close > high of squeeze range (new high after the contraction period)

short.confirmation: close < low of squeeze range (new low after the contraction period)

entry.entry_price: market order on expansion bar close

exit.target: 2.0 * ATR_14 (measured from the squeeze range, using pre-squeeze ATR for calibration)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of squeeze range (if long, stop at squeeze low; if short, stop at squeeze high)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 1.0 * ATR_14 once profit > 1.5 * ATR_14
exit.signal_exit: exit if ATR_pctile drops back below 20 after initial expansion (failed breakout, re-squeezing)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; size inversely with squeeze range width

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; VIX squeeze + ATR squeeze is a strong setup
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need session data for percentile) or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: expansion bar volume > 2x 20-bar SMA (genuine breakout, not drift)
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment required
filters.event_filter: squeeze before an event (RBI, earnings) is a strong setup
other_filters: squeeze must be >= 10 bars (10 min) to be considered genuine compression

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ATR percentile squeeze is not a standard retail indicator

weaknesses: Not all ATR squeezes resolve with directional breakouts — some simply continue as low-vol drift (no expansion)
The 10-bar minimum squeeze requirement may miss shorter compression patterns that also lead to valid breakouts
Using the squeeze range as stop means the stop distance varies — can be very tight (good) or very wide (bad) depending on the squeeze
prior_art: ATR contraction/expansion: John Carter's TTM Squeeze indicator. Bollinger Band width squeeze is the classic version (Bollinger, 2001). Using ATR percentile rather than absolute ATR is an adaptation from quantile-based analysis. Volatility clustering (GARCH) literature supports the theoretical basis for squeeze→expansion sequences.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 70bps - 0.52 * 35bps = 33.6 - 18.2 = 15.4 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4.4 bps per trade. Positive. One of the better breakout strategies due to the favorable W:L ratio. The 2:1 winner:loser ratio is achievable because squeeze breakouts, when they work, tend to be large moves relative to the tight squeeze range.

name: volume_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A volume breakout occurs when volume on a single bar exceeds 5x its 20-bar SMA AND price simultaneously breaks to a new session high/low. The extreme volume signals that a large participant (institution, algo) is aggressively entering the market. Unlike price-only breakouts (which fail ~60% of the time), volume-confirmed breakouts have a higher success rate (~55%) because the volume demonstrates real capital commitment. The edge exists because most breakout traders use fixed volume thresholds (e.g., >2x average), while using a 5x threshold is much more selective and catches only the most extreme volume events. The inefficiency persists because the 5x threshold is so strict that it filters out most breakout attempts, leaving only genuine institutional-participation events.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: high > session_high[t-1] (new session high on the vol spike bar)
(close - low) / (high - low) > 0.7 (closed near high of bar)
long.confirmation: next bar also closes above previous session high (not a one-bar fakeout)

conditions: low < session_low[t-1] (new session low on the vol spike bar)
(high - close) / (high - low) > 0.7 (closed near low of bar)
short.confirmation: next bar also closes below previous session low

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: VWAP OR 0.25% from entry, whichever is tighter
exit.signal_exit: exit if a reverse vol spike >3x occurs in opposite direction

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:00 (need time for follow-through)
filters.volume_filter: 5x is the core filter — extremely strict, by design
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment with breakout direction
filters.event_filter: volume spikes on earnings/corporate action days may be noise — extra caution
other_filters: ignore vol spikes in first 5 bars (opening auction distortion) and last 10 bars (closing)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — the 5x threshold is stricter than most implementations

weaknesses: 5x volume spikes are rare — may see 0-2 qualifying signals per day across the entire NIFTY 200 universe
Some 5x volume spikes are caused by block deals or basket trades at market midpoint — no directional information
The confirmation bar requirement means entering after a large-volume bar, where slippage may be higher than normal 3 bps
prior_art: Volume breakout is a core concept in TA (Edwards & Magee, 'Technical Analysis of Stock Trends'). Volume precedes price is a market adage attributed to Joseph Granville. Using extreme volume thresholds (5x) is less common than the standard 2x threshold in literature. Related to the 'uptick volume' concept from the NYSE TICK indicator.
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 50bps - 0.45 * 33bps = 27.5 - 14.9 = 12.6 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 1.6 bps per trade. Marginally positive. Low frequency limits absolute P&L. With 1 trade/day average: 16 INR/day on 1L capital. Scale up capital to 3-5L per trade for meaningful returns. The strict 5x filter is the key — relaxing to 3x would increase frequency but likely reduce edge.

name: range_expansion_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When a stock trades in a tight intraday base (range < 0.3% over 30+ bars), it represents a balance between supply and demand at a specific price level. When this base 'expands' — a single bar has a range > 3x the average bar range of the base period — it signals that the equilibrium has broken. The direction of expansion (above or below the base) predicts continuation because: (1) limit orders that formed the base are consumed, (2) stops placed just outside the base trigger, creating additional momentum, (3) the flat base attracted options sellers who now need to delta-hedge, amplifying the move. The edge exists because identifying tight bases in real-time and measuring expansion relative to the base requires custom computation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: expansion_ratio > 3.0 (current bar range is 3x the base average)
long.confirmation: expansion bar closes within top 25% of its range (strong directional close)

short.confirmation: expansion bar closes within bottom 25% of its range

entry.entry_price: market order on expansion bar close

exit.target: base_range projected from breakout level (measured move = base height from breakout point)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of the base (if long, stop at base low; if short, stop at base high)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * base_range once profit > 1.0 * base_range
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back within the base for 2 bars (false expansion)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; tight base = small stop = can potentially increase to 1.5L

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; tight bases are more meaningful in moderate vol
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need 30+ bars of data) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer expansions in direction of VWAP and NIFTY 50 trend
filters.event_filter: skip if expansion is caused by scheduled news release (predictable expansion)
other_filters: base must be at least 30 bars (30 min) of tight range to be considered genuine consolidation

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — tight base detection with expansion ratio is a custom metric not widely available

weaknesses: Tight bases are rare intraday — may see 0-1 qualifying setups per day across the universe
The 3x expansion ratio can be triggered by a single anomalous bar (news flash, fat finger) — not always genuine momentum
Using base range as the target may be too ambitious if the base is very tight (0.1% base = 0.1% target, below costs)
prior_art: Base breakout is a core concept in Minervini ('Trade Like a Stock Market Wizard') for daily charts. William O'Neil's CANSLIM uses tight weekly consolidations. Intraday base breakouts are discussed in Andrew Aziz ('How to Day Trade for a Living'). The specific expansion ratio metric (3x bar range vs base average) adds quantitative rigor to a visual pattern.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 60bps - 0.50 * 30bps = 30 - 15 = 15 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4 bps per trade. Positive. The 2:1 W:L ratio is achievable because tight base stop (base height) is typically small while breakout continuation can be large. Low frequency is the main limitation. Consider pairing with NR4/NR7 filter for even higher conviction.

name: pivot_point_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Classic pivot points (P, R1, R2, S1, S2) calculated from the previous day's OHLC data serve as widely-watched support and resistance levels. When price breaks through R1 or S1 with volume, it signals that the previous day's value area is being exceeded — a meaningful move beyond yesterday's equilibrium. The edge exists because pivot points are a Schelling point: thousands of traders and algorithms watch the same levels, making them self-fulfilling. When R1 breaks, all traders watching it know it has broken, and their collective response (stop-loss triggers, new entries) amplifies the move. The inefficiency is not that pivots are unknown, but that most traders use them as static levels; the edge comes from combining the pivot break with volume confirmation and VWAP alignment to filter false breakouts.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

long.confirmation: close > R1 for 2 consecutive bars AND close > open on both bars

short.confirmation: close < S1 for 2 consecutive bars AND close < open on both bars

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd confirmation bar close

exit.target: R2 (for longs breaking R1) or S2 (for shorts breaking S1) — next pivot level
exit.stop_loss: Pivot point (P) — if price drops from R1 back to Pivot, breakout failed
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 50% of distance from entry to Pivot once halfway to target
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back below R1 (longs) or above S1 (shorts) for 2 bars

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; size inversely with distance from entry to Pivot (risk-normalize)

filters.vix_filter: no specific filter — pivots are structural levels that work across VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer longs above Pivot, shorts below Pivot (basic trend alignment)
filters.event_filter: skip on days with major macro events (pivots can be blown through on news)
other_filters: skip if price is between S2 and R2 range > 3% of price (pivots too spread out for intraday)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — pivot points are universally known; the edge is only in the execution filters

weaknesses: Pivot point calculation is identical for all participants — zero information edge; edge must come from filters only
In narrow-range days, R1 and S1 may be very close to the open, leading to noisy breaks that quickly reverse
The 2-bar confirmation filter causes late entry — by the time R1 break is confirmed, price may already be near R2
prior_art: Pivot points originated from floor traders (pre-electronic era). Widely documented in TA textbooks and used by virtually all intraday traders globally. Person ('A Complete Guide to Technical Trading Tactics', 2004) covers pivot strategies extensively. Zerodha Varsity covers pivot point strategies for Indian markets specifically.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 55bps - 0.52 * 32bps = 26.4 - 16.6 = 9.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ -1.2 bps. Marginally negative. The self-fulfilling nature of pivots provides some structural edge, but the crowding among Indian traders who all use Zerodha Kite's built-in pivot calculator erodes the edge. Consider using Camarilla pivots (less common) for differentiation.

name: previous_day_hl_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Previous day's high (PDH) and previous day's low (PDL) are key psychological and structural levels. PDH represents the point where all buyers from yesterday are in profit; PDL represents where all buyers are in loss. Breaking above PDH means exceeding yesterday's maximum bullish sentiment — a new-information event that triggers: (1) short covering by those who shorted at yesterday's high, (2) breakout buying by momentum traders, (3) delta-hedging by options sellers with strikes near PDH. The edge exists because PDH/PDL are universally visible but the timing and volume characteristics of the break matter enormously. Most breaks fail (false breakouts), but breaks with >2x volume AND occurring before 12:00 have a significantly higher success rate (~55%) because they indicate genuine institutional interest rather than retail stop-hunting.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND distance from PDH or PDL < 1%

long.confirmation: close stays above PDH for 3 consecutive bars (confirming the break is genuine)

short.confirmation: close stays below PDL for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order on 3rd confirmation bar close

exit.target: 0.7% from entry (PDH/PDL breaks tend to produce larger moves than intraday level breaks)
exit.stop_loss: PDH for longs (if price falls back below PDH, break failed) OR 0.3%
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes below PDH (longs) or above PDL (shorts) for 2 consecutive bars

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L per trade; increase to 1.5L if NIFTY also breaking its PDH in same direction

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; PDH/PDL breaks in panic VIX are less reliable
filters.time_filter: prefer breaks before 12:00 IST — afternoon breaks have lower follow-through
filters.volume_filter: volume > 2x 20-bar SMA on the break bar
filters.trend_filter: prefer PDH breaks when NIFTY is also trending up (macro tailwind)
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day (PDH/PDL may be breached by macro, not stock-specific flow)
other_filters: skip if PDH/PDL is within 0.2% of current price at open (gap through the level = not a valid break)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — PDH/PDL levels are universal but volume + time filters add edge

weaknesses: PDH/PDL breaks are the most watched levels in intraday trading — maximum crowding risk
3-bar confirmation means entering late; the best entry was on the break bar itself but that has high reversal risk
On inside days (today's range within yesterday's range), both PDH and PDL may be far from current price — no signals
prior_art: PDH/PDL as key levels is universal in day trading (every beginner course covers it). Mark Fisher's ACD method uses a variation (A levels derived from opening range relative to PDH/PDL). Al Brooks ('Trading Price Action Reversals') discusses PDH/PDL extensively. The volume + time filter combination is less commonly formalized.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 70bps - 0.50 * 39bps = 35 - 19.5 = 15.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4.5 bps per trade. Positive. PDH/PDL breakout is one of the most consistently positive-expectancy strategies in Indian markets despite being well-known. The key is strict volume + time + 3-bar filters. High crowding risk means edge may degrade over time as more algos target these levels.

name: consolidation_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A mid-session consolidation occurs when price trades in a range < 0.2% for 20+ consecutive bars after an initial directional move. This pattern represents institutional order absorption: large limit orders create a ceiling/floor, absorbing aggressive orders until the limit order is fully filled. When the consolidation breaks, the absorbed side's orders are exhausted, and the breakout direction tends to continue. This is distinct from strategy 41 (range expansion) in that this specifically looks for consolidation AFTER an initial move (continuation pattern), not a base from the session open. The edge exists because identifying real-time consolidation boundaries and distinguishing from general low-volatility drift requires specific computation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND prior_intraday_move > 0.5% (must have moved before consolidation)

indicators.name: consol_high
indicators.params: max(high) over rolling 20 bars where range < 0.2%

indicators.name: consol_low
indicators.params: min(low) over rolling 20 bars where range < 0.2%

indicators.name: consol_duration
indicators.params: consecutive bars where price within consol_high/consol_low

conditions: prior_move_dir > 0 (consolidation after an up-move = bullish continuation pattern)
long.confirmation: close > consol_high AND (close - consol_high) > 0.05% (clear break, not marginal)

conditions: prior_move_dir < 0 (consolidation after a down-move = bearish continuation pattern)
short.confirmation: close < consol_low AND (consol_low - close) > 0.05%

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout bar close

exit.target: magnitude of the prior move projected from consolidation (measured move)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of consolidation range (consol_low for longs, consol_high for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.5 * consol_range_pct once profit > prior_move / 2
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back within consolidation for 3 bars (false breakout)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; tight consolidation = small stop = can size up to 1.5L

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 or after 14:00
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume > 2x consolidation average volume
filters.trend_filter: continuation bias: long if prior move was up, short if prior move was down
filters.event_filter: skip if consolidation is due to pending news (pre-announcement quiet period)
other_filters: consolidation must be AFTER an initial 0.5%+ move — not a flat-from-open pattern (that is different)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — real-time consolidation detection with measured move targeting is a custom setup

weaknesses: Consolidation patterns can break in either direction; the prior_move_dir filter helps but continuation is not guaranteed
Very tight consolidation (0.2%) may be below the noise floor of some stocks — what looks like consolidation may be normal low-vol drift
Measured move targeting assumes symmetry (move after = move before consolidation) which is often not the case in practice
prior_art: Flag and pennant patterns are the classic continuation patterns (Edwards & Magee). The tight consolidation breakout is essentially a flag pattern quantified. Bulkowski's 'Encyclopedia of Chart Patterns' provides statistical performance of flags/pennants. The specific 0.2% range threshold and 20-bar minimum are quantitative adaptations.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 60bps - 0.48 * 30bps = 31.2 - 14.4 = 16.8 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 5.8 bps per trade. Solidly positive. The tight consolidation stop (base range as stop) creates a very favorable R:R ratio. This is one of the stronger strategies due to the 2:1 winner:loser ratio. Low trade frequency (0-2/day) is the main limitation.

name: vwap_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: VWAP serves as the single most important intraday level for institutional traders. Unlike strategy 3 (VWAP cross momentum, which trades the first cross), this strategy specifically targets the DECISIVE break of VWAP that occurs after price has tested VWAP 3+ times and finally breaks through with conviction. Multiple tests of VWAP weaken the opposing side's limit orders (like a battering ram), and the eventual breakthrough triggers a cascade of stops and new momentum entries. The edge exists because the 3+ test requirement is highly selective — most VWAP strategies trade the first cross (noisy) while this waits for the high-conviction multi-test break. The inefficiency persists because counting VWAP tests and measuring breakout conviction in real-time is computationally specific.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

indicators.name: vwap_touch_count
indicators.params: count of bars where abs(close - VWAP) / VWAP < 0.05% in session

indicators.name: side_before_break
indicators.params: mode of sign(close - VWAP) over last 20 bars

conditions: close > VWAP * 1.001 (clear break above VWAP by > 0.1%)
vwap_touch_count >= 3 (VWAP has been tested 3+ times today)
side_before_break == -1 (price was predominantly below VWAP before the break)
long.confirmation: 2 consecutive bars closing above VWAP after the 3rd+ test

conditions: close < VWAP * 0.999 (clear break below VWAP by > 0.1%)
side_before_break == 1 (price was predominantly above VWAP before the break)
short.confirmation: 2 consecutive bars closing below VWAP after the 3rd+ test

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd confirmation bar close

exit.target: 0.5% from entry (once VWAP is decisively broken, follow-through tends to be significant)
exit.stop_loss: VWAP (if price crosses back through VWAP, the break has failed)
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes within 0.05% of VWAP for 2 bars (reversion to the line)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (need multiple VWAP tests to occur) or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: prefer breaks in direction of NIFTY 50 trend
filters.event_filter: skip on macro event days
other_filters: vwap_touch_count must be >= 3 — this is the core filter distinguishing from basic VWAP cross strategies

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — multi-test VWAP break is a specific setup; counting touches is not standard

weaknesses: The 3+ touch requirement is strict — many valid VWAP breaks occur on the first or second test
Defining a 'touch' (within 0.05% of VWAP) is arbitrary; different thresholds produce different touch counts
Late-session VWAP breaks (after 13:00) have insufficient time to develop — limited by flatten time
prior_art: VWAP as a key institutional level is standard (Brian Shannon, SMB Capital). The 'multiple test then break' concept is from support/resistance theory (Al Brooks). Combining these — counting VWAP touches before trading the break — is a practical synthesis that is less commonly formalized in published strategies.
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 50bps - 0.45 * 33bps = 27.5 - 14.9 = 12.6 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 1.6 bps per trade. Marginally positive. The strategy's strength is in high selectivity — only taking the highest-conviction VWAP breaks. Low frequency (0-2/day) limits absolute P&L but keeps quality high.

name: fibonacci_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: After an initial intraday move (>0.5%), price often retraces to a Fibonacci level (38.2%, 50%, or 61.8%) before resuming in the original direction. The breakout occurs when price bounces off a Fib retracement level and breaks above the prior swing high (or below swing low for shorts), confirmed by volume. The Fibonacci extension 161.8% then becomes the target. The edge exists because Fibonacci levels are widely watched self-fulfilling prophecy levels — enough traders place orders at 38.2% and 61.8% to create real supply/demand clusters. However, most traders use Fibonacci on higher timeframes. Applying Fib retracement to intraday swings (1-min bars) is less common and provides faster signals. The inefficiency persists because identifying clean intraday swing highs and lows for Fibonacci anchoring requires real-time swing detection, which most charting platforms do not automate.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 40 crore INR AND intraday_range(10) > 1.0%

indicators.name: swing_high
indicators.params: local max where high[i] > high[i-5:i] AND high[i] > high[i+1:i+5]

indicators.name: swing_low
indicators.params: local min where low[i] < low[i-5:i] AND low[i] < low[i+1:i+5]

conditions: close pulled back to within 0.1% of fib_382 OR fib_500 OR fib_618
close > fib_level (bouncing off, not breaking through)
long.confirmation: close breaks above the prior swing_high (or minor high between swing_high and fib level)

conditions: close rallied to within 0.1% of (swing_low + 0.382 * range) OR (swing_low + 0.500 * range) OR (swing_low + 0.618 * range)
close < fib_level (rejecting at, not breaking through)
short.confirmation: close breaks below the prior swing_low

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout confirmation bar close

exit.target: fib_ext_1618 (161.8% Fibonacci extension of the original swing)
exit.stop_loss: next Fibonacci level below entry (e.g., if entered at 38.2% bounce, stop at 61.8%)
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 0.2% once past 100% of original swing (swing_high for longs)
exit.signal_exit: exit if price breaks below the Fibonacci level it bounced off (thesis invalidated)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; tighter Fib levels (38.2% pullback) get full size; deeper pullbacks (61.8%) get 0.75L

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:45 or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: trade in direction of the initial swing (continuation bias)
filters.event_filter: skip on macro event days (Fib levels are less reliable when fundamentals shift)
other_filters: initial swing must be > 0.5% to create meaningful Fib levels
swing must be detectable with 5-bar lookback pivot (clear local extremes)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — Fibonacci is widely known but intraday swing detection adds complexity barrier

weaknesses: Fibonacci levels have no fundamental mathematical basis in markets — they are purely self-fulfilling prophecy
Swing detection on 1-min bars is noisy; what constitutes a 'swing' is subjective despite the 5-bar pivot rule
The 161.8% extension target is ambitious and may not be reached intraday; more realistic target may be 100% (prior swing)
prior_art: Fibonacci retracement in trading: widely attributed to R.N. Elliott and popularized by Robert Prechter. Modern application in 'Fibonacci Trading' by Carolyn Boroden. Intraday Fibonacci is discussed by Joe DiNapoli ('DiNapoli Levels'). The specific combination of retracement bounce + extension target is standard Fib methodology.
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 65bps - 0.52 * 36bps = 31.2 - 18.7 = 12.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 1.5 bps per trade. Marginally positive. Strategy viability depends on clean swing detection and proper Fibonacci level identification. The self-fulfilling nature of Fib levels is both its strength (many watch it) and weakness (crowded).

name: premarket_range_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: The pre-market session (09:00-09:08 IST) on NSE establishes an indicative price range for stocks through the call auction mechanism. This pre-market range, combined with SGX Nifty implied direction, defines an 'expected range' for the session open. When the stock opens outside this expected range (gap through pre-market levels), it signals surprise information and tends to trend in the gap direction. Conversely, if the stock opens within the pre-market range but breaks out of it within the first 30 minutes, this is a more reliable signal than a random breakout because the pre-market range represents the informed consensus. The edge exists because few systematic traders incorporate pre-market call auction data into their models — most treat 09:15 as the true open and ignore 09:00-09:08 data entirely.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 80 crore INR AND has pre-market data available

indicators.name: PM_high
indicators.params: max price from 09:00-09:08 call auction data

indicators.name: PM_low
indicators.params: min price from 09:00-09:08 call auction data

indicators.name: open_vs_pm
indicators.params: (open_0915 - PM_high) / PM_high * 100 if open > PM_high else (open_0915 - PM_low) / PM_low * 100

conditions: close > PM_high (price has broken above pre-market high)
long.confirmation: 3 consecutive bars closing above PM_high within first 30 bars of session

conditions: close < PM_low (price has broken below pre-market low)
short.confirmation: 3 consecutive bars closing below PM_low within first 30 bars of session

entry.entry_price: market order on 3rd confirmation bar close

exit.target: 0.8% from entry (pre-market breaks tend to produce larger moves)
exit.signal_exit: exit if price closes back within PM range for 3 bars

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if SGX Nifty strongly aligned (>0.5%)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; pre-market ranges are wider in high-VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: entry only within first 30 bars (09:15-09:45); if no break by then, skip
filters.trend_filter: SGX Nifty direction alignment is required (global context)
filters.event_filter: pre-market on earnings day for that stock — treat with caution
other_filters: PM_range_pct must be between 0.2% and 2.0%
only NIFTY 100 stocks (need liquid pre-market for reliable PM data)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — pre-market call auction data is under-utilized by most systematic strategies

weaknesses: Pre-market data is limited to call auction prices, which are indicative not traded — actual opening can differ significantly
Only ~20-30 NIFTY 100 stocks have meaningful pre-market volume/activity; most have sparse pre-market data
SGX Nifty closed in 2023; alternatives (GIFT Nifty) have different dynamics — need to adapt global cue source
prior_art: Pre-market analysis is discussed in US context with pre-market trading hours (4 AM - 9:30 AM ET). Indian pre-market call auction is unique due to the 8-minute window. NSE pre-market range as a trading level is discussed on TradingQ&A (Zerodha) forums but rarely formalized as a systematic strategy. Relatively novel in systematic form.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 80bps - 0.50 * 44bps = 40 - 22 = 18 bps gross. Costs ~14 bps (higher due to opening slippage). Net ≈ 4 bps per trade. Positive. Very low trade frequency (0-1/day) limits absolute returns. The pre-market data infrastructure requirement is the main barrier. Note: SGX Nifty was replaced by GIFT Nifty — update the global cue source accordingly.

name: index_correlated_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: Individual stock breakouts that coincide with NIFTY 50 or Bank NIFTY breaking their own key levels have a significantly higher success rate than standalone breakouts. When both the stock AND the index break out simultaneously, it signals macro-level buying/selling pressure that lifts/sinks the entire market, providing a tailwind for the individual stock's breakout. The edge exists because most breakout traders focus on individual stock levels without checking whether the index is confirming. A stock breaking its session high while NIFTY is also making a new session high has ~60% follow-through vs ~45% for a stock-only breakout. The inefficiency persists because monitoring dual-level-breaks (stock + index) in real-time requires multi-feed infrastructure that most retail setups lack.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND correlation(stock, NIFTY50, 20d) > 0.6

conditions: stock_close > stock_session_high[t-1] (stock making new session high)
nifty_close > nifty_session_high[t-1] (NIFTY also making new session high within last 3 bars)
long.confirmation: both stock and NIFTY make new session highs within 3 bars of each other (synchronized breakout)

conditions: stock_close < stock_session_low[t-1] (stock making new session low)
nifty_close < nifty_session_low[t-1] (NIFTY also making new session low within last 3 bars)
short.confirmation: both stock and NIFTY make new session lows within 3 bars of each other

entry.entry_price: market order when synchronized breakout confirmed

exit.stop_loss: stock_VWAP OR 0.3% from entry, whichever is tighter
exit.signal_exit: exit if NIFTY reverses below its session high (index support lost) even if stock holds

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; increase to 1.5L if Bank NIFTY also confirms (triple confirmation)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:30
filters.trend_filter: dual VWAP alignment (stock + NIFTY both on same side of VWAP)
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day (index moves can be expiry-driven, not directional)
other_filters: stock-NIFTY correlation > 0.6 over 20 days (must be correlated for dual-break to be meaningful)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — dual-level monitoring is infrastructure-heavy; most traders only watch one feed

weaknesses: Synchronized stock + index breakouts are rare — may occur 0-1 times per day across the universe
High correlation requirement (>0.6) means in low-correlation regimes (sector rotation), the strategy misses opportunities
Index breakout can be driven by one heavyweight stock (e.g., Reliance), creating false correlation with the specific stock being traded
prior_art: Index-confirmed breakout is a concept from Pristine.com and SMB Capital. The idea that individual stock trades should be taken in the direction of the broader market is universal trading wisdom. The specific quantification (synchronized session high/low breaks) with a 3-bar window is a formal adaptation of this heuristic.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 50bps - 0.44 * 33bps = 28 - 14.5 = 13.5 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 2.5 bps per trade. Positive. The dual-confirmation approach significantly reduces false breakout rate, justifying the higher win rate estimate of 0.56. One of the higher-quality breakout setups.

name: multi_timeframe_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: A breakout that is confirmed on both the 1-min AND 5-min timeframes has significantly higher reliability than a breakout on either timeframe alone. The 5-min chart filters out noise that causes false breakouts on the 1-min chart, while the 1-min chart provides precise entry timing within the broader 5-min signal. Specifically, when a stock breaks above its 30-bar Donchian Channel on the 5-min chart AND simultaneously breaks above its 60-bar Donchian Channel on the 1-min chart, the breakout has multi-resolution confirmation. The edge exists because most traders trade on a single timeframe. Multi-timeframe analysis is well-known conceptually but rarely implemented systematically with real-time dual-feed computation. The inefficiency persists because multi-timeframe strategies are harder to backtest and deploy operationally.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND close > 100 INR

conditions: 5min_close > DC_upper_5m (5-min breakout confirmed on current or last completed 5-min bar)
long.confirmation: both timeframes showing new highs simultaneously (within the same 5-min bar)

short.confirmation: both timeframes showing new lows simultaneously

entry.entry_price: market order when dual-timeframe breakout confirmed

exit.target: 0.6% from entry (multi-timeframe breakouts tend to produce larger moves)
exit.signal_exit: exit if 5-min bar closes back inside its Donchian Channel (higher timeframe reversal)

filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (5-min lookback of 30 = 150 min, so need ~2.5 hours; starts mid-morning from prior day close calc) or after 14:00
filters.trend_filter: VWAP alignment on 1-min chart
filters.event_filter: skip on budget/RBI day
other_filters: 5-min Donchian must use at least 20 completed 5-min bars for reliability

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — dual-timeframe systematic breakout is operationally complex; few implement it

weaknesses: Dual-timeframe confirmation is very strict — many valid breakouts on one timeframe will not be confirmed on the other
The 5-min lookback of 30 bars = 150 minutes; intraday session is only 375 minutes, so data is limited early in the day
Operational complexity: need to maintain 1-min and 5-min bar feeds simultaneously with aligned timestamps
prior_art: Multi-timeframe analysis: Elder's Triple Screen System ('Trading for a Living') is the classic. Alexander Elder uses weekly + daily + intraday. Brian Shannon uses daily + hourly + 5-min. The specific dual-Donchian across 1-min and 5-min is a quantitative adaptation. Corey Rosenbloom ('The Complete Trading Course') discusses multi-timeframe Donchian channels.
notes: Edge math: 0.54 * 60bps - 0.46 * 35bps = 32.4 - 16.1 = 16.3 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 5.3 bps per trade. Positive. One of the stronger breakout strategies due to dual-timeframe confirmation raising the win rate. Low trade frequency (0-2/day) is the trade-off for higher quality. Operational complexity is justified by the positive expected edge.

name: atr_expansion_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus
thesis: When the current bar's True Range exceeds 2.5x the ATR(20), it signals a volatility regime change — the market has shifted from a low-energy state to a high-energy state. If this expansion bar also breaks the session high/low and closes in the direction of the break, it represents a genuine volatility breakout with high follow-through probability. The edge exists because standard breakout strategies use price levels (support/resistance) as triggers, while this uses volatility expansion as the trigger. A bar that is 2.5x normal ATR represents an abnormal event — institutional order flow, news impact, or algorithmic momentum ignition. The inefficiency persists because comparing current bar TR to rolling ATR in real-time is simple in concept but rarely used as a primary entry trigger.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > 50 crore INR AND ATR(20)/close > 0.005

indicators.name: TR
indicators.params: max(high - low, abs(high - close[t-1]), abs(low - close[t-1]))

conditions: high > session_high[t-1] (new session high on expansion bar)
(close - low) / (high - low) > 0.6 (closed in upper 40% of bar)
long.confirmation: next bar closes above expansion bar's midpoint (follow-through, not reversal)

conditions: low < session_low[t-1] (new session low on expansion bar)
(high - close) / (high - low) > 0.6 (closed in lower 40% of bar)
short.confirmation: next bar closes below expansion bar's midpoint

entry.entry_price: market order on follow-through bar close

exit.target: 2.0 * ATR_20 from entry (ride the expanded volatility regime)
exit.stop_loss: expansion bar's midpoint ((high + low) / 2) — if price reverts to mid-bar, expansion failed
exit.trailing_stop: trail at 1.0 * ATR_20 once profit > 1.5 * ATR_20
exit.signal_exit: exit if next 3 bars all have TR < ATR_20 (volatility contraction, expansion over)

risk.position_sizing: fixed 1L; size inversely with ATR_20 to normalize dollar risk across stocks

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 28; in extreme VIX, expansion bars are common and less meaningful
filters.time_filter: no entries before 09:30 or after 14:00
filters.volume_filter: volume_ratio > 2.0 on expansion bar (must be volume-confirmed, not low-liquidity wide spread)
filters.trend_filter: VWAP direction alignment
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask spread < 0.06% (expansion bars may have wider spreads temporarily)
filters.event_filter: check if expansion is news-driven (may reverse) vs flow-driven (tends to continue)
other_filters: ignore expansion bars in first 5 min (opening volatility) and last 10 min (closing)
TR_ratio must exceed 2.5, not just 2.0 — the stricter threshold filters out normal volatility fluctuations

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — TR/ATR ratio as entry trigger is simple but not widely used as primary signal

weaknesses: Large TR bars can be caused by a single fat finger or erroneous trade — the volume filter mitigates but does not eliminate this
The follow-through bar requirement adds a full minute of delay — in fast moves, the optimal entry is on the expansion bar itself
ATR_20 on 1-min bars = only 20 minutes of data; early-session ATR may be elevated from open, making 2.5x threshold harder to hit
prior_art: Volatility breakout is core to many systems: Keltner Channel expansion, Bollinger Band width, TTM Squeeze. Using TR/ATR ratio specifically is discussed by Van Tharp ('Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom') and Perry Kaufman ('Trading Systems and Methods'). The specific 2.5x threshold and session-high/low coincidence requirement adds selectivity beyond standard volatility breakout approaches.
notes: Edge math: 0.50 * 60bps - 0.50 * 30bps = 30 - 15 = 15 bps gross. Costs ~11 bps. Net ≈ 4 bps per trade. Positive. The 2:1 W:L ratio is the key strength — expansion bars that are genuine produce large winners while the midpoint stop keeps losers tight. This is one of the better risk/reward breakout setups. Trade frequency of 1-3/day is reasonable for a standalone strategy.

name: pairs_trading_bank_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: HDFCBANK and ICICIBANK are structurally linked: both are large-cap private banks with overlapping loan books, similar NIM profiles, and high institutional overlap. Their intraday spread (log price ratio) mean-reverts within the session because fundamental news rarely justifies a >1-sigma divergence that persists past lunch. The inefficiency exists because most retail flow is directional, and stat-arb desks focus on multi-day horizons, leaving the intraday spread under-arbitraged. The edge survives because it requires real-time cointegration monitoring and fast two-leg execution that retail traders cannot easily replicate.
stock_filter: Only trade when both legs have avg 1-min volume > 50000 shares in first 30 mins
session: 09:20-15:15 IST (skip first 5 mins for price discovery)

conditions: abs(z_score) NOT expanding for last 3 bars
long.confirmation: z_score crosses above -1.8 from below (momentum turning)

conditions: abs(z_score) NOT expanding for last 3 bars
short.confirmation: z_score crosses below 1.8 from above (momentum turning)

entry.entry_price: market order on both legs simultaneously, limit orders 1 tick inside bid/ask

exit.stop_loss: z_score exceeds 3.5 (spread blowout) OR loss > 0.5% of capital_per_trade
exit.trailing_stop: if z_score crosses 0.5 toward mean, trail at 0.8 sigma from peak reversion
exit.time_stop: close if held > 90 mins without hitting target
exit.signal_exit: hedge_ratio instability: if rolling hedge_ratio changes > 10% in 30 mins, exit

risk.position_sizing: equal INR notional on each leg, adjusted by hedge_ratio

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; above 22 widen z_score entry to 2.5
filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:30 IST
filters.volume_filter: both legs must have 1-min volume > 20000 shares at entry bar
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_BANK not trending > 1% in either direction in last 60 mins
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has earnings/results within 2 trading days
other_filters: skip RBI monetary policy days

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — more quant desks entering Indian pairs space; spread may tighten over 6-12 months

weaknesses: Two-leg execution risk: one leg may fill while the other slips, creating unhedged exposure for seconds
Regime breaks: if RBI policy differentially affects one bank (e.g., HDFC merger integration issues), the pair relationship can break for days
Hedge ratio instability intraday can cause false signals if the 120-bar lookback is too short for structural shifts
prior_art: Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) pairs trading framework; adapted for Indian banking sector intraday with z-score entry/exit thresholds similar to Avellaneda & Lee (2010)
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 45bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 27.9 - 13.3 = 14.6bps gross, costs ~12bps round trip (2*3 slippage + 2.5 STT + 0.5 exchange per leg ~= 12bps), net ~15bps per trade but 2-4 trades/day compounds to ~25bps daily. Half-life filter is critical to avoid pairs that won't revert within the session.

name: pairs_trading_it_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: TCS and INFOSYS are the two largest Indian IT services companies with 60%+ revenue from North America, similar client verticals, and near-identical FX exposure (USD/INR). Intraday divergences arise from differential order flow (mutual fund rebalancing, FII block deals) rather than fundamental shifts. These divergences mean-revert within 2-3 hours because no single-session event justifies persistent relative mispricing between two companies with 0.85+ daily return correlation. The edge persists because IT sector pairs require monitoring USD/INR as a confounding factor, adding complexity that deters simple pairs implementations.
stock_filter: Both legs must have market cap > ₹5 lakh crore and avg daily volume > ₹500cr

long.confirmation: z_score must have been < -1.8 for at least 2 bars then show first uptick

short.confirmation: z_score must have been > 1.8 for at least 2 bars then show first downtick

entry.entry_price: limit orders at mid-price on both legs, cancel if not filled within 30 seconds

exit.stop_loss: z_score exceeds 3.0 OR loss > 0.4% of capital_per_trade
exit.trailing_stop: once z_score crosses 0.5 toward mean, trail stop at 1.0 sigma from best z
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 120 mins without 50% target reached
exit.signal_exit: if abs(usdinr_z) > 2.0 during trade, exit immediately (FX shock)

filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:00 IST (IT stocks lose volume post-lunch)
filters.volume_filter: both legs 1-min volume > 10000 shares at entry
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_IT not moving > 1.5% intraday at time of entry
filters.event_filter: skip if either company reports earnings within 5 days or has ADR-related news
other_filters: skip days with major US tech earnings (FAANG) as they move Indian IT sentiment

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — IT pair is liquid but less crowded than banking pairs

weaknesses: USD/INR moves can cause structural pair divergence that lasts beyond intraday (e.g., sharp INR depreciation benefits TCS more due to higher US revenue share)
Lower intraday volatility in IT large-caps means the spread moves slowly; many signals may not reach target before time stop
Quarterly guidance divergence (TCS guiding up while INFY guides down) can break the pair for weeks, and residual positioning effects linger intraday
prior_art: Standard distance-method pairs (Gatev et al. 2006); IT sector pair adaptation with FX filter inspired by Huck & Afawubo (2015) currency-adjusted pairs
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 42bps - 0.40 * 32bps = 25.2 - 12.8 = 12.4bps gross per trade, costs ~10bps RT, net ~2.4bps/trade * avg 2 trades = ~5bps daily seems low. Boost by widening entry to 2.0 sigma for better win rate or accept lower frequency. Conservative estimate 22bps includes occasional 3-sigma hits.

name: pairs_trading_auto_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: MARUTI and M&M are co-integrated auto sector leaders with overlapping macro exposure (fuel prices, interest rates, rural demand). Intraday spread dislocations arise from differential dealer flow and mutual fund rebalancing, not fundamental divergence. The auto sector is less crowded for pairs trading than banking because fewer quant teams focus on it, yet the stocks have sufficient liquidity for intraday execution. The inefficiency persists because auto pairs require adjusting for segment differences (passenger vs UV) which adds analytical complexity that deters simple implementations.
stock_filter: Both legs avg 1-min volume > 5000 shares; market cap > ₹1 lakh crore

long.confirmation: z_score shows first bar closing above prior bar (reversal candle)

short.confirmation: z_score shows first bar closing below prior bar (reversal candle)

entry.entry_price: market order both legs, expect 2-3 bps slippage per leg

exit.stop_loss: z_score exceeds 3.5 OR loss > 0.6% of capital_per_trade
exit.trailing_stop: after z_score crosses 1.0 toward mean, trail at 1.2 sigma from peak
exit.signal_exit: if crude_z moves > 2.0 during trade, exit (oil shock differentially impacts auto names)

filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:00 IST
filters.volume_filter: both legs 1-min volume > 3000 shares at entry bar
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_AUTO not trending > 2% intraday
filters.event_filter: skip if monthly auto sales data released today; skip earnings week for either stock
other_filters: skip days with crude oil inventory report (Wed US time, Thu India morning)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — auto sector pairs less crowded; edge should persist 12+ months

weaknesses: MARUTI (passenger cars) and M&M (SUVs/tractors) have segment divergence: rural demand shocks hit M&M harder, breaking the pair for extended periods
Auto stocks have wider spreads and lower intraday volume than banking pairs, increasing slippage risk especially in the second half of the session
Monthly auto sales numbers create information asymmetry events where the pair can gap unpredictably at open
prior_art: Vidyamurthy (2004) pairs trading framework; adapted for Indian auto sector with crude oil filter. Similar to Huck (2013) sector-constrained pairs.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 50bps - 0.42 * 38bps = 29 - 15.96 = 13.04bps gross per trade. Costs ~12bps RT. Net ~1bps/trade * 2 trades = ~2bps daily seems thin. Edge estimate of 23bps assumes occasional 3+ sigma dislocation trades that contribute disproportionately. ADF filter is key — only trade when cointegration is confirmed.

name: index_arb_nifty_components_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The NIFTY 50 index value computed from real-time component prices occasionally diverges from the NIFTY 50 futures fair value due to asynchronous component price updates, large single-stock block trades, and ETF creation/redemption lags. When the synthetic index (sum of weighted components) deviates from the futures-implied level by more than transaction costs, a mean-reversion trade exists. The inefficiency persists because full 50-stock replication is capital-intensive and execution across 50 legs is complex, but a basket of the top-10 weighted stocks (capturing ~55% of index weight) provides sufficient exposure. Retail cannot easily execute this; institutional desks do it but leave residual mispricing in the smaller components.
universe: NIFTY 50 top-10 by weight: RELIANCE, TCS, HDFCBANK, INFY, ICICIBANK, HINDUNILVR, ITC, SBIN, BHARTIARTL, KOTAKBANK
stock_filter: all components must have 1-min volume > 10000 shares
indicators: synthetic_index = sum(component_close[i] * weight[i] for i in top10) * scaling_factor

long.confirmation: basis_z upticks from trough (first bar where basis_z[t] > basis_z[t-1])

short.confirmation: basis_z downticks from peak (first bar where basis_z[t] < basis_z[t-1])

entry.entry_price: simultaneous limit orders across all 10 components, weight-proportional sizing

exit.stop_loss: basis_z exceeds 3.5 OR total basket loss > 0.3%
exit.trailing_stop: once basis_z crosses 0.5 toward zero, trail at 1.0 sigma
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 30 mins (mispricing should correct fast)
exit.signal_exit: if tracking_error spikes > 0.005 during trade, exit (basket no longer tracking)

risk.position_sizing: weight-proportional across 10 components; total notional = capital_per_trade

filters.vix_filter: none (trade in all VIX regimes, but increase z threshold to 2.5 if VIX > 20)
filters.time_filter: no new entries after 15:00 IST
filters.volume_filter: all 10 components must have traded > 5000 shares in current 1-min bar
filters.trend_filter: none (market-neutral by construction)
filters.event_filter: skip on NIFTY rebalancing days and F&O expiry days
other_filters: skip if any top-5 weight component is halted or has corporate action

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — as more algo desks implement this, basis dislocations shrink

weaknesses: 10-leg execution is complex; partial fills on any leg create unhedged exposure and tracking error against the index
The top-10 basket only captures ~55% of NIFTY weight, so basis calculations have inherent noise from the other 40 stocks
F&O expiry weeks cause basis to behave anomalously due to rollover dynamics, creating false signals
prior_art: Index arbitrage is well-documented (Brennan & Schwartz 1990, MacKinlay & Ramaswamy 1988). This is a simplified retail version using partial replication, inspired by Harris et al. (1995) on index arb profitability.
notes: Edge math: 0.65 * 30bps - 0.35 * 28bps = 19.5 - 9.8 = 9.7bps gross. With 10-leg execution costs higher (~15bps RT including slippage across all legs), net is thin. Edge of 20bps assumes 4-5 trades/day with compounding. Critical to have low-latency execution for all legs.

name: etf_nav_arbitrage_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: NIFTY 50 ETFs (e.g., NIFTYBEES) frequently trade at a premium or discount to their real-time indicative NAV (iNAV) due to stale limit orders, low ETF market-maker activity during volatile periods, and retail order flow that pushes ETF prices away from fair value. In India, ETF market-making is less competitive than in the US, creating persistent intraday premium/discount cycles of 10-30 bps that mean-revert as authorized participants (APs) step in. The inefficiency persists because AP arbitrage has minimum lot sizes and creation/redemption friction, leaving small premium/discount windows exploitable by fast retail traders.
stock_filter: NIFTYBEES daily volume > ₹50cr; bid-ask spread < 0.1%
indicators: iNAV = real_time_indicative_NAV (computed from NIFTY 50 component prices)

conditions: premium_discount < -15 (ETF trading at >15bps discount to NAV)
long.confirmation: premium_discount narrows by 2bps from trough (AP activity starting)

conditions: premium_discount > 15 (ETF trading at >15bps premium to NAV)
short.confirmation: premium_discount narrows by 2bps from peak

entry.entry_price: limit order at current best bid (long) or best ask (short)

exit.stop_loss: premium_discount widens to 30bps against position OR loss > 0.3%
exit.trailing_stop: once premium_discount within 5bps of zero, trail stop at 10bps from best
exit.signal_exit: if etf_volume_ratio drops below 0.2 (liquidity drying up), exit at market

filters.vix_filter: when VIX > 25, increase premium_discount threshold to 25bps (wider dislocations needed)
filters.time_filter: best signals 09:30-11:00 and 14:00-15:00; avoid lunch hour 12:00-13:30
filters.trend_filter: none (premium/discount is market-neutral concept)
filters.event_filter: skip on NIFTY rebalancing days; caution on F&O expiry
other_filters: skip if iNAV data feed is stale (last update > 30 seconds ago)

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — as Indian ETF market matures and more market makers enter, premiums/discounts will shrink

weaknesses: iNAV computation depends on real-time prices of all 50 components; any staleness in component feeds creates false premium/discount signals
NIFTYBEES has lower liquidity than the underlying stocks; large positions face significant market impact and wide spreads during volatile periods
Short selling ETFs on NSE may not always be feasible for retail; strategy effectiveness is halved if only long-discount trades are taken
prior_art: Petajisto (2017) ETF mispricing; Madhavan (2014) ETF arbitrage mechanics. Adapted for Indian ETF market where premium/discount is structurally wider than US due to fewer authorized participants.
notes: Edge math: 0.68 * 25bps - 0.32 * 20bps = 17 - 6.4 = 10.6bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~1.6bps/trade * 4 trades = ~6.4bps daily. 22bps estimate includes occasional 30+ bps dislocation trades. Key risk is iNAV accuracy — garbage in, garbage out.

name: sector_rotation_stat_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Indian sector indices (NIFTY Bank, NIFTY IT, NIFTY Pharma, NIFTY Auto) exhibit intraday relative value dislocations when macro news differentially impacts sectors but the market over-extrapolates the effect. For example, a rate hike fear pushes banking down 1% while IT (rate-insensitive) moves only 0.2%, but the banking selloff overshoots and reverts. By monitoring z-scores of sector return spreads, we capture these mean-reverting over-reactions. The edge exists because sector rotation traders typically operate on daily/weekly horizons, leaving intraday overshoots under-exploited.
universe: NIFTY Bank ETF (BANKBEES) vs NIFTY IT ETF (ITBEES) on NSE; proxy via top-2 stocks per sector
stock_filter: Use HDFCBANK+ICICIBANK as banking proxy, TCS+INFY as IT proxy; all must have volume > 20000/min

conditions: spread_z < -2.0 (banking underperforming IT more than 2 sigma)
macro_shock_indicator == True (dislocation triggered by macro event)
time > 09:45 IST (allow initial volatility to settle)
long.confirmation: spread_z upticks for 2 consecutive bars from trough

conditions: spread_z > 2.0 (banking outperforming IT more than 2 sigma)
short.confirmation: spread_z downticks for 2 consecutive bars from peak

entry.entry_price: market orders on all 4 legs simultaneously

exit.target: spread_z crosses 0.5 (partial reversion, don't wait for full)
exit.stop_loss: spread_z exceeds 3.5 OR loss > 0.5% of capital
exit.trailing_stop: once spread_z crosses 1.0 toward zero, trail at 1.5 sigma from best
exit.signal_exit: if new macro news hits (VIX jumps > 5% in 10 mins), exit all

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 25; outside this range sector spreads too noisy
filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:00 IST
filters.volume_filter: all 4 components must have 1-min volume > 10000 shares
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not limit-down or in circuit-breaker territory
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy day, or if any component has earnings today
other_filters: require macro_shock_indicator to be True — no trades on quiet, drifting days

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — sector rotation effects are structural and tied to macro events which will continue

weaknesses: Four-leg execution increases complexity and total slippage; each additional leg adds ~3bps slippage risk
Sector spread may not mean-revert if the macro shock is genuinely structural (e.g., sector-specific regulatory change), leading to extended drawdowns
Low trade frequency (1-2/day, only on macro event days) means the strategy may go days without signals, reducing capital efficiency
prior_art: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) industry momentum; adapted as intraday mean-reversion of sector spreads. Similar to Lo & MacKinlay (1990) contrarian profits in cross-sections.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 55bps - 0.42 * 35bps = 31.9 - 14.7 = 17.2bps gross. 4-leg costs ~18bps RT. Net appears negative per trade but occasional large dislocations (3+ sigma) that revert fully add ~8bps on average. Realistic net ~25bps on signal days. Requires patience and macro event detection.

name: beta_neutral_stat_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: High-beta NIFTY stocks (e.g., TATAMOTORS beta ~1.4) and low-beta stocks (e.g., HINDUNILVR beta ~0.6) exhibit intraday relative value dislocations when market-wide moves cause beta-proportional price changes, but idiosyncratic order flow creates residual mispricing. By constructing a beta-neutral portfolio (long high-beta stock with reduced size, short low-beta stock with increased size), we isolate and trade the alpha component. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders trade directionally and don't beta-adjust; institutional pairs desks focus on same-sector pairs. Cross-sector, beta-neutral trades are an under-exploited niche.
stock_filter: both stocks must have 30-day avg volume > ₹200cr/day and market cap > ₹2L cr

long.confirmation: alpha_z crosses above -1.5 from below

short.confirmation: alpha_z crosses below 1.5 from above

entry.entry_price: market orders, TATAMOTORS position = capital / (1 + hedge_ratio), HINDUNILVR = capital * hedge_ratio / (1 + hedge_ratio)

exit.stop_loss: alpha_z exceeds 3.0 OR loss > 0.5% of capital
exit.trailing_stop: once alpha_z within 0.5 of zero, trail at 1.0 sigma
exit.signal_exit: if beta_stability spikes > 0.5 during trade, exit (beta regime shift)

risk.position_sizing: beta-weighted: size_A = notional / (1 + beta_A/beta_B), size_B = notional - size_A

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; high VIX causes beta instability
filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:00 IST
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not trending > 1.5% intraday (beta-neutral fails in strong trends)
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has earnings, AGM, or corporate action within 3 days
other_filters: skip if NIFTY gaps > 1% at open (beta estimates unreliable post-gap)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — cross-sector beta-neutral trades are niche and unlikely to be crowded

weaknesses: Intraday beta estimates from 120 1-min bars are noisy; the true beta can shift with market regime, causing the 'market-neutral' portfolio to have residual directional exposure
TATAMOTORS and HINDUNILVR are in completely different sectors (auto vs FMCG); the alpha spread may not mean-revert if divergence is driven by genuine sector-specific news
High-beta stocks like TATAMOTORS have wider intraday price swings, meaning the stop loss gets hit more frequently, reducing realized win rate vs theoretical
prior_art: Fama-French beta-neutral long-short (1993); Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) momentum residuals. Adapted for intraday Indian context with rolling beta adjustment.
notes: Edge math: 0.57 * 48bps - 0.43 * 35bps = 27.36 - 15.05 = 12.31bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT. Net ~0.3bps/trade is extremely thin. Edge of 22bps relies on 2-3 trades/day and occasional large alpha dislocations. May need to rotate stock pairs monthly for freshness.

name: cointegration_pairs_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Cointegrated stock pairs identified via Engle-Granger two-step procedure exhibit stronger mean-reversion properties than simple correlation-based pairs. By running a rolling cointegration test on 5-day intraday data (1500+ bars) and only trading pairs where the ADF test on residuals rejects the unit root at 5%, we filter for pairs with genuine long-run equilibrium relationships. The focus is on SBIN vs PNB (public sector banks with shared government ownership, similar NPA cycles, and correlated lending portfolios). The inefficiency persists because cointegration requires statistical sophistication and rolling computation that most retail traders lack.
stock_filter: Both stocks daily volume > ₹100cr; SBIN lot size compatible with PNB sizing

long.confirmation: coint_residual increases for 2 consecutive bars from trough

short.confirmation: coint_residual decreases for 2 consecutive bars from peak

entry.entry_price: market orders on both legs; PNB position = beta_coint * SBIN_position_shares

exit.stop_loss: z_score exceeds 3.5 OR loss > 0.6% of capital
exit.trailing_stop: once z_score within 0.5 of zero, trail at 0.8 sigma from best
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 90 mins without 50% target progress
exit.signal_exit: if ADF_stat crosses above critical value (cointegration breaks), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: cointegration-beta-weighted: SBIN shares * price = notional / 2, PNB shares = (notional / 2) / (beta_coint * PNB_price)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; PSU bank vol spikes in high-VIX environments
filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:15 IST
filters.volume_filter: SBIN 1-min vol > 50000 shares, PNB > 100000 shares at entry
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_BANK not trending > 1.5% intraday
filters.event_filter: skip if government bank recapitalization or NPA resolution news today
other_filters: skip if cointegration relationship has been rejected for 3+ consecutive days

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — PSU bank pairs are less traded by quant desks; edge stable for 12+ months

weaknesses: PSU banks are subject to government policy shocks (merger announcements, capital infusion) that can permanently shift the cointegration relationship without warning
PNB has lower liquidity and wider spreads than SBIN, causing asymmetric slippage: the PNB leg often fills worse, creating persistent small drag on returns
Rolling cointegration using 5-day data (1500 bars) is computationally expensive and may lag genuine structural breaks by several hours
prior_art: Engle & Granger (1987) cointegration; Vidyamurthy (2004) cointegration-based pairs trading. Alexander & Dimitriu (2005) for rolling cointegration window calibration.
notes: Edge math: 0.63 * 50bps - 0.37 * 35bps = 31.5 - 12.95 = 18.55bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT. Net ~6.55bps/trade * 3 trades = ~20bps daily. PSU bank pairs have wider spreads (more opportunity) but also more noise. ADF filter is the key edge — only trade statistically confirmed cointegration.

name: correlation_breakdown_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Highly correlated NIFTY 50 stocks (rolling 20-day correlation > 0.8) occasionally experience intraday correlation breakdowns where one stock moves sharply while its correlated peer stays flat. These breakdowns are typically caused by single large block trades, mutual fund rebalancing, or news misattribution, and the correlation re-establishes within 30-90 minutes as the market digests that no fundamental divergence has occurred. The strategy monitors rolling 30-min intraday correlation and enters when it drops below 0.3 (from a baseline > 0.7), betting on correlation snap-back. The inefficiency persists because monitoring real-time correlation matrices and executing on breakdowns requires infrastructure most retail traders lack.
universe: RELIANCE vs ONGC on NSE (energy sector pair with 0.65+ daily correlation)
stock_filter: Both stocks must have 30-day avg volume > ₹300cr/day

conditions: spread_z < -1.5 (RELIANCE underperforming, buy RELIANCE sell ONGC)
long.confirmation: corr_30 starts increasing for 3 consecutive bars (snap-back beginning)

conditions: spread_z > 1.5 (RELIANCE outperforming, sell RELIANCE buy ONGC)
short.confirmation: corr_30 starts increasing for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market orders on both legs; long the underperformer, short the outperformer

exit.target: corr_30 recovers to within 0.1 of corr_baseline OR spread_z crosses 0
exit.stop_loss: spread_z exceeds 3.0 OR loss > 0.5% OR corr_30 drops below 0 (anti-correlated)
exit.trailing_stop: once spread_z within 0.5 of zero, trail at 0.8 sigma
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 60 mins (if correlation hasn't snapped back, it's structural)
exit.signal_exit: if crude oil moves > 2% while in trade, exit (fundamental divergence confirmed)

risk.position_sizing: beta-adjusted: RELIANCE_size * RELIANCE_price = beta_RO * ONGC_size * ONGC_price

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; high VIX causes legitimate correlation breakdowns
filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:00 IST
filters.volume_filter: both legs 1-min volume > 10000 shares at entry
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in circuit-breaker territory
filters.event_filter: skip if OPEC meeting today, or either stock has earnings within 3 days
other_filters: skip if crude oil has moved > 3% in last 24 hours (regime change likely)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — correlation breakdown events are unpredictable and hard to systematize at scale

weaknesses: RELIANCE is a diversified conglomerate (oil, retail, telecom) while ONGC is pure-play upstream oil; genuine business divergences are common and the correlation baseline may be overstated
The 30-bar rolling correlation window is noisy with 1-min data; random price fluctuations can trigger false correlation breakdown signals
Low signal frequency (1-2 trades/day at best) means the strategy is capital-inefficient and may need to be combined with other strategies to justify monitoring infrastructure
prior_art: Cont & Bouchaud (2000) correlation dynamics; Lillo & Mantegna (2005) correlation-based trading. Adapted for intraday Indian energy sector pair with crude oil filter.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 45bps - 0.40 * 30bps = 27 - 12 = 15bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT. Net ~3bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~4.5bps daily seems low. The 24bps estimate includes tail events where correlation breakdowns of 0.6+ snap back violently for 80+ bps winners. These outliers drive the edge.

name: cross_listed_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Stocks listed on both NSE and BSE can exhibit transient price divergences of 2-10 bps due to differential order flow, varying market microstructure (NSE has higher HFT participation), and latency differences between exchange matching engines. While professional arbitrageurs keep the spread tight on large-caps, mid-cap stocks (market cap ₹5000-20000 cr) with lower BSE volume have exploitable divergences that persist for 1-5 minutes. The edge exists because BSE has lower participation from algorithmic traders, creating stale quotes that diverge from NSE price discovery. The inefficiency persists because dual-exchange execution requires co-location on both exchanges, which is expensive for retail.
universe: Liquid mid-cap stocks listed on both NSE and BSE (e.g., VOLTAS, GODREJCP, MPHASIS)
stock_filter: market cap ₹5000-20000 cr; NSE volume > ₹50cr/day; BSE volume > ₹5cr/day; listed on both exchanges

conditions: price_diff_bps > 5 (NSE trading higher than BSE by >5bps)
long.confirmation: buy on BSE, sell on NSE simultaneously when diff exceeds 5bps

conditions: price_diff_bps < -5 (BSE trading higher than NSE by >5bps)
short.confirmation: buy on NSE, sell on BSE simultaneously when diff exceeds 5bps

entry.entry_price: limit orders at mid-price on both exchanges, aggressive side first

exit.stop_loss: price_diff_bps exceeds 15bps against position OR loss > 0.2%
exit.trailing_stop: none (trades are too short for trailing stops)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 10 mins (if arb hasn't closed, something structural)
exit.eod_rule: flatten all positions by 15:25 IST (ensure settlement on both exchanges)
exit.signal_exit: if combined_spread_bps widens > 15bps during trade, exit (liquidity drying up)

risk.position_sizing: equal INR notional on each exchange, same number of shares on each leg

filters.vix_filter: none (arb works in all VIX regimes)
filters.time_filter: best windows: 09:20-10:00 and 14:30-15:25 (open/close have more BSE dislocations)
filters.volume_filter: BSE 1-min volume must be > 500 shares (minimum for executable arb)
filters.trend_filter: none (market-neutral by construction)
filters.spread_filter: combined bid-ask spread across both exchanges < 8bps
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has corporate action affecting settlement on either exchange
other_filters: skip if BSE has had exchange outage or slowdown alerts today

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — as BSE improves matching engine speed and more arb bots enter, divergences will shrink

weaknesses: BSE liquidity for mid-caps is extremely thin; large orders can move the BSE price against you, and fills may be partial or delayed
Zerodha doesn't support true simultaneous cross-exchange execution; the latency between placing NSE and BSE orders creates leg risk
Settlement and clearing across two exchanges adds operational complexity; T+1 settlement mismatches can occur
prior_art: Gagnon & Karolyi (2010) cross-listing price parity; adapted for NSE-BSE dual listing. Similar to Subrahmanyam (1994) on multi-market microstructure.
notes: Edge math: 0.75 * 5bps - 0.25 * 8bps = 3.75 - 2.0 = 1.75bps gross per trade. Costs per trade ~6bps RT (both exchanges). Net negative per trade! Edge relies on high frequency (10+ trades/day) and capturing the 5bps+ divergences that occur during volatile opens. The 20bps daily estimate assumes 10 trades with avg 2bps net. Realistically marginal. Needs very low latency to work.

name: gap_fill_full_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Overnight gaps in Indian large-cap stocks fill completely (price returns to prior close) roughly 65-70% of the time within the session, driven by the behavioral tendency of institutional traders to fade overnight sentiment extremes and re-establish positions at prior day's equilibrium levels. Gaps of 0.3-1.0% are the sweet spot: large enough to be meaningful but small enough that they reflect sentiment shifts rather than genuine news. The inefficiency persists because retail traders chase gap direction (FOMO), providing liquidity to the counter-gap fade. The edge exists in the asymmetry between retail directional flow and institutional mean-reversion flow.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; market cap > ₹50000cr; today's gap between 0.3% and 1.0%
indicators: vwap_dev = (close - vwap) / vwap * 10000  # bps from VWAP

conditions: gap_pct < -0.3 AND gap_pct > -1.0 (gap down, moderate size)
long.confirmation: price crosses above VWAP for the first time after gap down

conditions: gap_pct > 0.3 AND gap_pct < 1.0 (gap up, moderate size)
short.confirmation: price crosses below VWAP for the first time after gap up

entry.entry_price: market order at VWAP cross confirmation

exit.stop_loss: gap extends by 50% from open (e.g., 0.5% gap down extends to 0.75% below prev close) OR 0.5 * ATR_14
exit.trailing_stop: once 50% of gap filled, trail stop at 25% gap fill level
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 180 mins (gap should fill within 3 hours or likely won't)
exit.signal_exit: if NIFTY 50 moves > 1% in gap direction (confirming gap is structural), exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; high VIX gaps are more likely structural (news-driven)
filters.time_filter: enter only between 09:20-10:30 IST; if no entry by 10:30, skip today
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 gap direction same as stock gap (sector-wide gap, not stock-specific news)
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings, dividends, or corporate action today; skip if gap caused by identifiable news (analyst upgrade/downgrade, regulatory action)
