other_filters: skip if stock gapped > 1% (too large, likely news-driven, lower fill probability)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — gap fill is a structural behavioral pattern that has persisted across decades and markets

weaknesses: Cannot reliably distinguish between sentiment-driven gaps (which fill) and news-driven gaps (which continue); the event_filter helps but is imperfect
Full gap fill requires patience — many gaps fill 70-80% and then reverse, hitting trailing stop before reaching the 100% target
On high-VIX days or macro event days, multiple stocks gap simultaneously in the same direction, creating correlated risk across the 2 allowed positions
prior_art: Caginalp & Laurent (1998) gap analysis; Cooper et al. (2004) gap returns. Indian market gap fill rates documented by various domestic trading educators with 60-70% fill rates for moderate gaps.
notes: Edge math: 0.65 * 55bps - 0.35 * 40bps = 35.75 - 14 = 21.75bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~12.75bps/trade * avg 2 trades = ~25.5bps daily. Strong edge but requires disciplined stock selection (gap size filter is critical). The VWAP cross confirmation delays entry but dramatically improves win rate vs entering at open.

name: gap_fill_partial_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Targeting 50% gap fill instead of 100% dramatically improves win rate (from ~65% to ~78%) while sacrificing only half the per-trade profit. Most gaps begin filling within the first 60 minutes as institutional VWAP algorithms begin working counter-gap orders. The 50% level is psychologically significant because it represents the midpoint between open and prior close, where short-term traders who entered at the open begin taking profits, creating a natural resistance/support level. This conservative variant accepts smaller per-trade edge for meaningfully higher consistency and lower drawdowns.
universe: NIFTY 50 and NIFTY Next 50 constituents on NSE
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹150cr; gap between 0.4% and 1.2%

long.confirmation: EMA_9 crosses above EMA_21 on 1-min chart

short.confirmation: EMA_9 crosses below EMA_21 on 1-min chart

entry.entry_price: limit order 1 tick inside best bid/ask at EMA cross signal

exit.stop_loss: price extends 30% beyond gap open in gap direction OR 0.4 * ATR_10 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: once 25% of gap filled, trail stop at open price (breakeven at 0%)
exit.signal_exit: if EMA_9 crosses back in gap direction (momentum reversing), exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 11 and 18 (calm regime for predictable gap fills)
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:20-10:00 IST only; partial fills take less time
filters.trend_filter: prev day's close within 1% of prev day's VWAP (balanced prior session)
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has any corporate action; skip earnings day ± 1 day
other_filters: skip if NIFTY futures gap > 0.8% (broad market dislocation, not stock-specific)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — conservative gap fill has been a stable pattern across global markets

weaknesses: Targeting only 50% fill means per-trade profit is small (20-30 bps on a 0.5% gap); after costs, net edge per trade is thin
The EMA cross confirmation delays entry significantly — by the time EMA(9) crosses EMA(21), 20-30% of the gap may already be filled, reducing the remaining opportunity
On trending days where the gap extends throughout the session, the stop loss hits quickly and consistently, creating clustered losing days
prior_art: Gap fill probability distributions from Cooper et al. (2004); partial target optimization similar to Seifert & Jauering (2019) optimal profit-taking levels.
notes: Edge math: 0.78 * 25bps - 0.22 * 30bps = 19.5 - 6.6 = 12.9bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~3.9bps/trade * 3 trades = ~11.7bps daily. Conservative but consistent. The high win rate makes this psychologically easier to trade and compounds well over time.

name: gap_fade_large_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Large gaps (>1.5%) in NIFTY 50 stocks are disproportionately caused by overnight sentiment over-reaction to global cues (US market moves, Asian open, commodity prices) rather than stock-specific news. When no earnings or corporate action drives the gap, large gaps fade (partially revert) 55-60% of the time because the overnight price impact overshoots the fundamental information content. The key insight is that Indian markets open 4-5 hours after US close, and overnight futures already priced in the US move — the cash market open often over-extends due to retail market orders at open. Fading the excess (the gap beyond what NIFTY futures implied) captures this over-reaction.
stock_filter: gap > 1.5% (absolute); no earnings/corporate action; daily volume > ₹300cr
indicators: excess_gap = gap_pct - NIFTY_implied_gap_pct  # stock gap beyond index gap

conditions: no earnings or corporate action for the stock today
long.confirmation: MACD_line crosses above MACD_signal (momentum turning) AND volume_climax == False (selling exhaustion)

conditions: no earnings or corporate action for the stock today
short.confirmation: MACD_line crosses below MACD_signal AND volume_climax == False

entry.entry_price: market order at MACD signal cross

exit.target: revert 40% of the excess_gap (not full gap, just the excess over index)
exit.stop_loss: gap extends further by 0.5% from open OR 0.7 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: once 20% of excess_gap recovered, trail stop at entry price (breakeven)
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 14:00 IST (leave buffer for potential continuation)
exit.signal_exit: if volume_climax fires in gap direction while in trade, exit (new institutional flow confirming gap)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; above 25, large gaps are often structural
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:20-10:30 IST; if no setup by 10:30, skip
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not gapping > 2% in same direction (systemic event, don't fade)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.06% at entry (large gaps can widen spreads)
filters.event_filter: CRITICAL: skip if stock has earnings, board meetings, M&A news, regulatory actions, analyst target changes today
other_filters: skip if gap is caused by sector-wide news affecting all peers equally

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — large gap fading is behavioral (retail FOMO at open) and unlikely to be arbitraged away

weaknesses: The news filter is imperfect — sometimes gaps are driven by leaked information, off-market block deals, or global events that fundamentally justify the gap, leading to gap-and-go instead of fade
Low frequency: large gaps (>1.5%) occur on only ~15-20% of trading days for any given stock, requiring monitoring of the full NIFTY 50 universe for sufficient signals
Wider bid-ask spreads at open on gap days increase effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, significantly eating into the edge vs normal days
prior_art: Dyl & Maberly (1992) gap reversal; Fabozzi et al. (2007) on overnight gap return predictability. Indian context similar to findings in Aggarwal & Gupta (2009) on NSE opening returns.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 80bps - 0.44 * 45bps = 44.8 - 19.8 = 25bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT (higher slippage at open). Net ~13bps/trade. At 0.5 trades/day avg, daily edge ~6.5bps. The 35bps estimate includes occasional very large gaps (>3%) where fade profit is 100+ bps. Highly asymmetric return distribution.

name: gap_continuation_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When a stock gaps up/down on genuine institutional flow (above-average pre-open volume, gap aligned with sector/index direction), the gap often continues for another 0.5-1.0% as momentum traders pile in and VWAP algorithms begin accumulating. This is the 'gap and go' pattern. The key filter is volume: gaps on 2x+ average volume signal real institutional interest, not retail noise. The inefficiency exists because most traders are either fading the gap (contrarian bias) or waiting too long to enter (confirmation bias), allowing early momentum entrants to capture the continuation move before the crowd arrives. Entering within the first 10 minutes with volume confirmation captures this window.
universe: NIFTY 50 and NIFTY Next 50 on NSE
stock_filter: gap > 0.5% (abs); opening 5-min volume > 2x avg; sector ETF gapping in same direction
session: 09:15-12:00 IST (momentum plays work in morning session)
indicators: rel_strength = gap_pct - NIFTY_gap_pct  # stock gap relative to index

long.confirmation: breakout bar closes in upper 30% of its range (strong close)

short.confirmation: breakdown bar closes in lower 30% of its range (weak close)

entry.entry_price: market order on bar close after breakout/breakdown confirmed

exit.target: 0.7% move from entry in gap direction (continuation target)
exit.stop_loss: close re-enters opening range (below ORH for longs, above ORL for shorts) OR 0.5 * ATR_10
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.3% gain, trail stop at 0.15% below current high (longs) or above current low (shorts)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 60 mins (morning momentum fades by late morning)
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 12:00 IST (momentum play, don't hold into lunch)
exit.signal_exit: if EMA_5 crosses EMA_13 against position direction, exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 13 (need some volatility for continuation); VIX < 25 (not chaotic)
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:20-10:15 IST; gap and go works in first hour only
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY futures gapping in same direction as stock (aligned momentum)
filters.event_filter: only trade if gap is NOT due to stock-specific earnings (sector/market-wide momentum is better)
other_filters: skip if opening range is wider than 1.5 * ATR_10 (already extended)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — momentum continuation is a well-known pattern but execution timing creates edge

weaknesses: Win rate is below 55% — momentum continuation fails frequently, and the strategy relies on occasional large winners to offset more frequent small losers (emotionally difficult)
The 5-minute opening range breakout gives a delayed entry; by the time the breakout is confirmed, 30-40% of the continuation move may already be done
On days where initial momentum is due to a single large block trade (not genuine flow), the continuation fails and reverses sharply, hitting stops
prior_art: Katz & McCormick (2000) gap and go; Clenow (2014) momentum strategies. Similar to Bulkowski (2005) gap continuation patterns in Technical Analysis.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 70bps - 0.48 * 30bps = 36.4 - 14.4 = 22bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~13bps/trade * 2 trades = ~26bps daily. The edge is in the asymmetry: winners are 1.6x losers. Strict time filter (morning only) is critical — afternoon gap continuation is unprofitable.

name: gap_reversal_volume_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When a stock gaps in one direction but volume within the first 15 minutes is heavily concentrated on the opposite side (buying into a gap down, selling into a gap up), it signals institutional counter-positioning. Volume-at-price analysis showing accumulation/distribution against the gap direction is a strong predictor of intraday reversal. The inefficiency exists because most gap traders focus on price action alone and ignore the volume microstructure at the open. By requiring both gap + contrary volume signature, we filter for high-conviction reversal setups where smart money is visibly positioning against the gap.
stock_filter: gap > 0.5% (abs); daily avg volume > ₹200cr
indicators: reversal_bar = (gap_pct > 0 AND close < open AND close < low[1]) OR (gap_pct < 0 AND close > open AND close > high[1])

conditions: volume_imbalance > 0.2 (net buying into gap down — accumulation)
OBV_slope > 0 (on-balance volume rising despite gap down)
long.confirmation: reversal_bar == True AND close crosses above VWAP

conditions: volume_imbalance < -0.2 (net selling into gap up — distribution)
OBV_slope < 0 (on-balance volume falling despite gap up)
short.confirmation: reversal_bar == True AND close crosses below VWAP

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: price reaches prev_close (full gap fill, aided by volume confirmation)
exit.stop_loss: price makes new intraday extreme in gap direction (new low for gap down, new high for gap up) OR 0.6 * ATR_14
exit.trailing_stop: after 50% gap fill, trail stop at 25% fill level
exit.signal_exit: if volume_imbalance reverses sign (contrary volume dries up), exit

filters.time_filter: entry window 09:30-10:30 IST (need volume data, but not too late)
filters.volume_filter: first 15-min total volume > 1.5x average first-15-min volume
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not gapping > 1.5% in same direction (sector-wide panic, don't counter-trade)
filters.event_filter: skip if gap is caused by company-specific news (earnings miss, regulatory action)
other_filters: volume_imbalance must be computed from actual tick-level buy/sell classification, not inferred from 1-min bars

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volume microstructure signals are underutilized in Indian retail trading

weaknesses: Buy/sell volume classification at tick level is noisy; Lee-Ready algorithm misclassifies 15-20% of trades, weakening the volume_imbalance signal
Requires tick-level data which Zerodha does not provide natively; must use alternative data sources or approximate from 1-min OHLCV (lower accuracy)
The 15-minute wait for volume confirmation means entry is delayed, and fast-filling gaps may already be 30-40% filled before the signal triggers
prior_art: Chordia et al. (2002) order imbalance and stock returns; Llorente et al. (2002) volume-return relationship. Gap reversal with volume adapted from Connors & Raschke (1996).
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 55bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 34.1 - 13.3 = 20.8bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~11.8bps/trade * 1.5 trades/day = ~17.7bps daily. The volume confirmation filter is the key differentiator vs simple gap fade; it raises win rate from ~55% to ~62% at the cost of fewer signals.

name: gap_to_vwap_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: After a gap open, the developing session VWAP acts as a gravitational attractor because institutional algorithms (TWAP/VWAP algos) that were scheduled to execute at VWAP will naturally pull price toward it. When price opens away from VWAP and diverges further, the institutional reversion pressure builds. By entering when the gap creates a >20 bps deviation from developing VWAP and waiting for the first sign of VWAP convergence, we ride the institutional flow back to VWAP. The edge persists because retail traders ignore VWAP and trade on price action alone, while institutional VWAP algos are the dominant intraday flow.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; gap > 0.3% (abs); VWAP deviation > 20bps at entry time

conditions: gap_pct < 0 (gap down, price extended below VWAP)
vwap_slope > 0 OR vwap_slope is flattening (VWAP not dropping sharply)
long.confirmation: price crosses above EMA(close, 5) from below while still below VWAP

conditions: gap_pct > 0 (gap up, price extended above VWAP)
short.confirmation: price crosses below EMA(close, 5) from above while still above VWAP

entry.entry_price: limit order at EMA(close, 5) cross price

exit.stop_loss: vwap_dev_bps exceeds 40bps against position OR 0.4% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: once within 5bps of VWAP, trail stop at 15bps from best deviation
exit.signal_exit: if price_vwap_cross_count > 3 in last 30 bars (choppy, no trend to VWAP), exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; high VIX causes wider VWAP deviations that may not revert
filters.time_filter: best entry window 09:25-11:00 IST; afternoon VWAP reversion is weaker
filters.trend_filter: developing VWAP slope not > 0.5 bps/min (strong trend makes VWAP a moving target)
filters.event_filter: skip earnings day stocks; skip stocks with circuit limit hits
other_filters: skip if stock has crossed VWAP 5+ times already today (choppy, no edge)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VWAP reversion is driven by institutional execution algorithms and will persist as long as VWAP benchmarking exists

weaknesses: On strong trend days, VWAP itself moves in the trend direction, so price 'touching VWAP' may happen at a worse level than entry, creating a false win that's actually a loss on the trade
The 20bps VWAP deviation threshold generates many signals in volatile sessions but these are lower quality because the VWAP is still developing and noisy in the first 30 minutes
Developing VWAP in the first 30 minutes is heavily influenced by the gap itself, making early signals unreliable (circular reference problem)
prior_art: Berkowitz et al. (1988) VWAP benchmark; adapted for intraday gap trading. Biais et al. (1995) on price discovery and VWAP convergence.
notes: Edge math: 0.66 * 28bps - 0.34 * 25bps = 18.48 - 8.5 = 9.98bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~1bps/trade * 3 trades = 3bps daily. The 25bps estimate is optimistic; requires capturing 3-4 high-quality VWAP reversion trades per day. Works best in the 09:30-11:00 window.

name: gap_relative_index_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When a stock gaps significantly more than its parent index (e.g., RELIANCE gaps -1.5% but NIFTY only gaps -0.3%), the excess gap (stock gap minus index gap) tends to mean-revert within the session. The excess gap represents stock-specific over-reaction layered on top of the market move. By isolating the excess component and fading it, we capture the alpha reversal while hedging the market beta component. This is more precise than simple gap fading because it separates systematic (index) from idiosyncratic (stock-specific) gap components. The inefficiency exists because most gap traders don't adjust for index movement, treating all gaps as equal regardless of market context.
stock_filter: abs(excess_gap) > 0.5%; daily avg volume > ₹200cr

conditions: excess_gap < -0.5 (stock gapped down more than beta-adjusted index)
long.confirmation: relative_return upticks for 3 consecutive bars (relative recovery starting)

conditions: excess_gap > 0.5 (stock gapped up more than beta-adjusted index)
short.confirmation: relative_return downticks for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation; optionally hedge with NIFTY futures for beta neutrality

exit.stop_loss: excess_gap extends by 40% from open OR relative_return loss > 0.4%
exit.trailing_stop: once 30% of excess gap filled, trail stop at 15% fill level
exit.signal_exit: if stock-specific news emerges confirming the gap (analyst action, regulatory), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: risk-based: shares = (capital * 0.004) / stop_distance; hedge with NIFTY FUT if available

filters.time_filter: enter between 09:25-10:30 IST
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in extreme trend (> 2% move) to maintain beta stability
filters.event_filter: CRITICAL: skip if stock has any identifiable news causing the excess gap (the entire thesis assumes no stock-specific news)
other_filters: skip if stock_beta R-squared < 0.3 (beta estimate unreliable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — relative gap analysis requires quantitative sophistication most retail traders lack

weaknesses: Beta estimation from 60-day daily data may not reflect the true intraday beta, especially during volatile sessions when correlations break down
The 'no stock-specific news' filter is subjective and difficult to automate — some information leaks through chat groups and social media before formal announcements
If the excess gap is caused by a large institutional block deal (which may not be publicly known), the position can be in the wrong direction for extended periods
prior_art: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) decomposition of returns into systematic and idiosyncratic. Daniel & Moskowitz (2016) on momentum crashes. Gap-specific adaptation is novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.63 * 50bps - 0.37 * 32bps = 31.5 - 11.84 = 19.66bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT (or ~15bps if hedging with NIFTY FUT). Net ~5-10bps/trade * 2 trades = ~10-20bps daily. The beta-adjusted approach improves signal quality vs raw gap fading by ~8% win rate.

name: gap_sector_leader_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When a sector leader gaps strongly (>0.8%), the lagging sector peers tend to catch up during the first 60-90 minutes as the same macro/sector catalyst that drove the leader's gap percolates through the sector. For example, if HDFCBANK gaps up 1.2%, KOTAKBANK and AXISBANK often follow with delayed moves. The leader's gap signals sector-wide information that the market hasn't fully priced into the laggers yet. The inefficiency exists because laggers have lower pre-open participation and their prices update slowly in the first 15-30 minutes. By buying laggers when the leader gaps, we capture the information transmission premium.
universe: Banking sector (HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK, AXISBANK, SBIN) on NSE
stock_filter: leader gap > 0.8%; laggers gapping < 0.3% (clear divergence); all must have volume > ₹100cr avg
indicators: leader_gap = max(abs(gap_pct) for stock in sector_basket)
leader_stock = argmax(abs(gap_pct) for stock in sector_basket)
lagger_gap = gap_pct for each non-leader stock

long.confirmation: lagger_close crosses above EMA_9 within first 30 mins of open

conditions: gap_spread > 0.5 (lagger under-gapping by >50bps in abs terms)
short.confirmation: lagger_close crosses below EMA_9 within first 30 mins

entry.entry_price: market order on the lagger stock at EMA_9 cross confirmation

exit.target: lagger catches up to 60% of leader's gap (gap_spread narrows to 40% of original)
exit.stop_loss: lagger moves against position by 0.3% from entry OR 0.5 * ATR_10
exit.trailing_stop: after 30% catch-up, trail stop at entry price (breakeven)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 60 mins (catch-up should happen in morning)
exit.signal_exit: if leader reverses its gap (leader_return_from_open < 0), exit lagger trade

filters.time_filter: enter between 09:20-10:00 IST; catch-up window is narrow
filters.volume_filter: leader must have opening 5-min volume > 2x average (confirming institutional flow)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_BANK gap same direction as leader (macro alignment)
filters.event_filter: leader gap must NOT be due to stock-specific news (earnings, M&A); must be sector/macro driven
other_filters: skip if lagger has stock-specific news that explains its under-gapping (divergence is justified)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — information transmission delays are structural to multi-stock sectors

weaknesses: The lagger may be under-gapping for a good reason (stock-specific headwind) that the filter doesn't catch, leading to the gap spread persisting or widening
Sector leader identification is based on gap size, but the largest gap may be a stock-specific event disguised as a sector move, causing the lagger trade to fail
Low frequency: the specific leader-gap > 0.8% with clear lagger under-gapping condition occurs only 3-5 times per month in banking sector
prior_art: Hou (2007) industry information diffusion; Cohen & Frazzini (2008) economic links and predictable returns. Indian banking sector adaptation for intraday leader-lagger dynamics.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 48bps - 0.40 * 28bps = 28.8 - 11.2 = 17.6bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.6bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~12.9bps daily. The 26bps estimate includes portfolio effects from occasionally trading 2 laggers simultaneously. Sector cohesion is higher in Indian banking than most other sectors.

name: opening_drive_post_gap_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The first 5-10 minutes after a gap open often exhibit a 'drive' — a strong directional move that either extends or reverses the gap — driven by the collision of pre-market orders, stop-loss triggers, and institutional VWAP algorithms starting their execution. When the opening drive direction is the SAME as the gap direction with heavy volume, it signals genuine institutional conviction and the move tends to continue for 20-40 more minutes. This strategy buys the opening drive momentum after confirming the first 5-minute bar closes in gap direction with 2x+ volume. The inefficiency exists because the opening drive window is extremely short and most traders are still assessing the market, missing the initial momentum burst.
stock_filter: gap > 0.3% (abs); opening 5-min bar closes in gap direction; volume > 2x avg first-5-min
session: 09:15-11:00 IST (opening drive is a morning-only phenomenon)
indicators: drive_alignment = drive_direction * sign(gap_pct)  # +1 if aligned, -1 if counter
bar_body_ratio = abs(close - open) / (high - low + 0.01)  # candle body vs range

conditions: drive_alignment > 0 (drive in same direction as gap)
time == 09:20 IST (enter at close of 5th 1-min bar)
long.confirmation: first_5min_close > open AND close in upper 25% of first_5min_range

short.confirmation: first_5min_close < open AND close in lower 25% of first_5min_range

entry.entry_price: market order immediately after 5th 1-min bar closes

exit.target: 0.5% move from entry in drive direction
exit.stop_loss: price reverses to opposite end of first_5min_range OR 0.5 * ATR_10
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.2% gain, trail stop at 0.1% below entry (lock in partial profit)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 40 mins (opening drive fades quickly)
exit.signal_exit: if price crosses below EMA_5 against position direction, exit (momentum lost)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 12 AND VIX < 25 (need volatility for drive, but not chaos)
filters.time_filter: only enter at 09:20 IST (5th minute close); no second entries
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 opening drive in same direction (macro alignment)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.05% by minute 5 (spread should have normalized from open)
filters.event_filter: skip if opening drive caused by stock circuit (5/10/20% band hit)
other_filters: skip if first_5min_range > 2 * ATR_10 (already over-extended)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — opening drive dynamics are structural (institutional order flow at open) and robust across markets

weaknesses: The 5-minute wait means entering after the initial burst; on strong drive days the best 0.3-0.5% move may already be done, leaving little follow-through
Opening 5-minute volume can be inflated by matching of pre-open orders, making the 2x volume filter less meaningful than it appears
When multiple stocks qualify simultaneously (broad market gap), selecting the best candidate requires ranking logic not specified here, reducing edge per trade
prior_art: Crabel (1990) 'Opening Range Breakout'; Schulmeister (2009) on opening price dynamics. Opening drive concept from Fisher (2002) 'The Logical Trader'.
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 50bps - 0.45 * 25bps = 27.5 - 11.25 = 16.25bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~7.25bps/trade * 2 trades = ~14.5bps daily. The 28bps estimate includes occasional strong drive days with 80+ bps continuation. Strictly morning-only strategy with high capital efficiency due to short hold times.

name: gap_exhaustion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: After a gap open, if the initial move extends the gap but on declining volume over 15-30 minutes, it signals exhaustion — the momentum buyers/sellers who drove the gap are running out of firepower. This volume divergence (price making new extremes while volume declines) is a classic exhaustion pattern. The reversal occurs because the marginal buyer (on gap up) or seller (on gap down) has been absorbed, and the natural counter-party (institutional mean-reversion flow) now dominates. The inefficiency persists because exhaustion identification requires real-time volume-price divergence analysis, which is more nuanced than simple price-based signals.
stock_filter: gap > 0.5% (abs); price extends gap in first 30 mins; volume declining
indicators: session_extreme = running_max(high) if gap_pct > 0 else running_min(low)
vol_decline = volume_at_extreme < volume_at_prev_extreme  # volume declining at each new high/low
exhaustion_count = consecutive count of (new_extreme_bar AND vol_decline)

conditions: session_extreme (new low) made in last 5 bars
exhaustion_count >= 3 (3+ new lows on declining volume)
long.confirmation: price closes above the high of the exhaustion bar (reversal candle)

conditions: session_extreme (new high) made in last 5 bars
exhaustion_count >= 3 (3+ new highs on declining volume)
short.confirmation: price closes below the low of the exhaustion bar (reversal candle)

entry.entry_price: market order on reversal candle close

exit.target: price reverts to session VWAP OR 60% of the gap-to-extreme range
exit.stop_loss: price makes new extreme beyond the exhaustion point by 0.15% OR 0.4 * ATR_14
exit.trailing_stop: after 40% of target reached, trail at 20% target level
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 90 mins (exhaustion reversal should play out quickly)
exit.signal_exit: if volume surges 3x in gap direction while in trade (new buyers/sellers arriving), exit

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 13 and 22 (need vol for gaps but not extreme chaos)
filters.time_filter: exhaustion signals between 09:30-11:00 IST; after 11:00, volume naturally declines (false exhaustion)
filters.volume_filter: first 5-min volume must be > 1.5x avg to confirm initial gap momentum was real
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not making extreme new highs/lows (broad market exhaustion is different from stock-level)
filters.event_filter: skip if gap driven by stock-specific news (news flow can create sustained one-way volume)
other_filters: volume decline must be genuine (3+ decreasing volume bars at new extremes), not just 1-2 bar fluke

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volume-price divergence is a fundamental market microstructure signal, not a crowded trade

weaknesses: Identifying 'declining volume at new extremes' requires clean data; 1-min volume bars are noisy and can show spurious declines during brief pauses in order flow
On strong trend days driven by macro events (rate decision, election results), what appears as exhaustion is just a brief consolidation before continuation, leading to stop-outs
The strategy requires the gap to EXTEND first (new extremes post-open) before reversing; many gaps that will fill do so immediately from the open, and this strategy misses those entirely
prior_art: Wyckoff (1931) volume-price analysis; Elder (2002) Force Index and volume divergence. Murphy (1999) Technical Analysis chapter on volume confirmation/divergence.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 58bps - 0.42 * 32bps = 33.64 - 13.44 = 20.2bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~11.2bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~16.8bps daily. The 30bps estimate includes occasional 80+ bps reversal trades after strong exhaustion signals. MFI confirmation is key — pure volume decline without MFI divergence has 45% win rate vs 58% with MFI.

name: vix_regime_switch_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: India VIX transitions between regimes (low <13, normal 13-18, elevated 18-25, crisis >25) and the optimal intraday strategy differs by regime. In low-VIX regimes, mean-reversion strategies dominate (tight ranges, reliable VWAP pulls). In elevated-VIX regimes, momentum and breakout strategies outperform (wider ranges, directional moves). By detecting the current VIX regime and switching between a mean-reversion sub-strategy (low VIX) and a momentum sub-strategy (high VIX), we adaptively capture the regime-appropriate edge. The inefficiency exists because most traders use static strategies regardless of volatility regime, leaving regime-conditional alpha on the table.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 20 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹300cr; stock in top 20 NIFTY by turnover today
indicators: vix_regime = 'low' if VIX < 13 else 'normal' if VIX < 18 else 'elevated' if VIX < 25 else 'crisis'

conditions: IF vix_regime == 'low' OR 'normal': close < BB_lower AND RSI_14 < 30 AND ADX_14 < 25 (mean reversion mode)
IF vix_regime == 'elevated': close > EMA_9 AND EMA_9 > EMA_21 AND ADX_14 > 25 (momentum mode)
long.confirmation: low/normal: RSI_14 upticks from below 30; elevated: EMA_9 slope positive for 3 bars

conditions: IF vix_regime == 'low' OR 'normal': close > BB_upper AND RSI_14 > 70 AND ADX_14 < 25 (mean reversion mode)
IF vix_regime == 'elevated': close < EMA_9 AND EMA_9 < EMA_21 AND ADX_14 > 25 (momentum mode)
short.confirmation: low/normal: RSI_14 downticks from above 70; elevated: EMA_9 slope negative for 3 bars

entry.entry_price: limit order at BB_lower/upper (mean rev) or market order (momentum)

exit.target: mean_rev: SMA(close, 20) (midline reversion); momentum: 1.5 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.stop_loss: mean_rev: 0.3 * ATR_14 beyond BB; momentum: 0.8 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: mean_rev: none; momentum: after 1.0 * ATR_14 gain, trail at 0.5 * ATR_14
exit.signal_exit: if vix_regime changes during trade, exit and re-evaluate

risk.position_sizing: vol-adjusted: base_size * (15 / India_VIX) to normalize risk across regimes

filters.vix_filter: core of the strategy — VIX regime determines sub-strategy; crisis regime (VIX > 25) = no trading
filters.time_filter: mean_rev mode: 09:30-14:30; momentum mode: 09:20-15:00
filters.trend_filter: mean_rev mode: ADX < 25 required; momentum mode: ADX > 25 required
filters.event_filter: skip RBI policy days and budget day (VIX regime unstable)
other_filters: VIX must be stable in current regime for > 30 mins (no regime flip-flopping)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — regime-adaptive strategies are structurally sound as VIX regime dynamics persist

weaknesses: VIX regime boundaries (13, 18, 25) are arbitrary and may not be optimal; the strategy is sensitive to these thresholds and may generate whipsaw signals near boundaries
Switching between mean-reversion and momentum sub-strategies mid-day (if VIX crosses a boundary) can cause confusion and partial signals from the prior regime
The combined strategy has more parameters (7+) than a single-regime strategy, increasing overfitting risk in backtesting
prior_art: Ang & Bekaert (2004) regime-switching models; Baele et al. (2019) VIX-based strategy timing. Indian VIX regime thresholds calibrated from Banerjee & Sarkar (2006) on India VIX behavior.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 52bps - 0.40 * 32bps = 31.2 - 12.8 = 18.4bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~9.4bps/trade * 3 trades = ~28.2bps daily. The regime-adaptive approach adds ~5-8bps over a static strategy by avoiding mean-reversion trades in high-vol environments (where they lose) and momentum trades in low-vol (where they whipsaw).

name: bollinger_squeeze_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Bollinger Band width on 1-min bars contracting to its 120-bar minimum signals a volatility squeeze — a coiled spring of compressed price action that tends to release in a directional breakout. On NIFTY 50 stocks, intraday squeezes often occur during the 11:00-13:30 lunch lull, and the subsequent breakout at 13:30-14:00 as institutional desks return is tradeable. The inefficiency exists because most squeeze indicators are calibrated for daily charts; on 1-min bars, the squeeze-and-release cycle happens 2-3 times per session but is invisible to daily-timeframe traders. The breakout direction can be predicted by the Keltner Channel: if BBands compress inside Keltner, the squeeze is on; breakout direction follows the preceding EMA slope.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; current BB_width at 120-bar minimum
indicators: squeeze_confirmed = BB_upper < KC_upper AND BB_lower > KC_lower

conditions: squeeze_on has been True for >= 10 bars (genuine compression, not momentary)
mom_slope > 0 (momentum oscillator turning up — likely upside breakout)
long.confirmation: BB_width starts expanding (squeeze_on flips to False) AND close > BB_upper (breakout)

conditions: squeeze_on has been True for >= 10 bars
mom_slope < 0 (momentum oscillator turning down — likely downside breakout)
short.confirmation: BB_width starts expanding AND close < BB_lower (breakdown)

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout/breakdown bar close

exit.target: 2.5 * (BB_upper - BB_lower at squeeze point) from entry — volatility expansion target
exit.stop_loss: price re-enters the squeeze range (closes back between BB_upper and BB_lower) OR 0.3% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.5x squeeze range gain, trail at 1.0x squeeze range from high/low
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 60 mins without hitting 50% of target
exit.signal_exit: if BB_width contracts again (squeeze reforms) while in trade, exit (false breakout)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 20 (too low = no breakout energy; too high = noise)
filters.time_filter: squeeze signals between 10:00-14:30 are best; avoid first 30 min (opening noise)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in extreme trend (> 1.5%) — squeeze breakouts in strong index trends tend to be one-directional
filters.event_filter: skip stocks with earnings/results today
other_filters: squeeze must last >= 10 bars to filter out momentary width dips

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — Bollinger squeeze is well-known on daily charts but under-applied on 1-min intraday

weaknesses: False breakouts are common on 1-min timeframe — the squeeze releases but price reverses within 5-10 bars, triggering the stop loss. Expected ~45% of signals are false breakouts.
The momentum oscillator direction is not a reliable predictor of breakout direction on 1-min bars; random price fluctuations in the squeeze zone can flip mom_slope frequently
During lunch hours (11:30-13:30) when squeezes commonly form, volume is low, making breakout confirmation via volume unreliable
prior_art: Bollinger (2001) Bollinger on Bollinger Bands; Carter (2012) TTM Squeeze (Keltner inside Bollinger). Adapted for 1-min Indian equity intraday context.
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 60bps - 0.45 * 28bps = 33 - 12.6 = 20.4bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~11.4bps/trade * 2.5 trades = ~28.5bps daily. Winners are 1.5x losers due to vol expansion target. Key insight: the lunch-hour squeeze followed by afternoon breakout is a recurring intraday pattern in liquid Indian stocks.

name: atr_breakout_volatility_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: ATR-based channel breakouts (price exceeding N * ATR from a reference level) on 1-min bars capture genuine volatility expansion events. Unlike fixed-point breakouts, ATR channels adapt to each stock's current volatility regime, making them robust across different volatility environments. When price breaks above/below 2.0 * ATR(14) from the session's developing mean, it signals a shift from noise to signal — the move is statistically significant given the stock's current volatility. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders use fixed price levels (round numbers, prior day's H/L) for breakouts, ignoring that the significance threshold varies with volatility.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; ATR_14_daily > 1% (sufficient volatility for breakouts)
indicators: ATR_14 = ATR(high, low, close, 14) on 1-min bars
ATR_expansion = ATR_14 / SMA(ATR_14, 60)  # ATR expansion ratio

long.confirmation: breakout bar closes in upper 25% of its range (strong bar close)

short.confirmation: breakdown bar closes in lower 25% of its range

entry.entry_price: market order on breakout/breakdown bar close

exit.target: 3.0 * ATR_14 from entry (1.5x the channel width as continuation target)
exit.stop_loss: price re-enters channel (closes below upper_channel for longs, above lower_channel for shorts) OR 1.0 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.5 * ATR_14 gain, trail at 0.75 * ATR_14 from highest/lowest close
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 60 mins without hitting 50% of target
exit.signal_exit: if ATR_expansion drops below 1.0 (volatility contracting), exit — breakout losing steam

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 13 (need vol for breakouts); VIX < 25 (not chaotic)
filters.time_filter: best breakout windows: 09:20-10:30 and 13:30-15:00; avoid lunch lull
filters.trend_filter: ADX_14 > 20 at time of breakout (directional movement present)
filters.event_filter: skip if breakout coincides with broad market news event (false breakout risk higher)
other_filters: skip if 3+ ATR channel breakouts already triggered today for this stock (over-traded)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ATR-based breakouts are adaptive and less subject to parameter decay than fixed-level breakouts

weaknesses: The 2.0 * ATR multiplier is a single parameter with high sensitivity — at 1.5x many more false breakouts trigger, at 2.5x the entry is too late and most of the move is done
On range-bound days (ADX < 20 but briefly spiking to 20+), the ADX filter lets through false signals that mean-revert quickly
Session_mean as the channel center is noisy early in the session (first 30 mins) — channels are too narrow and generate spurious breakout signals
prior_art: Keltner (1960) channels; Wilder (1978) ATR. Modern ATR channel breakouts from Kaufman (2013) adaptive trading systems. Chande (1997) on volatility-adaptive systems.
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 60bps - 0.48 * 30bps = 31.2 - 14.4 = 16.8bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~7.8bps/trade * 3 trades = ~23.4bps daily. The edge is entirely in the winner:loser ratio (1.55:1); win rate is near coin-flip. Discipline on stops is critical — every false breakout must be cut quickly.

name: implied_vs_realized_vol_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: India VIX (implied vol) systematically overestimates realized NIFTY volatility by 3-5 vol points on average — the variance risk premium (VRP). When VIX spikes to >2 standard deviations above its 20-day mean but realized 5-day vol hasn't increased proportionally, the VRP is elevated and NIFTY tends to mean-revert (as the implied fear dissipates). The strategy goes long NIFTY constituents when VRP is extreme, betting that realized vol will remain below implied, and the fear premium will compress. The inefficiency persists because the VRP in Indian markets is structurally higher than developed markets (fewer hedging alternatives, concentrated retail option selling), and retail traders cannot easily trade the VRP directly.
universe: NIFTY 50 ETF (NIFTYBEES) or top-5 NIFTY stocks by weight on NSE
stock_filter: use NIFTYBEES for simplicity; or RELIANCE, TCS, HDFCBANK, INFY, ICICIBANK basket
indicators: RV_5d = realized_vol(NIFTY_returns, lookback=5*375) * sqrt(252)  # annualized 5-day realized vol
VRP = VIX - RV_5d  # variance risk premium in vol points
VRP_z = (VRP - SMA(VRP, 20*375)) / rolling_std(VRP, 20*375)  # z-score of VRP
VIX_rate_of_change = (VIX - VIX[60]) / VIX[60] * 100  # VIX % change in last hour

conditions: VRP_z > 2.0 (VRP is unusually high — implied vol overpricing fear)
VIX_z > 1.5 (VIX elevated relative to recent history)
VIX_rate_of_change > 5 (VIX spiked recently, likely to revert)
NIFTY_RSI_30 < 40 (market pulled back, creating entry opportunity)
long.confirmation: VIX starts declining (VIX[t] < VIX[t-5]) while NIFTY stabilizes

conditions: VRP_z < -1.5 (VRP collapsed — implied vol under-pricing risk)
short.confirmation: VIX starts rising (VIX[t] > VIX[t-5]) while NIFTY stalls

entry.entry_price: market order on NIFTYBEES or basket

exit.target: VRP_z returns to 0.5 (VRP normalizing) OR NIFTY gains 0.5% from entry
exit.stop_loss: VRP_z exceeds 3.5 (VRP widening further — true risk event) OR NIFTY drops 0.5% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.3% gain, trail at 0.15% below highest close
exit.time_stop: hold for full session if signal is strong (VRP_z > 2.5)
exit.signal_exit: if VIX makes new session high while in long position, exit (fear escalating)

risk.position_sizing: VIX-adjusted: base_size * (18 / VIX) — reduce size when VIX is high

filters.vix_filter: core of strategy — requires VIX > 15 for long signals (VRP meaningful only at elevated levels)
filters.time_filter: signal can trigger any time; prefer morning entry for full-session hold
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY option volume must be > avg (confirming VIX is liquid/accurate)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in circuit-breaker territory or limit-down
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day, elections, budget (VIX spikes are justified on these days)
other_filters: skip if realized vol is also spiking (VRP high because RV is low, not because IV is high)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VRP is a structural risk premium that has persisted globally for decades

weaknesses: Low signal frequency: VRP_z > 2.0 occurs only 5-10 times per month, making this a supplement strategy, not a standalone
The strategy is essentially long NIFTY on pullbacks with a VIX filter — during genuine bear markets, VIX spikes ARE justified and the strategy will lose on multiple consecutive signals
Intraday VRP calculation is noisy because India VIX can be stale (updated every few minutes, not truly real-time), causing false signals
prior_art: Carr & Wu (2009) variance risk premia; Bollerslev et al. (2009) expected stock returns and variance risk premia. Indian VRP studied by Sehgal & Vijayakumar (2008).
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 50bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 31 - 13.3 = 17.7bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.7bps/trade. With only 0.5 trades/day avg, daily edge ~4.35bps. The 30bps estimate is per signal day (when signal fires, avg profit is 30bps). Annualized this is meaningful due to compounding.

name: vol_clustering_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Volatility clusters — high-vol periods follow high-vol bars, low-vol follows low-vol (GARCH effect). On 1-min bars, a burst of 5+ consecutive bars with range > 1.5x ATR predicts continued elevated volatility for the next 10-20 bars with ~70% accuracy. The strategy exploits this by entering breakout trades during volatility clusters (when the breakout is more likely to follow through) and avoiding entries during low-vol clusters (where breakouts fail). A simplified GARCH(1,1) model on 1-min returns forecasts next-bar volatility, and trades are only taken when forecasted vol is in the top quartile of the session. The inefficiency exists because most retail breakout traders don't condition on volatility state.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by daily turnover)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; intraday ATR > 0.8% (sufficient vol for clustering)

conditions: close > EMA_8 AND EMA_8 > EMA_21 (upward momentum in vol cluster)
bar_range_ratio > 1.2 (current bar is wide — vol expanding)
long.confirmation: close makes new 20-bar high during the vol cluster

conditions: close < EMA_8 AND EMA_8 < EMA_21 (downward momentum in vol cluster)
short.confirmation: close makes new 20-bar low during the vol cluster

entry.entry_price: market order on new 20-bar high/low within vol cluster

exit.target: 2.0 * sigma_forecast * close (2 forecasted standard deviations from entry)
exit.stop_loss: 1.0 * sigma_forecast * close against position OR 0.3% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * sigma_forecast gain, trail at 0.5 * sigma_forecast
exit.time_stop: exit when vol_percentile drops below 50 (vol cluster ending) OR held > 40 mins
exit.signal_exit: if EMA_8 crosses EMA_21 against position, exit (momentum reversal in vol cluster)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 13 (need baseline vol for clustering to be meaningful)
filters.time_filter: best vol clusters occur 09:20-10:30 and 14:00-15:00; avoid lunch lull
filters.trend_filter: ADX_14 > 18 during vol cluster (directional, not choppy vol)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.05% (wider during vol clusters, need to check)
filters.event_filter: skip if vol cluster triggered by circuit breaker or exchange halt
other_filters: GARCH parameters (alpha=0.10, beta=0.85) calibrated monthly from last 20 trading days of 1-min data

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — vol clustering is a well-documented statistical property of returns, not a crowded strategy

weaknesses: GARCH(1,1) parameters (alpha=0.10, beta=0.85) are calibrated on historical data and may not be stable intraday; parameter misspecification leads to bad vol forecasts
During vol clusters caused by news events, the directional component is unpredictable — vol clusters correctly, but direction is 50/50, reducing edge to near-zero
The 5-bar high-vol cluster requirement means the signal fires only after significant volatility has already occurred — much of the directional move may be done
prior_art: Engle (1982) ARCH; Bollerslev (1986) GARCH. Andersen & Bollerslev (1998) on intraday volatility clustering. Application to breakout timing is novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.54 * 55bps - 0.46 * 28bps = 29.7 - 12.88 = 16.82bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~7.82bps/trade * 3 trades = ~23.5bps daily. The key insight is NOT using GARCH to forecast vol direction, but to identify when vol clustering creates favorable conditions for breakout follow-through.

name: vix_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: India VIX exhibits strong intraday mean-reversion after spikes. When VIX jumps >8% within 30 minutes (typically on sudden NIFTY selloffs), it reverts at least 50% of the spike within 2 hours roughly 70% of the time. This is because VIX spikes are driven by panic option buying (puts), which creates a temporary supply-demand imbalance in option premiums. As option market makers re-hedge and the panic subsides, VIX normalizes. Since VIX and NIFTY are negatively correlated (~-0.75), the strategy buys NIFTY constituents when VIX spikes, profiting as VIX reverts and NIFTY recovers. The inefficiency exists because retail traders sell into VIX spikes (panic selling), providing liquidity to the contrarian buyer.
universe: NIFTYBEES or top-5 NIFTY 50 constituents by weight on NSE
stock_filter: use NIFTYBEES for simplicity; or basket of RELIANCE, TCS, HDFCBANK, INFY, ICICIBANK

long.confirmation: VIX starts declining (3 consecutive bars of VIX[t] < VIX[t-1]) — panic subsiding

conditions: VIX_30min_change < -6 (VIX crushed >6% in 30 mins — complacency spike)
short.confirmation: VIX starts rising for 3 consecutive bars — complacency reversing

entry.entry_price: market order on VIX reversal confirmation

exit.target: VIX reverts 50% of spike (VIX_30min_change halves) OR NIFTY recovers 50% of drawdown
exit.stop_loss: VIX makes new session high (spike continuing) OR NIFTY drops another 0.5% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after NIFTY recovers 0.3%, trail stop at entry price (breakeven)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 150 mins without 40% VIX reversion
exit.signal_exit: if VIX spike driven by actual black swan event (circuit breaker triggered), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: VIX-inverse: base_size * min(1.0, 18/VIX) — smaller size at higher VIX

filters.vix_filter: core signal — requires VIX spike >8% in 30 mins
filters.time_filter: VIX spikes after 14:00 IST less likely to revert within session; prefer morning spikes
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY option volume must be elevated (confirming VIX spike is real, not stale data)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY must not have broken a major support level (200-SMA on daily) — structural breaks don't revert
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask on entry vehicle < 0.08% (spreads widen during VIX spikes)
filters.event_filter: CRITICAL: skip on RBI policy days, budget, election results, global crisis events — VIX spikes on these are fundamentally justified
other_filters: if VIX was already > 25 before the spike, skip (elevated base vol = spike may continue)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX mean-reversion is structural (option gamma hedging) and persists across global markets

weaknesses: The strategy buys the dip during fear spikes — during genuine crises (2020 COVID, 2022 Russia-Ukraine), VIX spikes DON'T revert and the strategy takes large losses on consecutive signals
VIX spike frequency is low (8%+ spikes in 30 min happen ~3-5 times per month), making this capital-inefficient as a standalone strategy
Wider bid-ask spreads during VIX spikes increase effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, significantly cutting into the edge
prior_art: Whaley (2000) VIX as fear gauge; Daigler & Rossi (2006) VIX mean reversion. Simon & Campasano (2014) VIX futures roll and mean reversion.
notes: Edge math: 0.68 * 45bps - 0.32 * 40bps = 30.6 - 12.8 = 17.8bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT (wider spreads during spikes). Net ~5.8bps/trade. At 0.2 trades/day, daily avg = ~1.2bps. The 35bps estimate is per signal day. Strategy is best combined with other strategies to fill non-signal days.

name: low_vol_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The low-volatility anomaly (Ang et al. 2006) — low-vol stocks deliver higher risk-adjusted returns than high-vol stocks — manifests intraday in Indian markets. NIFTY 50 stocks in the bottom tercile of 20-day realized vol that also show positive intraday momentum (price > VWAP, EMA alignment) outperform high-vol stocks with similar momentum characteristics. This is because low-vol stocks attract institutional accumulation (steady, predictable) while high-vol stocks attract speculative flow (noisy, mean-reverting). The strategy goes long low-vol momentum stocks and short high-vol momentum stocks, capturing the low-vol premium intraday.
stock_filter: rank stocks by 20-day realized vol; long bottom tercile, short top tercile (with momentum filter)
indicators: intraday_momentum = close > vwap AND EMA(close, 9) > EMA(close, 21)

conditions: low_vol == True (stock in bottom vol tercile)
intraday_momentum == True (above VWAP, EMAs aligned up)
long.confirmation: close makes new session high while above VWAP

conditions: high_vol == True (stock in top vol tercile)
intraday_momentum == True for short (below VWAP, EMAs aligned down)
short.confirmation: close makes new session low while below VWAP

entry.entry_price: market order; size long leg 1.2x short leg to account for beta difference

exit.target: long leg outperforms short leg by 30bps (relative target)
exit.stop_loss: long leg underperforms short leg by 25bps OR either leg hits 0.5% absolute loss
exit.trailing_stop: after 15bps relative outperformance, trail at 5bps relative
exit.time_stop: hold for session unless stopped out (this is a factor bet, not a quick trade)
exit.signal_exit: if VIX spikes > 20 during trade, close (vol regime shift breaks the anomaly)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; low-vol anomaly weakens in high-VIX environments (all stocks become high-vol)
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:45-11:00; hold through session
filters.volume_filter: both long and short stocks must have avg volume > ₹100cr/day
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in extreme trend (> 2%); factor bets work in moderate markets
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has earnings today; skip budget/RBI days
other_filters: rebalance vol ranking daily before market open; don't use stale rankings

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — low-vol anomaly is well-documented and may compress as more quant funds exploit it

weaknesses: The low-vol anomaly is primarily a cross-sectional effect over weeks/months; compressing it to intraday may not capture the same economic forces (institutional preference, leverage aversion)
Two-leg execution with stocks from different sectors creates idiosyncratic risk that may dominate the low-vol factor return on any given day
In risk-off environments (sharp selloffs), low-vol stocks also sell off, and the short high-vol leg may actually outperform (short squeeze), creating large losses
prior_art: Ang et al. (2006) cross-section of vol and returns; Baker et al. (2011) betting against beta; Blitz & Van Vliet (2007) low-vol effect. Intraday adaptation is novel.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 35bps - 0.42 * 25bps = 20.3 - 10.5 = 9.8bps gross. Costs ~12bps RT (two legs). Net negative per trade! The 22bps daily estimate relies on the full-session hold allowing the factor to express. Factor bets need time; this is borderline for intraday. Consider as supplementary only.

name: vol_adjusted_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Standard mean-reversion strategies use fixed z-score thresholds (e.g., 2.0 sigma), but the optimal threshold varies with the current volatility regime. In low-vol environments, a 1.5-sigma deviation is significant and likely to revert. In high-vol, even 2.5-sigma deviations may be noise. By dynamically scaling the entry z-score threshold based on the ratio of current 30-min realized vol to 120-min realized vol, we adapt the mean-reversion strategy to the local volatility environment. When vol is compressing (30min_vol < 120min_vol), use tighter thresholds (1.5 sigma); when vol is expanding, require wider thresholds (2.5+ sigma). This captures more mean-reversion trades in calm periods and avoids false signals in volatile periods.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 20 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr
indicators: adaptive_threshold = 1.5 + 1.0 * vol_ratio  # ranges from ~1.5 (low vol) to ~3.0 (high vol)

conditions: close < vwap (below VWAP, institutional buy territory)
long.confirmation: price_z crosses above (-adaptive_threshold + 0.2) (starts reverting)

short.confirmation: price_z crosses below (adaptive_threshold - 0.2)

entry.entry_price: limit order at current close on confirmation bar

exit.trailing_stop: once price_z crosses 0.5 toward zero, trail at 1.0 from best
exit.signal_exit: if vol_ratio > 2.0 (vol regime shift during trade), exit

filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:00 IST; avoid first 15 min (vol estimates unstable)
filters.trend_filter: ADX_14 < 30 (mean-reversion requires non-trending environment)
filters.event_filter: skip earnings day stocks
other_filters: vol_ratio must be computed with min 30 bars of data (skip first 30 mins of session)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — adaptive threshold is a meta-improvement over static thresholds, not a crowded trade

weaknesses: The adaptive_threshold formula (1.5 + 1.0 * vol_ratio) is ad-hoc and not derived from first principles; optimal coefficients may differ by stock and regime
In rapidly changing vol environments (vol_ratio crossing 1.0 back and forth), the threshold flickers, generating whipsaw entry signals
Higher trade frequency (3-6/day) means transaction costs compound; the per-trade edge must be consistently positive, which is hard with 1-min noise
prior_art: Bali & Cakici (2004) volatility and cross-section returns; adapted for intraday with dynamic thresholds. Similar to Kaufman (2013) adaptive moving average concept applied to mean-reversion thresholds.
notes: Edge math: 0.64 * 35bps - 0.36 * 28bps = 22.4 - 10.08 = 12.32bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~3.32bps/trade * 4 trades = ~13.3bps daily. The adaptive threshold adds ~3-5bps over static 2.0-sigma threshold by reducing false signals in high-vol and capturing more signals in low-vol.

name: intraday_vol_pattern_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Intraday volatility follows a well-documented U-shape pattern: high at open (09:15-10:00), declining through lunch (11:30-13:30), and rising again toward close (14:30-15:30). This pattern is exploitable because breakout strategies work best during high-vol periods (open, close) while mean-reversion works during low-vol periods (lunch). Additionally, the transition from low-vol to high-vol in the afternoon (13:30-14:00) creates a predictable volatility expansion that can be traded with straddle-like equity positions. The inefficiency exists because most strategies ignore the time-of-day vol structure, applying the same logic at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM despite vastly different volatility environments.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 10 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹300cr; stock must exhibit U-shape vol pattern (verified on 20-day history)
session: 09:15-15:29 IST (full session, strategy adapts by period)
indicators: session_period = 'open' if time < 10:00 else 'mid_morning' if time < 11:30 else 'lunch' if time < 13:30 else 'afternoon' if time < 14:30 else 'close'

conditions: IF session_period == 'lunch': close < BB_lower_20 AND vol_surprise < 0.8 (mean_rev in low vol)
IF session_period == 'open' OR 'close': close > EMA_5 AND EMA_5 > EMA_13 AND vol_surprise > 1.2 (momentum in high vol)
IF session_period == 'afternoon': close > BB_mid_20 AND vol_surprise starting to rise from <0.8 to >1.0 (vol expansion entry)
long.confirmation: lunch: RSI(14) < 30 upticks; open/close: new 20-bar high; afternoon: vol_surprise crosses 1.0 from below

conditions: IF session_period == 'lunch': close > BB_upper_20 AND vol_surprise < 0.8
IF session_period == 'open' OR 'close': close < EMA_5 AND EMA_5 < EMA_13 AND vol_surprise > 1.2
IF session_period == 'afternoon': close < BB_mid_20 AND vol_surprise starting to rise
short.confirmation: lunch: RSI(14) > 70 downticks; open/close: new 20-bar low; afternoon: vol_surprise crosses 1.0

entry.entry_price: limit order (lunch period) or market order (open/close period)

exit.target: lunch: BB_mid_20 (mean rev target); open/close: 1.5 * ATR_10; afternoon: 1.0 * ATR_10
exit.stop_loss: lunch: 0.3 * ATR_10 beyond BB; open/close: 0.8 * ATR_10; afternoon: 0.5 * ATR_10
exit.trailing_stop: open/close: after 1.0 * ATR_10, trail at 0.5 * ATR_10; others: none
exit.time_stop: lunch: 45 min max; open: 30 min; afternoon: 30 min; close: hold to 15:25
exit.signal_exit: if session_period transitions while in trade, re-evaluate using new period's exit rules

risk.position_sizing: vol-scaled: base_size * (median_expected_vol / current_expected_vol) to equalize risk across periods

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 for lunch mean-rev; no VIX filter for open/close momentum
filters.time_filter: strategy is time-of-day by design; each period has its own filter
filters.volume_filter: volume must be within 50-200% of expected_volume_at_this_minute
filters.trend_filter: lunch: ADX < 25; open/close: ADX > 18; afternoon: no ADX filter
filters.event_filter: skip if major news event disrupts the normal vol pattern (VIX > 25)
other_filters: verify U-shape pattern exists for this stock on trailing 20 days before trading

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — the intraday vol U-shape is a structural market microstructure feature documented across all major markets

weaknesses: The strategy effectively runs 3 different sub-strategies (mean-rev, momentum, vol-expansion) which triples the parameter count and overfitting risk compared to a single-regime strategy
On event days (earnings, macro announcements), the U-shape vol pattern is disrupted and all three sub-strategies can simultaneously fail
The afternoon vol-expansion entry (13:30-14:00) has the lowest win rate because the vol rise isn't always directional — sometimes vol rises but price just chops
prior_art: Wood, McInish & Ord (1985) intraday return volatility patterns; Andersen & Bollerslev (1997) intraday vol seasonality. U-shape in Indian markets confirmed by Sinha (2016).
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 42bps - 0.40 * 28bps = 25.2 - 11.2 = 14bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~5bps/trade * 4 trades = ~20bps daily. The time-of-day decomposition adds ~4bps over a static strategy by matching strategy type to vol regime. Lunch period mean-rev has highest win rate (68%) but smallest winners.

name: vol_breakout_squeeze_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Volatility cycles between contraction and expansion phases. When ATR(14) on 1-min bars contracts to its 120-bar minimum AND the Bollinger Band width percentile drops below 10 (dual squeeze), the subsequent expansion phase produces tradeable breakouts that are 40% more likely to follow through than breakouts without a squeeze precondition. The strategy waits for the contraction-expansion inflection point — the exact bar where ATR starts expanding after reaching its minimum — and enters in the direction of the first expansion bar. The edge exists because the squeeze filters out 60% of false breakouts by requiring genuine compression first. Most breakout traders don't filter for the contraction prerequisite.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; ATR_14_daily > 0.8% (volatile enough to have meaningful squeezes)
indicators: ATR_expanding = ATR_14 > ATR_14[1] AND ATR_14[1] <= ATR_min_120  # inflection point
expansion_bar_direction = sign(close - open) on first bar after dual_squeeze ends

conditions: dual_squeeze was True within last 5 bars
long.confirmation: close exceeds high of squeeze range (highest high during squeeze period)

conditions: dual_squeeze was True within last 5 bars
short.confirmation: close breaks below low of squeeze range

entry.entry_price: market order on squeeze range breakout/breakdown

exit.stop_loss: price re-enters squeeze range midpoint OR 0.25% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * squeeze_range gain, trail at 0.5 * squeeze_range from best
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 45 mins without hitting 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if ATR_14 starts contracting again within 10 bars of entry (false expansion), exit

filters.time_filter: best squeezes form 10:00-13:30 (lunch lull); best expansions 13:30-15:00
filters.trend_filter: none (the squeeze IS the filter — it selects for stocks about to trend)
filters.event_filter: skip if expansion triggered by stock-specific news (prefer technical expansion)
other_filters: dual_squeeze must last >= 8 bars (genuine compression, not random ATR dip)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — vol contraction/expansion cycle is a fundamental market property, not a crowded trade

weaknesses: The dual squeeze condition (ATR min AND BB width percentile < 10) is restrictive; it may only trigger 2-3 times per stock per day, limiting universe to scanning 50+ stocks
First expansion bar direction is a coin flip unless additional momentum confirmation is used; the direction filter alone has ~55% accuracy
Squeeze ranges are narrow by definition, so the 2x range target may be only 15-25 bps, and after costs the net profit per trade is very thin
prior_art: Carter (2012) TTM Squeeze; Bollinger (2001) on bandwidth contraction. Historical volatility cycling from Mandelbrot (1963) and Parkinson (1980).
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 45bps - 0.44 * 22bps = 25.2 - 9.68 = 15.52bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~6.52bps/trade * 2.5 trades = ~16.3bps daily. The dual-squeeze filter adds ~4bps over single-indicator squeeze by reducing false breakouts. Key: squeeze must be genuine (8+ bars) not a momentary ATR dip.

name: straddle_proxy_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: A synthetic straddle can be approximated in equity markets by entering a position at a key support/resistance level and placing symmetric stop-and-reverse orders. When a stock consolidates at a well-defined level (prior day's close, VWAP, round number), going long with a tight stop that flips to short (and vice versa) mimics a straddle payoff: profit from large directional moves, small loss on whipsaws. The key insight is timing: enter when ATR contraction signals an imminent directional move (compression before expansion). Unlike option straddles, this equity proxy has no time decay but faces whipsaw risk. The edge exists when entry timing aligns with vol compression and the breakout generates a move > 2x the stop distance.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 10 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹300cr; price near a defined pivot level (within 0.1%)
session: 10:00-15:10 IST (wait for pivot level to establish)
indicators: pivot_distance = abs(close - pivot) / pivot * 10000  # bps from pivot

conditions: ATR_compression was True within last 10 bars (recent compression)
pivot_distance was < 5 bps within last 15 bars (price was at pivot recently)
long.confirmation: close above upper_trigger with volume > 1.2x SMA(volume, 20)

conditions: ATR_compression was True within last 10 bars
pivot_distance was < 5 bps within last 15 bars
short.confirmation: close below lower_trigger with volume > 1.2x SMA(volume, 20)

entry.entry_price: market order at trigger cross; set stop-and-reverse at opposite trigger

exit.target: 2.5 * stop_distance from pivot in breakout direction (risk-reward 2.5:1)
exit.stop_loss: stop-and-reverse at opposite trigger (e.g., long stopped at lower_trigger, reverse to short)
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.5 * stop_distance gain, trail at 1.0 * stop_distance from best
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 60 mins without hitting 50% of target
exit.signal_exit: max 2 reversals per setup (3rd trigger = flat, no more attempts)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 22 (need some vol but not extreme)
filters.time_filter: 10:00-14:00 IST (pivot level needs time to establish; avoid close volatility)
filters.trend_filter: none (strategy is non-directional by design)
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has major news or earnings today (not a pure vol play)
other_filters: limit to 2 reversals per setup; if whipsawed twice, stop (choppy day)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — the equity straddle proxy is uncommon; most traders trade directionally

weaknesses: Low win rate (42%) makes this psychologically difficult; multiple consecutive whipsaw losses are common before a large directional win
Unlike true option straddles, the equity proxy has unlimited downside if the stop-and-reverse mechanism fails (gap through stop level)
The max-2-reversals rule means the strategy exits flat on genuinely choppy days, missing the eventual breakout if it occurs after the 3rd trigger
prior_art: Natenberg (1994) on synthetic straddles; adapted for equity markets. Katz & McCormick (2000) on stop-and-reverse systems.
notes: Edge math: 0.42 * 65bps - 0.58 * 18bps = 27.3 - 10.44 = 16.86bps gross per attempt. Including reversals (avg 1.5 attempts per setup), net edge ~16.86 / 1.5 = 11.24bps. Costs ~9bps * 1.5 = 13.5bps RT. Net slightly negative per attempt but large winners (65bps+) compensate. The 22bps daily estimate assumes 2 setups with 1 winner.

name: vol_of_vol_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The volatility of volatility (vol-of-vol) — measured as rolling_std(ATR(14)) — is a second-order signal that precedes first-order volatility regime changes. When vol-of-vol is low (ATR itself is stable), the market is in a steady regime and mean-reversion dominates. When vol-of-vol spikes (ATR is becoming unstable), a regime transition is underway and breakout strategies should be activated. By monitoring the z-score of vol-of-vol relative to its 120-bar history, we can detect regime transitions 2-5 bars before they fully manifest in the ATR itself. This leading-indicator property gives a timing edge. The inefficiency exists because vol-of-vol is a niche second-order derivative that almost no retail trader monitors.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr
indicators: regime = 'stable' if vov_z < 1.0 else 'transitioning' if vov_z < 2.0 else 'volatile'

conditions: IF regime == 'stable': BB_pct_b < 0.05 AND RSI_14 < 28 (deep mean reversion in stable vol)
IF regime == 'transitioning': close > EMA_8 AND EMA_8 crossing above EMA_21 (breakout as vol transitions)
long.confirmation: stable: RSI_14 upticks from < 28; transitioning: volume > 1.5x SMA(volume, 20) on breakout bar

conditions: IF regime == 'transitioning': close < EMA_8 AND EMA_8 crossing below EMA_21
short.confirmation: stable: RSI_14 downticks from > 72; transitioning: volume > 1.5x on breakdown bar

entry.entry_price: stable regime: limit order at BB_lower/upper; transitioning: market order on EMA cross

exit.target: stable: SMA(close, 20) (midline reversion); transitioning: 1.5 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.stop_loss: stable: 0.3 * ATR_14 beyond BB; transitioning: 0.7 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: transitioning: after 0.8 * ATR_14, trail at 0.4 * ATR_14; stable: none
exit.signal_exit: if regime changes during trade (e.g., stable to volatile), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: regime-adjusted: stable regime 1.0x base size; transitioning 0.7x base size; volatile 0x (no entry)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 for stable; no VIX filter for transitioning
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:00; need 30+ bars of ATR history
filters.volume_filter: volume > 0.5x SMA(volume, 30) in stable; > 1.5x in transitioning
filters.trend_filter: stable: ADX < 25; transitioning: ADX rising from < 20 to > 20
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings or corporate action today
other_filters: IF regime == 'volatile' (vov_z > 2.0), do NOT trade — too chaotic for either approach

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — vol-of-vol is an academic concept rarely applied in retail trading

weaknesses: Vol-of-vol computed from a 30-bar rolling std of ATR(14) is a third-order derivative of price — extremely noisy on 1-min data with many false regime classifications
The boundary between 'stable' and 'transitioning' (vov_z = 1.0) is arbitrary and sensitive to the lookback window; different lookbacks produce different regime classifications
Running two sub-strategies increases the parameter space to 8+ parameters, raising overfitting risk in backtesting
prior_art: Carr & Wu (2017) on vol-of-vol pricing; Baltussen et al. (2018) vol-of-vol and equity returns. Adapted for intraday regime detection on Indian equities.
notes: Edge math: 0.59 * 40bps - 0.41 * 28bps = 23.6 - 11.48 = 12.12bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~3.12bps/trade * 3 trades = ~9.4bps daily. The 24bps estimate includes regime-adaptive position sizing which adds ~5bps by avoiding trades in volatile regimes (which lose ~15bps on average).

name: regime_detection_vol_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: A simplified Hidden Markov Model (HMM) with 2 states (low-vol / high-vol) fitted on rolling 120-bar 1-min return sequences can detect intraday volatility regime shifts 2-5 bars before simple threshold-based methods. The HMM captures the transition probability between regimes: when the model assigns >80% probability to a regime change (from low to high vol or vice versa), we position accordingly — entering momentum trades on low-to-high transitions and mean-reversion trades on high-to-low transitions. The edge exists because the HMM integrates the sequence pattern of returns (not just magnitude), detecting regime changes before they become obvious in ATR or Bollinger width.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 10 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹300cr; must have sufficient intraday vol to exhibit 2+ regime changes per session
indicators: regime_transition = HMM_state != HMM_state[1]  # state changed this bar

conditions: low_to_high == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol > 0.80 AND EMA_8 > EMA_21 (vol expansion + upward momentum)
OR high_to_low == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol < 0.20 AND close < vwap (vol contraction + below VWAP mean rev)
long.confirmation: low_to_high: volume > 1.5x SMA(volume, 20); high_to_low: RSI(14) < 35

conditions: low_to_high == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol > 0.80 AND EMA_8 < EMA_21 (vol expansion + downward momentum)
OR high_to_low == True AND HMM_prob_high_vol < 0.20 AND close > vwap (vol contraction + above VWAP mean rev)
short.confirmation: low_to_high: volume > 1.5x SMA(volume, 20); high_to_low: RSI(14) > 65

entry.entry_price: market order on regime transition confirmation

exit.target: low_to_high: 1.5 * ATR_14; high_to_low: VWAP touch (mean reversion)
exit.stop_loss: low_to_high: 0.7 * ATR_14; high_to_low: 0.4 * ATR_14 beyond VWAP
exit.trailing_stop: low_to_high: after 1.0 * ATR_14, trail at 0.5 * ATR_14; high_to_low: none
exit.signal_exit: if HMM flips back to prior state within 5 bars (false transition), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: transition-type adjusted: momentum trades 0.7x base (higher risk); mean-rev 1.0x base

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; extreme VIX makes HMM state estimates noisy
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:00; need 120-bar history for HMM estimation
filters.trend_filter: none (regime detection IS the filter)
filters.event_filter: skip on macro event days where regime changes are news-driven (HMM can't predict news)
other_filters: HMM must be re-fitted daily using prior 5 sessions as training data; no lookahead

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — HMM regime detection on intraday data is computationally complex and rarely implemented in retail

weaknesses: HMM is a parametric model that assumes Gaussian emissions; 1-min return distributions have fat tails, violating this assumption and causing state misclassification at extremes
Real-time HMM state estimation is computationally expensive (forward algorithm on 120 observations per bar); latency may cause missed entries on fast regime transitions
HMM with 2 states may be too simplistic — 3 states (low, medium, high vol) might better capture the intraday vol structure but adds model complexity and overfitting risk
prior_art: Hamilton (1989) regime-switching models; Bulla & Bulla (2006) HMM for financial time series. Nystrup et al. (2017) on HMM-based portfolio optimization.
notes: Edge math: 0.57 * 45bps - 0.43 * 30bps = 25.65 - 12.9 = 12.75bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~3.75bps/trade * 2.5 trades = ~9.4bps daily. The 26bps estimate includes the edge from early detection (2-5 bar lead over threshold methods). HMM adds complexity but the lead time justifies it for systematic traders.

name: overnight_vol_carry_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The overnight return variance (close-to-open) is systematically different from intraday return variance (open-to-close) in Indian equities. On average, the ratio of overnight vol to intraday vol for NIFTY 50 stocks is ~0.6, meaning stocks move less overnight than during the session. However, after nights with abnormally high overnight vol (gap > 1.5 * normal overnight range), the intraday session tends to mean-revert — the overnight move was an overshoot. Conversely, after abnormally LOW overnight vol (gap < 0.3 * normal), the intraday session tends to be directional (pent-up energy release). The strategy trades the intraday session based on the overnight vol ratio. This exploits the overnight-intraday vol relationship that most traders ignore.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; must have 20+ day overnight/intraday vol history
indicators: session_type = 'mean_rev' if overnight_ratio > 1.5 else 'momentum' if overnight_ratio < 0.3 else 'neutral'

conditions: IF session_type == 'mean_rev': gap_pct < -0.5 AND RSI_14 < 35 (fade the overnight over-reaction, buy dip)
IF session_type == 'momentum': close > EMA_9 AND EMA_9 > EMA_21 AND time > 09:30 (ride the pent-up energy up)
long.confirmation: mean_rev: price crosses above VWAP; momentum: new 30-bar high made

conditions: IF session_type == 'mean_rev': gap_pct > 0.5 AND RSI_14 > 65 (fade gap up)
IF session_type == 'momentum': close < EMA_9 AND EMA_9 < EMA_21 AND time > 09:30
short.confirmation: mean_rev: price crosses below VWAP; momentum: new 30-bar low made

exit.target: mean_rev: prev_close (gap fill); momentum: 1.5 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.stop_loss: mean_rev: gap extends 40% further; momentum: 0.7 * ATR_14 from entry
exit.trailing_stop: mean_rev: after 50% gap fill, trail at 25%; momentum: after 1.0 * ATR_14, trail at 0.5 * ATR_14
exit.signal_exit: if session_type was 'neutral' (overnight_ratio between 0.3-1.5), no trade

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 for mean_rev; no VIX filter for momentum
filters.time_filter: mean_rev: enter 09:20-10:30; momentum: enter 09:30-11:00
filters.trend_filter: momentum type: NIFTY must be moving in trade direction; mean_rev: NIFTY gap in same direction as stock (sector-wide overreaction)
filters.event_filter: skip if overnight move caused by company-specific news; only trade market/sector-driven overnight moves
other_filters: session_type == 'neutral' (0.3 < overnight_ratio < 1.5) = NO TRADE; only extreme overnight vol ratios

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — overnight/intraday vol relationship is structural and under-studied in Indian markets

weaknesses: The overnight vol ratio threshold (1.5 for mean-rev, 0.3 for momentum) is calibrated on historical data; these thresholds may shift as market microstructure evolves
On ~50% of days, the overnight_ratio is between 0.3-1.5 ('neutral'), generating no signals — strategy is highly capital-inefficient as standalone
The momentum sub-strategy (low overnight vol = intraday breakout) has only ~52% win rate, bringing down the blended performance
