prior_art: French & Roll (1986) stock return variances: trading vs non-trading hours. Lockwood & Linn (1990) on overnight vs intraday volatility. Cliff et al. (2008) on overnight returns.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 50bps - 0.40 * 32bps = 30 - 12.8 = 17.2bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.2bps/trade * 1 trade/day = ~8.2bps daily on signal days. The 28bps estimate is boosted by mean_rev sub-strategy which has 0.66 win rate. Signals fire ~50% of trading days.

name: vol_surface_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The NIFTY option volatility surface (IV across strikes and expiries) contains predictive information for intraday equity direction. Specifically, the put-call IV skew — the difference between OTM put IV and OTM call IV at the same delta — signals institutional hedging demand. When 25-delta put IV is >5 vol points above 25-delta call IV (steep skew), institutions are paying up for downside protection, suggesting elevated tail risk. Paradoxically, extremely steep skew (>8 vol points) tends to precede intraday rallies as the feared event doesn't materialize and the skew premium unwinds. The strategy fades extreme skew levels, buying NIFTY components when put skew is extreme and selling when it normalizes.
universe: NIFTY 50 top-5 weighted stocks or NIFTYBEES on NSE
stock_filter: use NIFTYBEES for simplicity; requires NIFTY weekly option chain data
indicators: skew = put_IV_25d - call_IV_25d  # in vol points
skew_rate = (skew - skew[30]) / 30  # skew change per minute
term_structure = IV_next_week_ATM - IV_this_week_ATM  # term structure slope

conditions: NIFTY_RSI_30 < 40 (NIFTY has pulled back, confirming fear)
term_structure > 0 (contango — not a crisis term structure)
long.confirmation: skew starts declining (skew_rate < 0 for 5 consecutive bars) — fear premium unwinding

conditions: skew_z < -1.5 (skew compressed — complacency, calls bid up)
short.confirmation: skew starts rising (skew_rate > 0 for 5 consecutive bars) — complacency reversing

entry.entry_price: market order on NIFTYBEES at skew reversal confirmation

exit.target: skew_z normalizes to 0.5 (long) or -0.5 (short); OR NIFTY moves 0.5% in trade direction
exit.stop_loss: skew_z exceeds 3.5 (long) suggesting genuine crisis OR NIFTY drops 0.5% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.3% gain, trail at 0.15% below best
exit.time_stop: hold for full session if skew still normalizing; exit if >240 mins without progress
exit.signal_exit: if ATM_IV spikes > 3 vol points in 30 mins while in long position, exit (genuine risk event)

risk.position_sizing: skew-adjusted: base_size * (1 - 0.05 * (skew - 5)) — smaller when skew is extreme

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 14 and 25 (need options to be liquid for accurate IV)
filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-13:00; skew signals need session time to play out
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY option volume at 25-delta strikes > 1000 contracts (ensuring IV is reliable)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not limit-down or in circuit-breaker mode
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day (skew is mechanically distorted by rollover); skip budget, RBI
other_filters: option IV data must be real-time (not delayed >5 min); stale IV creates false skew signals

edge.edge_decay_risk: moderate — as more traders access real-time option analytics, the skew signal may weaken

weaknesses: Requires real-time option chain data with accurate IV computation; Zerodha's API provides delayed option quotes which can make the skew signal stale
Extremely low frequency: skew_z > 2.0 signals fire only 2-4 times per month, making this a supplementary strategy only
When the skew is extreme for a genuine reason (geopolitical crisis, systemic risk), fading it produces large losses — the event filter cannot catch all such scenarios
prior_art: Bali & Hovakimian (2009) option implied volatility and equity returns; Xing et al. (2010) on skew and stock returns. Indian vol surface analysis by Jain & Jain (2019).
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 50bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 31 - 13.3 = 17.7bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.7bps/trade. At 0.15 trades/day avg, daily edge ~1.3bps. The 30bps estimate is per signal day. This is a high-conviction, low-frequency strategy best combined with others.

name: orb_5min_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The 5-minute opening range (high and low of 09:15-09:20) captures the initial price discovery auction. Breakout above/below this range with volume confirmation signals institutional direction for the session. The 5-min ORB is the fastest variant — it works best on high-conviction gap days where institutions have clear directional intent from pre-open orders. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders are still deciding whether to trade during the first 5 minutes, missing the institutional flow signal. The 5-min range is narrow enough that false breakouts are frequent (~55% fail), so the edge comes entirely from asymmetric payoffs: winners run 2x+ losers.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; today's gap > 0.2% (some directional energy at open)
indicators: ORB_range_vs_ATR = ORB_range / (ATR_14_daily / 6.5)  # normalized by per-hour ATR

conditions: close > vwap (above VWAP for additional confirmation)
long.confirmation: breakout bar closes in upper 30% of its range with volume > 1.5x avg

short.confirmation: breakdown bar closes in lower 30% of its range with volume > 1.5x avg

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmed breakout bar close

exit.stop_loss: close re-enters ORB range (crosses below ORB_high for longs, above ORB_low for shorts) OR midpoint of ORB range
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range gain, trail at ORB_high (longs) or ORB_low (shorts)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 120 mins without 60% of target reached
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 14:00 IST (early — 5-min ORB momentum fades by afternoon)
exit.signal_exit: if NIFTY reverses > 0.5% against trade direction, exit (macro headwind)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 22 (need vol for breakout but not chaos)
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:20-09:45 IST; breakout must occur within 25 mins of range formation
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not limit-down or circuit-breaker; gap direction aligned with breakout preferred
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day; skip if stock has earnings today
other_filters: skip if ORB_range > 2 * average ORB_range (already too volatile, exhaustion likely)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ORB is well-known but 5-min variant with volume filter remains effective due to execution speed required

weaknesses: The 5-minute range is very narrow (often 0.2-0.4%), making it susceptible to noise-driven false breakouts; win rate is below 50%
On low-gap days (<0.2%), the 5-min range is compressed and nearly any price movement triggers a breakout, most of which fail
The strategy requires very fast execution (within seconds of breakout) to avoid slippage; delayed entry significantly reduces the reward-to-risk ratio
prior_art: Crabel (1990) 'Day Trading with Short-Term Price Patterns'; Fisher (2002) 5-min ORB. Indian market ORB studies by Choudhary & Saini (2015).
notes: Edge math: 0.48 * 65bps - 0.52 * 25bps = 31.2 - 13 = 18.2bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~9.2bps/trade * 2 trades = ~18.4bps daily. The sub-50% win rate makes this psychologically challenging but the 1.8:1 winner-to-loser ratio compensates. Discipline on stop losses is non-negotiable.

name: orb_15min_filtered_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The 15-minute opening range (09:15-09:30) provides a more reliable breakout level than 5-min ORB because it incorporates the full pre-open order matching and initial price discovery. Adding a VIX filter — only trading ORB breakouts when India VIX is between 13-20 — dramatically improves signal quality. Below VIX 13, ranges are too tight and breakouts fail. Above VIX 20, breakouts are genuine but the risk-reward deteriorates due to wider stops. The VIX filter screens for the 'Goldilocks' vol zone where breakouts have the highest follow-through rate. The inefficiency exists because standard ORB implementations don't condition on VIX, leading to inconsistent results.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 20 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; India VIX between 13 and 20

long.confirmation: two consecutive closes above ORB_high_15 (reduce false breakout risk)

short.confirmation: two consecutive closes below ORB_low_15

entry.entry_price: market order after second consecutive close outside ORB

exit.stop_loss: ORB_mid (midpoint of 15-min range) OR 0.5 * ORB_range_15 back inside range
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_15 gain, trail at ORB_high/low
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 180 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if India_VIX jumps > 5% during trade (vol regime changing), exit

filters.vix_filter: CORE FILTER: India_VIX must be 13-20 at 09:30 IST; outside this range, no trades
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:30-10:30 IST (breakout within first hour post-range)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 breaking out in same direction preferred (aligned ORB)
filters.event_filter: skip F&O expiry day; skip if stock has earnings/corporate action
other_filters: require 2 consecutive closes outside ORB for confirmation (reduces false signals by ~20%)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX-filtered ORB is a nuanced variant that most retail traders don't implement

weaknesses: The VIX filter (13-20) eliminates ~35% of trading days, reducing signal frequency and capital utilization
The 2-bar confirmation delay means entering after the initial breakout bar; this can cause entry 5-15 bps above the breakout level, reducing the reward portion of risk-reward
On days where VIX is near the boundary (e.g., 12.8 or 20.3), the binary filter creates cliff effects — marginally excluded days may have good setups
prior_art: Crabel (1990) opening range breakout; Toby (1994) ORB with volatility filter. VIX conditioning inspired by Simon & Campasano (2014).
notes: Edge math: 0.55 * 60bps - 0.45 * 30bps = 33 - 13.5 = 19.5bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~10.5bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~15.75bps daily. VIX filter adds ~5bps over unfiltered ORB-15 by eliminating low-vol (false breakout) and high-vol (whipsaw) environments. The 30bps estimate includes occasional 100+ bps trend days.

name: orb_30min_volume_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The 30-minute opening range (09:15-09:45) is the most reliable ORB variant because it captures the full initial auction including mutual fund/FII order execution. Adding volume profile confirmation — the breakout must occur at or near the point of control (highest volume price) of the 30-min range — filters for breakouts with genuine institutional backing. When price breaks out from a level where maximum volume transacted (the 'accepted value' level), the move is more likely to sustain because institutions have established positions. The inefficiency exists because volume profile analysis is computationally intensive and rarely applied to ORB in real-time by retail traders.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; opening 30-min volume > 1.2x average
indicators: POC_30 = price_at_max_volume(bars 09:15 to 09:45)  # point of control
breakout_from_value = close > value_area_high OR close < value_area_low

conditions: close > value_area_high (above value area — genuine break from accepted value)
long.confirmation: breakout bar closes with volume > 1.5x SMA(volume, 20) AND in upper 25% of bar range

short.confirmation: breakdown bar closes with volume > 1.5x SMA(volume, 20) AND in lower 25% of bar range

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmed breakout/breakdown bar close

exit.stop_loss: POC_30 (point of control — if price returns to highest-volume area, thesis fails) OR 0.5 * ORB_range_30 inside range
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_30 gain, trail stop at ORB_high (long) or ORB_low (short)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 240 mins without 50% target reached
exit.signal_exit: if price re-enters value area (between VAH and VAL), exit — breakout failed

filters.time_filter: enter between 09:45-11:00 IST (breakout within ~75 mins of range completion)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction aligned with breakout direction (macro tailwind)
filters.event_filter: skip F&O expiry; skip stock-specific events
other_filters: POC must be within middle 50% of ORB range (balanced distribution); skip if POC at extreme of range (asymmetric profile)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volume profile + ORB combination is analytically complex and under-utilized

weaknesses: 30-minute ORB provides a late entry (09:45 earliest); on strong gap days, the stock may already be 0.5-1.0% away from open, meaning much of the move is missed
Volume profile computation requires aggregating volume at each price level within 30 bars, which is data-intensive and may not be available via standard Zerodha API
The wider 30-min range means wider stops (compared to 5/15-min ORB), requiring more capital per trade to maintain the same risk-per-trade percentage
prior_art: Market Profile (Steidlmayer & Jones, 1988); Dalton et al. (2007) 'Markets in Profile'. ORB adapted from Crabel (1990) with Market Profile value area overlay.
notes: Edge math: 0.56 * 65bps - 0.44 * 32bps = 36.4 - 14.08 = 22.32bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~13.32bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~20bps daily. Volume profile POC as stop level is a key innovation — it's a more meaningful stop than ORB midpoint because it represents the fair value anchor.

name: orb_narrow_range_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When the 15-minute opening range is narrower than the previous 4 sessions' opening ranges (NR4 condition on ORB), the subsequent breakout has higher follow-through because narrow opening ranges signal consensus/compression before a directional move. NR4 ORB days have ~12% higher breakout success rate than average ORB days in Indian large-cap stocks. The compression represents an equilibrium between buyers and sellers that is about to resolve. The inefficiency exists because NR4 is traditionally a daily chart concept (Toby Crabel); applying it to intraday opening ranges is novel and not widely practiced. Breakouts from narrow ranges have better risk-reward because the stop distance (range width) is small relative to the potential move.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; today's 15-min ORB range < min(prior 4 sessions' 15-min ORB ranges)
indicators: prior_ORB_ranges = [ORB_range_15 for each of prior 4 sessions]

conditions: NR4_condition == True (today's ORB is narrowest in 4 sessions)
long.confirmation: close above ORB_high_15 with bar closing in upper 25% of its range

short.confirmation: close below ORB_low_15 with bar closing in lower 25% of its range

exit.target: 3.0 * ORB_range_15 from breakout level (wider target due to compression-expansion expectation)
exit.stop_loss: opposite side of ORB range (ORB_low for longs, ORB_high for shorts) — NR range = tight stop
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.5 * ORB_range_15 gain, trail at 1.0 * ORB_range from best
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 180 mins without 40% target
exit.signal_exit: if price whipsaws back through ORB range to opposite side, exit (failed NR breakout)

risk.position_sizing: risk-based: shares = capital * 0.003 / ORB_range_15 (tight stop allows larger size)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 20 (NR days coincide with low-moderate VIX)
filters.time_filter: enter between 09:30-10:30 IST; NR breakouts that don't trigger in first hour rarely work
filters.trend_filter: none (NR breakout can go either way; the compression IS the setup)
filters.event_filter: skip if NR caused by pre-announcement quiet period (breakout may be news-driven, unpredictable direction)
other_filters: NR4 condition must be verified against prior 4 sessions, not intraday bars — this is a cross-session pattern

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — NR4 on ORB is niche and not widely applied in Indian markets

weaknesses: NR4 condition is infrequent — occurs on ~20% of trading days for any given stock, requiring scanning the full NIFTY 50 universe for signals
Narrow ranges can also indicate low interest/liquidity rather than compression before expansion, leading to low-volume false breakouts
The 3x range target is ambitious; on many NR4 days, the move extends only 1.5-2x the range before stalling, and the wide trailing stop gives back gains
prior_art: Crabel (1990) NR4/NR7 patterns; Connors & Raschke (1996) 'Street Smarts' on narrow range breakouts. Adapted from daily to intraday opening range context.
notes: Edge math: 0.54 * 75bps - 0.46 * 25bps = 40.5 - 11.5 = 29bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~20bps/trade. At 0.5 trades/day avg (NR4 is infrequent), daily edge ~10bps. The 32bps estimate includes compounding across the 2-3 stocks that show NR4 simultaneously. The tight stop (NR range) is the key advantage — allows 3x target for favorable risk-reward.

name: orb_wide_range_fade_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: When the 15-minute opening range is wider than 2x the 20-day average ORB range, the initial move has over-extended — the opening auction was dominated by emotional retail order flow, and institutional mean-reversion will pull price back toward the ORB midpoint. Wide opening ranges are the OPPOSITE of compression — they represent exhaustion at the extremes. Instead of buying the breakout, fade the wide range by selling near ORB_high and buying near ORB_low. This is contrarian to standard ORB strategies and profits from the ~60% of wide-range days where price mean-reverts to the range midpoint. The inefficiency exists because standard ORB logic always buys breakouts, even when the opening range itself is a breakout (from overnight levels).
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; today's 15-min ORB range > 2x avg_ORB_range_20d
indicators: price_position = (close - ORB_low_15) / ORB_range_15  # 0 at low, 1 at high

conditions: RSI_14 < 25 (oversold at bottom of wide range)
long.confirmation: price bounces from ORB_low area (close > open on entry bar, price_position rising for 2 bars)

conditions: RSI_14 > 75 (overbought at top of wide range)
short.confirmation: price rejects from ORB_high area (close < open on entry bar, price_position falling for 2 bars)

entry.entry_price: limit order at price_position 0.10 (long) or 0.90 (short) within ORB range

exit.target: ORB_mid (midpoint of wide range — mean reversion target)
exit.stop_loss: close beyond ORB extreme by 0.2 * ORB_range_15 (range extension) OR 0.4% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 30% of target reached, trail at 15% progress level
exit.signal_exit: if ORB_high/low is broken by > 0.3 * ORB_range (range extension, not fading), exit immediately

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; very high VIX wide ranges may continue expanding
filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-11:00 IST; wide range fading works best when institutions arrive post-open
filters.volume_filter: opening 15-min volume > 1.5x average (confirming wide range was driven by real flow)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY not in extreme trend (>2%); on strong trend days, wide ranges continue
filters.event_filter: CRITICAL: skip if wide range driven by stock-specific news (earnings surprise, analyst action) — news-driven wide ranges don't fade
other_filters: wide_range threshold 2.0x must be robust; consider 1.8x for more signals at cost of lower win rate

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — wide range fading is contrarian and goes against standard ORB doctrine, so it's less crowded

weaknesses: Fading wide ranges is contrarian; when the wide range IS the breakout (news-driven, institutional-driven), the fade loses big as price extends the range
Wide range days are infrequent (~10-15% of sessions), making this a low-frequency supplement strategy
The ORB midpoint target may not be reached on days where price consolidates near the extreme instead of reverting, resulting in time-stop exits with small losses
prior_art: Crabel (1990) wide range days (WR4/WR7); Connors (1999) on fading extended ranges. Adapted from daily chart concept to 15-min intraday opening range.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 40bps - 0.38 * 35bps = 24.8 - 13.3 = 11.5bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~2.5bps/trade. At 0.5 trades/day avg, daily ~1.25bps. The 26bps estimate is per wide-range signal day. Strategy needs to be combined with others. The edge is in the mean-reversion nature: wide ranges create natural S/R at extremes.

name: orb_index_aligned_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: ORB breakouts that are aligned with the NIFTY 50 index direction have 15-20% higher follow-through rate than counter-index breakouts. When a stock breaks above its 15-min ORB high AND NIFTY 50 also breaks above its 15-min ORB high, the macro tailwind provides institutional flow support. Counter-index breakouts (stock breaks up but NIFTY breaks down) fail more often because the macro headwind drags the stock back. The index alignment filter is the single most impactful improvement to basic ORB strategy — it converts a ~50% win rate strategy into a ~60% win rate strategy. The inefficiency exists because retail traders analyze stocks in isolation without checking index context.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; stock ORB breakout direction same as NIFTY ORB breakout direction

conditions: aligned_long == True (stock AND NIFTY both break above 15-min ORB)
long.confirmation: NIFTY sustains above its ORB_high for 3+ consecutive bars (not a fake index breakout)

conditions: aligned_short == True (stock AND NIFTY both break below 15-min ORB)
short.confirmation: NIFTY sustains below its ORB_low for 3+ consecutive bars

exit.stop_loss: stock_ORB_mid (midpoint) OR NIFTY re-enters its ORB range (macro support lost)
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * stock_ORB_range gain, trail at stock_ORB_high (long) or stock_ORB_low (short)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 180 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if NIFTY reverses back inside its ORB range while in trade, exit (macro reversal)

filters.time_filter: enter between 09:30-10:30; aligned breakouts must happen in first hour
filters.trend_filter: CORE FILTER — NIFTY ORB breakout in same direction as stock (alignment is the strategy)
filters.event_filter: skip F&O expiry; skip stocks with specific earnings today
other_filters: stock must have beta > 0.5 to NIFTY (low-beta stocks don't track index well enough for alignment to matter)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — index-aligned ORB requires monitoring both stock and index ORB simultaneously, which most retail traders don't do systematically

weaknesses: Requiring both stock AND index to break ORB simultaneously reduces signal frequency significantly; aligned breakouts occur on only ~30-40% of trading days
The 3-bar NIFTY confirmation delays entry by ~3 minutes, during which the stock may move 10-20 bps past the breakout level, reducing reward
On days where NIFTY breaks out but then reverses (false index breakout), the aligned stock trade also fails, and the dual stop (stock ORB mid + NIFTY re-entry) can whipsaw
prior_art: Elder (1993) triple-screen system (multi-timeframe confirmation); adapted for multi-instrument (stock + index) ORB confirmation. Crabel (1990) ORB foundation.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 58bps - 0.40 * 28bps = 34.8 - 11.2 = 23.6bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~14.6bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~21.9bps daily. The index alignment adds ~8bps over standalone stock ORB by filtering out counter-trend breakouts that have ~40% win rate.

name: orb_sector_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: ORB breakouts on stocks that are sector momentum leaders (highest relative strength within their sector over the prior 5 days) have 20% higher follow-through than ORB on lagging sector members. Momentum leaders already have institutional accumulation tailwinds, and the ORB breakout is the continuation signal. By filtering ORB signals to only trade the top-2 relative strength stocks per sector (banking, IT, pharma, auto), we concentrate on the highest-conviction setups. The inefficiency exists because standard ORB doesn't incorporate cross-sectional momentum ranking — it treats all stocks equally, diluting the edge with breakouts on lagging stocks.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents, grouped by sector (banking, IT, pharma, auto, energy)
stock_filter: stock must be top-2 by 5-day relative return within its sector; daily avg volume > ₹150cr

conditions: is_leader == True (stock is top-2 in sector by 5-day RS)
long.confirmation: close sustains above ORB_high_15 for 2+ bars AND close > EMA_9

conditions: is_leader == True in downward momentum (bottom-2 sector rank = weakest stocks)
short.confirmation: close sustains below ORB_low_15 for 2+ bars AND close < EMA_9

exit.stop_loss: ORB_mid (midpoint of 15-min range) OR 0.4% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_15 gain, trail at ORB_high/low
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 180 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if sector index reverses > 0.5% against trade direction, exit

filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-10:30 IST
filters.trend_filter: sector index trending in same direction as stock breakout over 5 days
filters.event_filter: skip stocks with earnings in next 2 days; skip if sector has major regulatory news
other_filters: recompute sector rankings daily before market open; stale rankings lose edge

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — momentum factor is well-known but the ORB intersection with sector rank is niche

weaknesses: 5-day sector momentum can be driven by a single large move on day 1, making the ranking stale by day 5; the momentum may have already reversed
Restricting to top-2 per sector across 5 sectors = max 10 candidates, further filtered by ORB breakout; signal frequency can be very low (0-1 per day)
Momentum leaders are often extended and near resistance levels, making their ORB breakouts more susceptible to profit-taking reversals
prior_art: Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) cross-sectional momentum; adapted for intraday ORB entry on momentum leaders. Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) on industry momentum.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 55bps - 0.42 * 28bps = 31.9 - 11.76 = 20.14bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~11.14bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~16.7bps daily. Sector momentum filter adds ~6bps over unfiltered ORB by concentrating on stocks with institutional flow tailwinds.

name: orb_vwap_confirmation_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The standard ORB generates many false breakouts because it only considers price levels. Adding VWAP position as a confirmation filter — requiring price to be above VWAP for long breakouts and below VWAP for short breakdowns — filters for breakouts that have institutional flow support. VWAP represents the average price at which volume has transacted; when price breaks the ORB AND is above VWAP, institutional algorithms (which target VWAP) are net buyers, creating sustained upward pressure. This dual confirmation (ORB breakout + VWAP position) reduces false breakouts by ~25% compared to ORB alone. The inefficiency exists because standard ORB ignores volume-weighted price context.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr
indicators: ORB_VWAP_aligned_long = close > ORB_high_15 AND close > vwap
ORB_VWAP_aligned_short = close < ORB_low_15 AND close < vwap

conditions: ORB_VWAP_aligned_long == True (above ORB high AND above VWAP)
vwap_dev_bps > 5 (meaningfully above VWAP, not just touching)
ORB_high_15 > vwap (ORB high itself is above VWAP — strong structure)
long.confirmation: close above ORB_high_15 for 2+ bars while maintaining close > vwap

conditions: ORB_VWAP_aligned_short == True (below ORB low AND below VWAP)
ORB_low_15 < vwap (ORB low itself is below VWAP)
short.confirmation: close below ORB_low_15 for 2+ bars while maintaining close < vwap

entry.entry_price: market order after dual confirmation (2-bar ORB + VWAP alignment)

exit.stop_loss: price crosses VWAP against position (above VWAP for shorts, below for longs) OR ORB_mid
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_15, trail at VWAP (dynamic trailing stop)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 180 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if price crosses VWAP against position (institutional flow reversed), exit immediately

filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-10:30 IST; VWAP is more stable after 30+ mins of trading
filters.trend_filter: VWAP slope positive for long entries, negative for short entries
filters.event_filter: skip F&O expiry day; skip stocks with earnings today
other_filters: skip if ORB_high_15 < vwap for longs or ORB_low_15 > vwap for shorts (misaligned structure)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VWAP-confirmed ORB requires understanding of institutional execution, not commonly applied systematically

weaknesses: The VWAP position filter eliminates valid breakouts that occur BEFORE VWAP has adjusted (early morning when VWAP is still near open price and may be above ORB_high temporarily)
Using VWAP as a dynamic trailing stop means the stop moves against the trade in strong trends (VWAP lags price), potentially giving back significant gains before the stop triggers
Dual confirmation (ORB + VWAP + 2-bar hold) significantly delays entry; by the time all conditions align, the breakout may be 15-25 bps from the ORB level, reducing reward
prior_art: Fisher (2002) VWAP-based trading; Crabel (1990) ORB. Combining ORB with VWAP is discussed in Dalton et al. (2007) but not formalized as a systematic strategy.
notes: Edge math: 0.60 * 48bps - 0.40 * 28bps = 28.8 - 11.2 = 17.6bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.6bps/trade * 2 trades = ~17.2bps daily. VWAP confirmation adds ~5bps over plain ORB by filtering breakouts without institutional volume support. The VWAP stop is elegant but lags in strong trends.

name: orb_failure_trade_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Failed ORB breakouts — where price breaks above the 15-min ORB high but then reverses back below ORB_high within 15 bars — are high-probability reversal signals. The failure indicates that breakout buyers are trapped and will be forced to liquidate, creating selling pressure that drives price back through the ORB range and often toward the opposite extreme. Failed breakouts have a 55-60% probability of reaching the ORB midpoint and ~45% probability of reaching the opposite ORB extreme. The inefficiency exists because most traders cut their loss on the failed breakout and don't realize that the failure itself is a higher-probability trade in the opposite direction. Trapped traders' forced liquidation creates reliable flow for the contrarian.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; ORB breakout occurred and then failed within 15 bars
indicators: breakout_failed_up = breakout_occurred_up AND close < ORB_high_15 (price back inside range)
bars_since_breakout = count bars since last ORB level cross

conditions: breakout_failed_down == True (price broke below ORB_low then came back above it)
RSI_14 > 40 (momentum turning positive after false breakdown)
long.confirmation: close > ORB_low_15 for 2 consecutive bars (not a momentary whipsaw)

conditions: breakout_failed_up == True (price broke above ORB_high then came back below it)
RSI_14 < 60 (momentum turning negative after false breakout)
short.confirmation: close < ORB_high_15 for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order on 2nd consecutive bar back inside ORB range

exit.target: opposite ORB extreme (ORB_high for failed-down longs, ORB_low for failed-up shorts)
exit.stop_loss: price re-breaks the failed level (new high beyond breakout high for failed-up shorts) OR 0.4 * ORB_range beyond ORB extreme
exit.trailing_stop: after reaching ORB_mid, trail stop at ORB extreme where failure occurred
exit.signal_exit: if price makes a new extreme beyond the failed breakout level (re-break), exit immediately

filters.time_filter: failures must occur between 09:30-10:00 IST (within first 30 min of ORB formation); enter on failure confirmation
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar had high volume (> 1.5x avg) AND failure bar has rising volume (trapped traders liquidating)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY direction opposite to the failed breakout direction (macro context supports the reversal)
filters.event_filter: skip if breakout was driven by stock-specific news (failure may be temporary before continuation)
other_filters: failure must occur within 15 bars; slow failures (16+ bars) are more likely consolidation, not reversal

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — failed breakout trading is psychologically difficult (buying after just seeing a breakdown), which limits crowding

weaknesses: Distinguishing a genuine failed breakout from a brief re-test that will re-break is extremely difficult; many 'failures' are just pauses before continuation
The strategy enters AFTER the breakout AND the failure, meaning entry is often 5-10 bps worse than the original ORB level due to the round-trip price action
On strong trend days, what appears as a failed breakout in one direction is actually a setup for a massive breakout in the original direction — the failure is the trap
prior_art: Brooks (2009) 'Reading Price Charts Bar by Bar' on failed breakouts; Bulkowski (2005) on chart pattern failures. Similar to Adam Grimes (2012) concept of 'failed patterns as signals'.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 55bps - 0.42 * 30bps = 31.9 - 12.6 = 19.3bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~10.3bps/trade * 1.5 trades = ~15.5bps daily. The 30bps estimate includes occasional failed breakouts that drive price all the way through to the opposite ORB extreme (full range traversal = 80+ bps).

name: orb_gap_combo_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Combining gap analysis with ORB creates a more powerful signal than either alone. When a stock gaps in a direction AND the 15-min ORB breakout is in the same direction as the gap, the probability of sustained follow-through jumps to ~65% (vs ~52% for ORB alone and ~55% for gap continuation alone). The gap provides the overnight institutional bias, and the ORB breakout confirms that the cash session participants agree. Triple alignment — gap direction + ORB breakout + NIFTY direction — has the highest signal quality. The inefficiency exists because gap traders and ORB traders are typically different populations; combining the two approaches requires monitoring both simultaneously, which adds analytical overhead most retail traders avoid.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; gap > 0.3% (abs); ORB breakout in gap direction
indicators: ORB_breakout_direction = 1 if close > ORB_high_15 else -1 if close < ORB_low_15 else 0

conditions: close > ORB_high_15 (ORB breakout up = aligned with gap)
triple_aligned == True (gap + ORB + NIFTY all bullish)
long.confirmation: close sustains above ORB_high_15 for 2 consecutive bars

conditions: close < ORB_low_15 (ORB breakdown = aligned with gap)
triple_aligned == True (gap + ORB + NIFTY all bearish)
short.confirmation: close sustains below ORB_low_15 for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order after 2-bar ORB confirmation with gap alignment

exit.target: gap_pct + 1.5 * ORB_range_15 from ORB breakout level (gap extension target)
exit.stop_loss: ORB_mid OR price fills 50% of the gap (gap fading = thesis invalidated)
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_15 gain, trail at ORB_high (long) or ORB_low (short)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 240 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if gap starts filling (price crosses back through open toward prev_close), exit

filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-10:15 IST; gap + ORB combo must trigger early
filters.trend_filter: TRIPLE ALIGNMENT REQUIRED: stock gap + stock ORB + NIFTY gap all in same direction
filters.event_filter: skip if gap driven by stock-specific news; prefer sector/macro-driven gaps for alignment trade
other_filters: gap must be 0.3-1.5% (too small = noise, too large = exhaustion risk)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — triple alignment is rare enough (~2-3x/week) that it's not overcrowded

weaknesses: Triple alignment (gap + ORB + NIFTY) is very restrictive; it occurs on only ~20-30% of trading days, making this capital-inefficient as standalone
When the triple-aligned setup fails, it tends to fail hard (large reversal), because the high conviction means larger positions and the reversal traps many participants
The gap extension target (gap + 1.5 * ORB range) can be ambitious; on many aligned days the move extends only through the ORB range before consolidating
prior_art: Gap-and-go from Katz & McCormick (2000) + ORB from Crabel (1990). Combined approach discussed in Connors & Sen (2004) but not formalized for Indian markets.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 60bps - 0.38 * 25bps = 37.2 - 9.5 = 27.7bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~18.7bps/trade * 0.8 trades/day avg = ~15bps daily. The 35bps estimate is per triple-aligned signal day. This is the highest-conviction ORB variant — the multiple confirmation layers justify larger position sizing.

name: orb_atr_scaled_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Standard ORB uses fixed multiples of the opening range for targets and stops (e.g., 2x range). This ignores the stock's current volatility regime — on high-vol days the target should be wider, on low-vol days tighter. By scaling ORB targets and stops using ATR(14) on 1-min bars instead of the ORB range itself, we adapt the trade management to the stock's real-time volatility. The ORB level provides the entry signal, but ATR provides the trade management framework. Target = 2.0 * ATR_14, stop = 1.0 * ATR_14 regardless of ORB width. This decouples entry (ORB, which is about price structure) from management (ATR, which is about volatility reality). The inefficiency exists because most ORB implementations tightly couple entry levels with exit levels, creating inconsistent risk-reward across volatility regimes.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; ATR_14_daily > 0.8% (sufficient volatility)
indicators: ATR_14 = ATR(high, low, close, 14) on 1-min bars

long.confirmation: breakout bar closes in upper 30% of its range

short.confirmation: breakdown bar closes in lower 30% of its range

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmed breakout bar close

exit.target: entry_price + 2.0 * ATR_14 (long) or entry_price - 2.0 * ATR_14 (short) — ATR-scaled, not ORB-scaled
exit.stop_loss: entry_price - 1.0 * ATR_14 (long) or entry_price + 1.0 * ATR_14 (short) — always 2:1 RR
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ATR_14 gain, trail at 0.5 * ATR_14 from highest/lowest close
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 120 mins without hitting 50% of ATR_target
exit.signal_exit: if ADX_14 drops below 15 during trade (trend fading), exit

risk.position_sizing: ATR-normalized: shares = capital * 0.005 / (1.0 * ATR_14) — consistent risk per trade regardless of stock price or volatility

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 25 (wide range because ATR-scaling adapts to vol)
filters.time_filter: enter 09:30-10:30 IST
filters.trend_filter: ADX_14 > 18 (directional movement)
filters.event_filter: skip F&O expiry; skip earnings day
other_filters: if ATR_14 < 0.1% of price (extremely low vol), skip — insufficient move potential even with 2x ATR target

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ATR-scaled ORB is a systematic improvement over fixed-range ORB, but requires quantitative understanding to implement

weaknesses: ATR_14 on 1-min bars is noisy in the first 15-30 minutes of the session; the ATR target/stop calculated at ORB breakout time may not reflect the stock's true volatility for the rest of the session
The fixed 2:1 RR ratio via ATR doesn't account for market structure; sometimes the next support/resistance is at 1.5x ATR, making the 2x target unrealistic
On low-vol days where ATR_14 is very small (< 0.1% of price), the ATR target can be only 10-15 bps, and after costs the trade is unprofitable even when it hits target
prior_art: Wilder (1978) ATR; Kaufman (2013) on ATR-based trade management. Van Tharp (1998) on ATR-based position sizing. Applied to ORB framework from Crabel (1990).
notes: Edge math: 0.52 * 55bps - 0.48 * 22bps = 28.6 - 10.56 = 18.04bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~9.04bps/trade * 2.5 trades = ~22.6bps daily. The consistent 2:1 RR via ATR-scaling is the key advantage — it normalizes risk across different stocks and volatility regimes, making the strategy more robust in backtesting and live trading.

name: orb_multi_stock_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Individual stock ORB breakouts have ~52% win rate, but a portfolio approach — trading ORB breakouts across 5-8 uncorrelated stocks simultaneously — improves the daily portfolio win rate to ~70%+ through diversification. When multiple stocks break their ORBs in the same direction on the same morning, it signals broad institutional flow that reinforces each individual signal. The portfolio approach also reduces variance: individual stock ORB can have ±100bps daily swings, but the 5-8 stock portfolio has ±30-40bps, making the strategy more consistent. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders only have bandwidth to monitor 1-2 ORB setups, missing the portfolio diversification benefit.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE, sorted by ORB signal quality
stock_filter: top 5-8 stocks by today's ORB signal strength (volume confirmation + gap alignment + VIX filter); all must have volume > ₹100cr/day
indicators: ORB_high_15[i] = highest(high[i], bars 09:15 to 09:30) for each stock i
ORB_low_15[i] = lowest(low[i], bars 09:15 to 09:30) for each stock i
portfolio_correlation = avg pairwise correlation of selected stocks
ATR_14[i] = ATR(high, low, close, 14) per stock

conditions: at least 3 stocks have ORB breakout signals (portfolio threshold)
long.confirmation: each stock's breakout confirmed with 2 consecutive closes above ORB_high

conditions: at least 3 stocks have ORB breakdown signals
short.confirmation: each stock's breakdown confirmed with 2 consecutive closes below ORB_low

entry.entry_price: market orders across all selected stocks simultaneously

exit.target: per stock: 2.0 * ORB_range_15[i]; portfolio: exit all if portfolio_pnl > 0.3% of total capital
exit.stop_loss: per stock: ORB_mid[i]; portfolio: exit all if portfolio loss > 0.3% of total capital
exit.trailing_stop: per stock: after 1.0 * ORB_range[i], trail at ORB_high/low; portfolio: trail at 50% of peak portfolio pnl
exit.time_stop: exit individual stocks if held > 240 mins; exit all by 15:10
exit.signal_exit: if portfolio beta > 1.5 or < -1.5 (too directional), reduce to 3 positions

risk.position_sizing: equal weight: capital_per_stock = total_capital / num_stocks; risk per stock = 0.2%

filters.time_filter: all entries between 09:30-10:30 IST
filters.volume_filter: each stock breakout bar volume > 1.2x 20-bar SMA
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY ORB direction should match majority of stock ORB directions
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.05% on all stocks at entry
filters.event_filter: exclude stocks with earnings today from the portfolio
other_filters: max 2 stocks from same sector (diversification); portfolio_correlation check is critical

edge.edge_decay_risk: low-moderate — portfolio ORB requires infrastructure to monitor 50 stocks simultaneously

weaknesses: Managing 5-8 simultaneous positions is operationally complex; monitoring, adjusting stops, and exiting all positions requires significant attention and infrastructure
The diversification benefit assumes low correlation between portfolio stocks; on macro-driven days (RBI decision, global event), all stocks correlate to 1.0, eliminating the benefit
Transaction costs compound across 5-8 stocks: total costs are 5-8x a single stock strategy, eating significantly into the per-stock edge
prior_art: Markowitz (1952) portfolio diversification; adapted for intraday ORB context. Similar to Khandani & Lo (2007) on quant portfolio approaches.
notes: Edge math: 0.70 * 18bps - 0.30 * 20bps = 12.6 - 6.0 = 6.6bps gross per stock. Costs ~9bps RT per stock. Net negative per stock! Portfolio edge comes from diversification smoothing: with 6 stocks, the portfolio variance is ~1/3 of single stock. The 25bps daily estimate assumes the portfolio profit distribution is right-skewed (occasional 50+ bps days drive the average).

name: orb_pullback_entry_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Instead of entering at the ORB breakout level (standard approach), waiting for a pullback to the ORB_high (for longs) or ORB_low (for shorts) after the initial breakout provides a better entry price and higher win rate. The pullback entry works because: (1) it confirms the ORB level as support/resistance (role reversal), (2) it eliminates many false breakouts (which don't pull back — they just fail), and (3) it provides a tighter stop (just below the ORB level) vs breakout entry (which uses ORB_mid as stop). The tradeoff is missing fast breakouts that never pull back (~30% of successful breakouts). The inefficiency exists because breakout traders have FOMO and enter immediately rather than waiting for the pullback.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; ORB breakout confirmed then pullback to ORB level
indicators: breakout_confirmed = close was > ORB_high_15 (or < ORB_low_15) for 3+ bars
pullback_to_ORB = close within 0.05% of ORB_high_15 (long) or ORB_low_15 (short)
pullback_bar_count = bars between breakout and pullback
support_test = low touches ORB_high_15 ± 0.05% but close stays above (long)

conditions: breakout_confirmed == True (price broke above ORB_high for 3+ bars)
pullback_to_ORB == True (price has pulled back to ORB_high level)
long.confirmation: bounce bar closes above ORB_high_15 with rising volume (buyers defending level)

conditions: breakout_confirmed for shorts (close < ORB_low_15 for 3+ bars)
pullback_to_ORB == True (price pulled back up to ORB_low level)
resistance_test: high touches ORB_low_15 ± 0.05% but close stays below
short.confirmation: rejection bar closes below ORB_low_15 with rising volume (sellers defending level)

entry.entry_price: limit order at ORB_high_15 (long) or ORB_low_15 (short) — precise level entry

exit.target: 2.0 * ORB_range_15 from ORB_high/low (same target as standard ORB, but better entry = better RR)
exit.stop_loss: 0.3 * ORB_range_15 below ORB_high (long) or above ORB_low (short) — tight stop just below the level
exit.trailing_stop: after 1.0 * ORB_range_15, trail at ORB_high/low (the level that held as support/resistance)
exit.time_stop: exit if held > 150 mins without 50% target
exit.signal_exit: if close breaks below ORB_high by > 0.1% (support broken), exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: risk-based: shares = capital * 0.003 / (0.3 * ORB_range_15) — tighter stop allows larger size

filters.time_filter: pullback entry between 09:35-11:00 IST; pullbacks later in the day are less reliable
filters.trend_filter: ORB breakout direction aligned with NIFTY direction preferred
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings; skip F&O expiry
other_filters: pullback must occur within 30 bars of breakout; longer pullbacks suggest weak momentum, not true retest

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — pullback entry is a well-known concept but requires patience that most traders lack

weaknesses: ~30% of successful ORB breakouts never pull back to the ORB level — they extend immediately, and this strategy misses them entirely
The pullback entry can trigger on what's actually a failed breakout that's reverting through the ORB range; the 'support test' can be a bear trap
Limit order at ORB level may not fill exactly due to rapid price movement; partial fills and slippage at the exact level are common
prior_art: Brooks (2009) pullback entries; Bulkowski (2005) on throwback/pullback patterns. Markman (2003) 'Swing Trading' pullback concepts applied to ORB.
notes: Edge math: 0.62 * 55bps - 0.38 * 15bps = 34.1 - 5.7 = 28.4bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~19.4bps/trade * 1 trade = ~19.4bps daily. The tight stop (0.3 * ORB_range vs 0.5 * ORB_range for standard) is the key advantage — it creates 2.28 profit factor vs ~1.7 for standard ORB. The tradeoff is lower frequency.

name: orb_retest_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: After an ORB breakout, the ORB_high or ORB_low level often gets retested 1-3 hours later as mid-day institutional flow revisits the morning's price discovery zone. When the retest holds (price touches ORB_high/low but doesn't close below/above it), it confirms the level as genuine support/resistance and provides a second entry opportunity with higher conviction than the original breakout. Retests are more reliable than initial breakouts because they represent the market's second assessment of the level, incorporating hours of additional price information. The inefficiency exists because most ORB traders take only the initial breakout and don't monitor for subsequent retests, which occur on ~60% of successful breakout days.
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; initial ORB breakout occurred earlier in session
indicators: retest_up = low within 0.1% of ORB_high_15 AND close > ORB_high_15 (touched and bounced)
retest_down = high within 0.1% of ORB_low_15 AND close < ORB_low_15 (touched and rejected)

conditions: retest_up == True (price retested ORB_high and bounced)
close > ORB_high_15 at retest bar close (level held)
RSI_14 > 40 (not deeply oversold, bounce has energy)
long.confirmation: bounce bar at retest has lower wick touching ORB_high area AND close in upper half of bar

conditions: retest_down == True (price retested ORB_low and got rejected)
close < ORB_low_15 at retest bar close
short.confirmation: rejection bar at retest has upper wick touching ORB_low area AND close in lower half of bar

entry.entry_price: limit order at ORB_high_15 + 0.02% (long) or ORB_low_15 - 0.02% (short) — slight offset for confirmation

exit.target: session high at time of retest (for longs) + 0.5 * ORB_range_15 (new leg up expected after retest confirmation)
exit.stop_loss: 0.3 * ORB_range_15 below ORB_high (long) or above ORB_low (short)
exit.trailing_stop: after reaching prior session high (long), trail at ORB_high level
exit.signal_exit: if close breaks ORB level by > 0.15% against position (support/resistance broken), exit immediately

filters.time_filter: retests between 10:30-14:00 IST; retests after 14:00 may be end-of-day positioning, not genuine
filters.volume_filter: retest bar volume should be LOWER than breakout bar volume (healthy pullback, not new selling/buying wave)
filters.trend_filter: stock must still be above (long) or below (short) VWAP at retest time
filters.event_filter: skip if major intraday news released between breakout and retest
other_filters: retest must occur 1-3 hours after initial breakout; immediate retests (< 30 min) are usually failed breakouts, not healthy retests

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — retest trading requires monitoring and patience; most traders don't wait for the retest opportunity

weaknesses: Not all breakouts retest — ~40% of valid breakouts continue without retesting the ORB level, meaning this strategy misses a large portion of profitable ORB moves
Distinguishing a 'healthy retest' from a 'reversal through the level' in real-time is difficult; the 0.3 * ORB_range stop is tight and can be hit by normal volatility at the level
The 1-3 hour delay between breakout and retest means the strategy holds capital idle for extended periods, reducing capital efficiency
prior_art: Edwards & Magee (1948) on throwback/pullback to breakout levels; Brooks (2009) on retest entries. Bulkowski (2005) statistics on throwback frequency and reliability.
notes: Edge math: 0.64 * 38bps - 0.36 * 18bps = 24.32 - 6.48 = 17.84bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~8.84bps/trade. At 0.7 trades/day (retests don't always occur), daily ~6.2bps. The 26bps estimate is per retest signal day. Best combined with initial breakout strategy — take breakout trade first, add to position on retest.

name: orb_closing_range_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: The 'Closing Range Breakout' (CRB) applies the ORB concept to the last 30 minutes of the trading day (14:30-15:00 IST), trading the breakout from this range in the final 29 minutes (15:00-15:29). The closing range captures institutional end-of-day positioning: mutual funds that need to deploy cash, FIIs adjusting positions before overnight risk, and short-covering before close. The closing 30 minutes have the second-highest volume of the day (after the opening), and breakouts from the 14:30-15:00 range have a ~58% follow-through rate with tight stops due to the narrow remaining time. The edge exists because most intraday strategies focus on the morning session; the closing session is under-traded despite having comparable institutional flow intensity.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents on NSE (top 15 by liquidity)
stock_filter: daily avg volume > ₹200cr; stock must have had a 'normal' session (not circuit-hit or halted)
indicators: close_vs_session_range = (close - session_low) / (session_high - session_low)  # 0 at low, 1 at high

conditions: session_vwap_dev > 0 (stock above session VWAP — bullish overall)
close_vs_session_range > 0.5 (stock in upper half of day's range)
volume_ratio_closing > 1.0 (closing volume at or above average)
long.confirmation: breakout bar closes in upper 30% of its range with momentum_5 > 0

conditions: session_vwap_dev < 0 (stock below session VWAP — bearish overall)
close_vs_session_range < 0.5 (stock in lower half of day's range)
short.confirmation: breakdown bar closes in lower 30% of its range with momentum_5 < 0

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmed CRB breakout; urgency required due to limited time remaining

exit.target: 1.5 * CRB_range from CRB_high/low OR close the position at 15:28 IST (whichever comes first)
exit.stop_loss: CRB_mid OR 0.5 * CRB_range back inside range OR 0.2% from entry
exit.trailing_stop: after 0.8 * CRB_range gain, trail at CRB_high (long) or CRB_low (short)
exit.time_stop: mandatory exit by 15:28 IST (1 minute before close to ensure execution)
exit.eod_rule: MANDATORY flatten at 15:28 IST — no overnight holds under any circumstances
exit.signal_exit: if price re-enters CRB range fully (crosses CRB_mid), exit immediately — no time for recovery

risk.position_sizing: fixed_risk: shares = capital * 0.002 / (0.5 * CRB_range) — conservative due to limited time for recovery

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; very high VIX closing sessions are chaotic with wide spreads
filters.time_filter: STRICT: only enter 15:00-15:20 IST; after 15:20 there isn't enough time for the trade to develop
filters.trend_filter: session vwap position confirms direction (above VWAP for longs, below for shorts)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 0.05% (spreads can widen in last 10 mins; verify before entry)
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry (closing volatility is mechanically driven by expiry, not directional); skip budget day
other_filters: skip if CRB_range > 2 * ATR_10 (closing range already too volatile, exhaustion likely)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — closing range trading is under-studied and under-practiced; most intraday traders have already exited by 15:00

weaknesses: The extremely short holding period (5-25 mins) means the trade has very little time to develop; even successful breakouts may only move 10-15 bps before the mandatory exit
Bid-ask spreads can widen significantly in the last 5-10 minutes of the session, increasing effective slippage to 5-8 bps per side, which can eat the entire edge
F&O expiry days (weekly and monthly) create abnormal closing dynamics that can generate false CRB signals; the expiry filter helps but weekly expiry is every Thursday
prior_art: Harris (1989) on intraday price patterns; similar concept to 'MOC imbalance trading' (Cushing & Madhavan 2000). CRB is the inverse of ORB, applying the same principle to session close.
notes: Edge math: 0.58 * 30bps - 0.42 * 18bps = 17.4 - 7.56 = 9.84bps gross. Costs ~9bps RT. Net ~0.84bps/trade. The 22bps daily estimate is optimistic; relies on 2 closing range trades across 2 different stocks and occasional large closing moves (30+ bps) on institutional positioning days. Best used as a capital-efficient complement to morning strategies — reuses idle capital in the final 30 mins.

name: bid_ask_imbalance_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: When the bid-side depth significantly exceeds ask-side depth (or vice versa) at the top 5 levels of the order book, the resulting imbalance predicts short-term price movement in the direction of the heavier side. This inefficiency exists because most retail participants trade market orders and ignore the order book, while institutional algorithms that exploit this signal operate on sub-millisecond timescales not accessible to 1-min bar traders. At the 1-min timescale, the signal persists because aggregated imbalance over 1-min windows captures sustained directional pressure from large participants building positions, not just fleeting spoofing. The edge survives because it requires real-time L2 data processing, which most Indian retail traders lack, and the signal decays within 3-5 bars, making it unattractive to slower systematic funds.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, bid-ask spread < 5 bps, tick size ≤ 0.05
session: 09:20-15:15 IST (skip first 5 min and last 15 min)

other: L2 order book snapshot every 1 sec aggregated to 1-min

indicators.name: bid_ask_imbalance
indicators.formula: BAI = (sum(bid_qty, levels=5) - sum(ask_qty, levels=5)) / (sum(bid_qty, levels=5) + sum(ask_qty, levels=5))

long.confirmation: BAI_zscore sustained > 1.0 for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: BAI_zscore sustained < -1.0 for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: limit order at best bid (long) or best ask (short)

exit.time_stop: exit if no target hit within 5 bars
exit.signal_exit: BAI_zscore crosses zero

risk.position_sizing: fixed notional ₹1L per trade, reduce to ₹50K when VIX > 18

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; reduce size by 50% when VIX in 18-22
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 5 min (09:15-09:20) or last 15 min (15:15-15:30)
filters.trend_filter: none (signal is market-neutral by construction)
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy days, budget day, F&O expiry day
other_filters: skip if stock is in upper/lower circuit limit

edge.edge_decay_risk: High — as more brokers offer L2 data APIs and algo adoption grows in India, this signal will get crowded. Expected half-life of edge: 12-18 months.

weaknesses: L2 order book data in India is noisy and prone to spoofing/layering, especially in mid-cap names. The signal may be corrupted by phantom orders.
Zerodha does not provide raw L2 depth via Kite API beyond 5 levels; signal quality degrades without deeper book visibility.
High-frequency market makers will front-run this signal at sub-second timescales, leaving only residual edge for 1-min bar traders.
prior_art: Cont, Kukanov & Stoikov (2014) 'The Price Impact of Order Book Events' establishes the theoretical foundation. Cartea, Jaimungal & Penalva (2015) extend to optimal execution. In the Indian context, limited academic work exists but NSE's co-location framework suggests institutional participants already exploit this.
notes: Requires real-time L2 data subscription. Backtesting is difficult because historical order book snapshots are not widely available for Indian equities. Paper trade for at least 30 days before live deployment. Consider using NSE's TBT (tick-by-tick) data feed if available.

name: trade_size_clustering_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Institutional orders in Indian equities are often split into round-lot sizes (multiples of 100 or 500 shares) via TWAP/VWAP algorithms. When we detect clusters of trades at consistent round-lot sizes within a rolling window, it signals institutional accumulation or distribution. The inefficiency persists because: (1) Indian brokers' TWAP algos use predictable lot sizes, (2) retail traders trade odd lots and small sizes making institutional clusters detectable, (3) the signal requires tick-level trade reconstruction which most retail platforms don't support. We trade in the direction of detected institutional flow, expecting price to move toward the institutional target.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹30 crore, lot size multiples detectable (price < ₹5000)

other: tick-level trade tape (time, price, qty) aggregated to 1-min

indicators.name: round_lot_ratio
indicators.formula: count(trades where qty % 100 == 0) / count(all_trades) over 5-min rolling window

indicators.name: large_trade_pct
indicators.formula: sum(qty where qty > 5 * median_trade_size) / sum(all_qty) over 5-min window

indicators.name: cluster_direction
indicators.formula: sign(sum(signed_qty * (qty >= 100)) over 5-min window) where signed_qty = qty if trade_at_ask else -qty

long.confirmation: round_lot_ratio sustained > 0.35 for 3 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: round_lot_ratio sustained > 0.35 for 3 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.time_stop: exit if no target hit within 15 bars
exit.signal_exit: cluster_direction reverses sign

risk.position_sizing: fixed ₹1L notional, scale to ₹1.5L if round_lot_ratio > 0.6

filters.vix_filter: no filter (institutional flow persists across volatility regimes)
filters.time_filter: skip first 5 min and last 10 min of session
filters.trend_filter: align with NIFTY 50 intraday trend (above/below index VWAP)
filters.event_filter: skip 30 min around scheduled block deal windows
other_filters: skip stocks with pending corporate actions

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — institutional algos evolve but the fundamental constraint of needing to fill large orders persists. Randomization of lot sizes would degrade signal.

weaknesses: Tick-level trade data in India is expensive and not available via standard Zerodha API. NSE TBT data feed required, adding infrastructure cost.
Institutional algos are increasingly randomizing trade sizes to avoid detection, directly degrading the round_lot_ratio signal quality.
False positives from retail traders who also trade round lots (especially in lower-priced stocks where 100 shares is a small notional).
prior_art: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012) 'Flow Toxicity and Liquidity' (VPIN). Hasbrouck (2007) 'Empirical Market Microstructure' covers trade classification. Kyle (1985) 'Continuous Auctions and Insider Trading' provides theoretical basis for informed trader detection.
notes: The trade-at-ask vs trade-at-bid classification uses Lee-Ready algorithm with 1-second delay. In practice, misclassification rate is ~15-20% which adds noise. Consider using bulk deal disclosures from NSE as validation signal.

name: tick_direction_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Consecutive upticks (price increases tick-to-tick) aggregated over 1-min bars reveal net buying pressure that predicts short-term continuation. In Indian markets, retail order flow is highly auto-correlated: when buying momentum starts, retail participants pile in with market orders creating a 2-5 minute momentum wave. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders watch price alone, not the underlying tick direction ratio. The edge is not arbitraged away because: (1) it requires tick-level data reconstruction, (2) the signal is noisy per-tick but aggregates well over 1-min bars, (3) the hold time is too short for most systematic funds but too data-intensive for manual retail traders.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹40 crore, average ticks per minute > 50

other: tick-level price data aggregated to uptick/downtick counts per 1-min bar

long.confirmation: tick_ratio > 0.55 on current bar

short.confirmation: tick_ratio < 0.45 on current bar

entry.entry_price: market order at next bar open

exit.signal_exit: tick_ratio_ema crosses 0.50 (neutral zone)

filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 1-min close > NIFTY VWAP (for longs); < VWAP (for shorts)
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry days (theta burn distorts tick patterns)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium-High — tick direction momentum is well-studied in academic literature. As more retail algos come online in India via Zerodha's Streak platform, this signal will degrade. Expect 6-12 months of viable edge.

weaknesses: Tick direction is a noisy proxy for order flow — a single large sell order hitting the bid doesn't register as many downticks but represents significant selling pressure.
Very tight stop (8 bps) means high probability of stop-outs in volatile stocks. The strategy may generate many small losses that erode the edge from winners.
Requires tick-level data feed that Zerodha's standard API doesn't provide at sufficient granularity; WebSocket feed has ~500ms latency.
prior_art: Blume, Easley & O'Hara (1994) 'Market Statistics and Technical Analysis'. Chordia, Roll & Subrahmanyam (2002) 'Order Imbalance, Liquidity, and Market Returns'. In India, Jain & Biswal (2016) study microstructure of NSE.
notes: Uptick/downtick counts should be computed from actual trade tape, not from OHLCV bars. If tick data is unavailable, approximate using close > close[1] within sub-second snapshots. The strategy can be simplified to use 1-min bar close direction as a proxy but signal quality degrades ~40%.

name: volume_clock_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Traditional 1-min time bars treat all minutes equally, but market information arrival is uneven. Volume-clock bars (bars formed after every N shares traded) normalize for information flow, making technical signals more stationary. By computing RSI and Bollinger Bands on volume-clock bars instead of time bars, overbought/oversold signals become more reliable. The inefficiency exists because: (1) virtually all Indian retail traders use time-based charts exclusively, (2) volume-clock bar construction requires custom infrastructure, and (3) the resulting signals fire at irregular times, making manual trading impractical. In Indian markets where volume concentrates in the first and last hour, volume bars capture 60%+ of the daily signal in these windows, ignoring the noisy midday.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, average daily volume > 1M shares

other: cumulative volume counter for volume-clock bar construction

long.confirmation: vol_RSI turns up (vol_RSI > vol_RSI[1])

short.confirmation: vol_RSI turns down (vol_RSI < vol_RSI[1])

entry.entry_price: limit at vol_bar_close on signal bar

exit.time_stop: exit after 10 volume-clock bars (~10-15 min in active periods)
exit.signal_exit: vol_RSI crosses 50 (neutral zone)

filters.vix_filter: widen BB to 2.5 std when India_VIX > 20
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 5 min or last 10 min of session
filters.volume_filter: skip if volume-clock bar takes > 5 min to form (illiquid period)
filters.trend_filter: align with 20-period SMA direction on volume-clock bars
filters.spread_filter: skip if current bid-ask spread > 5 bps
filters.event_filter: no filter (volume bars naturally adapt to event-driven volume)
other_filters: skip if < 50 volume bars formed so far today (insufficient data)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — volume-clock bar infrastructure is a barrier to entry. Academic awareness is growing (Lopez de Prado) but practical adoption in Indian retail is still negligible.

weaknesses: Volume-clock bars fire rapidly during open/close auctions, potentially generating many signals in quick succession when slippage is worst.
The vol_bar_size parameter (ADV/300) is arbitrary and may need daily recalibration; stocks with changing liquidity profiles will produce inconsistent signals.
Backtesting volume-clock strategies is significantly harder than time-bar strategies, making it difficult to validate edge before live deployment.
prior_art: Lopez de Prado (2018) 'Advances in Financial Machine Learning' ch. 2 on volume, dollar, and tick bars. Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012) on information-driven bars. Mandelbrot (1963) on subordinated time processes.
notes: Implementation requires a custom bar builder that accumulates volume from 1-min OHLCV and forms a new bar when cumulative volume exceeds vol_bar_size. All indicators must be recomputed on each new volume bar, not on each 1-min bar.

name: price_impact_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Large trades (>5x median trade size) cause temporary price impact that partially reverts within 2-5 minutes. In Indian mid-cap equities where liquidity is thinner, a single large market order can push the price 10-30 bps beyond fair value. Market makers and informed traders step in to capture the reversion, but retail traders who observe the move interpret it as momentum and pile in, slowing the reversion. The inefficiency persists because: (1) detecting large trades requires tick-level monitoring, (2) the reversion window is narrow (2-5 min), and (3) distinguishing informed large trades (no reversion) from uninformed ones (reversion) requires context. We use VWAP deviation as a filter: large trades that push price far from VWAP are more likely uninformed liquidity-seeking orders.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents (focus on names ranked 51-100 for thinner liquidity)
stock_filter: ADV ₹20-80 crore range (liquid enough to trade but thin enough for impact)

other: trade-level data for large trade detection

indicators.name: impact_bps
indicators.formula: (close - close[1]) / close[1] * 10000 on bars where large_trade_flag == 1

long.confirmation: close > low of impact bar (initial bounce)

short.confirmation: close < high of impact bar (initial rejection)

entry.entry_price: limit order at close of impact bar

exit.target: reversion to 50% of impact (e.g., if impact = -20 bps, target +10 bps)
exit.stop_loss: impact extends by 50% (e.g., if impact = -20 bps, stop at -30 bps from pre-impact)
exit.time_stop: exit after 5 bars if target not hit
exit.signal_exit: price returns to VWAP

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L notional, reduce to ₹50K for stocks with ADV < ₹30 crore

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; impacts in high-VIX tend to be informed (no reversion)
filters.time_filter: skip first 10 min (opening auction distorts impact measurement)
filters.volume_filter: bar volume > 2x SMA(volume, 20) (confirm the large trade bar)
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades against intraday trend (counter-trend reversion more reliable)
filters.spread_filter: skip if bid-ask spread > 10 bps (wide spread erases reversion profit)
filters.event_filter: skip on result days for the specific stock (impacts may be informed)
other_filters: skip if stock hit circuit limits within last 30 min

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — the structural need for large orders to cross the spread in thin markets is permanent. As Indian market cap grows and liquidity deepens, impact sizes will shrink but not disappear.

weaknesses: Cannot distinguish informed vs uninformed large trades with certainty. Trading against an informed institutional buyer means catching a falling knife / fighting momentum.
In NIFTY 100 stocks ranked 51-100, liquidity can dry up suddenly, making exit at target price difficult and widening actual slippage beyond the 3 bps assumption.
Result season (Jan-Feb, Apr-May, Jul-Aug, Oct-Nov) increases false signals as earnings-driven large trades are informed and don't revert.
prior_art: Bouchaud, Farmer & Lillo (2009) 'How Markets Slowly Digest Changes in Supply and Demand' — foundational work on price impact and reversion. Almgren & Chriss (2000) 'Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions'. In India, SEBI's impact cost reports for index constituents provide empirical basis.
notes: The 50% reversion target is based on empirical studies showing temporary impact reverts ~60-70% on average, but we conservatively target 50%. The key implementation challenge is real-time large trade detection, which requires streaming trade tape.

name: order_flow_imbalance_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Cumulative order flow imbalance (OFI) — the running sum of signed trade volume classified as buyer-initiated or seller-initiated — predicts short-term price direction. When OFI diverges from price (e.g., OFI rising while price is flat), it signals latent buying pressure that will soon manifest in price. In Indian equities, the OFI signal is particularly valuable because: (1) NSE's continuous matching engine processes ~15,000 orders/sec creating rich flow data, (2) retail participation (~45% of cash turnover) is heavily momentum-driven, amplifying OFI trends, (3) the absence of designated market makers in most stocks means OFI reflects genuine directional pressure rather than market-making inventory management.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, daily trade count > 50,000

other: trade-level data with buy/sell classification via Lee-Ready

indicators.name: OFI_1min
indicators.formula: sum(signed_volume) per 1-min bar where signed_volume = +qty if buyer_initiated else -qty

indicators.name: cumulative_OFI
indicators.formula: cumsum(OFI_1min) from session start, reset daily

conditions: OFI_price_divergence == True AND OFI_momentum > 0 (flow says buy, price hasn't moved)
long.confirmation: OFI_1min > 0 for 2 of last 3 bars

short.confirmation: OFI_1min < 0 for 2 of last 3 bars

entry.entry_price: market order at signal bar close

exit.signal_exit: OFI_momentum crosses zero against position direction

risk.position_sizing: fixed ₹1L, increase to ₹1.5L when OFI_momentum magnitude > 2 * std(OFI_momentum, 60)

filters.time_filter: skip first 5 min and last 10 min
filters.volume_filter: 1-min volume > 50th percentile of day's volume distribution
filters.trend_filter: OFI direction aligns with NIFTY 50 intraday direction
filters.event_filter: reduce size on F&O expiry days
other_filters: skip if cumulative_OFI changes sign > 5 times today (choppy flow)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — OFI is well-established in academic literature but requires implementation effort. Edge may compress as algo platforms democratize order flow analytics in India.

weaknesses: Lee-Ready trade classification has ~15-20% misclassification rate, directly corrupting the OFI signal. In fast-moving markets, accuracy drops further.
Cumulative OFI is susceptible to large single-trade outliers (e.g., a block deal) that can flip the signal without genuine change in market sentiment.
The divergence signal (flow says X but price says Y) may simply reflect informed sellers distributing into buying flow, making the 'buy' signal a trap.
prior_art: Cont, Stoikov & Talreja (2010) 'A Stochastic Model for Order Book Dynamics'. Chordia & Subrahmanyam (2004) 'Order Imbalance and Individual Stock Returns'. Bouchaud et al. (2004) 'Fluctuations and Response in Financial Markets'.
notes: The OFI_price_divergence is the key alpha signal — when flow and price agree, the trade is just momentum following. The divergence trades are fewer but higher quality. Consider weighting the OFI by trade size to emphasize institutional flow.

name: adverse_selection_filter_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Flow toxicity — the probability that trade flow is informed — varies throughout the day. Using Volume-Synchronized Probability of Informed Trading (VPIN), we can estimate when flow is toxic (high informed trading) vs benign (retail/noise). The strategy: (1) compute VPIN in real-time, (2) only take mean-reversion trades when VPIN is LOW (benign flow, prices revert), (3) only take momentum trades when VPIN is HIGH (informed flow, prices trend). The inefficiency exists because most Indian traders apply the same strategy regardless of flow toxicity, leading to systematic losses when they mean-revert against informed flow or fade momentum during noise trading. By conditioning on VPIN, we avoid adverse selection and improve signal quality by ~30% vs unconditional signals.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹40 crore

other: volume-bucketed trade data for VPIN computation

indicators.name: VPIN
indicators.formula: abs(V_buy - V_sell) / V_total over rolling 50 volume buckets

conditions: close > VWAP * 0.998 (for benign reversion) OR close > VWAP (for toxic momentum)
long.confirmation: RSI_14 turning up (benign mode) OR momentum sustained 2 bars (toxic mode)

conditions: close < VWAP * 1.002 (for benign reversion) OR close < VWAP (for toxic momentum)
short.confirmation: RSI_14 turning down (benign mode) OR momentum sustained 2 bars (toxic mode)

entry.entry_price: limit at close of signal bar (benign mode), market order (toxic mode)

exit.target: 20 bps (benign mode), 30 bps (toxic mode — trend continuation expected)
exit.signal_exit: VPIN_regime flips during trade

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L notional in benign mode, ₹75K in toxic mode (higher uncertainty)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; VPIN thresholds recalibrate in high-VIX regimes
filters.time_filter: skip first 5 min and last 10 min
filters.volume_filter: skip bars with volume < 30th percentile of session
filters.trend_filter: in toxic mode, trade only in direction of NIFTY trend
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread > 8 bps (wide spread = high adverse selection cost)
filters.event_filter: recalibrate VPIN history on result days (regime shift)
other_filters: skip if VPIN oscillates between toxic/benign > 3 times in 30 min

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — VPIN conditioning is a meta-strategy that improves any underlying signal. Even as individual signals decay, the VPIN filter retains value because flow toxicity is a structural market property.

weaknesses: VPIN computation requires volume-bucketed data which introduces look-ahead bias if not carefully implemented (each bucket spans variable time).
The 75th percentile threshold for toxic/benign classification is calibrated on historical data and may shift during structural market changes (e.g., post-COVID volatility regime).
Running two parallel strategies (reversion in benign, momentum in toxic) doubles the complexity and the number of parameters to monitor and maintain.
prior_art: Easley, Lopez de Prado & O'Hara (2012) 'The Volume Clock: Insights into the High-Frequency Paradigm' — original VPIN paper. Abad & Yague (2012) validate VPIN in European markets. Wei, Gerace & Frino (2013) test VPIN as a risk metric.
notes: VPIN bucket size should be calibrated to the stock's ADV to ensure ~300 buckets/day. The strategy essentially acts as a regime-switching model where VPIN determines which alpha signal to activate. In practice, ~60% of trading time is benign and ~40% is toxic.

name: liquidity_provision_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: By placing limit orders around the running VWAP, we effectively provide liquidity to participants executing VWAP algorithms. Institutional VWAP algos are the single largest source of predictable order flow in Indian equities (estimated 20-30% of institutional volume). These algos target VWAP and will systematically buy below and sell above it throughout the day. By posting bids slightly below VWAP and asks slightly above, we earn the spread while positioning to benefit from VWAP mean reversion. The inefficiency persists because: (1) it requires continuous limit order management which retail traders can't do manually, (2) adverse selection risk from informed traders limits profitability, and (3) capital tied up in open orders reduces return on capital for most participants.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents (most liquid names for tight spread capture)
stock_filter: ADV > ₹100 crore, bid-ask spread < 3 bps average

long.confirmation: limit bid placed at VWAP_band_lower, filled

short.confirmation: limit ask placed at VWAP_band_upper, filled

entry.entry_price: limit order at VWAP_band_lower (long) or VWAP_band_upper (short)

exit.time_stop: exit if VWAP not reached within 5 bars
exit.eod_rule: flatten all positions by 15:15 IST; cancel all open orders by 15:10
exit.signal_exit: price touches VWAP

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per trade, max 3 concurrent positions across different stocks

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 18; this strategy fails in high-vol (VWAP bands widen, stops hit)
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 5 min (VWAP unstable) or last 15 min (closing pressure)
