filters.volume_filter: skip if volume_participation < 0.6 (abnormally low volume day)
filters.trend_filter: reduce size if |VWAP_deviation_bps| > 30 (strong trend, reversion less likely)
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread_ratio > 2.0 (adverse selection risk elevated)
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI day, budget day, stock result day (informed flow dominates)
other_filters: skip if stock gapped > 1% at open (VWAP anchored to distorted level)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — VWAP-targeting institutional flow is structurally persistent. As long as institutions benchmark to VWAP (which is industry standard), this strategy has counterparty flow.

weaknesses: Limit orders may not fill in fast-moving markets, leading to opportunity cost. In trending days, the strategy may generate zero trades.
Adverse selection: fills are more likely when informed traders push price through the limit level, meaning fills are negatively selected vs random.
Zerodha does not support placing and managing limit orders programmatically with sub-second latency; Kite API has ~200ms round-trip introducing fill risk.
prior_art: Avellaneda & Stoikov (2008) 'High-Frequency Trading in a Limit Order Book' — foundational market-making model. Gueant, Lehalle & Fernandez-Tapia (2012) extend to optimal inventory management. Berkowitz et al. (1988) original VWAP benchmark.
notes: This is essentially a simplified market-making strategy. Unlike HFT market makers, we don't quote continuously but only place orders when price reaches VWAP bands. The key advantage is avoiding inventory risk that comes with continuous quoting. Consider using Zerodha's GTT (Good Till Triggered) orders for automation.

name: trade_arrival_rate_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Trade arrival rate (number of trades per unit time) follows a predictable intraday pattern (U-shaped: high at open/close, low at midday). When the actual arrival rate deviates significantly from the expected pattern, it signals unusual activity — likely informed trading or news-driven flow. A sudden spike in trade arrival rate (>2x expected) with consistent price direction signals momentum that will persist for 3-8 minutes. Conversely, a spike with no net price change signals churn and imminent reversal. The inefficiency persists because: (1) trade count data is not displayed on most Indian retail platforms, (2) computing expected intraday arrival profiles requires historical calibration, and (3) the signal fires infrequently (2-4 times/day), making it unattractive for high-frequency strategies.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, average trade count > 40,000/day

indicators.name: trade_count
indicators.formula: number of trades in each 1-min bar

indicators.name: expected_trade_count
indicators.formula: SMA of trade_count at same time-of-day over last 20 sessions

indicators.name: arrival_direction
indicators.formula: sign(close - open) of the anomaly bar

long.confirmation: arrival_ratio > 1.5 on the next bar (sustained anomaly)

short.confirmation: arrival_ratio > 1.5 on the next bar

entry.entry_price: market order at confirmation bar close

exit.signal_exit: arrival_ratio drops below 1.0 (activity normalizes)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L, increase to ₹1.5L if arrival_ratio > 3.0 (very strong signal)

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (anomaly detection is self-calibrating)
filters.time_filter: skip first 10 min (arrival rates naturally elevated) and last 10 min
filters.volume_filter: volume_1min must also be > 1.5x expected (confirms trade count anomaly)
filters.trend_filter: prefer trades aligned with NIFTY 50 intraday direction
filters.spread_filter: skip if bid-ask spread > 8 bps (spread widening negates edge)
filters.event_filter: skip scheduled news times (arrival spike is expected, not anomalous)
other_filters: skip if arrival_ratio was > 2.0 within last 10 bars (recent anomaly exhaustion)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — trade count anomaly detection is uncommon in Indian retail. The signal fires infrequently, making it unattractive for crowding.

weaknesses: Low trade frequency (2-4/day) means long periods of inactivity and high variance in daily P&L. May have weeks of flat or negative returns.
Expected trade count profile requires 20+ days of calibration data; newly listed or recently volatile stocks will have stale profiles.
Cannot distinguish news-driven spikes (which may persist all day) from algorithmic order bursts (which revert quickly). Wrong classification leads to wrong hold time.
prior_art: Engle & Russell (1998) 'Autoregressive Conditional Duration' — foundational work on trade arrival modeling. Hawkes (1971) point process models applied to trade arrivals by Bacry et al. (2015). In Indian context, Mukherjee & Mishra (2010) study NSE microstructure.
notes: The expected_trade_count profile should be a smooth function (e.g., kernel-smoothed average) to avoid overfitting to specific minutes. Consider using Hawkes process for more sophisticated anomaly detection. The key insight is that arrival rate spikes with directional price impact are more informative than pure volume spikes.

name: spread_dynamics_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Bid-ask spread expansion in Indian equities precedes short-term volatility by 1-3 minutes because market makers widen quotes before anticipated information events (pre-news, large order detection). After the volatility event, spreads contract back to normal levels, and prices often overshoot then revert. The strategy: (1) detect spread expansion events (>2x normal), (2) wait for the volatility event to occur (price moves), (3) fade the move when spreads begin contracting (informed participants have completed their activity). The inefficiency persists because: (1) real-time spread monitoring is not standard on Indian retail platforms, (2) the window between spread contraction and price reversion is narrow (1-3 min), and (3) trading during wide-spread periods requires precise limit order placement that is psychologically difficult.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, typical bid-ask spread < 5 bps

conditions: close > low of spread expansion period
long.confirmation: spread_ratio < 1.8 (spread significantly contracting)

conditions: close < high of spread expansion period
short.confirmation: spread_ratio < 1.8

entry.entry_price: limit order at midprice when spread_ratio < 1.8

exit.target: reversion to pre-event price (50-70% of event move)
exit.stop_loss: event move extends by 50% (e.g., if price dropped 20 bps, stop at -30 bps)
exit.trailing_stop: 5 bps trailing after 10 bps reversion achieved
exit.signal_exit: spread_ratio re-expands > 2.0 (new event incoming)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L notional, reduce to ₹50K if spread_ratio peaked above 3.0 (high uncertainty event)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; in high VIX, spread expansions are more often informed
filters.time_filter: skip first 10 min and last 10 min (spreads naturally volatile)
filters.volume_filter: volume during spread event > 2x normal (confirms actual event, not illiquidity)
filters.trend_filter: fade only moves that are counter to the day's VWAP trend
filters.spread_filter: only trade when spread_ratio peaked > 2.0 but has started contracting
filters.event_filter: skip if the spread event coincides with scheduled news (informed, no reversion)
other_filters: skip if stock had > 2 spread events already today (repeated events suggest persistent information flow)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — spread dynamics are observable to sophisticated participants but the contrarian entry (fading the event move) is psychologically difficult, keeping retail crowding low.

weaknesses: Spread expansion may indicate a genuine information event (earnings leak, regulatory action) where the price move is permanent, not temporary. Fading such moves leads to large losses.
Limit order entry during spread contraction may not fill — if the reversion starts before fill, the entry is at a worse price; if it doesn't fill, opportunity is missed.
Low signal frequency (3-6 per day across the universe) limits the strategy's contribution to overall portfolio returns.
prior_art: Madhavan (2000) 'Market Microstructure: A Survey' covers spread dynamics theory. Huang & Stoll (1997) 'The Components of the Bid-Ask Spread'. Glosten & Milgrom (1985) foundational model of spread as adverse selection cost. Copeland & Galai (1983).
notes: The critical implementation detail is detecting the spread expansion peak in real-time — you need to identify that the spread has peaked and started contracting, not just that it is wide. This requires a rolling max with lookback. Consider pairing this with the adverse_selection_filter (strategy 107) to avoid informed events.

name: sector_momentum_rotation_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Intraday sector rotation in Indian markets follows a predictable pattern: the strongest performing sector in the first hour tends to continue outperforming through midday, but reverts in the last hour. This pattern exists because: (1) FII/DII flows often target sectors, not individual stocks, creating sector-wide momentum, (2) retail herding amplifies sector moves through the day via financial media and social media signals, (3) profit-taking and portfolio rebalancing in the last hour creates mean reversion. We buy the top 2 sectors (via their most liquid constituent) in the morning and rotate to laggards in the last 90 minutes. NSE sector indices (NIFTY Bank, IT, Pharma, Auto, Metal, FMCG, Realty, Energy, Infra, PSE) provide real-time sector tracking.
universe: NSE sectoral index constituents (top 2 liquid stocks per sector)
stock_filter: Top 2 by ADV in each of 10 NSE sectors, ADV > ₹30 crore
session: 10:15-15:20 IST (wait for 1 hour of data to rank sectors)
hold_time: 30-120 min (two rotation windows: momentum then reversion)

data.index: NIFTY 50, NIFTY Bank, NIFTY IT, NIFTY Pharma, NIFTY Auto, NIFTY Metal, NIFTY FMCG, NIFTY Realty, NIFTY Energy, NIFTY Infra

conditions: stock_close > stock_VWAP (momentum phase) OR stock_close < stock_VWAP (reversion phase)
long.confirmation: sector maintaining rank for 2 consecutive 30-min windows

conditions: stock_close < stock_VWAP (momentum phase) OR stock_close > stock_VWAP (reversion phase)
short.confirmation: sector maintaining rank for 2 consecutive 30-min windows

exit.target: 30 bps from entry (momentum phase), 25 bps (reversion phase)
exit.time_stop: exit momentum trades by 13:30, reversion trades by 15:20
exit.signal_exit: sector_rank changes by > 3 positions (rotation shift)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per sector trade, max 2 sectors at a time

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; skip in high-vol (all sectors correlated, rotation fails)
filters.time_filter: wait until 10:15 for first-hour ranking data
filters.trend_filter: momentum phase: NIFTY 50 directional (not range-bound); reversion phase: any
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy day (all sectors move together)
other_filters: skip if top and bottom sector return difference < 30 bps (no clear rotation)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — sector rotation is a well-known phenomenon but intraday rotation timing is less studied. The two-phase approach (momentum then reversion) is non-obvious and provides additional edge.

weaknesses: On strong trending days (macro events, global risk-on/off), all sectors move together and rotation signals generate noise. The 30 bps minimum dispersion filter helps but doesn't eliminate this.
The 13:30 switch from momentum to reversion is arbitrary and may not align with actual flow patterns, which vary by day of week and proximity to expiry.
Using single stocks as sector proxies introduces idiosyncratic risk — a stock-specific event can distort sector-level signal.
prior_art: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) 'Do Industries Explain Momentum?' establishes sector momentum. Bali, Engle & Murray (2016) cover cross-sectional momentum. In Indian context, Sehgal & Jain (2011) study sector rotation in Indian markets.
notes: Consider trading sector ETFs (BANKBEES, NIFTYIT, etc.) instead of individual stocks to reduce idiosyncratic risk. However, ETF liquidity in India is limited for intraday trading. Alternative: use NIFTY sector futures where available.

name: banking_vs_it_rotation_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: BANK NIFTY and NIFTY IT are the two largest sector indices by weight in NIFTY 50 and exhibit a well-documented negative intraday correlation driven by opposing macro sensitivities: banking benefits from rate cuts and domestic growth (INR strength), while IT benefits from INR weakness and global tech demand. When one sector significantly outperforms the other intraday (>30 bps spread), mean reversion occurs as institutional portfolio rebalancers adjust exposure. This inefficiency persists because: (1) the correlation regime shifts (sometimes positive, sometimes negative) making static pairs trading unreliable, (2) the reversion time is variable (30 min to 2 hours), and (3) retail traders treat banking and IT as independent, not as a rotation pair.
universe: BANK NIFTY constituents + NIFTY IT constituents
stock_filter: Top 3 by weight: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, SBI (banking) + TCS, Infosys, HCL Tech (IT)

conditions: spread_zscore < -2.0 (IT outperforming, banking lagging — expect banking catch-up)
USDINR_direction <= 0 (INR not weakening further — supports banking recovery)
long.confirmation: spread_zscore starts rising (crosses above -1.8 from below -2.0)

conditions: spread_zscore > 2.0 (banking outperforming, IT lagging — expect IT catch-up)
USDINR_direction >= 0 (INR not strengthening further — supports IT recovery)
short.confirmation: spread_zscore starts falling (crosses below 1.8 from above 2.0)

entry.entry_price: market order: long banking proxy + short IT proxy (or vice versa)

exit.target: spread_zscore reverts to 0 (spread mean reversion complete)
exit.stop_loss: spread_zscore extends to ±3.0 (spread widening, stop out)
exit.time_stop: exit after 90 bars if spread hasn't reverted
exit.signal_exit: correlation_regime turns positive (rotation dynamic broken)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; in high VIX, both sectors sell off together (positive correlation)
filters.time_filter: wait until 10:00 for stable intraday spread; stop new entries after 14:00
filters.volume_filter: both sector indices trading at > 0.7x normal volume participation
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 is moving > 1% intraday (macro dominating, rotation suppressed)
filters.spread_filter: individual stock spreads < 5 bps for all 6 proxy stocks
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy days (banking directional), IT result days (IT directional)
other_filters: skip if correlation_regime > 0.3 (sectors moving together, not rotating)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — the opposing macro sensitivities of banking (domestic rates) and IT (FX, global tech) are structural and unlikely to change. Rotation dynamics persist as long as both sectors have significant NIFTY weight.

weaknesses: The correlation regime between banking and IT is unstable — in risk-off events, both sectors sell off together and the rotation trade gets stopped out.
Using individual stocks as sector proxies introduces stock-specific risk (e.g., HDFC Bank result surprise moves the banking leg without sector-wide implication).
Very low trade frequency (1-2/day) means the strategy cannot stand alone and must be part of a portfolio of strategies.
prior_art: Granger & Morgenstern (1970) early work on spectral analysis of market relationships. Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) pairs trading framework. In India, Srivastava (2019) studies BANK NIFTY-IT NIFTY dynamics. The USDINR linkage is documented in CCIL reports.
notes: Alternative implementation: trade BANK NIFTY futures vs NIFTY IT futures directly. This eliminates stock-specific risk but introduces basis risk and requires higher margin. The USDINR filter is critical — when INR is in a strong one-directional trend, the rotation dynamic breaks down.

name: large_vs_mid_cap_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: The intraday return spread between NIFTY 50 (large cap) and NIFTY Midcap 100 reflects shifting risk appetite. When mid-caps outperform large-caps early in the day (risk-on), the spread tends to mean-revert in the afternoon as profit-taking and risk-reduction flows dominate. Conversely, when large-caps outperform (risk-off), the spread reverts as bargain hunters enter mid-caps. This pattern exists because: (1) institutional flows hit large-caps first (more liquid) creating a lead-lag, (2) retail traders pile into mid-caps with a delay (checking social media, WhatsApp tip groups), (3) end-of-day risk reduction favors exiting mid-caps first. The reversion is incomplete (30-50% of the peak spread) but reliable.
universe: NIFTY 50 liquid names + NIFTY Midcap 100 liquid names
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 proxy: NIFTY 50 ETF or top 5 by weight. Midcap proxy: top 5 NIFTY Midcap 100 by ADV (>₹20 crore)

other: FII/DII cash market net buy/sell data (available by 09:30 next day for calibration)

conditions: spread_zscore > 1.5 (large-caps outperforming, mid-caps lagging — expect mid-cap catch-up)
midcap_volume_ratio > 0.7 (mid-caps still actively traded, not abandoned)
long.confirmation: spread_zscore starts declining from peak (crosses below 1.3 from above 1.5)

conditions: spread_zscore < -1.5 (mid-caps outperforming, large-caps lagging — expect large-cap catch-up)
short.confirmation: spread_zscore starts rising from trough (crosses above -1.3 from below -1.5)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation: long mid-cap proxy + short large-cap proxy (or vice versa)

exit.time_stop: exit by 15:00 if target not reached
exit.signal_exit: vix_level spikes > 22 during trade (regime change to risk-off)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; in high VIX, flight-to-quality means large-cap outperformance persists all day
filters.time_filter: no entries before 11:00 (need 1.75 hours of spread data) or after 14:00
filters.volume_filter: both NIFTY 50 and Midcap 100 trading at > 0.7x typical volume
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 |return| > 1.5% intraday (strong trend day, no reversion)
filters.spread_filter: individual stock bid-ask < 10 bps (mid-caps can be wider)
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry, RBI policy, budget day
other_filters: skip if spread_zscore hasn't reached ±1.5 by 13:00 (insufficient divergence)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — the large/mid-cap risk appetite rotation is a structural feature of Indian markets driven by persistent differences in investor composition (FIIs dominate large-cap, retail/DII dominate mid-cap).

weaknesses: Mid-cap stocks have wider bid-ask spreads and thinner liquidity, making the short leg (or long leg in mid-caps) more expensive to execute and exit.
On genuine risk-off days (global crisis, geopolitical events), large-caps keep outperforming all day and the spread never reverts — the stop loss at z-score ±2.5 gets hit.
Very low trade frequency (1-2/day) and long hold time (45-120 min) mean the strategy ties up capital with modest expected return per trade.
prior_art: Banz (1981) 'The Relationship Between Return and Market Value of Common Stocks' — size effect foundation. Hong, Lim & Stein (2000) on slow information diffusion in small/mid-cap stocks. In India, Agarwal (2012) studies size-based anomalies in NSE.
notes: The mid-cap leg should use a basket of 3-5 stocks to diversify idiosyncratic risk. Single-stock mid-cap positions are too volatile for a relative value strategy. NIFTY Midcap 100 futures (if available) would be ideal for the mid-cap leg.

name: fno_vs_cash_rotation_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Stocks in the F&O segment experience different intraday dynamics than cash-only stocks because F&O stocks attract leveraged speculative flow. On days when F&O stocks with high open interest (OI) buildup outperform, it signals leveraged speculation that tends to unwind intraday. Cash-only stocks, driven by delivery buyers, show more persistent moves. The strategy exploits this divergence: when F&O-active stocks spike due to futures-driven buying (visible via OI increase + price rise), fade the move expecting intraday profit-taking by leveraged traders. Simultaneously, when cash-only stocks show similar momentum, follow it as it's more likely delivery-driven and persistent. This inefficiency exists because most retail traders don't separate their analysis by F&O vs cash dynamics.
universe: NIFTY 200: split into F&O segment (~180 stocks) and cash-only (~20 stocks)
stock_filter: F&O stocks: ADV > ₹20 crore, daily OI data available. Cash-only: ADV > ₹10 crore

other: intraday OI change for F&O stocks

indicators.name: fno_momentum_bps
indicators.formula: median(return_30min) across top 10 F&O stocks by intraday OI increase

indicators.name: cash_momentum_bps
indicators.formula: median(return_30min) across top 10 cash-only stocks by 30-min return

conditions: OI_change_pct > 5 for F&O leader stocks (speculative buildup)
F&O leader stock close > VWAP (momentum still active)
long.confirmation: short the F&O leader (fade speculative spike); long the cash leader (follow delivery flow)

conditions: OI_change_pct decreasing for F&O laggard stocks (unwinding)
short.confirmation: long the F&O laggard (bounce from unwind); short the cash leader (fade after overshoot)

entry.entry_price: market order on both legs simultaneously

exit.trailing_stop: 5 bps trailing on each leg independently
exit.signal_exit: OI starts building in opposite direction (regime change)

risk.position_sizing: ₹50K per leg (F&O leg + cash leg), market-neutral

filters.time_filter: no new entries after 14:00; allow first entry after 10:00
filters.volume_filter: F&O stock volume > 1.5x average (confirms speculative activity)
filters.trend_filter: prefer days when NIFTY 50 is range-bound (±0.5% intraday)
filters.event_filter: skip on monthly F&O expiry day (OI dynamics distorted by rollover)
other_filters: skip if fewer than 5 cash-only stocks have meaningful volume

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — the structural difference between leveraged F&O flow and delivery-based cash flow is permanent. Edge may narrow as more traders monitor OI data but will not disappear.

weaknesses: Cash-only stocks in NIFTY 200 are few (~20) and often illiquid. Executing meaningful positions without market impact is challenging.
Intraday OI data from NSE is delayed and noisy — real-time OI is approximated from option chain snapshots, not precise.
The premise that F&O flow is speculative and cash flow is delivery-driven is an oversimplification. Institutional F&O hedging activity creates non-speculative OI buildup.
prior_art: Ni, Pan & Poteshman (2008) 'Volatility Information Trading in the Option Market'. Easley, O'Hara & Srinivas (1998) 'Option Volume and Stock Prices'. In India, Srivastava et al. (2015) study F&O activity impact on underlying prices.
notes: SEBI's periodic reduction of F&O-eligible stocks means the cash-only universe is shrinking over time. If the cash-only segment becomes too small, the strategy may need to pivot to comparing high-OI vs low-OI within the F&O segment.

name: sector_leader_follower_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Within each NSE sector, information diffuses from the largest, most liquid stock (the 'leader') to smaller constituents (the 'followers') with a 3-10 minute lag. For example, when HDFC Bank (leader) moves sharply, ICICI Bank, Kotak, and Axis Bank (followers) follow with a measurable delay. This lag exists because: (1) institutional algos and news-trading systems focus on the leader first, (2) retail traders watch the leader for confirmation before trading followers, (3) smaller stocks have fewer market participants monitoring them continuously. The strategy buys followers when the leader makes a decisive move in either direction, capturing the lagged information diffusion.
universe: NSE sectoral indices — top 5 stocks by market cap in each sector
stock_filter: Leader: #1 by market cap in sector. Followers: #2-#5 by market cap, ADV > ₹20 crore

conditions: leader_move_zscore > 2.0 (leader made a significant up move)
follower_relative_return < -5 bps (follower hasn't caught up yet)
long.confirmation: follower starts upticking (follower_close > follower_close[1])

conditions: leader_move_zscore < -2.0 (leader made a significant down move)
follower_relative_return > 5 bps (follower hasn't caught up yet)
short.confirmation: follower starts downticking (follower_close < follower_close[1])

entry.entry_price: market order on follower stock at confirmation

exit.target: follower catches up to leader (follower_relative_return crosses 0)
exit.time_stop: exit after 10 bars (if follower doesn't catch up, signal is wrong)
exit.signal_exit: leader_move_zscore drops below 1.0 (leader move fading)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25; in high VIX, lead-lag relationships break down
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 5 min or last 10 min
filters.trend_filter: leader and NIFTY 50 moving in same direction (sector move is market-aligned)
filters.event_filter: skip if follower stock has specific news/result today (independent move, not lag)
other_filters: skip if historical_beta < 0.5 (weak relationship)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — lead-lag relationships are well-known academically but the specific lag times and beta estimates need continuous recalibration. The edge narrows as information diffusion speeds up via social media.

weaknesses: If the leader's move is stock-specific (not sector-driven), followers won't follow. E.g., HDFC Bank result surprise doesn't predict ICICI Bank move.
Lead-lag relationships are time-varying and can flip (sometimes ICICI leads HDFC). The fixed leader/follower assignment may be wrong on any given day.
The directional (unhedged) nature means the strategy has net market exposure, unlike true relative value trades.
prior_art: Lo & MacKinlay (1990) 'When Are Contrarian Profits Due to Stock Market Overreaction?' on lead-lag effects. Hou (2007) 'Industry Information Diffusion and the Lead-lag Effect'. Chordia & Swaminathan (2000) 'Trading Volume and Cross-Autocorrelations in Stock Returns'.
notes: Pre-compute the leader for each sector using a 20-day rolling market cap rank. In banking, the leader is typically HDFC Bank. In IT, it's TCS. In pharma, Sun Pharma. Maintain a lookup table of leader-follower pairs and their historical betas.

name: industry_group_reversion_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Within tightly correlated industry sub-groups (e.g., private banks, PSU banks, IT services, generic pharma), individual stock returns tend to revert to the group mean within the same trading day. When a stock deviates >15 bps from its industry group average return, the deviation is likely noise (order flow imbalance, temporary liquidity events) rather than stock-specific news. The inefficiency persists because: (1) most traders analyze stocks individually, not relative to their industry group, (2) constructing real-time industry group baskets requires infrastructure, (3) the reversion window is 10-30 minutes — too slow for HFTs, too fast for fundamentals-driven traders. In Indian markets, industry groups have historically high within-group correlations (0.6-0.8 for private banks, 0.5-0.7 for IT services) making this signal reliable.
universe: 6 industry groups: private banks (5), PSU banks (5), IT services (4), generic pharma (4), cement (4), auto OEMs (4)
stock_filter: Top 4-5 stocks by market cap in each industry group, ADV > ₹20 crore

other: industry group constituent list and weights (equal-weighted)

indicators.name: group_avg_return
indicators.formula: mean(cum_return_bps) across all stocks in industry group from 09:15

indicators.name: group_correlation
indicators.formula: average pairwise rolling_corr(stock_i, stock_j, 60) within group

conditions: stock has no specific news today
long.confirmation: deviation_zscore starts rising (crosses above -1.7 from below -2.0)

conditions: stock has no specific news today
short.confirmation: deviation_zscore starts falling (crosses below 1.7 from above 2.0)

entry.entry_price: limit order at midprice on confirmation bar

exit.target: stock_deviation reverts to 0 (stock returns to group average)
exit.stop_loss: deviation_zscore extends to ±3.0 (deviation widening — likely news-driven)
exit.trailing_stop: none (target is full reversion to group mean)
exit.signal_exit: group_correlation drops below 0.3 (group dispersion, reversion fails)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L on divergent stock (directional on the stock, hedged by group mean expectation)

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (intra-group reversion works across vol regimes)
filters.time_filter: skip first 15 min (group relationships establishing) and last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: divergent stock volume > 50th percentile of its typical volume
filters.trend_filter: no trend filter (relative reversion is trend-independent)
filters.event_filter: skip stocks with scheduled results, AGMs, or corporate actions today
other_filters: skip if divergent stock is the only one moving (all others flat — it's the divergent stock that has news)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — within-group mean reversion is driven by structural correlation in fundamentals. As long as companies in the same industry share common drivers (rates for banks, INR for IT), the signal persists.

weaknesses: Stock-specific news (analyst upgrade/downgrade, management commentary, deal wins) can cause legitimate divergence that doesn't revert. The 'no news' filter is imperfect.
Within-group correlation is not constant — on result season days, correlations drop as individual earnings drive stocks, reducing signal reliability.
Equal-weighted group averages may not be appropriate when one stock dominates the group by market cap (e.g., HDFC Bank in private banks).
prior_art: Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) 'Pairs Trading: Performance of a Relative-Value Arbitrage Rule' — the foundational statistical arbitrage paper. Avellaneda & Lee (2010) 'Statistical Arbitrage in the US Equities Market'. In India, Bhushan & Singh (2014) test pairs trading in NSE.
notes: Maintain a daily updated list of industry group constituents. Stocks may be added or removed from groups based on business changes (e.g., HDFC merged with HDFC Bank, changing the private bank group). Use a 20-day rolling correlation to validate group membership before each session.

name: nifty_banknifty_spread_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: BANK NIFTY carries ~33% weight in NIFTY 50, creating a tight but imperfect correlation. The intraday return spread between BANK NIFTY and NIFTY 50 exhibits mean-reverting behavior around a slowly drifting mean. When BANK NIFTY outperforms NIFTY 50 by > 30 bps intraday (or vice versa), the spread tends to compress over the next 30-60 minutes. The inefficiency exists because: (1) BANK NIFTY is the most traded F&O instrument and attracts speculative overreaction, (2) passive index funds rebalance toward NIFTY 50 weights, creating a natural reversion mechanism, (3) the spread is only mean-reverting intraday — overnight the spread can shift permanently based on macro factors. We trade this as a spread trade using NIFTY and BANK NIFTY futures (or their most liquid ETFs).
stock_filter: Trade via NIFTY 50 futures + BANK NIFTY futures (or NIFTYBEES + BANKBEES ETFs)

conditions: nb_spread_zscore < -1.5 (NIFTY outperforming BANK NIFTY — expect BANK NIFTY catch-up)
spread_velocity < -3 (spread still widening — wait for it to slow)
long.confirmation: spread_velocity crosses above -1 (widening slowing down)

conditions: nb_spread_zscore > 1.5 (BANK NIFTY outperforming NIFTY — expect compression)
short.confirmation: spread_velocity crosses below 1 (widening slowing down)

entry.entry_price: market order on both legs: long BANK NIFTY + short NIFTY (or vice versa)

exit.stop_loss: nb_spread_zscore extends to ±2.5 (spread diverging beyond threshold)
exit.time_stop: exit after 60 bars if target not reached
exit.signal_exit: India_VIX spikes > 22 during trade (correlation structure may break)

risk.position_sizing: ₹50K per leg, beta-adjusted (multiply NIFTY leg by BANK NIFTY beta to NIFTY, ~1.3)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 20; in high VIX, BANK NIFTY drops faster (higher beta) and spread may not revert
filters.time_filter: no trades in first 15 min or last 10 min
filters.volume_filter: both futures trading at > 0.8x normal volume participation
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 intraday move > 1.5% (strong trend makes spread directional, not mean-reverting)
filters.spread_filter: futures bid-ask spread < 0.05% on both legs
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI policy day (banking-specific), budget day, F&O expiry
other_filters: skip if HDFC Bank/ICICI Bank have results today (distorts BANK NIFTY)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — NIFTY/BANK NIFTY spread mean reversion is structural due to the weight overlap and passive fund rebalancing. This trade has been viable for years in Indian markets.

weaknesses: On RBI policy days or banking-specific regulatory events, BANK NIFTY diverges from NIFTY permanently intraday. The stop loss at z-score ±2.5 gets hit on such days.
Trading two index futures requires significant margin (especially BANK NIFTY at ~₹10L notional). The ₹1L capital allocation may be insufficient for proper sizing.
The beta-adjustment ratio between BANK NIFTY and NIFTY is time-varying (1.2-1.5) and using a stale beta leads to imperfect hedging.
prior_art: Vidyamurthy (2004) 'Pairs Trading: Quantitative Methods and Analysis' — seminal text on spread trading. Elliot, van der Hoek & Malcolm (2005) 'Pairs Trading' for mean-reverting spread models. In India, the NIFTY/BANK NIFTY spread is widely discussed but typically traded on daily charts, not intraday.
notes: Consider using options for the spread trade: buy BANK NIFTY calls + NIFTY puts (or vice versa) to limit downside risk. This converts the trade from a spread trade to a relative volatility trade but caps the loss at premium paid.

name: defensive_cyclical_switch_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Indian market intraday rotation between defensive sectors (FMCG, Pharma, IT) and cyclical sectors (Auto, Metal, Realty, Infra) is predicted by changes in India VIX within the session. When VIX rises >0.5 points intraday, money flows from cyclicals to defensives within 15-30 minutes. When VIX falls >0.5 points, the reverse occurs. This pattern exists because: (1) institutional risk management systems adjust sector exposure based on real-time VIX, (2) Indian mutual fund managers use VIX as a tactical allocation signal, (3) the flow from cyclicals to defensives is slower than the VIX move itself, creating a tradeable lag. Unlike daily-frequency rotation strategies, intraday VIX changes are mean-reverting (VIX itself mean-reverts intraday), providing natural profit-taking opportunities.
universe: Defensives: NIFTY FMCG, NIFTY Pharma, NIFTY IT. Cyclicals: NIFTY Auto, NIFTY Metal, NIFTY Realty, NIFTY Infra
stock_filter: Top 2 by ADV in each sector, ADV > ₹20 crore, total 14 stocks

indicators.name: vix_regime
indicators.formula: 'risk_off' if vix_change_30min > 0.5 else ('risk_on' if vix_change_30min < -0.5 else 'neutral')

conditions: vix_regime == 'risk_off' AND dc_spread < 0 (VIX rising but cyclicals still outperforming — rotation hasn't happened yet)
long.confirmation: dc_spread starts turning positive (defensives beginning to outperform)

conditions: vix_regime == 'risk_on' AND dc_spread > 0 (VIX falling but defensives still outperforming — rotation hasn't happened yet)
short.confirmation: dc_spread starts turning negative (cyclicals beginning to outperform)

entry.entry_price: market order: long defensive basket + short cyclical basket (risk_off) or vice versa

exit.target: dc_spread moves 20 bps in expected direction (rotation complete)
exit.stop_loss: dc_spread moves 15 bps against position (rotation not happening)
exit.trailing_stop: 8 bps trailing after 12 bps profit on spread
exit.signal_exit: vix_regime changes (VIX reverses direction)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX absolute level > 12 (in very low VIX, changes are too small to drive rotation)
filters.time_filter: no trades before 10:00 (VIX needs time to establish direction) or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: all basket stocks trading at > 0.7x normal volume
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 is moving > 1.5% intraday (macro overwhelms rotation)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI day (VIX changes are one-directional, not mean-reverting)
other_filters: skip if fewer than 5 of the 14 stocks are actively traded

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — defensive/cyclical rotation is a permanent feature of equity markets driven by institutional risk management frameworks. The intraday timing component adds alpha over well-known daily-frequency rotation.

weaknesses: Trading 4-8 stocks simultaneously (basket approach) is operationally complex with Zerodha's API limits and increases total transaction costs.
India VIX 1-min data can be noisy (computed from NIFTY option chain every 15 sec). A 0.5-point change may be noise, not signal.
On trend days (strong VIX expansion), the rotation happens once and doesn't revert. The strategy assumes mean-reverting VIX, which fails on tail days.
prior_art: Asness, Moskowitz & Pedersen (2013) 'Value and Momentum Everywhere' — factor rotation literature. Mohanram (2005) on defensive vs cyclical characteristics. In India, Amundi-ACPI studies VIX-based sector allocation for Indian mutual funds.
notes: The VIX threshold of 0.5 points change is calibrated to India VIX typical daily range of 1-3 points. If VIX regime is persistently 'neutral', no trades are generated — this is by design. The strategy naturally avoids low-conviction days.

name: sector_vwap_divergence_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: When a stock trades persistently above its VWAP while its sector index trades below its VWAP (or vice versa), the divergence signals either (a) stock-specific strength that will pull the sector up (if the stock is a leader), or (b) stock-specific overextension that will revert to sector performance. The key insight: VWAP reflects the average institutional execution price for the day. A stock above VWAP means institutions who bought are sitting on profits, a stock below means they're in drawdown. When the stock and its sector disagree on VWAP positioning, the tension resolves within 15-30 minutes in favor of the sector direction ~60% of the time (the stock reverts to sector trend). The 40% case where the stock leads the sector is captured by a separate confirmation filter.
universe: NSE sector indices and their top 5 constituents
stock_filter: Top 5 by market cap in each of 6 major sectors (Bank, IT, Pharma, Auto, FMCG, Metal), ADV > ₹20 crore

data.index: NIFTY 50, NIFTY Bank, NIFTY IT, NIFTY Pharma, NIFTY Auto, NIFTY FMCG, NIFTY Metal
other: sector index VWAP computed from constituent VWAPs

indicators.name: vwap_divergence
indicators.formula: stock_vwap_pos - sector_vwap_pos (positive = stock stronger than sector)

indicators.name: divergence_duration
indicators.formula: count of consecutive bars where sign(stock_vwap_pos) != sign(sector_vwap_pos)

conditions: sector_vwap_pos > 5 (sector above VWAP) AND stock_vwap_pos < -5 (stock below VWAP)
stock_is_leader == 0 (trade followers reverting to sector, not leaders diverging)
long.confirmation: stock_close crosses above stock_VWAP (reversion starting)

conditions: sector_vwap_pos < -5 (sector below VWAP) AND stock_vwap_pos > 5 (stock above VWAP)
short.confirmation: stock_close crosses below stock_VWAP (reversion starting)

entry.entry_price: market order at VWAP cross confirmation

exit.stop_loss: 15 bps from entry in adverse direction
exit.signal_exit: sector_vwap_pos changes sign (sector crossed VWAP, invalidating thesis)

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (VWAP divergence works across vol regimes)
filters.time_filter: wait until 10:00 (VWAP needs 45 min to stabilize); stop new entries at 14:30
filters.volume_filter: stock volume > 50th percentile of its typical 1-min volume
filters.trend_filter: trade in direction of sector VWAP position (sector above VWAP = bullish)
filters.event_filter: skip stocks with results/AGMs today (legitimate divergence, not reversion candidate)
other_filters: skip if stock_is_leader == 1 (leaders may be leading, not diverging)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — VWAP is the institutional benchmark and VWAP-relative positioning is a fundamental market feature. The divergence signal adds a novel layer over basic VWAP strategies.

weaknesses: Sector index VWAP is an approximation (weighted sum of constituent VWAPs) and may not perfectly reflect actual sector flow dynamics.
The leader/follower distinction is rigid — sometimes the #2 stock by market cap acts as the leader (e.g., ICICI Bank when it has results but HDFC Bank doesn't).
The 5-bar minimum divergence duration may cause late entry, missing the initial reversion move and entering mid-way with reduced reward-to-risk.
prior_art: Berkowitz et al. (1988) 'The Total Cost of Transactions on the NYSE' — original VWAP benchmark paper. Bialkowski, Darolles & Le Fol (2008) 'Improving VWAP Strategies'. In India, NSE's own VWAP reports and institutional best execution policies establish VWAP as the dominant benchmark.
notes: Sector VWAP should be computed as a market-cap-weighted average of constituent VWAPs, not as VWAP of the sector index level (which is not a traded instrument). Use NIFTY Bank VWAP = sum(weight_i * VWAP_i) for all Bank NIFTY constituents.

name: market_breadth_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Market breadth — the proportion of stocks advancing vs declining — diverges from the headline NIFTY 50 index during distribution (narrow rally in 5-10 heavy-weight stocks while breadth deteriorates) and accumulation (broad-based buying while index is flat due to weakness in heavyweights). When NIFTY 50 makes a new intraday high but the advance-decline ratio is declining, it signals unsustainable narrowing and a likely reversal within 15-30 minutes. In Indian markets, this divergence is amplified because NIFTY 50 is top-heavy: top 10 stocks represent ~55% of weight. A rally in HDFC Bank + Reliance + TCS can push NIFTY up while 40 other stocks are flat or down. The inefficiency persists because most retail traders watch only the index level, not breadth metrics, and breadth data requires monitoring all 50 constituents simultaneously.
stock_filter: All NIFTY 50 constituents for breadth computation; trade via NIFTY 50 futures or NIFTYBEES

other: 1-min OHLCV for all 50 NIFTY constituents for breadth computation

indicators.name: advance_decline_ratio
indicators.formula: count(stocks where close > close[5]) / count(stocks where close < close[5])

conditions: breadth_ema > 1.2 (but majority of stocks are actually advancing)
long.confirmation: NIFTY 50 1-min close > NIFTY 50 1-min close[1] (first uptick from the low)

conditions: breadth_ema < 0.8 (but majority of stocks are actually declining)
short.confirmation: NIFTY 50 1-min close < NIFTY 50 1-min close[1] (first downtick from the high)

entry.entry_price: market order on NIFTY 50 futures at confirmation

exit.target: NIFTY 50 moves 20 bps in direction of breadth (reversal from divergence)
exit.stop_loss: NIFTY 50 makes another new high/low extending 10 bps beyond entry
exit.time_stop: exit after 30 bars (if divergence doesn't resolve, it may be a legitimate new trend)
exit.signal_exit: breadth_ema realigns with index direction (divergence resolved without reversal)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L in NIFTY futures (1 mini lot if available) or NIFTYBEES

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22; in high VIX, breadth divergences may not revert (panic selling)
filters.time_filter: skip first 15 min (breadth metrics need stabilization) and last 10 min
filters.trend_filter: divergence is more reliable when NIFTY is near day's VWAP (not extreme trend)
filters.event_filter: skip on broad macro event days (all stocks move together, breadth uninformative)
other_filters: require at least 30 of 50 stocks to have meaningful 5-min returns (exclude those halted or illiquid)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — breadth divergence is a classic technical analysis concept but its real-time intraday computation at 1-min resolution is novel. Most practitioners use daily breadth, not intraday.

weaknesses: Breadth divergence can persist for extended periods (2+ hours) before resolving. The 30-bar time stop may exit positions prematurely before the thesis plays out.
On days with heavy FII selling in large-caps only (e.g., MSCI rebalance), breadth divergence is genuine and NIFTY decline will persist despite positive breadth.
Computing real-time breadth for all 50 stocks requires monitoring 50 simultaneous data feeds, which is resource-intensive and may have data latency issues.
prior_art: Zweig (1986) 'Winning on Wall Street' popularized breadth indicators. McClellan Oscillator and Summation Index are classic breadth tools. In India, intraday breadth analysis is nascent — BSE/NSE publish daily A/D ratios but not intraday.
notes: The 5-bar lookback for advance/decline classification is a balance between responsiveness and noise. 1-bar lookback is too noisy; 10-bar lookback is too slow. Experiment with VWAP-based classification (advancing = close > VWAP, declining = close < VWAP) as an alternative to close-over-close.

name: earnings_surprise_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Post-Earnings Announcement Drift (PEAD) is one of the most robust anomalies in finance. In Indian markets, earnings are typically announced after market hours (16:00-20:00 IST) or before market open. Stocks that gap >2% at open on result days exhibit intraday momentum continuation in the gap direction for the first 60-90 minutes, driven by: (1) retail traders who read the headline but take 30+ minutes to act, (2) mutual fund NAV-driven flows that execute throughout the day, (3) analyst upgrades/downgrades that trickle in during the session, amplifying the initial move. The intraday drift is 30-50% of the gap magnitude on average. The inefficiency persists because many traders fade gaps (expecting reversion) when the correct action on earnings gaps is to follow the gap direction.
universe: NIFTY 200 constituents (only on their result days)
stock_filter: Stock must have announced earnings in the last 18 hours, ADV > ₹15 crore
session: 09:15-12:00 IST (first 2.75 hours only — drift fades after noon)

conditions: close_5min > open_today (gap not fading in first 5 minutes)
long.confirmation: close at 09:20 > high of 09:15-09:20 range (breakout above opening range)

conditions: close_5min < open_today (gap not bouncing in first 5 minutes)
short.confirmation: close at 09:20 < low of 09:15-09:20 range

exit.target: 50% of gap magnitude as continuation target (e.g., gap=3%, target=1.5% further)
exit.stop_loss: gap fills 50% (e.g., gap=3%, stop if retraces 1.5%)
exit.trailing_stop: 20 bps trailing after 30 bps of continuation achieved
exit.time_stop: exit by 12:00 IST regardless (drift exhausts by midday)
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 12:00 IST (not 15:29 — drift is a morning phenomenon)
exit.signal_exit: volume_surge drops below 1.0 (interest fading)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L, reduce to ₹50K for stocks with ADV < ₹30 crore

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (earnings drift works across vol regimes)
filters.time_filter: entry only between 09:20-10:00; exit by 12:00
filters.volume_filter: volume_surge > 2.0 on opening bars (must be heavily traded result day)
filters.trend_filter: prefer gap direction aligned with NIFTY 50 direction (tailwind)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 15 bps (spreads widen on result day but must be tradeable)
filters.event_filter: only trade on result day, not day after (PEAD at daily level is different)
other_filters: skip if gap > 10% (circuit limit risk)
skip if option IV > 80% (priced in)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — PEAD is one of the most persistent anomalies in finance, documented since Ball & Brown (1968). In India, the anomaly is still strong because retail gap-faders provide liquidity for drift traders.

weaknesses: Earnings surprise data (consensus estimates) is not freely available real-time. Bloomberg/Refinitiv subscriptions cost ₹10L+/year, creating a data barrier.
Gap direction and earnings quality may disagree — a positive gap on low-quality earnings (one-time gains) will revert, not drift. Qualitative filtering is needed but hard to automate.
The strategy generates trades only during result season (~8 weeks/year across 4 quarters), leaving it idle for ~70% of trading days.
prior_art: Ball & Brown (1968) original PEAD discovery. Bernard & Thomas (1989, 1990) confirm persistence. In India, Dutta & Girish (2013) study PEAD in BSE stocks. DellaVigna & Pollet (2009) show PEAD is stronger when investor attention is low (Friday announcements).
notes: Consider using option IV crush as a confirming signal — if IV drops significantly on result day open, it means the move is in line with expected; if IV stays elevated, the market expects more movement. The opening range breakout (09:15-09:20) filter is critical to avoid fading into gap-fill traps.

name: rbi_policy_reaction_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: RBI monetary policy announcements (6 per year, typically at 10:00 IST) create a predictable intraday pattern: (1) pre-announcement compression (09:15-10:00) where volatility drops and prices consolidate, (2) knee-jerk reaction (10:00-10:15) where BANK NIFTY moves 50-200 bps in the direction of the surprise, (3) partial reversal (10:15-10:45) as the initial reaction overshoots, (4) trend resumption (10:45-12:00) as the market digests the full statement. The strategy trades phase 3 (fade the overshoot) and phase 4 (follow the trend). The inefficiency exists because retail traders react emotionally to headlines ('rate cut!' or 'hawkish hold!') without reading the statement, creating an overshoot that sophisticated participants fade. The phase 4 trend is driven by institutional portfolio adjustments.
universe: BANK NIFTY index (via futures) and top 3 private bank stocks
stock_filter: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank, Kotak Bank (most rate-sensitive, liquid)

conditions: PHASE 3 (10:15-10:45): banknifty_reaction < -50 bps (sold off on hawkish surprise) AND retracement_pct > 0.3 (already started bouncing)
OR PHASE 4 (10:45-12:00): banknifty_reaction > 0 (dovish surprise) AND close > VWAP AND gilt_yield_change < -3 bps (yields confirming dovishness)
long.confirmation: Phase 3: BANK NIFTY 1-min close > 1-min close[2] for 2 bars. Phase 4: BANK NIFTY > VWAP and rising

conditions: PHASE 3: banknifty_reaction > 50 bps (rallied on dovish surprise) AND retracement_pct > 0.3
OR PHASE 4: banknifty_reaction < 0 (hawkish surprise) AND close < VWAP AND gilt_yield_change > 3 bps
short.confirmation: Phase 3: BANK NIFTY 1-min close < 1-min close[2] for 2 bars. Phase 4: BANK NIFTY < VWAP and falling

exit.target: Phase 3: 50% retracement of reaction move. Phase 4: 30 bps from entry
exit.stop_loss: Phase 3: reaction_peak extends (new extreme). Phase 4: 15 bps from entry
exit.trailing_stop: 10 bps trailing after 20 bps profit (Phase 4 only)
exit.time_stop: Phase 3: exit by 10:45. Phase 4: exit by 13:00
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 13:00 (post-RBI volatility settles by afternoon)
exit.signal_exit: vix_spike reverses direction sharply

risk.position_sizing: ₹75K per trade (reduced size due to event volatility)

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (VIX spike is part of the signal, not a filter)
filters.time_filter: only trade on RBI policy announcement days (6 per year)
filters.volume_filter: BANK NIFTY volume > 1.5x normal on policy day (confirmed interest)
filters.trend_filter: Phase 3 is contrarian (fade); Phase 4 follows confirmed trend
filters.spread_filter: BANK NIFTY futures spread < 0.1% (spreads widen on policy day)
filters.event_filter: ONLY trade on RBI days — this is the event
other_filters: skip if policy outcome is exactly as expected (no surprise = no overshoot)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — RBI policy events happen only 6 times/year and the reaction pattern is consistent. Limited sample size makes it hard for systematic traders to optimize against, preserving the edge.

weaknesses: Only 6 trade days per year (RBI policy meetings) — the strategy cannot be a primary income source and contributes minimally to annual P&L.
The Phase 3/Phase 4 framework assumes a standard reaction pattern, but emergency meetings or coordinated global central bank actions create non-standard patterns.
Slippage on RBI policy days is significantly higher than normal — the 3 bps assumption is optimistic; actual slippage may be 5-10 bps during peak reaction.
prior_art: Lucca & Moench (2015) 'The Pre-FOMC Announcement Drift' — the Fed equivalent of this strategy. Bernanke & Kuttner (2005) 'What Explains the Stock Market's Reaction to Federal Reserve Policy?'. In India, Patel (2017) studies RBI rate decision impact on banking stocks.
notes: Track the RBI calendar religiously. The governor's press conference (10:30-11:30) is Phase 4's primary driver. Consider hedging with Bank NIFTY options (buy straddle before 10:00, then trade the directional leg after the announcement).

name: expiry_day_pattern_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: F&O expiry days (weekly Thursday for NIFTY/BANK NIFTY, monthly last Thursday for stocks) exhibit distinct intraday patterns driven by options market makers' gamma hedging and pin risk. On expiry day: (1) stocks/indices tend to pin near the strike with maximum open interest ('max pain'), (2) gamma exposure amplifies moves away from max pain in the morning but dampens them in the afternoon, (3) the last 90 minutes see accelerated theta decay forcing option sellers to unwind hedges, creating directional moves. The strategy: trade mean-reversion toward max pain in the morning, then trade breakouts in the last 90 minutes as gamma hedging unwinds. The inefficiency exists because most retail traders trade options directly on expiry day (hoping for lottery payoffs) rather than trading the predictable underlying patterns created by options dynamics.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 and BANK NIFTY futures — most liquid, tightest spreads on expiry

other: max pain strike (computed from option chain OI)

indicators.name: max_pain_strike
indicators.formula: strike_price that minimizes sum(OI_call * max(0, strike - S) + OI_put * max(0, S - strike)) across all strikes

indicators.name: net_gamma
indicators.formula: sum(OI_call * gamma_call - OI_put * gamma_put) across all strikes

conditions: (expiry_phase == 'morning_pin' AND distance_to_max_pain < -30 bps) — below max pain, expect pin rally
OR (expiry_phase == 'afternoon_unwind' AND close > high_of_last_30_bars AND net_gamma > 0) — gamma squeeze up
long.confirmation: morning: close > close[2] for 2 bars (bounce starting). afternoon: volume_surge > 1.5

conditions: (expiry_phase == 'morning_pin' AND distance_to_max_pain > 30 bps) — above max pain, expect pin pullback
OR (expiry_phase == 'afternoon_unwind' AND close < low_of_last_30_bars AND net_gamma < 0) — gamma squeeze down
short.confirmation: morning: close < close[2] for 2 bars. afternoon: volume_surge > 1.5

exit.target: morning_pin: price reaches max_pain_strike. afternoon_unwind: 30 bps from entry
exit.stop_loss: morning_pin: 15 bps beyond max pain distance (diverging). afternoon_unwind: 15 bps from entry
exit.time_stop: morning trades exit by 13:00. afternoon trades exit by 15:25
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 15:29 IST (absolute last minute before expiry close)
exit.signal_exit: max_pain_strike shifts by >0.5% (OI structure changed, thesis invalidated)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 12 AND < 25 (need some vol for gamma effects but not too much chaos)
filters.time_filter: morning phase: 09:20-13:00. afternoon phase: 13:30-15:25
filters.volume_filter: index futures volume > 1.2x normal (confirmed active expiry)
filters.trend_filter: morning: contrarian toward max pain. afternoon: trend-following breakout
filters.event_filter: ONLY on expiry days (weekly or monthly)
other_filters: skip if max_pain_strike has shifted >1% from previous day's close (unusual OI buildup)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — expiry day patterns are increasingly discussed on Indian trading social media, but the two-phase approach (pin + unwind) is more sophisticated than the simple 'sell options on expiry' strategy most retail traders use.

weaknesses: Max pain calculation requires full option chain data and is sensitive to OI changes during the day. Stale OI data (even 30-min old) can mislead.
With weekly expiries, every Thursday is an expiry day but gamma effects are smaller for weekly options (less OI). Monthly expiry effects are stronger but only 12 per year.
The afternoon gamma squeeze can be violent and fast — if the stop loss is too tight (15 bps), it may get hit before the squeeze completes.
prior_art: Ni, Pearson & Poteshman (2005) 'Stock Price Clustering on Option Expiration Dates'. Avellaneda & Lipkin (2003) 'A market-induced mechanism for stock pinning'. In India, expiry day effects are widely discussed by practitioners but limited academic study exists.
notes: Max pain computation: iterate through all active strikes, for each compute the total loss for option buyers (calls + puts), and find the strike that maximizes total loss. This strike is where option sellers (who are short gamma) benefit most. For weekly expiry, focus on NIFTY/BANK NIFTY only — stock weekly options have too little OI for meaningful gamma effects.

name: global_cue_reaction_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Indian markets open at 09:15 IST, by which time SGX NIFTY futures (trading in Singapore from 06:30 IST) have already priced in overnight US, European, and Asian market moves. The opening gap in NIFTY relative to SGX NIFTY's implied open provides a tradeable signal: (1) when NIFTY opens at a PREMIUM to SGX NIFTY implied level (domestic enthusiasm exceeds global cues), the premium fades within 30 minutes as arbitrageurs and institutions align prices, (2) when NIFTY opens at a DISCOUNT to SGX NIFTY, the discount closes similarly. The inefficiency exists because: retail traders react to absolute NIFTY gap direction without comparing to SGX NIFTY, and the SGX NIFTY / NSE NIFTY convergence is a near-arbitrage that institutions exploit but retail misses.
stock_filter: NIFTY 50 futures (current month)

conditions: premium_bps < -10 (NIFTY opened at discount to SGX — expect convergence upward)
SGX NIFTY was stable in last 30 min before NSE open (not trending against India)
long.confirmation: NIFTY futures 1-min close > NIFTY futures open (first uptick from discount)

conditions: premium_bps > 10 (NIFTY opened at premium to SGX — expect convergence downward)
SGX NIFTY was stable in last 30 min before NSE open
short.confirmation: NIFTY futures 1-min close < NIFTY futures open (first downtick from premium)

entry.entry_price: market order on NIFTY futures at first confirmation bar

exit.target: premium_bps reverts to 0 (NIFTY aligns with SGX implied level)
exit.stop_loss: premium_bps extends to ±25 bps (domestic flow overpowering arbitrage)
exit.trailing_stop: 5 bps trailing after 10 bps convergence achieved
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 10:30 IST (this is a morning-only strategy)
exit.signal_exit: SGX NIFTY itself moves significantly during NSE session (new information)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 (in high VIX, convergence may not happen as domestic fear dominates)
filters.time_filter: entry only in 09:15-09:30; exit by 10:30
filters.volume_filter: NIFTY futures volume > 0.8x normal in first 15 min
filters.trend_filter: skip if overnight S&P 500 moved > 2% (extreme global event, convergence won't apply)
filters.event_filter: skip on RBI day, budget day (domestic factors dominate global cues)
other_filters: skip if SGX NIFTY moved > 1% in last hour before NSE open (trending, not stable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — SGX NIFTY convergence is well-known among Indian institutional traders. However, retail traders still primarily watch absolute gap, not SGX-relative gap, preserving some edge.

weaknesses: SGX NIFTY data is not freely available via Zerodha. Requires separate data subscription or scraping from financial portals with latency.
On days with significant India-specific overnight news (regulatory changes, geopolitical events), the premium/discount is justified and won't converge.
The signal generates only 1 trade per day and targets a small edge (~22 bps). Annual returns depend heavily on consistency across 250 trading days.
prior_art: Madhavan (2000) 'Market Microstructure' on price discovery across venues. Eun & Sabherwal (2003) 'Cross-Border Listings and Price Discovery'. In India, Mukherjee (2011) studies NIFTY-SGX NIFTY price discovery. NSE's GIFT NIFTY (replacing SGX NIFTY) maintains the same dynamics.
notes: As of 2024, SGX NIFTY has been replaced by GIFT NIFTY (trading at GIFT City IFSC). The dynamics are similar but GIFT NIFTY trades in Indian time zone, potentially reducing the premium/discount at open. Monitor whether the signal degrades post-migration.

name: block_deal_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Block deals on NSE (trades > 5 lakh shares or ₹10 crore, executed in a separate window 08:45-09:00 or during market hours in 15-min blocks) signal large institutional position changes. When a block deal occurs at a premium to the previous close, it signals institutional buying conviction; when at a discount, selling pressure. The stock subsequently drifts in the block deal direction over the next 1-2 hours as: (1) information about the block deal disseminates (NSE discloses block deals with a 15-min delay), (2) other institutions follow the signal, (3) retail traders notice the unusual volume and pile in. The inefficiency exists because block deal data is disclosed with a lag, and most retail traders don't monitor the block deal window.
universe: All NSE stocks eligible for block deals
stock_filter: Stock must have a block deal today, ADV > ₹10 crore, price > ₹100
session: 09:15-12:00 IST (block deal momentum fades by midday)

other: NSE block deal disclosures (via NSE bulk/block deal API)

conditions: block_premium_pct > 1.0 (block deal at 1%+ premium — bullish signal)
block_size_relative > 0.5 (deal size > 50% of ADV — meaningful size)
long.confirmation: close > VWAP AND close > open_today after block deal disclosure

conditions: block_premium_pct < -1.0 (block deal at 1%+ discount — bearish signal)
short.confirmation: close < VWAP AND close < open_today after block deal disclosure

entry.entry_price: market order 15-20 min after block deal disclosure (let initial reaction settle)

exit.time_stop: exit by 12:00 IST (drift fades by midday)
exit.eod_rule: flatten by 12:00 IST (not EOD — this is a morning strategy)
exit.signal_exit: post_block_volume_ratio drops below 1.0 (interest fading)

filters.time_filter: entry only after block deal disclosure + 15 min settling period
filters.trend_filter: prefer block deal direction aligned with NIFTY 50 trend
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 10 bps (block deal stocks can have temporarily wide spreads)
filters.event_filter: skip if stock also has earnings/corporate action today (confounding signals)
other_filters: skip if block_size_relative < 0.5 (too small to be meaningful)
skip if block deal is between group companies (not arms-length)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — block deal data is public but the 15-min disclosure delay creates an information asymmetry window. Faster data access (direct NSE feed) would reduce the edge for slower participants.

weaknesses: Block deals happen irregularly — some days have zero, others have 5+. The strategy has highly variable daily P&L and long idle periods.
Block deals between promoter entities or for regulatory compliance (SEBI MPS norms) don't signal genuine institutional conviction and create false signals.
The 15-minute disclosure delay means by the time we see the data and confirm, the initial momentum may already be exhausted, leaving only residual drift.
prior_art: Holthausen, Leftwich & Mayers (1990) 'Large-Block Transactions, the Speed of Response'. Saar (2001) 'Price Impact Asymmetry of Block Trades'. In India, SEBI circular on block deal framework (2017) defines the mechanism. Banerjee & Ghosh (2019) study NSE block deals.
notes: Monitor NSE's block deal disclosures via their website API or scraping. The pre-open block deal window (08:45-09:00) is especially informative — deals in this window are visible before market open, giving an early signal for the day's direction. Bulk deals (different from block deals, disclosed T+1) are not useful for intraday.

name: corporate_action_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: On ex-dividend/ex-bonus/ex-split dates, NSE adjusts the previous close by the corporate action amount, but the market's opening price frequently overshoots or undershoots this theoretical adjusted price. For dividends, stocks often open at a smaller discount than the dividend amount (partial adjustment) — especially for special dividends — creating a long opportunity. For stock splits, the post-split price often overshoots the theoretical adjustment due to retail 'cheap stock' bias. The inefficiency exists because: (1) many retail traders don't correctly compute the adjusted price, (2) limit orders from the previous day carry over unadjusted, creating temporary mispricing, (3) the adjustment is mechanical but the market's reaction is behavioral.
universe: All NSE stocks with corporate actions (dividend, split, bonus)
stock_filter: Ex-date today, ADV > ₹10 crore, corporate action value > 1% of stock price

other: theoretical adjusted price (prev_close - dividend, or prev_close / split_ratio)

indicators.name: theoretical_adjusted_price
indicators.formula: prev_close - dividend_amount (for dividends) OR prev_close / split_ratio (for splits) OR prev_close * shares_old / shares_new (for bonus)

conditions: adjustment_error_bps < -20 (stock opened too low relative to theoretical — overadjusted)
long.confirmation: adjustment_convergence improving (moving toward 0 from negative)

conditions: adjustment_error_bps > 20 (stock opened too high — underadjusted, especially for splits)
short.confirmation: adjustment_convergence declining (moving toward 0 from positive)

entry.entry_price: market order within first 15 min of detecting mispricing

exit.target: adjustment_error_bps converges to ±5 bps (near fair value)
exit.stop_loss: adjustment_error_bps extends to ±50 bps (mispricing is genuine, not noise)
exit.time_stop: exit by 11:00 IST (adjustment should complete by then)
exit.signal_exit: stock trades through theoretical_adjusted_price and keeps going (overshoot in other direction)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per trade, reduce for stocks with ADV < ₹20 crore

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter (corporate action adjustment is independent of volatility regime)
filters.time_filter: entry only in 09:15-09:45; exit by 11:00
filters.trend_filter: skip if NIFTY 50 is moving > 1% in first 30 min (market move dominates adjustment effect)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 15 bps (ex-date spreads can be wider)
filters.event_filter: only trade on ex-dates with corporate action value > 1% of stock price (material)
other_filters: skip bonus issues < 1:5 (too small to create meaningful mispricing)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — corporate action adjustment errors are driven by behavioral biases and mechanical order book issues that are structural. As long as corporate actions occur, the signal persists.

weaknesses: Corporate actions are infrequent for any single stock, and material actions (>1% of price) are rarer still. The strategy may generate only 5-10 trades per month.
For dividends, the stock may legitimately open below theoretical adjustment if the market is pricing in reduced future earnings or if it's an unsustainable special dividend.
The theoretical adjusted price computation can be complex for combined actions (e.g., dividend + bonus on same date) leading to calculation errors.
prior_art: Elton & Gruber (1970) 'Marginal Stockholder Tax Rates and the Clientele Effect' — original ex-dividend pricing research. Frank & Jagannathan (1998) 'Why Do Stock Prices Drop by Less Than the Value of the Dividend?'. In India, Mishra (2005) studies ex-dividend behavior in NSE.
notes: Critical: verify the corporate action type and amount from NSE's corporate action calendar at least one day before ex-date. Compute theoretical_adjusted_price before market open. Monitor F&O adjustment circulars for stocks in F&O segment — NSE adjusts strike prices and lot sizes, which can affect option chain pricing.

name: index_rebalance_flow_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: NSE announces NIFTY 50 / NIFTY Next 50 index rebalances semi-annually (March and September), with the effective date 2-3 weeks after announcement. Stocks being ADDED to the index experience sustained buying pressure from passive funds and ETFs (NIFTY BeES, SBI NIFTY ETF, etc.) that must buy before the effective date. Stocks being REMOVED face selling pressure. The rebalance-driven flow is predictable because: (1) passive fund AUM in India has grown to ₹7+ lakh crore, (2) the buying/selling is mandatory and concentrated in the week before the effective date, (3) the flow size relative to ADV can be 5-20% for NIFTY Next 50 additions. On the EFFECTIVE DATE itself, the final adjustment happens in the closing auction, but intraday we can capture the drift as passive funds execute throughout the day.
universe: Stocks being added/removed from NIFTY 50, NIFTY Next 50, NIFTY 100
stock_filter: Stocks announced for addition/removal, ADV > ₹15 crore

other: passive fund AUM tracking NIFTY indices
estimated shares to be bought/sold by passive funds

indicators.name: estimated_passive_demand
indicators.formula: total_passive_aum * new_index_weight / stock_price (shares to be bought by passives)

conditions: stock is being ADDED to index
rebalance_countdown <= 5 (within 5 trading days of effective date)
demand_to_adv > 10 (meaningful passive demand relative to daily volume)
close > VWAP (passive buying already pushing price up)
long.confirmation: volume_today > 1.3 * ADV_20 (passive flow visibly increasing volume)

conditions: stock is being REMOVED from index
close < VWAP (passive selling pushing price down)
short.confirmation: volume_today > 1.3 * ADV_20

exit.target: 30 bps from entry (capturing a slice of the multi-day drift)
exit.time_stop: exit by 15:15 IST (intraday only, no overnight hold)
exit.signal_exit: cumulative_flow_estimate > 80% (most passive rebalancing complete)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 (market stress may overwhelm rebalance flow)
filters.time_filter: no entries after 14:00 (too close to EOD flatten)
filters.trend_filter: prefer rebalance direction aligned with NIFTY 50 direction
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has earnings/corporate action during rebalance window
other_filters: skip stocks with demand_to_adv < 10 (passive flow too small to move price)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — passive fund growth in India is accelerating, making rebalance flows larger over time. The edge may actually INCREASE as passive AUM grows. However, more front-runners will also enter, compressing returns.

weaknesses: Only 4-6 stocks are added/removed per semi-annual rebalance. The strategy generates trades on only ~10 days per year (5 days before each rebalance).
Index rebalance front-running is increasingly crowded. Hedge funds and prop desks buy additions weeks before the effective date, reducing the residual edge for last-week entries.
Passive fund managers may not execute VWAP — some use closing auction, some spread over multiple days. Our estimate of daily flow may be wrong.
prior_art: Harris & Gurel (1986) 'Price and Volume Effects Associated with Changes in the S&P 500'. Chen, Noronha & Singal (2004) 'The Price Response to S&P 500 Index Additions and Deletions'. In India, Chakrabarti et al. (2005) study index effect in emerging markets. Petajisto (2011) estimates cost of index rebalancing.
notes: Monitor NSE index advisory committee announcements (typically 4 weeks before effective date). Start tracking the announced additions/deletions immediately. The intraday component captures only a fraction of the total rebalance effect — most of the alpha is in the multi-day drift, which requires overnight positions (out of scope for this intraday-only constraint).

name: monthly_settlement_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Monthly F&O settlement (last Thursday of each month) creates predictable intraday patterns due to: (1) futures rollover — open interest migrates from current month to next month, causing basis changes and temporary mispricings, (2) physical settlement for stock futures (since Oct 2019) forces position unwinding if traders don't want delivery, (3) the settlement price is computed from the weighted average of the last 30 minutes, incentivizing specific order flow patterns. On settlement day: morning is dominated by last-minute rollover activity (high volume, range-bound), then the afternoon sees directional positioning as market makers adjust. The key trade: fade unusual divergences between current and next month futures prices (basis spread) during rollover, and trade the directional bias in the last 90 minutes driven by settlement price fixation.
universe: NIFTY 50 and BANK NIFTY (via futures), select stock futures with high OI
stock_filter: NIFTY/BANK NIFTY futures (most liquid), top 10 stock futures by OI

other: current month and next month futures prices

conditions: settlement_window == 'rollover' AND calendar_spread > historical_75th_percentile (next month at unusual premium — rollover buying next month too aggressively)
OR settlement_window == 'settlement_fix' AND NIFTY_close > VWAP AND volume increasing (directional bias up during settlement fixation)
long.confirmation: rollover: calendar_spread starts compressing. settlement_fix: 2 consecutive up bars

conditions: settlement_window == 'rollover' AND calendar_spread < historical_25th_percentile (next month at unusual discount)
OR settlement_window == 'settlement_fix' AND NIFTY_close < VWAP AND volume increasing
short.confirmation: rollover: calendar_spread starts expanding. settlement_fix: 2 consecutive down bars

exit.target: rollover: calendar_spread reverts to median. settlement_fix: 20 bps from entry
exit.stop_loss: rollover: calendar_spread extends to 90th/10th percentile. settlement_fix: 12 bps
exit.time_stop: rollover trades exit by 14:00. settlement_fix trades exit by 15:25
exit.signal_exit: rollover_pct plateaus (rollover activity exhausted)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 (high VIX settlement days are chaotic, patterns break)
filters.time_filter: rollover trades: 09:20-14:00; settlement_fix trades: 14:00-15:25
filters.volume_filter: futures volume > 1.5x normal day (confirms active settlement)
filters.trend_filter: settlement_fix trades follow intraday trend; rollover trades are mean-reversion
filters.event_filter: ONLY on monthly settlement days (12 per year)
other_filters: skip if rollover_pct > 85% by morning (rollover already complete, no signal)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — settlement day patterns are structural, driven by the mechanics of futures expiry and physical delivery. As long as the F&O framework exists, these patterns persist.

weaknesses: Only 12 monthly settlement days per year. The strategy generates very few trades annually and cannot be a standalone income source.
Physical delivery for stock futures means position must be closed regardless — the 'unwinding pressure' signal may be obvious and already priced in by the morning.
Calendar spread percentile thresholds based on historical data may not reflect current cost-of-carry (which changes with interest rates and dividend expectations).
prior_art: Stoll & Whaley (1987) 'Program Trading and Expiration-Day Effects'. Karolyi (1996) 'Stock Market Volatility Around Expiration Days in Japan'. In India, Thenmozhi (2002) studies F&O expiry effects on NSE. SEBI circular on physical delivery settlement.
notes: The settlement price fixation in the last 30 minutes is weighted-average-based, which means large orders in this window disproportionately affect settlement. Some traders intentionally push prices during this window — be aware of potential manipulation. The rollover percentage data is available from NSE's daily F&O reports and also in near real-time from option chain snapshots.

name: budget_day_strategy_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Union Budget day (typically Feb 1) is the single highest-volatility scheduled event in Indian markets. The budget speech starts at 11:00 IST and runs for 90-120 minutes. The intraday pattern: (1) 09:15-11:00: pre-speech compression with low volume, (2) 11:00-12:30: sector-specific knee-jerk reactions as tax changes, capex allocations, and subsidy announcements are read out, (3) 12:30-15:30: digestion and reversion of overreactions. The key insight: sector-specific reactions during the speech (e.g., infrastructure capex increase → infra stocks spike) overshoot by 30-50% because retail traders act on headlines without reading details. By 14:00, as analysts digest the full budget, partial reversion occurs. The strategy: identify sector winners/losers during the speech, then fade the extreme movers after 12:30.
stock_filter: Focus on sectors historically affected by budget: Infra, Defence, Pharma, Auto, FMCG, Tobacco, Real Estate, Banking
session: 12:30-15:15 IST (budget day only — post-speech reversion phase)

conditions: sector_reaction_rank >= 8 (bottom 3 sectors — biggest losers during speech)
long.confirmation: reaction_reversion > 0 (reversion has started)

conditions: sector_reaction_rank <= 2 (top 2 sectors — biggest winners during speech)
short.confirmation: reaction_reversion < 0 (reversion has started)

exit.target: 30-50% reversion of speech reaction (e.g., if lost 200 bps, target 60-100 bps recovery)
exit.stop_loss: reaction extends by 50% beyond speech extreme (e.g., if lost 200 bps, stop at 300 bps loss)
exit.trailing_stop: 20 bps trailing after 30 bps reversion achieved
exit.signal_exit: vix_change_budget > +5 (panic mode, all sectors selling, no reversion)

risk.position_sizing: ₹75K per trade (reduced due to budget day extreme volatility)

filters.vix_filter: no VIX filter on budget day (VIX will be elevated by definition)
filters.time_filter: entry only in 12:30-13:30 window; exit by 15:15
filters.volume_filter: sector stocks trading at > 2x normal volume (confirms interest)
filters.trend_filter: fade extreme sector movers (contrarian by design)
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 20 bps (wider tolerance on budget day)
filters.event_filter: ONLY on budget day (1 per year)
other_filters: skip sectors where budget impact is structural, not cyclical (e.g., new tax on tobacco is permanent, not overreaction)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Very Low — budget day happens once per year and the overreaction/reversion pattern is robust because retail emotional reactions to fiscal policy announcements are deeply behavioral.

weaknesses: Only 1 trade day per year. The strategy's contribution to annual P&L is minimal unless the edge per trade is very large (~50 bps) and size is scaled up.
Distinguishing structural budget changes (new tax, sector deregulation) from cyclical allocations (higher capex for one year) is qualitative and hard to automate.
Slippage on budget day is extreme — true slippage may be 10-20 bps, not 3 bps. The edge math assumes normal slippage which is unrealistic.
