prior_art: Cutler, Poterba & Summers (1989) 'What Moves Stock Prices?' — event-driven returns. In India, Gupta & Kundu (2006) study budget day stock market reactions. Mohanty (2013) analyzes fiscal policy impact on Indian equity sectors.
notes: This is the single highest expected-bps strategy in the portfolio but also the lowest frequency. Consider using options for leverage on budget day: buy sector ETF options to limit downside while capturing the reversion. Historical budget day sector returns (available from NSE) provide a useful calibration dataset.

name: circuit_breaker_proximity_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: NSE has stock-level circuit limits at 5%, 10%, or 20% (depending on the stock's circuit filter band). When a stock approaches within 1-2% of its upper or lower circuit limit, two opposing forces create tradeable patterns: (1) the 'magnet effect' where prices accelerate TOWARD the circuit as momentum traders and stop losses cascade, and (2) 'circuit reversion' where if the stock doesn't hit the circuit, it bounces back sharply as selling/buying exhaustion kicks in. The strategy: when a stock reaches 80% of its circuit distance (e.g., 4% for a 5% circuit stock), monitor for signs of exhaustion. If volume dries up and the approach velocity slows, fade the move for a reversion trade. If volume surges and velocity accelerates, trade the magnet effect toward the circuit. The inefficiency exists because retail traders panic near circuit limits, creating predictable behavioral patterns.
stock_filter: Stocks approaching within 20% of their circuit limit, ADV > ₹10 crore

other: stock circuit limit bands from NSE

indicators.name: circuit_distance_pct
indicators.formula: (circuit_limit - close) / close * 100 for upper; (close - lower_circuit) / close * 100 for lower

indicators.name: approach_velocity
indicators.formula: (circuit_distance_pct[5] - circuit_distance_pct) / 5 (how fast price is approaching circuit per bar)

indicators.name: volume_profile_circuit
indicators.formula: volume_1min / SMA(volume_1min, 20) as price approaches circuit

conditions: stock approaching LOWER circuit (circuit_distance_pct for lower < 2%)
exhaustion_signal == True (velocity slowing, volume declining — sellers exhausted)
close > low_of_last_10_bars (not making new lows — potential bottom forming)
long.confirmation: close > close[1] AND close > close[2] (two consecutive up bars near lower circuit)

conditions: stock approaching UPPER circuit (circuit_distance_pct for upper < 2%)
exhaustion_signal == True (velocity slowing, volume declining — buyers exhausted)
close < high_of_last_10_bars (not making new highs — potential top forming)
short.confirmation: close < close[1] AND close < close[2] (two consecutive down bars near upper circuit)

entry.entry_price: limit order near current price (don't chase into circuit)

exit.target: 50% reversion from circuit approach extreme (e.g., if stock at -4% from prev close and circuit at -5%, target -2%)
exit.stop_loss: stock hits circuit (locks, no exit possible — maximum adverse scenario)
exit.signal_exit: approach_velocity re-accelerates (exhaustion signal was false)

risk.position_sizing: ₹50K per trade (half size due to tail risk of circuit lock)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 25 (in extreme VIX, circuits hit more often and don't revert)
filters.time_filter: skip last 30 min (circuit hits in last 30 min may not revert before EOD)
filters.trend_filter: fade circuit approach only when NIFTY 50 is not moving > 1.5% in same direction
filters.spread_filter: bid-ask < 20 bps (spreads widen near circuit — accept wider tolerance)
filters.event_filter: skip if stock has news/result today (circuit approach may be fundamental, not technical)
other_filters: skip stocks with 5% circuit band (too tight, hits frequently, less signal)
skip if stock was at circuit yesterday (multi-day trending toward circuit is fundamental)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — circuit limit effects are structural features of Indian market microstructure. The magnet effect and reversion are well-documented in academic literature and driven by permanent behavioral factors.

weaknesses: If the stock hits the circuit limit, all orders lock and position becomes un-exitable. For lower circuit, this means unlimited holding period risk until market reopens.
Circuit proximity events are rare for NIFTY 200 stocks (5-10% circuit bands). Most events occur in lower-liquidity stocks where execution is challenging.
The exhaustion signal (declining velocity + volume) has a high false positive rate — sometimes volume drops temporarily before a final surge to circuit.
prior_art: Subrahmanyam (1994) 'Circuit Breakers and Market Volatility'. Kim & Rhee (1997) 'Price Limit Performance: Evidence from the Tokyo Stock Exchange'. Cho et al. (2003) 'Magnet Effect of Price Limits'. In India, SEBI's circuit breaker framework and NSE's dynamic price bands.
notes: CRITICAL RISK: if a stock hits lower circuit, your long position is locked and you cannot exit until the circuit reopens (may be next day or multiple days in extreme cases). This violates the 'no overnight positions' constraint. The strategy must therefore use very small position sizes (₹50K) and accept the tail risk. Consider using put options as insurance if available.

name: tata_group_pairs_v1

TCS (IT) and Tata Motors (auto) are the two largest by market cap but have low fundamental correlation (IT exports vs domestic auto). However, 'Tata premium' sentiment creates intraday co-movement — when TCS rallies strongly, Tata Motors gets a sympathy bid from retail traders. The divergence between fundamental drivers (TCS tracks IT sector, Tata Motors tracks auto/JLR) and sentiment linkage (both trade on Tata brand) creates a pairs opportunity. Additionally, Tata Steel and Tata Power share macro sensitivity to industrial growth, providing a tighter pair. The inefficiency exists because retail traders apply 'Tata brand premium' uniformly, ignoring business-specific drivers.

name: psu_bank_pairs_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: PSU (Public Sector Undertaking) banks share nearly identical business models, regulatory frameworks, government ownership, and macro sensitivity. SBI, Bank of Baroda, PNB, and Canara Bank exhibit 0.65-0.80 daily correlation — among the highest in any Indian sector — because: (1) government policies affect all PSU banks simultaneously (recapitalization, merger mandates, priority sector lending), (2) they compete for the same customer base with similar product offerings, (3) RBI rate decisions impact them identically (similar CASA ratios, NIM sensitivity). When one PSU bank diverges from the group (e.g., SBI reports good numbers but PNB lags on a day with no PNB-specific news), the laggard catches up within 30-60 minutes. This is the tightest pairs opportunity in Indian equities due to the exceptional homogeneity of PSU bank fundamentals.

weaknesses: PSU bank stocks can gap significantly on NPA/provision news for individual banks, creating overnight risk that bleeds into the next day's intraday correlation.
Government actions (merger announcements, recapitalization) can permanently change the relative value of PSU banks, invalidating the equal-weighted group mean.
PNB and Canara Bank have lower liquidity than SBI, creating execution challenges and wider slippage on the divergent stock when it's not SBI.

A market-neutral version would use SBI as the hedge leg against the divergent stock, but this requires larger capital allocation. Consider switching to NIFTY PSU Bank futures as hedge when available.

name: telecom_pairs_v1

Airtel and Jio compete for the same ~1.1 billion subscribers with near-identical pricing plans (post-tariff hikes), similar capex cycles (5G rollout), and shared regulatory framework (TRAI). The intraday correlation between Airtel and Reliance (overall) is 0.35-0.45, but when isolated to telecom-specific news events (tariff hikes, TRAI regulations, spectrum auctions, ARPU data), the correlation spikes to 0.65+. The pairs trade: when telecom-specific news drives one stock but the other lags, fade the laggard expecting catch-up. Vodafone Idea serves as a useful sentiment indicator — when Vi rallies, it signals sector-wide positive sentiment.

other: Jio revenue estimate based on RIL segment reporting

indicators.name: telecom_sentiment
indicators.formula: (airtel_return + ril_return * 0.3 + vi_return * 0.2) / 1.5 (Jio is ~30% of RIL value)

indicators.name: airtel_ril_spread
indicators.formula: airtel_return - ril_return * 0.3 (comparing Airtel to Jio-equivalent RIL move)

conditions: vi_return > 0 (Vi rising confirms telecom sector sentiment is positive, Airtel should follow)
telecom-specific news today (tariff, TRAI, spectrum — not RIL conglomerate news)
long.confirmation: Airtel starts turning up (close > close[1] AND close > VWAP * 0.999)

conditions: vi_return < 0 (Vi falling confirms sector pressure, Airtel should underperform)
short.confirmation: Airtel starts turning down (close < close[1] AND close < VWAP * 1.001)

entry.entry_price: market order on Airtel (more liquid telecom pure-play, no conglomerate noise)

exit.signal_exit: vi_return flips sign (sector sentiment changing)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L on Airtel (directional, using RIL-Jio as reference)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: Vi direction confirms entry direction
filters.event_filter: prefer telecom-specific news days. Skip on RIL result day (conglomerate noise dominates Jio signal)
other_filters: skip if RIL is moving on O2C/Retail news (not Jio-driven, RIL_return * 0.3 is meaningless)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — the Airtel-Jio duopoly is structural, but the RIL-Jio value decomposition (30% weight) is a crude approximation that may shift as Jio prepares for a potential IPO.

weaknesses: Using RIL as a Jio proxy is fundamentally flawed — RIL moves on O2C, Retail, and group-level news. The 0.3 weight is an estimate that may be inaccurate on any given day.
Vodafone Idea is a distressed stock with high speculative activity. Its return direction may reflect speculative flows, not genuine telecom sector sentiment.
Trade frequency is low — telecom-specific news days occur perhaps 2-4 times per month. The strategy is idle most of the time.
prior_art: Pairs trading literature. In India, telecom duopoly dynamics are studied by ICRA and CRISIL in their sector reports. TRAI quarterly performance indicator reports provide subscriber/ARPU data. Morgan Stanley SOTP analysis of RIL for Jio valuation.
notes: If Jio IPOs separately, this strategy becomes significantly cleaner — direct Airtel-Jio pair without the RIL conglomerate noise. Monitor SEBI filings for Jio Platforms listing plans. Also consider using NIFTY Telecom ETF if it becomes liquid enough for intraday trading.

name: energy_pairs_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: India's energy sector has a natural upstream-downstream split: upstream producers (ONGC, Oil India) benefit from high oil prices, while downstream refiner-marketers (IOC, BPCL, HPCL — the 'OMCs') are hurt by high crude because their retail margins get squeezed (government-regulated fuel prices lag crude movements). This creates a NEGATIVE correlation between upstream and downstream on days with significant crude price movements. The pairs trade: when Brent crude moves sharply intraday, go long upstream + short downstream (if crude rises) or vice versa. The inefficiency exists because: (1) retail traders trade all 'oil' stocks the same way, not distinguishing upstream from downstream, (2) the negative correlation only manifests with a 10-20 minute lag as the market processes the crude-margin implication, (3) on non-oil-move days, the stocks are positively correlated (sector sentiment), making the signal regime-dependent.
universe: ONGC, Oil India (upstream), IOC, BPCL, HPCL (downstream OMCs), Reliance (refiner but not OMC)
stock_filter: ONGC: ADV > ₹100 crore. IOC/BPCL/HPCL: ADV > ₹50 crore each

other: Brent crude futures 1-min data (MCX or ICE)

conditions: brent_change_bps > 50 (crude rising — bullish upstream, bearish downstream)
up_down_spread < 10 bps (spread hasn't widened yet — upstream hasn't outperformed)
long.confirmation: up_down_spread starts widening (crosses above 5 bps from below)

conditions: brent_change_bps < -50 (crude falling — bearish upstream, bullish downstream)
short.confirmation: up_down_spread starts narrowing / inverting

entry.entry_price: market order both legs: long upstream + short downstream (crude up) or vice versa

exit.target: up_down_spread reaches ±25 bps (full crude impact priced in)
exit.stop_loss: up_down_spread moves 15 bps against position (wrong direction on crude impact)
exit.trailing_stop: 8 bps trailing after 15 bps spread movement achieved
exit.signal_exit: crude_regime changes to 'non_oil' (crude move reverses, thesis invalidated)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: trade direction must align with crude price direction
filters.event_filter: skip on OPEC meeting day, Indian fuel price revision day (OMC margins directly affected)
other_filters: skip if crude_regime is 'non_oil' (no crude catalyst, upstream-downstream correlation is positive, not negative)
skip if government announces fuel price change today (OMC margins directly reset)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — the upstream-downstream margin dynamic is structural. Until Indian fuel pricing is fully deregulated (unlikely politically), OMC margin squeeze during crude spikes will persist.

weaknesses: The crude_regime threshold (50 bps = 0.5% intraday crude move) may not be reached on most days. The strategy fires only on significant crude move days (~30% of trading days).
Government fuel price interventions (price cuts before elections, subsidy changes) can flip the upstream-downstream dynamic unexpectedly.
ONGC's gas business and Oil India's exploration portfolio mean they're not pure crude oil plays. The upstream-downstream model is an approximation.
prior_art: Energy sector pairs trading is well-established in US markets (XOP vs XLE). Driesprong, Jacobsen & Maat (2008) 'Striking Oil: Another Puzzle?'. In India, PPAC (Petroleum Planning & Analysis Cell) data on OMC under-recoveries provides the empirical basis for crude-margin inverse relationship.
notes: Reliance Industries should NOT be included in the downstream group because its refining margins are market-linked (GRM = gross refining margin, not regulated). RIL is a refiner, not a marketer, and its margin dynamics differ from OMCs. Brent crude data on MCX (CRUDEOIL contract) is available via Kite API for commodities.

name: harmonic_pattern_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Harmonic patterns (AB=CD, Gartley, Butterfly) are Fibonacci-based price structures where the completion point (D) predicts a reversal with 55-60% accuracy. In Indian intraday markets, the AB=CD pattern on 1-min charts identifies institutional VWAP-execution waves: A→B is the initial impulse (institutional entry), B→C is the retracement (profit-taking), C→D is the second leg (institutional continuation). When D completes at a key Fibonacci extension (1.0, 1.272, or 1.618 of AB), the move is likely exhausted and mean-reversion begins. The inefficiency exists because: (1) pattern detection on 1-min bars requires automated scanning across many stocks, (2) Fibonacci levels create self-fulfilling prophecy — enough traders watch them to create real support/resistance, (3) the pattern filters out noise by requiring specific geometric relationships, improving signal quality over random entry.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, 1-min bar range > 0.02% average (sufficient intraday volatility)

indicators.name: swing_detector
indicators.formula: zigzag(close, threshold=0.1%) identifying A, B, C, D pivot points

conditions: bearish ABCD pattern completing at D (AB down, CD down, D is the bottom)
D_price near a VWAP or support level (confluence)
long.confirmation: close > D_price AND RSI(close, 14) > 30 AND RSI turning up

conditions: bullish ABCD pattern completing at D (AB up, CD up, D is the top)
D_price near a resistance level or VWAP overhead
short.confirmation: close < D_price AND RSI(close, 14) < 70 AND RSI turning down

entry.entry_price: limit order at D_price level on pattern completion

exit.target: 38.2% retracement of the CD leg (first Fibonacci pullback target)
exit.time_stop: exit after 20 bars (pattern reversal should be quick)
exit.signal_exit: price closes beyond D by > 1 ATR(14) (pattern failed)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 (patterns are less reliable in high volatility)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: volume at D-point bar > SMA(volume, 20) (confirms interest at completion)
filters.trend_filter: prefer D-point reversals against the short-term trend (contrarian)
filters.event_filter: skip on high-news days (patterns are technical, not event-driven)
other_filters: pattern must complete within 30 bars from A to D (not stale patterns)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — harmonic patterns are well-known in technical analysis communities. However, automated detection on 1-min bars is uncommon, and the Fibonacci self-fulfilling prophecy effect provides a structural (not just informational) edge.

weaknesses: Zigzag and pivot detection on 1-min bars is extremely noisy. The 0.1% threshold generates many false pivots, and pattern detection has high look-ahead bias if not carefully implemented.
Fibonacci levels have no fundamental basis — they work only to the extent that other traders believe in them. In Indian markets, harmonic pattern awareness is growing but still limited.
The pattern's tolerance ranges (0.836-1.322 for ratio, 0.382-0.886 for retracement) are wide enough that many random price movements will falsely qualify as patterns.
prior_art: Carney (1999) 'The Harmonic Trader' — original harmonic pattern framework. Pesavento & Jouflas (2008) 'Trade What You See'. In India, harmonic patterns are popular on tradingview.com among Indian retail traders, but systematic 1-min implementation is rare.
notes: Pattern detection algorithm: use a zigzag indicator with 0.1% threshold to identify swing highs/lows. Then scan for 4-point patterns (ABCD) where the ratios match. Confluence with VWAP or round number levels significantly improves win rate. Consider using fractal detection (strategy 146) as an alternative pivot identification.

name: elliott_impulse_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: A simplified Elliott Wave impulse detection: instead of full 5-3 wave counting (which is subjective and unreliable on 1-min bars), we detect WAVE 3 characteristics — the strongest, most tradeable wave. Wave 3 has specific measurable properties: (1) it's the longest wave (>1.618x Wave 1 length), (2) volume is highest during Wave 3, (3) RSI reaches its most extreme reading during Wave 3. We identify a potential Wave 3 by detecting: a completed Wave 1 (impulse) + Wave 2 (retracement of 38.2-61.8% of Wave 1) + breakout above Wave 1 high with surge in volume. The trade enters at the Wave 2 completion / Wave 3 beginning and targets the 1.618 Fibonacci extension of Wave 1. The inefficiency exists because Elliott Wave is typically applied on daily/weekly charts; the 1-min application captures institutional order flow waves that repeat 3-5 times per session.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, intraday range > 0.5% average

indicators.name: wave1_detection
indicators.formula: impulse move > 15 bps within 5-10 bars, identified by zigzag(0.1%)

indicators.name: volume_surge_w3
indicators.formula: volume_1min / SMA(volume_1min, 20) at wave3 breakout bar

long.confirmation: RSI_14 > 50 AND RSI_14 > RSI_14[1] (momentum confirming)

short.confirmation: RSI_14 < 50 AND RSI_14 < RSI_14[1]

entry.entry_price: market order at wave3 breakout confirmation

exit.target: 1.618 * wave1_length extension from wave2 end (standard Wave 3 target)
exit.stop_loss: wave2 low (bullish) or wave2 high (bearish) violated (wave count invalid)
exit.time_stop: exit after 30 bars (wave3 should complete quickly)
exit.signal_exit: RSI_14 reaches extreme (>80 for long, <20 for short) — wave3 likely exhausting

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per trade, scale to ₹1.5L if wave1_length > 30 bps (strong pattern)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX > 12 AND < 25 (need some vol for wave patterns but not chaotic)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: wave direction aligned with 50-bar EMA slope on 1-min chart
filters.event_filter: skip on high-impact news days (wave patterns are noise during events)
other_filters: wave1 must have completed within last 20 bars (fresh pattern, not stale)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — Elliott Wave is subjective on higher timeframes but the simplified 3-indicator approach (impulse + retracement + breakout) is more systematic. The edge is in the automation, not the theory.

weaknesses: Elliott Wave counting is inherently subjective — even the simplified version has ambiguity in identifying wave boundaries on noisy 1-min data.
The 0.382-0.618 retracement range for Wave 2 is wide. Many random pullbacks will qualify, generating false Wave 3 signals.
Wave 3 targets (1.618 extension) may not be reached intraday for lower-volatility stocks, causing frequent time-stop exits with partial gains.
prior_art: Elliott (1938) 'The Wave Principle'. Prechter & Frost (2001) 'Elliott Wave Principle'. Neely (1990) 'Mastering Elliott Wave'. In India, Elliott Wave is popular in technical analysis circles but systematic automated implementation is rare.
notes: The key simplification: we don't count all 5 waves. We only identify Wave 1 (impulse), Wave 2 (retracement), and trade the Wave 3 extension. Waves 4 and 5 are ignored. This avoids the primary criticism of Elliott Wave — subjective wave counting — by reducing the pattern to three objective measurements.

name: market_profile_poc_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Market Profile theory (developed by J. Peter Steidlmayer at CBOT) organizes price-time data into a distribution showing where volume was transacted. The Point of Control (POC) — the price level with the highest traded volume — acts as a magnet for price during range-bound days and as a launchpad during trend days. On 1-min Indian intraday charts, we compute the developing POC and Value Area (VA: price range containing 70% of volume) in real-time. When price deviates beyond the VA boundary but then fails to sustain the breakout, it reverts to POC. The inefficiency exists because: (1) Market Profile requires volume-at-price computation which standard charting platforms don't compute in real-time for Indian stocks, (2) the developing VA changes throughout the day, requiring dynamic recalculation, (3) most Indian traders use traditional support/resistance, not volume-based levels.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents + NIFTY 50 / BANK NIFTY index
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, sufficient tick count for volume-at-price computation
session: 10:00-15:15 IST (need 45 min for initial profile development)

other: volume-at-price distribution (computed from 1-min OHLCV by allocating bar volume across bar range)

indicators.name: POC
indicators.formula: price_level with max(volume_at_price) from session start to current bar

indicators.name: VA_high
indicators.formula: upper boundary of price range containing 70% of total session volume

indicators.name: VA_breakout_failed
indicators.formula: (close was > VA_high within last 5 bars AND close now < VA_high) OR (close was < VA_low AND close now > VA_low)

conditions: VA_breakout_failed == True (price broke below VA_low but came back)
POC_distance_bps < -10 (still below POC — room to revert up)
long.confirmation: close > close[1] AND volume_1min > SMA(volume, 10) (buying interest at VA boundary)

conditions: VA_breakout_failed == True (price broke above VA_high but came back)
POC_distance_bps > 10 (still above POC — room to revert down)
short.confirmation: close < close[1] AND volume_1min > SMA(volume, 10)

entry.entry_price: limit order at VA boundary level

exit.target: price reaches POC (full mean reversion to highest volume node)
exit.stop_loss: price breaks back beyond VA boundary by > 10 bps (failed reversion)
exit.trailing_stop: 5 bps trailing after 50% of POC distance achieved
exit.signal_exit: POC shifts significantly (>10 bps) due to heavy volume at new price level

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 (Market Profile works best in range-bound markets)
filters.time_filter: wait until 10:00 for profile to develop. No new trades after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: total session volume > 0.5x typical (sufficient data for profile)
filters.trend_filter: skip on strong trend days where VA_high keeps rising (single-distribution trend day)
filters.event_filter: skip on event days (profile is distorted by event-driven volume concentration)
other_filters: VA width must be > 20 bps (too narrow = insufficient range for reversion)
profile shape must be roughly Gaussian (not bimodal — bimodal suggests two competing levels)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — Market Profile is well-established in US futures markets but underutilized in Indian equities. As volume profile tools become available on Indian platforms (TradingView, Zerodha), the edge may compress.

weaknesses: Volume-at-price computation from OHLCV bars is an approximation — we distribute bar volume uniformly across the bar's range, which is inaccurate for bars with large wicks.
On trend days (estimated 20-30% of sessions), the Market Profile is one-directional with no reversion to POC. The strategy loses on trend days.
The developing POC and VA boundaries shift throughout the day, making the 'target' a moving target. A POC shift mid-trade can invalidate the exit level.
prior_art: Steidlmayer & Koy (1986) 'Markets and Market Logic' — original Market Profile. Dalton, Jones & Dalton (1990) 'Mind Over Markets'. In India, Market Profile is taught by traders like Bramesh (Bramesh Tech) and used by prop firms in Mumbai.
notes: Volume-at-price construction: divide the day's price range into bins of 0.05% width. For each 1-min bar, distribute the bar's volume evenly across all bins that fall within the bar's high-low range. The bin with the highest cumulative volume is POC. VA is computed by expanding from POC outward until 70% of volume is captured.

name: order_block_entry_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Order Blocks (OBs) are the last opposite-direction candle before a strong impulse move — theoretically marking where institutional orders were placed. Fair Value Gaps (FVGs) are three-candle patterns where the wick of candle 1 doesn't overlap with the wick of candle 3, creating an 'unfilled' price gap that price tends to revisit. In Indian 1-min intraday charts, OBs and FVGs identify zones where institutional algorithmic orders created supply/demand imbalances. When price returns to these zones, the remaining unfilled orders provide support (bullish OB) or resistance (bearish OB). The inefficiency exists because: (1) OB/FVG analysis (ICT methodology) is popular among forex retail traders but barely adopted in Indian equity markets, (2) identifying OBs requires tracking every candle's relationship to subsequent impulses, which is computationally intensive, (3) the zones are specific enough to provide precise entry levels with tight stops.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents + NIFTY 50 / BANK NIFTY index
stock_filter: ADV > ₹40 crore, 1-min bar range > 0.02% average

indicators.name: bullish_OB
indicators.formula: last bearish candle (close < open) before a bullish impulse of > 10 bps within next 3 bars. OB zone = [low, high] of that bearish candle.

indicators.name: bearish_OB
indicators.formula: last bullish candle (close > open) before a bearish impulse of > 10 bps within next 3 bars. OB zone = [low, high] of that bullish candle.

indicators.name: bullish_FVG
indicators.formula: gap where candle[0].high < candle[2].low (3-bar pattern with upward gap). FVG zone = [candle[0].high, candle[2].low]

indicators.name: bearish_FVG
indicators.formula: gap where candle[0].low > candle[2].high (3-bar pattern with downward gap). FVG zone = [candle[2].high, candle[0].low]

indicators.name: zone_revisit
indicators.formula: 1 if current close enters a previously identified OB or FVG zone for the first time

conditions: zone_revisit == 1 for a bullish OB or bullish FVG
close enters the OB/FVG zone from above (pullback into demand zone)
overall intraday trend is bullish (close > VWAP)
zone is less than 60 bars old (fresh zone)
long.confirmation: bullish engulfing candle or hammer at the zone boundary

conditions: zone_revisit == 1 for a bearish OB or bearish FVG
close enters the OB/FVG zone from below (rally into supply zone)
overall intraday trend is bearish (close < VWAP)
zone is less than 60 bars old
short.confirmation: bearish engulfing candle or shooting star at the zone boundary

exit.target: re-test of the impulse move high (bullish OB) or low (bearish OB) that created the zone
exit.stop_loss: 2 bps beyond the far edge of the OB/FVG zone (zone fully breached = invalidated)
exit.signal_exit: close breaks through the OB/FVG zone entirely (zone failed to hold)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 (zones are more reliable in moderate volatility)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: impulse move that created the OB/FVG had volume > 1.3x SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: trade OBs in direction of VWAP trend (bullish OBs when above VWAP, bearish below)
filters.event_filter: skip on major news days (zones from before the news are invalidated)
other_filters: only use zones that haven't been revisited yet (first touch only)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — ICT methodology is gaining popularity on YouTube/social media in India but is still niche compared to traditional technical analysis. As adoption grows, OB/FVG zones may become self-defeating (too many limit orders at the zone).

weaknesses: Order Block theory assumes institutional orders create identifiable candle patterns, but in reality, institutional algorithms distribute orders across many candles, not concentrated in one.
FVGs on 1-min bars are common (hundreds per session) — without strict filtering, the signal-to-noise ratio is very low. The age limit (60 bars) and volume filter help but don't fully solve this.
The 'first touch only' rule means zones can only be traded once. If the first touch results in a loss, the zone is removed, even if the second touch would have worked.
prior_art: Inner Circle Trader (ICT) methodology (Michael Huddleston) — popularized OB/FVG concepts in forex. Wyckoff (1931) 'The Richard D. Wyckoff Method of Trading and Investing in Stocks' for supply/demand zone theory. In India, ICT methodology is taught by several YouTube channels but formal academic validation is lacking.
notes: OB identification is retrospective (you see the OB only after the impulse move). This is fine because we trade the REVISIT, not the initial impulse. Maintain a rolling list of active OB and FVG zones (max 60 bars old) for each monitored stock. When price approaches any active zone, trigger the zone_revisit signal.

name: ichimoku_cloud_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Ichimoku Kinko Hyo ('one glance equilibrium chart') provides a multi-factor trend assessment system: Tenkan-sen (conversion), Kijun-sen (base), Senkou Span A/B (cloud), and Chikou Span (lagging). On 1-min Indian intraday charts, Ichimoku with adapted parameters (9/26/52 replaced with 7/22/44 for 1-min frequency) provides: (1) trend direction via cloud color and price position relative to cloud, (2) momentum via Tenkan/Kijun cross, (3) support/resistance via cloud boundaries. The inefficiency exists because: (1) Ichimoku is designed for daily charts (Japanese trading week = 9/26/52 days); the 1-min adaptation requires parameter recalibration, (2) most Indian traders use Ichimoku with default daily parameters even on intraday, getting lagged signals, (3) the 'cloud twist' signal (Senkou A crosses Senkou B) on 1-min charts predicts trend changes 22 bars ahead, providing a forward-looking signal unique to Ichimoku.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore, sufficient intraday range (>0.5% typical daily range)
session: 09:30-15:15 IST (need 44 bars for full Ichimoku initialization)

conditions: close > senkou_span_a AND close > senkou_span_b (price above cloud — bullish)
long.confirmation: tenkan crosses above kijun (TK bullish cross event)

conditions: close < senkou_span_a AND close < senkou_span_b (price below cloud — bearish)
short.confirmation: tenkan crosses below kijun (TK bearish cross event)

entry.entry_price: market order at TK cross confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: price enters the cloud (close between senkou_span_a and senkou_span_b)
exit.trailing_stop: kijun_sen acts as trailing stop (exit if close crosses kijun against position)
exit.signal_exit: TK cross reverses (tenkan crosses kijun against position direction)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 22 (Ichimoku needs trending markets, not dead or chaotic)
filters.time_filter: wait until 09:30 (need 44 bars for full initialization at 7/22/44); stop at 14:30
filters.trend_filter: all 5 Ichimoku signals must agree (price above cloud, TK bullish, chikou bullish, green future cloud)
filters.event_filter: skip on range-bound choppy days (Ichimoku generates false crosses in ranges)
other_filters: skip if cloud thickness < 3 bps (thin cloud = weak trend, unreliable signal)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — Ichimoku is well-known but rarely calibrated for 1-min intraday. The adapted parameters (7/22/44) for 1-min bars are non-standard and provide an edge over traders using default 9/26/52 on intraday charts.

weaknesses: Ichimoku is a lagging indicator system — all signals are confirmed after the move has started. On 1-min bars, even the adapted parameters create 5-10 bar lag, missing the initial move.
Range-bound days generate multiple false TK crosses. The 'all 5 signals agree' filter reduces false signals but also reduces trade frequency significantly.
The forward-projected cloud (22 bars ahead) uses current data to project future support/resistance, but new information in those 22 bars can completely change the cloud structure.
prior_art: Hosoda Goichi (1969) original Ichimoku development. Sasaki & Takita (2015) 'Ichimoku Charts: An Introduction to Ichimoku Kinko Clouds'. Elliott & Kildahl (2007) 'Ichimoku Charts' — English language reference. In India, Ichimoku is featured on Kite/TradingView but with daily parameters.
notes: Parameter rationale: 7/22/44 instead of 9/26/52 because 1-min bars generate ~375 bars per session vs ~250 daily bars per year. The ratio 7:22:44 ≈ 1:3:6 matches the original 9:26:52 ≈ 1:3:6 structure but for faster timeframes. Some practitioners use 9/26/52 even on 1-min; we find 7/22/44 more responsive.

name: fractal_breakout_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Williams Fractals identify swing highs and lows as 5-bar patterns where the middle bar has the highest high (up fractal) or lowest low (down fractal) compared to the 2 bars on each side. On 1-min Indian intraday charts, fractal breakouts — when price breaks above an up fractal or below a down fractal — signal the start of a new micro-trend lasting 5-15 minutes. The inefficiency exists because: (1) fractals are commonly used on daily charts but rarely on 1-min charts where they identify institutional price discovery waves, (2) the 5-bar pattern provides natural noise filtering (random 1-bar spikes don't create fractals), (3) fractal levels align with where institutional limit orders cluster (at recent swing points), making breakouts significant. We combine fractals with the Alligator indicator (Bill Williams) to filter breakouts in trending vs ranging conditions.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹40 crore, sufficient intraday volatility (>0.4% daily range)

indicators.name: fractal_up
indicators.formula: 1 if high[2] > high[0] AND high[2] > high[1] AND high[2] > high[3] AND high[2] > high[4] else 0 (confirmed 2 bars after formation)

indicators.name: fractal_down
indicators.formula: 1 if low[2] < low[0] AND low[2] < low[1] AND low[2] < low[3] AND low[2] < low[4] else 0

conditions: alligator_lips > alligator_teeth > alligator_jaw (Alligator is 'eating' — trending up)
fractal_up_level is within last 20 bars (fresh fractal, not stale)
long.confirmation: close > fractal_up_level for 2 consecutive bars (sustained breakout)

short.confirmation: close < fractal_down_level for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order at confirmation (second bar beyond fractal level)

exit.stop_loss: fractal level violated in reverse (close back below up fractal for longs, above down fractal for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: alligator_teeth acts as trailing stop (exit if close crosses teeth against position)
exit.signal_exit: opposite fractal forms (up fractal after long entry signals potential top)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: breakout bar volume > SMA(volume, 10) (volume confirms breakout)
filters.trend_filter: Alligator must be trending (lips/teeth/jaw separated, not intertwined/sleeping)
filters.event_filter: no filter (fractals adapt to any market condition)
other_filters: skip if Alligator lines are intertwined (market is ranging, breakouts fail)
fractal level must be at least 5 bps away from current price (meaningful breakout)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — Williams Fractals are well-known but the combination with Alligator on 1-min bars is non-standard. The 5-bar noise filter provides a structural advantage over simpler breakout strategies.

weaknesses: Fractals are confirmed 2 bars after formation (need bars -1, 0, +1, +2 beyond the fractal bar). By the time the breakout is confirmed, the move may be 30-50% complete.
On range-bound days, fractal levels cluster densely, generating many false breakouts. The Alligator filter helps but doesn't eliminate all false signals.
The Alligator indicator with shifted SMAs introduces additional lag — the 'lips/teeth/jaw separated' condition confirms trends that are already well-established.
prior_art: Williams (1995) 'Trading Chaos' — original fractal and Alligator system. Williams (1998) 'New Trading Dimensions'. Mandelbrot (1982) 'The Fractal Geometry of Nature' for mathematical fractal theory. In India, Williams' system is taught in advanced technical analysis courses.
notes: The Alligator 'sleeping' state (lines intertwined) is as informative as the 'eating' state — it signals to AVOID trading. Approximately 30-40% of the session may be in 'sleeping' mode, naturally reducing trade frequency. Consider using Awesome Oscillator (AO) as additional confirmation — positive AO for long fractals, negative for short.

name: demark_sequential_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Tom DeMark's TD Sequential identifies trend exhaustion by counting consecutive bars that close higher (or lower) than the close 4 bars earlier. A 'setup' phase counts 1-9; a completed 9-count signals potential exhaustion. This is followed by a 'countdown' phase (13-count) for stronger confirmation. On 1-min Indian intraday charts, the 9-count setup identifies micro-trend exhaustion points where momentum is about to reverse. The inefficiency exists because: (1) TD Sequential is complex to implement correctly (many rules for perfection, recycling, and qualification), (2) most Indian traders use simple RSI overbought/oversold instead of the more precise TD Sequential counting, (3) the 4-bar lookback comparison filters out noise better than 1-bar momentum indicators. The signal is contrarian — we fade the trend at the 9-count completion.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹50 crore

indicators.name: td_buy_setup
indicators.formula: consecutive count of bars where close < close[4]. Count resets on close >= close[4]. Signal on count == 9.

indicators.name: td_sell_setup
indicators.formula: consecutive count of bars where close > close[4]. Count resets on close <= close[4]. Signal on count == 9.

indicators.name: td_perfection_buy
indicators.formula: 1 if low of bar 8 or 9 <= low of bar 6 (DeMark perfection rule for buy setup)

indicators.name: td_perfection_sell
indicators.formula: 1 if high of bar 8 or 9 >= high of bar 6

conditions: td_buy_setup == 9 (9 consecutive bars closing below close[4] — downtrend exhaustion)
close > low of setup bar 9 (first sign of bounce)
long.confirmation: close > close[1] on the bar immediately after setup completion

short.confirmation: close < close[1] on the bar immediately after setup completion

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: close crosses above close[4] (trend reversal confirmed by the same DeMark logic)
exit.stop_loss: 12 bps from entry (absolute stop) OR new bar extends the setup beyond 9 (count 10 — extreme exhaustion overshoot)
exit.time_stop: exit after 15 bars (if reversal hasn't materialized, setup failed)
exit.signal_exit: close resumes the previous trend (close < close[4] again for a buy setup entry)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per trade, increase to ₹1.5L if both perfection and RSI extremes confirm

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 (perfected setups are more reliable in moderate vol)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: declining volume on the last 3 bars of the setup (confirms exhaustion)
filters.trend_filter: contrarian by design — fade the trend at count 9
filters.event_filter: skip during strong macro events (trending market can extend setup beyond 13)
other_filters: skip if setup completed in < 9 consecutive minutes (overly fast, likely noise)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — TD Sequential is complex enough that most traders implement it incorrectly or use simplified versions. The full perfection rules and qualification criteria are rarely coded correctly, preserving edge for proper implementations.

weaknesses: The 4-bar comparison offset on 1-min charts means setups complete in minimum 9 minutes. On strong trend days, the trend continues well beyond the 9-count, hitting stops.
TD Sequential has many nuanced rules (recycling, qualifier, TDST levels) that are difficult to implement correctly. Partial implementation may degrade signal quality.
Contrarian signals in strong trends are inherently risky — 'catching falling knives' is the primary failure mode, and on trend days this strategy will underperform badly.
prior_art: DeMark (1994) 'The New Science of Technical Analysis'. DeMark (1997) 'New Market Timing Techniques'. Bloomberg's DeMark indicators (TD Sequential, TD Combo) are available on the Bloomberg terminal. In India, TD Sequential is used by some proprietary trading desks in Mumbai.
notes: The 'perfection' rule is critical — unperfected setups have significantly lower win rates (~45% vs ~55% for perfected). Always check perfection before entering. The countdown phase (13-count after setup) provides stronger signals but completes less frequently on 1-min charts. Consider using countdown for higher-conviction, lower-frequency trades.

name: pivot_camarilla_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Camarilla pivot points, derived from the previous day's OHLC using specific multipliers (1.1/12, 1.1/6, 1.1/4, 1.1/2), create 8 intraday support/resistance levels (S1-S4, R1-R4) that are more tightly clustered around the previous close than standard pivot points. The key Camarilla trade: price bouncing between S3/R3 levels (mean reversion zone) accounts for ~65% of trading days, while S4/R4 breakouts signal trend days (~35%). In Indian markets, Camarilla levels work particularly well because: (1) the previous close anchors retail trader sentiment heavily (Indian retail psychology fixates on daily P&L), (2) institutional VWAP algorithms naturally create support/resistance near these mathematically derived levels, (3) the S3/R3 bounce is a self-fulfilling prophecy — Indian technical analysis channels widely teach Camarilla, creating order flow at these levels.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents + NIFTY 50 / BANK NIFTY index
stock_filter: ADV > ₹40 crore, previous day's range > 0.5%

other: previous day OHLC for pivot computation

indicators.name: cam_zone
indicators.formula: 'range' if close between cam_S3 and cam_R3; 'breakout_up' if close > cam_R4; 'breakout_down' if close < cam_S4; 'transition' otherwise

conditions: (cam_zone == 'range' AND close <= cam_S3 * 1.001) — bouncing at S3 support
OR (cam_zone == 'breakout_up' AND close > cam_R4) — breakout above R4 (trend day)
close > low of last 3 bars (for S3 bounce) OR volume surge (for R4 breakout)
long.confirmation: S3 bounce: close > cam_S3 AND close > close[1]. R4 breakout: close > cam_R4 for 2 bars with volume > 1.5x average

conditions: (cam_zone == 'range' AND close >= cam_R3 * 0.999) — rejecting at R3 resistance
OR (cam_zone == 'breakout_down' AND close < cam_S4) — breakdown below S4
close < high of last 3 bars (for R3 rejection) OR volume surge (for S4 breakdown)
short.confirmation: R3 rejection: close < cam_R3 AND close < close[1]. S4 breakdown: close < cam_S4 for 2 bars with volume > 1.5x average

entry.entry_price: limit at S3/R3 level (bounce trades), market order (breakout trades)

exit.target: S3 bounce → target cam_R3 (full range traverse). R4 breakout → 20 bps beyond R4.
exit.stop_loss: S3 bounce → below S4 (support broken). R4 breakout → back below R3 (false breakout).
exit.trailing_stop: 10 bps trailing for breakout trades after 15 bps profit
exit.time_stop: exit after 45 bars (range trades); 30 bars (breakout trades)
exit.signal_exit: cam_zone changes (transition between range and breakout mode)

risk.position_sizing: ₹1L per trade. Increase to ₹1.5L for breakout trades with volume confirmation.

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 for range trades (S3/R3 bounce). No VIX filter for breakout trades.
filters.time_filter: no range trades first 5 min; breakout trades can start immediately
filters.volume_filter: breakout trades require volume > 1.5x average at breakout bar
filters.trend_filter: range trades: NIFTY range-bound. Breakout trades: NIFTY trending in breakout direction
filters.event_filter: prefer range trades on non-event days; breakout trades on event days
other_filters: skip if previous day range was < 0.3% (Camarilla levels too tight, no room for trades)
skip if gap > S4 or R4 at open (levels already breached by gap)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — Camarilla pivots are well-known among Indian retail traders. The edge is in correctly identifying range vs breakout days (which most traders don't do) and the self-fulfilling prophecy at S3/R3 levels.

weaknesses: On gap-up/gap-down days (opening beyond S4/R4), Camarilla levels are already breached and provide no useful structure for the day.
The 65/35 range/breakout day split is an average — in volatile regimes (VIX > 20), breakout days may dominate, and the range strategy will generate consecutive losses.
Camarilla levels are static (computed from previous day) and don't adapt to intraday price discovery. VWAP-based dynamic levels may be more appropriate.
prior_art: Nick Stott — original Camarilla equation (1989). Pivot point trading methodology is covered in Murphy (1999) 'Technical Analysis of the Financial Markets'. In India, Camarilla pivots are featured on moneycontrol.com and are standard on Zerodha Kite charts.
notes: Compute Camarilla levels before market open using previous day's OHLC data. The levels are fixed for the entire session. The key decision is early: is today a range day (trade S3/R3 bounces) or a trend day (trade S4/R4 breakouts)? India VIX level and gap size at open are useful predictors of day type.

name: heikin_ashi_trend_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Heikin Ashi (HA) candles smooth price action by averaging: HA_close = (O+H+L+C)/4, HA_open = (prev_HA_open + prev_HA_close)/2, HA_high = max(H, HA_open, HA_close), HA_low = min(L, HA_open, HA_close). The smoothing creates cleaner trends with fewer reversals, making trend identification on noisy 1-min bars more reliable. Key HA signals: (1) consecutive green HA candles with no lower wick = strong uptrend, (2) HA candles with both wicks = indecision/reversal, (3) consecutive red HA with no upper wick = strong downtrend. The inefficiency exists because: (1) most Indian retail traders use regular candles on 1-min charts, getting whipsawed by noise, (2) HA smoothing reveals the 'true' trend by filtering single-bar spikes that trigger false signals on regular charts, (3) HA color changes lag regular candles by 1-2 bars, but this lag is a feature — it confirms real reversals, not noise.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹40 crore

indicators.name: HA_strength
indicators.formula: 'strong_up' if HA_color == 'green' AND HA_low == HA_open (no lower wick); 'strong_down' if HA_color == 'red' AND HA_high == HA_open (no upper wick); 'weak' otherwise

conditions: HA_strength == 'strong_up' on the first green bar (no lower wick — conviction)
close > VWAP (actual price confirms HA signal)
HA_trend_count >= 2 for green (at least 2 consecutive green HA bars)
long.confirmation: EMA(close, 9) > EMA(close, 21) on actual (non-HA) price (dual confirmation)

conditions: HA_strength == 'strong_down' on the first red bar (no upper wick)
short.confirmation: EMA(close, 9) < EMA(close, 21) on actual price

entry.entry_price: market order at confirmation bar close (using actual close, not HA close)

exit.target: 20 bps from entry (actual price, not HA price)
exit.trailing_stop: HA color changes to opposite (red for longs, green for shorts) — HA trailing stop
exit.signal_exit: HA_strength changes to 'weak' (HA candle has both wicks — indecision)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 25 (need trends, not dead or chaotic markets)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: volume on color change bar > SMA(volume, 10)
filters.trend_filter: HA trend direction must align with 50-bar EMA slope on actual price
filters.event_filter: no filter (HA naturally smooths event-driven spikes)
other_filters: skip if previous HA trend was < 3 bars long (choppy, color changes are noise)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — Heikin Ashi is well-known but the specific entry criteria (color change + no-wick strength + EMA confirmation) create a more selective signal than simple HA color following.

weaknesses: HA candles are derived from actual prices, not market-observable. The HA_open is synthetic and can't be traded — all entries/exits must use actual prices, creating a disconnect between signal and execution.
HA smoothing inherently lags actual price action by 1-2 bars. In fast-moving markets, the entry is already 5-10 bps late, reducing the reward-to-risk ratio.
The 'no lower wick = strong uptrend' rule is overly strict on 1-min bars — many genuine trends have occasional bars with tiny lower wicks that break the signal.
prior_art: Munehisa Homma — historical Japanese candlestick analysis. Valcu (2004) 'Using Heikin Ashi Technique' in Technical Analysis of Stocks & Commodities. In India, HA charts are available on Zerodha Kite and are taught in basic technical analysis courses.
notes: CRITICAL: all order placement must use actual prices, not HA prices. HA prices are synthetic and not market-observable. The strategy uses HA for SIGNAL GENERATION only and actual prices for EXECUTION. This distinction is often missed by traders who place limit orders at HA levels. Consider relaxing the 'no wick' rule to 'wick < 20% of HA body' to allow minor wicks in strong trends.

name: elder_impulse_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Dr. Alexander Elder's Impulse System combines two indicators — EMA(13) for trend and MACD histogram for momentum — to color-code each bar as green (trend+momentum aligned bullish), red (aligned bearish), or blue (conflicting). The system's strict rule: NEVER short green bars, NEVER go long on red bars. On 1-min Indian intraday charts with adapted parameters (EMA(9) and MACD(9,21,7) for faster response), the Impulse System identifies periods of aligned momentum that last 5-15 bars, followed by transitions. The inefficiency exists because: (1) Elder's system is designed as a FILTER, not a signal — most implementations miss this and trade the color change directly, (2) the dual-indicator alignment (trend + momentum) provides higher-quality signals than either alone, (3) the 'forbidden trade' rule (no shorts in green, no longs in red) is psychologically difficult for traders who want to fade the move, creating persistent edge for followers.
stock_filter: ADV > ₹40 crore

indicators.name: impulse_color
indicators.formula: 'green' if EMA_9 > EMA_9[1] AND MACD_histogram > MACD_histogram[1]; 'red' if EMA_9 < EMA_9[1] AND MACD_histogram < MACD_histogram[1]; 'blue' otherwise

conditions: impulse_color changes from 'red' or 'blue' to 'green' (momentum alignment bullish)
long.confirmation: impulse_color remains 'green' for 2 consecutive bars (confirmed alignment)

conditions: impulse_color changes from 'green' or 'blue' to 'red' (momentum alignment bearish)
short.confirmation: impulse_color remains 'red' for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market order at second confirmed color bar close

exit.stop_loss: 10 bps from entry OR impulse_color turns 'red' (for longs) / 'green' (for shorts)
exit.trailing_stop: EMA_9 acts as trailing stop — exit if close crosses EMA_9 against position
exit.signal_exit: impulse_color changes to opposite color (full reversal confirmed)

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX between 12 and 22 (need trends for color alignment to persist)
filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min (EMA needs warm-up) or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: volume on color change bar > SMA(volume, 10)
filters.trend_filter: impulse direction aligned with NIFTY 50 intraday direction
filters.event_filter: skip during whipsaw periods (rapid green-blue-red transitions within 5 bars)
other_filters: skip if impulse_color has changed > 5 times in last 30 bars (choppy, no persistent trends)
NEVER long on red bars, NEVER short on green bars (Elder's core rule)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — Elder's system is well-published but the adapted MACD(9,21,7) parameters for 1-min bars are non-standard. The 'forbidden trade' discipline is psychologically hard for most traders, reducing crowding.

weaknesses: The dual-indicator system generates many 'blue' (neutral) bars — approximately 40-50% of the session. During these periods, no trades are taken, reducing opportunities.
On range-bound days, the impulse color alternates rapidly between green, blue, and red, generating whipsaw losses. The 5-change-per-30-bar filter helps but doesn't fully prevent this.
The MACD histogram on 1-min bars is very noisy and can flip positive/negative on minor price fluctuations, creating false color changes.
prior_art: Elder (1993) 'Trading for a Living' — original Impulse System. Elder (2002) 'Come Into My Trading Room' — refined version. Elder (2014) 'The New Trading for a Living' — updated parameters. In India, Elder's system is taught in advanced TA courses and available as an indicator on TradingView.
notes: Parameter adaptation: Elder's original 13/12/26/9 (EMA/MACD) are for daily charts. For 1-min, we use 9/9/21/7, which is approximately 0.7x the daily parameters, scaled for the higher frequency. The key insight is using the Impulse System as a FILTER (don't trade against the color) rather than as a standalone signal. Pair with other entry signals (VWAP bounce, RSI oversold) for best results.

name: vwap_rsi_volume_hybrid_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Intraday price tends to revert toward VWAP, but naked VWAP mean-reversion suffers from high false-positive rates. Adding RSI as an oversold/overbought filter and requiring abnormal volume (>1.5x 20-bar average) as confirmation materially improves hit rate. The inefficiency persists because most retail participants trade VWAP or RSI in isolation, and the triple-confirmation window is narrow enough (typically <5 minutes per day per stock) that institutional algos focused on larger time-scales ignore it. The edge is further protected by restricting to mid-cap names (NIFTY Next 50) where algo coverage is thinner than in NIFTY 50.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹50 Cr; bid-ask spread < 5 bps; listed > 6 months

long.confirmation: Next bar close > previous bar close (uptick confirmation)

short.confirmation: Next bar close < previous bar close (downtick confirmation)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: close crosses vwap (VWAP_Distance crosses zero from entry side)
exit.stop_loss: 0.4% from entry price (40 bps hard stop)
exit.trailing_stop: After 20 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: Exit if no target hit within 60 bars (60 min)
exit.signal_exit: RSI crosses 50 from overbought/oversold

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L per trade; reduce to ₹75K if India VIX > 20

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; if VIX > 20, halve position size
filters.time_filter: No new entries after 15:00 IST; no entries before 09:20 IST
filters.volume_filter: Skip if stock 5-min volume < 50% of 20-day average for that 5-min bucket
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not down > 1.5% from previous close (avoid crash days)
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 5 bps at time of entry
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day and day after
other_filters: Skip if stock is in F&O ban period

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — VWAP-reversion is a crowded signal; edge decays if too many algos adopt triple-filter approach

weaknesses: Triple confirmation is restrictive — may generate only 1-2 signals per day across entire universe, leading to significant opportunity cost
RSI(14) on 1-min bars is noisy and can whipsaw rapidly; 14-bar lookback on 1-min data captures only 14 minutes of price action
VWAP mean-reversion breaks down on strong trend days (e.g., post-RBI policy, budget days) where price can stay 100+ bps from VWAP for hours
prior_art: Berkowitz et al. (2005) on VWAP execution; Connors & Alvarez RSI(2) mean-reversion; various retail strategies combining VWAP+RSI on TradingView
notes: Consider replacing RSI(14) with RSI(7) for faster signal on 1-min bars. Volume ratio threshold of 1.5x may need calibration per sector — banking stocks have naturally higher volume variance.

name: momentum_reversion_switch_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Intraday markets alternate between momentum and mean-reversion regimes. During high-ADX periods (ADX(14) > 25), trend-following via EMA crossover outperforms. During low-ADX periods (ADX(14) < 18), Bollinger Band mean-reversion dominates. The inefficiency arises because most strategies are static — they commit to one paradigm and suffer during the wrong regime. By using ADX as a real-time regime classifier and switching between two sub-strategies, we capture edge in both states. This is not arbitraged away because the switching cost and model complexity deter simpler algos, and the regime transitions are noisy enough that classification accuracy is imperfect.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; beta(NIFTY,60d) between 0.8 and 1.5

conditions: MOMENTUM_REGIME: ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(close,9) crosses above EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
REVERSION_REGIME: ADX(14) < 18 AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap
long.confirmation: Volume on entry bar > SMA(volume, 10)

conditions: MOMENTUM_REGIME: ADX(14) > 25 AND EMA(close,9) crosses below EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
REVERSION_REGIME: ADX(14) < 18 AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap
short.confirmation: Volume on entry bar > SMA(volume, 10)

entry.entry_price: market order on next bar open after signal

exit.target: MOMENTUM: 50 bps from entry; REVERSION: close crosses BB_mid (SMA(close,20))
exit.trailing_stop: MOMENTUM: trail 20 bps from high after 30 bps profit; REVERSION: none
exit.signal_exit: Regime switch (ADX crosses threshold) triggers immediate exit

filters.vix_filter: No filter — strategy is regime-adaptive by design
filters.time_filter: No entries in first 5 min (09:15-09:20) or after 15:00 IST
filters.volume_filter: Stock must have traded > 500 shares in last 5 bars
filters.trend_filter: None — strategy adapts to both trending and ranging
filters.event_filter: Avoid trading stock on result day
other_filters: ADX must have been computed on at least 28 bars of data since session open

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — regime switching adds complexity that is harder to replicate; but ADX-based regime detection is well-known

weaknesses: ADX(14) on 1-min bars takes ~28 bars to stabilize, losing the first 30 minutes of trading session to indicator warm-up
Regime classification in the ADX 18-25 'dead zone' is ambiguous — neither sub-strategy performs well, leading to whipsaws
Switching cost: each regime transition requires closing existing position and potentially reversing, doubling transaction costs during choppy transitions
prior_art: Ang & Timmermann (2012) regime-switching models; Kole & van Dijk (2017) on Markov-switching for trading; ADX regime classification is common in technical analysis literature
notes: Dead zone (ADX 18-25) could be handled by going flat or reducing size. Consider using a Markov switching model instead of hard ADX thresholds for smoother transitions.

name: trend_counter_trend_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Trend-following strategies on 1-min bars capture large intraday moves but give back significant profit at reversals because trailing stops lag. By using a trend-following entry (Supertrend-based) combined with a counter-trend exit (RSI divergence + VWAP distance extremes), the strategy captures the meat of the move while exiting before the trend exhausts. The inefficiency exists because most trend systems use symmetric trend-based exits; asymmetric entry/exit logic is less common in retail and requires more nuanced coding. Institutional algos focus on execution rather than directional signals at this frequency.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹75 Cr; ATR(14) / close > 0.005 (sufficient intraday volatility)

indicators.name: RSI_Divergence
indicators.params: close makes new high but RSI(14) < RSI(14)[prior_high_bar]

long.confirmation: Entry bar closes in top 30% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) > 0.7

short.confirmation: Entry bar closes in bottom 30% of its range: (close - low) / (high - low) < 0.3

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: After 1.0 * ATR(14) profit, trail at 0.5 * ATR(14) from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Counter-trend exit: RSI bearish divergence (for longs) AND abs(VWAP_Distance_bps) > 60

filters.vix_filter: Widen stops to 1.5 * ATR(14) when India VIX > 22
filters.time_filter: No entries after 15:10 IST; no entries before 09:20
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 must be trending (ADX(NIFTY,14) > 20)
filters.event_filter: Avoid stock on result day; avoid all entries within 30 min of RBI policy

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — Supertrend is a well-known indicator but the counter-trend exit overlay is less common and provides defensiveness

weaknesses: Lower win rate (45%) means longer losing streaks; need psychological discipline and sufficient capital to survive 8-10 consecutive losses
RSI divergence detection on 1-min bars is inherently noisy — false divergences are common and may trigger premature exits, cutting winners short
Supertrend(10, 3.0) on 1-min bars can whipsaw during the first hour when volatility is highest, generating false entries
prior_art: Supertrend indicator by Olivier Seban; RSI divergence widely used in technical analysis; asymmetric entry/exit discussed in Kaufman's 'Trading Systems and Methods'
notes: Consider adding a minimum holding period of 10 bars before counter-trend exit can trigger, to avoid premature exits. ATR-based stops auto-adapt to volatility, reducing need for manual parameter tuning on VIX changes.

name: multi_indicator_consensus_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Individual technical indicators have low signal-to-noise ratios on 1-min bars. By requiring consensus from 5 diverse indicators (VWAP position, RSI, MACD, Stochastic, and Volume Rate of Change), we filter out noise and only trade when multiple independent lenses agree. The inefficiency persists because most traders use 1-2 indicators; requiring 5/5 or 4/5 agreement dramatically reduces false signals but also reduces frequency, making it unattractive to high-frequency desks that need volume. The edge comes from precision: fewer trades but higher win rate.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; must not be in F&O ban

indicators.name: RSI_signal
indicators.params: 1 if RSI(close,14) < 35 else (-1 if RSI(close,14) > 65 else 0)

indicators.name: Stoch_signal
indicators.params: 1 if STOCH_K(14,3) < 25 else (-1 if STOCH_K(14,3) > 75 else 0)

long.confirmation: Consensus_Score must remain >= 4 for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: Consensus_Score must remain <= -4 for 2 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Consensus_Score drops to 0 (neutral) or flips sign

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; reduce position to ₹75K if VIX > 20
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 (indicator warm-up) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: At least 3 of 5 NIFTY 50 sector indices trending same direction
filters.event_filter: Skip stocks on earnings day
other_filters: All 5 indicators must have sufficient bars for computation (min 33 bars since open)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — consensus approach is robust but each individual indicator is well-known; edge comes from combination, not novelty

weaknesses: Very low signal frequency — requiring 4/5 consensus with 2-bar confirmation may produce only 0-1 trades per day across entire NIFTY 50 universe
Indicators are correlated (RSI, Stochastic, MACD all derived from price) — consensus may overweight price momentum and underweight independent information
Target/stop ratio of 40/25 = 1.6 is tight; with 63% win rate, the strategy is fragile — a 5% drop in win rate makes it unprofitable after costs
prior_art: Elder's Triple Screen System; consensus/voting systems discussed in Pardo's 'Design, Testing, and Optimization of Trading Systems'; multiple confirmation approaches common in retail TA
notes: Consider replacing one price-based indicator with an independent signal (e.g., order flow imbalance) to reduce correlation among voting members. Volume ROC provides some independence but is still derivative of market activity.

name: factor_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Academic factor investing (value + momentum) works at monthly frequencies but is under-explored intraday. Stocks that are relatively cheap (low P/E within sector) AND showing strong intraday momentum (top quartile of 60-min returns) tend to outperform in the subsequent 30-60 minutes. The inefficiency exists because institutional factor investors operate on daily+ horizons, and retail intraday traders ignore fundamental factors. The value tilt prevents chasing expensive momentum stocks that are prone to sharp reversals, while momentum prevents value traps that keep falling.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents grouped by GICS sector
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹50 Cr; sector must have >= 5 members for cross-sectional ranking

indicators.name: Value_Rank
indicators.params: percentile_rank(PE_ratio, sector_peers) — lower PE = higher value rank

long.confirmation: ROC(close, 5) > 0 (short-term momentum still positive over last 5 bars)

short.confirmation: ROC(close, 5) < 0 (short-term momentum still negative)

exit.trailing_stop: After 30 bps profit, trail at 20 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Composite_Score drops below 0.50 (for longs) or rises above 0.50 (for shorts)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for momentum calc) or after 15:00
filters.volume_filter: Stock volume in last 60 bars > 50th percentile of its 20-day avg
filters.trend_filter: Sector index for the stock must not be down > 2% from previous close
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day and for 2 days after
other_filters: Sector must have at least 5 liquid members for meaningful cross-sectional ranking

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — combining fundamental (value) with technical (momentum) factors at intraday frequency is uncommon; academic-to-practical gap protects edge

weaknesses: PE ratio is a daily/quarterly metric — using it for intraday decisions mixes time horizons awkwardly; PE does not change intraday, so value rank is static for the session
Cross-sectional ranking requires real-time computation across sector peers, adding latency; if a sector has only 5-6 liquid names, ranks are noisy
60-bar momentum lookback delays signals — by the time a stock reaches top quintile momentum, the move may be 50-70% complete, limiting remaining upside
prior_art: Fama-French factor models; Asness et al. (2013) 'Value and Momentum Everywhere'; Jegadeesh & Titman (1993) momentum; intraday factor application is novel but built on established theory
notes: The 0.4/0.6 value/momentum weighting favors momentum because intraday price dynamics matter more than static fundamental factors. Consider adding a quality factor (ROE rank) as a third component.

name: quality_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: High-quality companies (high ROE, low debt/equity, consistent earnings) that also exhibit strong intraday momentum are less likely to experience sharp reversals compared to low-quality momentum stocks. The quality filter acts as crash protection — high ROE, low-leverage names attract institutional buying on dips, creating a floor. The inefficiency persists because quality is typically a long-term factor (monthly rebalancing) and intraday traders ignore it. By restricting momentum trades to high-quality names, we reduce tail risk while maintaining trend-following returns.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹75 Cr; ROE > 15%; Debt/Equity < 1.0; 4 consecutive quarters of positive earnings

long.confirmation: EMA(close,9) - EMA(close,21) is widening (current gap > gap 5 bars ago)

short.confirmation: EMA(close,21) - EMA(close,9) is widening

exit.trailing_stop: After 1.0 * ATR(14) profit, trail at 0.5 * ATR(14)
exit.signal_exit: EMA(close,9) crosses EMA(close,21) against position direction

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; skip short entries if VIX < 12 (low-vol bullish regime)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction must agree with trade direction (NIFTY EMA(9) vs EMA(21))
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day and 1 day before earnings

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — quality factor is well-established but rarely applied intraday; combining with momentum is novel at this frequency

weaknesses: Quality filter is static (changes quarterly) — cannot adapt to rapid deterioration in company fundamentals; a company may report bad results tomorrow while still appearing high-quality today
Asymmetric long/short logic (long quality, short junk) creates directional bias — net long in bull markets, which may not be the strategy's intent
EMA(9)/EMA(21) crossover on 1-min bars generates frequent whipsaws; requires momentum confirmation to filter but still produces false signals in choppy markets
prior_art: Novy-Marx (2013) on quality factor; Asness et al. 'Quality Minus Junk'; momentum factor (Jegadeesh-Titman); quality-momentum combination explored in AQR research papers
notes: Short side is harder in Indian markets due to availability constraints and higher borrow costs. Consider making this a long-only quality-momentum strategy to simplify execution.

name: smart_beta_intraday_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The low-volatility anomaly (low-vol stocks deliver higher risk-adjusted returns) is documented at monthly horizons but has an intraday analog: stocks in the bottom tercile of realized intraday volatility (measured by 5-day average of intraday high-low range / close) that break out of their compressed range tend to sustain moves because low-vol names attract less noise trading and breakouts are more information-driven. The inefficiency persists because intraday traders prefer high-volatility stocks for larger absolute moves, leaving low-vol breakouts under-exploited. Smart beta indices (NIFTY Low Vol 30) demonstrate this effect at daily frequency; we exploit it at 1-min.
universe: NIFTY 100 constituents, bottom tercile by 5-day avg intraday range
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹50 Cr; 5-day average (high-low)/close < median of NIFTY 100

conditions: Stock is in bottom tercile of 5-day avg intraday range (low-vol name)
long.confirmation: Next bar close > Keltner_Upper (breakout holds for 1 bar)

conditions: Stock is in bottom tercile of 5-day avg intraday range
short.confirmation: Next bar close < Keltner_Lower

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.target: 60 bps from entry (low-vol stocks move less, target accordingly)
exit.stop_loss: 30 bps from entry (tight stop — false breakouts in low-vol names are quick)
exit.trailing_stop: After 35 bps profit, trail at 20 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Close re-enters Keltner Channel (close < Keltner_Upper for longs)

risk.position_sizing: Slightly larger size (₹1.25L) due to lower volatility of universe; risk-adjusted via ATR

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22; low-vol breakout strategy works best in calm markets
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 EMA(20) slope > 0 for longs; < 0 for shorts
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 4 bps (tighter for low-vol names)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock 2 days before and after earnings
other_filters: Vol_Percentile must be below 30 (confirming compressed volatility before breakout)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — low-volatility anomaly is persistent and structurally driven by institutional mandates that avoid volatile stocks

weaknesses: Low-vol stocks have smaller absolute moves — 60 bps target is ambitious for names in the bottom tercile of intraday range; many targets may not be hit within time stop
False breakouts in low-vol names often have low volume, making the volume filter critical but also restrictive — may only get 1-2 signals per week
The low-volatility anomaly is documented at monthly frequencies; its persistence at 1-min granularity is unproven and may not hold
prior_art: Baker, Bradley & Wurgler (2011) 'Benchmarks as Limits to Arbitrage'; Blitz & van Vliet (2007) low-volatility anomaly; NIFTY Low Volatility 30 index methodology; Keltner Channel breakouts in retail TA
notes: Consider pairing long low-vol breakouts with short high-vol breakdowns for a volatility-neutral portfolio. The strategy naturally has lower turnover and may benefit from slightly longer holding periods.

name: risk_parity_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Risk parity allocates capital inversely proportional to volatility so that each position contributes equal risk. Applied intraday across a basket of 5-10 stocks, this approach generates a directional signal when the risk-parity weighted basket diverges from NIFTY 50. If the equal-risk basket underperforms NIFTY by > 15 bps, it suggests temporary mispricing in the basket constituents. The inefficiency arises because risk parity is used for portfolio construction (Bridgewater, etc.) but rarely as a signal generator. By comparing the risk-parity portfolio's return to the benchmark, we identify when lower-risk names are disproportionately sold (opportunity to buy) or bought (opportunity to sell).
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents — select top 10 by inverse-ATR weighting
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; ATR(14) / close must be > 0.003 to ensure minimum tradability

indicators.name: ATR_14
indicators.params: ATR(high, low, close, 14) for each constituent

indicators.name: RP_Weight
indicators.params: (1 / ATR_14_i) / sum(1 / ATR_14_j for j in basket)

indicators.name: RP_Return_30
indicators.params: sum(RP_Weight_i * ROC(close_i, 30)) for i in basket

conditions: RP_Spread < -15 bps (risk-parity basket underperforming NIFTY — low-risk names oversold)
long.confirmation: RP_Spread stops declining (RP_Spread > RP_Spread[1 bar ago])

conditions: RP_Spread > 15 bps (risk-parity basket outperforming NIFTY — low-risk names overbought)
short.confirmation: RP_Spread stops rising (RP_Spread < RP_Spread[1 bar ago])

entry.entry_price: market order on the most dislocated constituent in the basket (largest individual deviation from its VWAP)

exit.target: RP_Spread reverts to 0 (basket re-aligns with NIFTY)
exit.stop_loss: RP_Spread widens to -30 bps (for longs) — 2x entry threshold
exit.signal_exit: RP_Spread crosses zero from entry side

risk.position_sizing: Inverse-ATR weighted: higher allocation to lower-vol names

filters.vix_filter: India VIX between 12-22 for longs; VIX > 14 for shorts
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (ATR warm-up) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: All basket constituents must have traded > 1000 shares in last 10 bars
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 intraday range < 2% (avoid extreme trend days where RP spreads are driven by macro, not mispricing)
filters.spread_filter: All basket constituents: bid-ask spread < 5 bps
filters.event_filter: Remove any constituent with earnings today; replace with next eligible by inverse-ATR weight
other_filters: Minimum basket size of 7 stocks after filters

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — risk parity as a signal is uncommon; the spread computation requires simultaneous tracking of 10 stocks, adding complexity that deters simpler competitors

weaknesses: The strategy trades only the single most dislocated stock, not the basket — this concentrates idiosyncratic risk and the individual stock may diverge from the basket signal
Risk parity weights depend on ATR(14) which is unstable on 1-min bars; small changes in ATR can cause large weight shifts, creating spurious RP_Spread signals
During genuine risk-off events (credit crisis, geopolitical shock), the RP_Spread dislocation is fundamental, not temporary — mean-reversion assumption fails
prior_art: Bridgewater All Weather risk parity; Qian (2005) 'Risk Parity Portfolios'; Maillard et al. (2010) on equal risk contribution; application as signal generator rather than portfolio construction is novel
notes: Could be extended to trade the full basket (multiple legs) for true risk parity, but this increases complexity and brokerage costs significantly. Single-stock entry keeps costs manageable.

name: mean_variance_optimal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Markowitz mean-variance optimization can be applied to intraday entry timing by computing rolling expected return (EMA of 1-min returns) and rolling variance (realized variance over 30 bars) for a stock, then entering when the instantaneous Sharpe ratio (expected return / sqrt(variance)) exceeds a threshold. The intuition is that favorable risk/reward moments are transient — they appear when a stock has positive momentum but temporarily compressed volatility (coiled spring). The inefficiency exists because mean-variance optimization is used for portfolio allocation, not trade timing. Retail traders use static indicators; computing rolling risk-adjusted signals at 1-min frequency requires quantitative infrastructure.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; traded every day for last 20 sessions

conditions: Instant_Sharpe > 2.0 (rolling risk-adjusted return is strongly positive)
Sharpe_Percentile > 0.90 (current Sharpe is in top 10% of recent 2-hour window)
long.confirmation: Instant_Sharpe remains > 1.5 on next bar (not a single-bar spike)
