conditions: Instant_Sharpe < -2.0 (rolling risk-adjusted return is strongly negative)
short.confirmation: Instant_Sharpe remains < -1.5 on next bar

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Instant_Sharpe crosses zero against position direction

risk.position_sizing: Size inversely proportional to Rolling_Variance: base ₹1L * (median_var / Rolling_Variance), capped at ₹1.5L

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 30 bars for variance) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not in extreme move (abs(ROC(NIFTY, 60)) < 100 bps)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: Rolling_Variance must be > 0 (non-zero variance — stock must be moving)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — instantaneous Sharpe ratio is a novel application of well-known theory; edge depends on the transient nature of high-Sharpe moments

weaknesses: Instant Sharpe on 1-min returns is extremely noisy — a single large bar can spike the Sharpe to > 2.0 and the confirmation bar check may not be sufficient to filter noise
Variance computed on 30 1-min returns is statistically unreliable; 30 data points give very wide confidence intervals on the variance estimate
The strategy assumes stationary return distributions within the 30-bar window, which is violated during news events, creating false high-Sharpe signals right before large adverse moves
prior_art: Markowitz (1952) mean-variance framework; applied to trade timing rather than portfolio construction; Lo (2002) on time-varying Sharpe ratios; rolling Sharpe used in portfolio analytics but not typically for entry signals
notes: Consider using a longer variance window (60 bars) for stability, accepting the trade-off of slower signal response. The position sizing rule (inverse variance) naturally reduces size during volatile periods, providing built-in risk management.

name: ensemble_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: No single strategy works in all market conditions. By running 4 distinct sub-strategies simultaneously — VWAP mean-reversion, EMA crossover trend, Bollinger breakout, and RSI reversal — and entering only when >= 3 of 4 agree on direction, we create a robust ensemble signal. Each sub-strategy captures a different market microstructure (reversion, trend, breakout, exhaustion), and their errors are partially uncorrelated. The inefficiency persists because building and maintaining multiple concurrent sub-strategies requires significant engineering effort. The ensemble's edge comes not from any single signal being novel, but from the diversification benefit of combining them.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; stock must have complete data for all 4 sub-strategy indicators

indicators.name: Sub1_VWAP_Signal
indicators.params: +1 if close < vwap AND (vwap - close)/close > 0.003 else (-1 if close > vwap AND (close - vwap)/close > 0.003 else 0)

indicators.name: Sub3_BB_Signal
indicators.params: +1 if close > SMA(close,20) + 2*STDDEV(close,20) else (-1 if close < SMA(close,20) - 2*STDDEV(close,20) else 0)

indicators.name: Sub4_RSI_Signal
indicators.params: +1 if RSI(close,14) < 30 else (-1 if RSI(close,14) > 70 else 0)

conditions: close > VWAP OR Ensemble_Score == 4 (override VWAP filter if full consensus)
long.confirmation: Ensemble_Score remains >= 3 for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: Ensemble_Score remains <= -3 for 2 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 12 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Ensemble_Score crosses zero (majority flips against position)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; scale to ₹1.25L if Ensemble_Score == 4 or -4 (full consensus)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; halve size if VIX > 20
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (indicator warm-up) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not down > 1.5% from previous close
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: Sub3 and Sub4 cannot both be 0 (at least one non-price signal must be active)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — each sub-strategy is well-known; ensemble benefit comes from combination but all inputs are public indicators

weaknesses: Sub-strategies are correlated — VWAP reversion and RSI reversal often agree, while EMA crossover and BB breakout often agree; effective diversification is less than 4 independent signals
The ensemble can produce conflicting signals between mean-reversion (Sub1, Sub4) and trend-following (Sub2, Sub3), creating a structural tension; 3/4 consensus rarely occurs
Target/stop ratio of 40/20 = 2.0 with 61% win rate seems optimistic; slippage and the tight 20 bps stop will cause many premature stop-outs in volatile 1-min bars
prior_art: Ensemble methods in ML (Random Forest voting); Elder's Triple Screen; combining mean-reversion and momentum signals discussed in Chan (2013) 'Algorithmic Trading'
notes: Consider weighting sub-strategies by their recent performance (adaptive weighting) rather than equal weighting. A sub-strategy that has been accurate in the last 20 signals should receive higher weight.

name: bayesian_update_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Markets provide a stream of evidence (price movements, volume, spread changes) that can be used to update the probability of a stock trending up or down in the next 30 minutes via Bayesian updating. Starting with a prior based on NIFTY direction and sector strength, each 1-min bar's return, volume, and VWAP position provides likelihood evidence that updates the posterior probability. We trade when the posterior exceeds 0.70 (strong directional conviction). The inefficiency exists because Bayesian updating requires explicit probability modeling, which is foreign to most retail and many institutional intraday traders. The edge comes from formally aggregating heterogeneous evidence rather than relying on ad-hoc indicator combinations.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; at least 60 days of historical 1-min data for prior calibration

indicators.name: Price_Likelihood
indicators.params: P(bar_return | trend_up) from historical distribution of 1-min returns

indicators.name: Volume_Likelihood
indicators.params: P(volume_ratio | trend_up) where volume_ratio = volume / SMA(volume,20)

indicators.name: VWAP_Likelihood
indicators.params: P(VWAP_distance | trend_up) from historical VWAP deviation distributions

indicators.name: Posterior_Prob
indicators.params: Bayesian update: Prior * Product(Likelihoods) / Normalizer, updated every bar

conditions: Posterior_Prob has been monotonically increasing for last 3 bars
long.confirmation: Posterior_Prob(trend_up) > 0.70 sustained for 2 consecutive bars

conditions: Posterior_Prob has been monotonically decreasing for last 3 bars
short.confirmation: Posterior_Prob(trend_up) < 0.30 sustained for 2 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 20 bps profit, trail at 12 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Posterior_Prob crosses 0.50 against position direction

risk.position_sizing: Scale with conviction: ₹75K if Posterior 0.70-0.75, ₹1L if 0.75-0.85, ₹1.25L if > 0.85

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; recalibrate likelihood distributions if VIX > 20
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (prior calibration needs initial bars) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Volume_Likelihood must not be degenerate (volume > 100 shares per bar)
filters.trend_filter: None — Bayesian framework naturally incorporates trend information via prior
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day — likelihood distributions not calibrated for event-day volatility
other_filters: Posterior must not be stuck at 0.50 ± 0.05 for > 30 bars (no information arriving)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — Bayesian updating framework is novel for intraday trading; calibration of likelihoods from historical data is the moat

weaknesses: Likelihood distributions must be calibrated from historical data and are assumed stationary — market regime changes invalidate the calibration, requiring periodic recalibration (at least monthly)
Bayesian updating with multiple likelihoods assumes conditional independence between price, volume, and VWAP evidence, which is clearly violated (high volume and large price moves are correlated)
The prior based on NIFTY and sector direction introduces look-ahead if not carefully lagged; must use strictly prior-bar values to avoid data leakage
prior_art: Bayesian methods in finance: Johannes & Polson (2010); West & Harrison (1997) dynamic linear models; Bayesian portfolio allocation (Black-Litterman); application to intraday entry timing is less explored
notes: Consider using a particle filter or sequential Monte Carlo instead of closed-form Bayesian updates to handle non-Gaussian likelihoods. The likelihood distributions should be estimated using kernel density estimation from the last 60 trading days.

name: adaptive_threshold_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Fixed indicator thresholds (e.g., RSI > 70 is overbought) fail because the distribution of indicators shifts with market regime. In trending markets, RSI can stay above 70 for extended periods; in ranging markets, RSI(14) rarely exceeds 65. By dynamically scaling thresholds using a rolling percentile approach — overbought = top 5th percentile of RSI over last 120 bars, oversold = bottom 5th percentile — the strategy adapts to current market conditions. Similarly, Bollinger Band width thresholds for breakout are scaled by recent volatility regime using ATR percentile. The inefficiency persists because most retail and systematic traders use static thresholds, creating predictable entry/exit clustering that we can front-run.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; at least 120 bars of data in current session

indicators.name: BB_Width_Threshold
indicators.params: percentile(BB_Width, 120, 20) — breakout when BB_Width < 20th pctile then expands

conditions: BB_Width was < BB_Width_Threshold within last 10 bars (recent squeeze)
long.confirmation: RSI_14 turns up: RSI_14 > RSI_14[1 bar ago]

conditions: BB_Width was < BB_Width_Threshold within last 10 bars
short.confirmation: RSI_14 turns down: RSI_14 < RSI_14[1 bar ago]

exit.target: Close reverts to VWAP (VWAP_Distance crosses zero)
exit.stop_loss: 0.35% from entry (35 bps); dynamically widened to 0.50% if ATR_Pctile > 80
exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: RSI_14 crosses median of 120-bar rolling RSI distribution (50th percentile)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; reduce to ₹75K if ATR_Pctile > 80 (high vol environment)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 11:15 (need 120 bars for percentile calibration) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — adaptive thresholds handle both trending and ranging markets
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day and RBI policy day
other_filters: RSI_Upper_Threshold - RSI_Lower_Threshold > 20 (sufficient RSI dispersion for meaningful thresholds)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — adaptive thresholds are conceptually straightforward; edge comes from execution discipline and proper percentile calibration

weaknesses: 120-bar lookback for percentile calibration means no trades until 11:15 IST, missing the often-volatile morning session where many intraday opportunities occur
Percentile-based thresholds can become very narrow in low-volatility regimes (RSI staying 45-55), triggering on minor fluctuations that lack follow-through
The strategy conflates two different setups — RSI extremes (mean-reversion) and BB squeeze (breakout) — which may point in opposite directions, reducing clarity
prior_art: Bollinger Band squeeze (John Bollinger); adaptive RSI thresholds discussed in Kaufman's 'New Trading Systems and Methods'; percentile-based dynamic thresholds used in some quant funds but not widely published
notes: The late session start (11:15) could be mitigated by using previous session's last 120 bars to warm-start the percentile computation. Consider using a separate percentile window for RSI and BB_Width since they have different distributional properties.

name: multi_asset_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Individual stock movements are driven by both idiosyncratic and systematic factors. By monitoring NIFTY 50, Bank NIFTY, and India VIX simultaneously, we can extract a cross-asset macro signal that identifies regime shifts before they fully propagate to individual stocks. Specifically: when NIFTY rises but VIX also rises (unusual divergence), it signals institutional hedging and an imminent pullback. When NIFTY falls but VIX falls (complacency), it signals a likely bounce. Bank NIFTY vs NIFTY relative performance provides sector rotation information. The inefficiency exists because most intraday traders focus on single-stock technicals and ignore cross-asset information available in real-time.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹75 Cr; beta to NIFTY > 0.7 (sufficiently correlated for macro signal to be relevant)

conditions: NIFTY_ROC_15 < -15 bps AND VIX_ROC_15 < 0 (NIFTY down but VIX also down — complacent dip)
Stock close < vwap AND RSI(close, 14) < 40 (stock oversold in dip)
long.confirmation: NIFTY_ROC_15 turns positive within next 3 bars OR VIX_ROC_15 stays negative

conditions: NIFTY_ROC_15 > 15 bps AND VIX_ROC_15 > 0 (NIFTY up but VIX also up — hedging divergence)
Stock close > vwap AND RSI(close, 14) > 60 (stock overbought in rally)
short.confirmation: NIFTY_ROC_15 turns negative within next 3 bars OR VIX continues rising

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Divergence_Signal flips (NIFTY and VIX re-align in normal relationship)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; select highest-beta stock in direction for amplified move

filters.vix_filter: India VIX between 12-28 (outside this range, NIFTY-VIX relationship is non-linear)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:20 or after 15:15
filters.trend_filter: None — strategy explicitly trades divergences from trend
filters.event_filter: Avoid 30 min before and after scheduled macro events (RBI, GDP, IIP releases)
other_filters: NIFTY-VIX divergence must persist for at least 5 bars before entry

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — cross-asset signal requires monitoring 3 assets simultaneously; complexity deters most retail traders; institutional algo desks may already capture this but focus on options, not equity

weaknesses: India VIX is updated every 15 seconds, not every second — the 1-min bar for VIX is constructed from sparse data points, making VIX_ROC_15 noisier than price-based indicators
NIFTY-VIX divergence is a necessary but not sufficient condition for reversal — divergences can persist for 1-2 hours in trending markets, leading to premature counter-trend entries
Selecting a single high-beta stock to express the macro view concentrates idiosyncratic risk; the stock may not respond to the macro signal if it has its own news/events
prior_art: VIX-equity divergence trading is well-known in US markets (CBOE VIX); Dennis & Mayhew (2002) on implied vol dynamics; India-specific application less documented; Bank NIFTY relative strength used by prop traders
notes: Consider trading NIFTY futures or options directly instead of individual stocks to get purer macro exposure. The stock-level entry adds unnecessary idiosyncratic noise to what is fundamentally a macro signal.

name: composite_breadth_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Market breadth — the proportion of stocks advancing versus declining — provides information about the strength or weakness of an index move that price alone cannot convey. A NIFTY 50 rally driven by only 10-15 stocks (narrow breadth) is fragile, while a rally with 35+ advancers (broad breadth) is sustainable. By computing a composite intraday breadth indicator from 1-min advances/declines across NIFTY 50, we can identify divergences: index rising but breadth deteriorating (sell signal), or index falling but breadth improving (buy signal). The inefficiency persists because real-time breadth computation across 50 stocks requires infrastructure that most retail traders lack, and institutional desks focus on their own book rather than market-wide breadth at 1-min frequency.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents — trade the 5 most dislocated from breadth signal
stock_filter: All NIFTY 50 constituents used for breadth computation; trades on those with ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr

indicators.name: Advance_Count
indicators.params: count of NIFTY 50 stocks where ROC(close,5) > 0

conditions: NIFTY_Trend < 0 (NIFTY falling) AND Breadth_EMA > 0.55 (majority advancing despite index fall)
Breadth_Divergence > 0 (positive divergence — breadth stronger than index)
Target stock: close < vwap AND ROC(close, 10) < -10 bps (lagging the breadth signal)
long.confirmation: Breadth_EMA increasing for 3 consecutive bars

conditions: NIFTY_Trend > 0 (NIFTY rising) AND Breadth_EMA < 0.45 (majority declining despite index rise)
Breadth_Divergence < 0 (negative divergence — breadth weaker than index)
Target stock: close > vwap AND ROC(close, 10) > 10 bps (leading the narrow rally)
short.confirmation: Breadth_EMA decreasing for 3 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Breadth_Divergence returns to zero (index and breadth re-align)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 (need breadth warm-up) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: At least 40 of 50 NIFTY stocks must have traded in the last 5 bars
filters.trend_filter: None — strategy explicitly trades breadth divergences regardless of trend
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 5 bps on target stock
filters.event_filter: Skip on budget day, RBI policy day (breadth skewed by sector-wide reactions)
other_filters: Breadth_Divergence must have persisted for at least 10 bars before entry

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — real-time breadth computation at 1-min frequency is infrastructure-heavy; most traders rely on end-of-day A/D data

weaknesses: Breadth divergences can persist for 1-3 hours before resolving — NIFTY can continue rallying on narrow breadth, causing premature short entries to be stopped out
Using ROC(close, 5) for advance/decline classification is sensitive to the lookback — a 5-bar lookback is noisy and can flip rapidly, creating false breadth signals
The target stock selection (most dislocated from breadth signal) adds a subjective element and may select stocks with idiosyncratic reasons for their dislocation (news, earnings, etc.)
prior_art: NYSE Advance-Decline Line (McClellan Oscillator); Zweig Breadth Thrust; intraday breadth less documented but used by institutional trading desks; Quantopian community explored similar concepts
notes: Consider computing breadth on a sector-by-sector basis (e.g., banking breadth, IT breadth) for more granular signals. The composite breadth across all 50 stocks may be too broad for stock-specific entry decisions.

name: weighted_indicator_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Static indicator weights (equal weighting in a consensus system) are suboptimal because different indicators perform better in different regimes. By tracking each indicator's recent predictive accuracy over the last 50 signals and dynamically adjusting weights via exponential performance weighting, the composite signal naturally emphasizes whichever indicator is currently 'hot'. This is a form of online learning applied to indicator combination. The inefficiency exists because dynamically weighting indicators requires tracking signal-level P&L attribution, which is computationally expensive and beyond most retail platforms. The edge is in the meta-level learning: the strategy improves its own indicator selection in real-time.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; stock must have generated at least 50 signals from each indicator in last 20 sessions for weight calibration

indicators.name: Ind2_RSI
indicators.params: 1 if RSI(close,14) < 35 else (-1 if RSI(close,14) > 65 else 0)

indicators.name: Weight_i
indicators.params: exp(alpha * hit_rate_i_last_50) / sum(exp(alpha * hit_rate_j_last_50)) where alpha=2.0

conditions: At least 3 of 5 indicators are +1 (minimum breadth requirement)
long.confirmation: Weighted_Score > 0.60 sustained for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: Weighted_Score < -0.60 sustained for 2 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 22 bps profit, trail at 12 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Weighted_Score crosses zero against position direction

risk.position_sizing: Scale with Weighted_Score: ₹75K if score 0.60-0.70, ₹1L if 0.70-0.85, ₹1.25L if > 0.85

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 not in extreme move (abs(ROC(NIFTY, 30)) < 80 bps)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: All indicator weights must be > 0.05 (no indicator completely zeroed out — prevents overfitting to recent regime)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — the meta-learning component adapts to indicator performance shifts; edge decays only if all 5 base indicators simultaneously lose predictive power

weaknesses: Performance-weighted indicators can overfit to recent regime — if RSI had a hot streak, it gets high weight just as the regime may be changing, causing the strategy to lag regime transitions

The alpha=2.0 temperature parameter in the softmax weighting is arbitrary and sensitive — too high concentrates weight on one indicator, too low approaches equal weighting, negating the strategy's purpose
Tracking 50 signal-level P&L attributions per indicator per stock requires substantial bookkeeping infrastructure; errors in P&L attribution corrupt the weights
prior_art: Exponential weighting in online learning (Hedge algorithm, Freund & Schapire 1997); dynamic model combination in Bayesian model averaging; applied to technical indicators is a practical extension
notes: Consider using a Thompson Sampling approach instead of softmax weighting — it naturally balances exploration (trying underperforming indicators) and exploitation (relying on proven ones). The minimum weight floor of 0.05 partially addresses this but is ad-hoc.

name: hmm_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Financial markets exhibit latent states (trending, mean-reverting, volatile-choppy) that are not directly observable but can be inferred from observable quantities (returns, volume, spread) using a Hidden Markov Model. By fitting a 3-state HMM on the previous session's 1-min data (observations: return, volume_ratio, range) and using the Viterbi algorithm to decode current state in real-time, we select the appropriate sub-strategy: trend-follow in state 1, mean-revert in state 2, and sit out in state 3 (choppy). The inefficiency exists because HMM implementation at 1-min frequency requires quantitative expertise and latency-sensitive computation. Most HMM applications in finance are at daily or lower frequency.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; stock must have complete previous session data for HMM fitting

indicators.name: HMM_State
indicators.params: 3-state Gaussian HMM fitted on [return_1min, volume_ratio, bar_range]; Viterbi decode
indicators.lookback: previous session for fitting; real-time for decoding

indicators.name: State_Prob
indicators.params: Forward algorithm posterior probability of current state

conditions: STATE_1 (trending): HMM_State == 1 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND EMA(close,9) > EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
STATE_2 (mean-reverting): HMM_State == 2 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND close < BB_lower
long.confirmation: State_Prob must remain > 0.65 on next bar

conditions: STATE_1 (trending): HMM_State == 1 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND EMA(close,9) < EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
STATE_2 (mean-reverting): HMM_State == 2 AND State_Prob > 0.70 AND close > BB_upper
short.confirmation: State_Prob must remain > 0.65 on next bar

entry.entry_price: market order after state probability confirmation

exit.target: STATE_1: 50 bps; STATE_2: close reverts to BB_mid
exit.trailing_stop: STATE_1: trail 20 bps after 30 bps profit; STATE_2: none
exit.signal_exit: HMM_State transitions to State 3 (choppy) — immediately flatten

risk.position_sizing: Scale by State_Prob: ₹75K if prob 0.70-0.80, ₹1L if prob 0.80-0.90, ₹1.25L if prob > 0.90

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; if VIX > 20, require State_Prob > 0.80 for entry
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:20 or after 15:15
filters.trend_filter: None — HMM handles regime detection internally
filters.event_filter: Re-fit HMM using event-day data if current day is earnings/RBI policy (different emission distributions)
other_filters: HMM must have converged during fitting (log-likelihood change < 1e-4 between EM iterations)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — HMM implementation at 1-min frequency with real-time Viterbi decoding is a significant technical barrier; academic knowledge-to-production gap protects edge

weaknesses: HMM fitted on previous session's data assumes stationarity of state dynamics across sessions — this breaks down during earnings season, macro events, or regime changes
3-state HMM is a strong modeling assumption — true market dynamics may have more states or non-Gaussian emissions; model misspecification leads to incorrect state decoding
Forward algorithm computation at each 1-min bar adds latency (O(N²) per bar where N=3 states); with many stocks this may exceed latency budget for real-time trading
prior_art: Bulla et al. (2011) on HMM for stock returns; Hamilton (1989) regime-switching models; Rydén et al. (1998) stylized facts and HMMs; hmmlearn library in Python widely available but intraday application is rare
notes: Consider using a Bayesian HMM (sticky-HDP-HMM) for more robust state estimation and to automatically determine number of states. The hmmlearn Python library provides efficient Baum-Welch fitting.

name: vol_regime_adaptive_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Intraday market behavior differs fundamentally across volatility regimes. In low-vol regimes (ATR percentile < 30), mean-reversion dominates because moves are small and revert quickly. In high-vol regimes (ATR percentile > 70), momentum dominates because large moves carry information and attract order flow. In medium-vol (30-70th percentile), both strategies underperform — the strategy goes flat. By bucketing ATR(14) into percentile categories using a 5-day rolling ATR distribution and applying different entry rules per regime, we capture regime-specific alpha. The inefficiency persists because volatility-conditional strategies require continuous regime monitoring and parameter switching that most static trading systems cannot accommodate.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; 5 days of historical 1-min data for ATR distribution

indicators.name: ATR_Percentile
indicators.params: percentile_rank(ATR_14, 5-day rolling distribution of 1-min ATR values)

indicators.name: Vol_Regime
indicators.params: LOW if ATR_Percentile < 30; MED if 30-70; HIGH if > 70

conditions: LOW-VOL: Vol_Regime == LOW AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap (mean-reversion buy)
HIGH-VOL: Vol_Regime == HIGH AND EMA(close,9) > EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap AND volume > 2 * SMA(volume,20) (momentum buy)
long.confirmation: LOW-VOL: next bar close > current close; HIGH-VOL: next bar close > EMA(close,9)

conditions: LOW-VOL: Vol_Regime == LOW AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap (mean-reversion sell)
HIGH-VOL: Vol_Regime == HIGH AND EMA(close,9) < EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap AND volume > 2 * SMA(volume,20) (momentum sell)
short.confirmation: LOW-VOL: next bar close < current close; HIGH-VOL: next bar close < EMA(close,9)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: HIGH-VOL only: trail 20 bps after 30 bps profit
exit.signal_exit: Vol_Regime transitions to MED (medium vol) — close position as edge dissipates

risk.position_sizing: LOW-VOL: ₹1.25L (larger size for smaller moves); HIGH-VOL: ₹75K (smaller size for larger moves). Inverse ATR scaling

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 28; adjust regime thresholds if VIX > 22 (shift ATR percentile buckets up by 10)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: HIGH-VOL entries require volume > 2x SMA(volume,20); LOW-VOL has no additional volume filter
filters.trend_filter: HIGH-VOL: NIFTY trend must agree; LOW-VOL: no trend filter
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 5 bps in LOW-VOL; < 8 bps in HIGH-VOL (wider spreads acceptable)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day; skip all entries within 15 min of macro events
other_filters: Vol_Regime must have been stable (same regime) for at least 10 bars before entry

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — volatility regime conditioning is well-known conceptually but implementing real-time regime switching with appropriate parameter sets is non-trivial

weaknesses: Medium-vol regime (30-70th percentile of ATR) accounts for ~40% of the time, during which the strategy is flat — significant opportunity cost and underutilization of capital
Regime transitions from LOW to HIGH can be abrupt (e.g., sudden news) — the 10-bar stability requirement causes the strategy to miss the most profitable initial bars of a vol spike
BB(20, 1.5) in low-vol regime uses narrow bands (1.5 sigma vs standard 2.0) — more signals but also more false signals in low-vol environments where noise dominates
prior_art: Volatility regime-switching in Ang & Chen (2002); ATR-based position sizing (Van Tharp); volatility clustering (Mandelbrot); regime-conditional mean-reversion/momentum widely discussed in quant literature
notes: The medium-vol dead zone could be partially addressed by using a transition strategy (e.g., reduced-size breakout) rather than going completely flat. Consider using VIX as an additional regime input alongside stock-specific ATR.

name: trend_strength_adaptive_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: ADX (Average Directional Index) measures trend strength on a 0-100 scale but is typically used with static thresholds (>25 = trending). Instead of binary classification, this strategy uses ADX as a continuous scaling parameter for both indicator lookback and position size. When ADX is high (strong trend), use shorter EMA lookbacks (faster signals, ride the trend) and larger positions. When ADX is low (ranging), use longer lookbacks (fewer whipsaws) and smaller positions. The relationship is: EMA_lookback = max(5, 25 - floor(ADX/5)). This creates a continuously adaptive system rather than a discrete regime switch. The inefficiency persists because most implementations use ADX as a filter, not as a parameter modifier.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; stock ADX(14) must have been > 20 at least once in last 5 sessions (has trending tendency)

conditions: Adaptive_EMA > Adaptive_EMA_Slow (adaptive fast EMA above adaptive slow EMA)
long.confirmation: ADX_14 is rising: ADX_14 > ADX_14[3 bars ago]

short.confirmation: ADX_14 is rising: ADX_14 > ADX_14[3 bars ago]

exit.target: max(30, ADX_14 * 1.5) bps from entry — higher ADX = wider target
exit.stop_loss: max(20, ADX_14 * 0.8) bps from entry — higher ADX = wider stop
exit.trailing_stop: After target*0.6 profit, trail at target*0.4 from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: max(30, 90 - ADX_14) bars — higher ADX = shorter time stop (trends resolve faster)
exit.signal_exit: +DI/-DI cross against position OR ADX drops below 12 (trend exhausted)

risk.position_sizing: ₹(75000 + ADX_14 * 1000), capped at ₹1.5L — higher ADX = larger position

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (ADX warm-up needs ~28 bars) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: ADX must be > 15 (minimum trend strength to trade)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: Adaptive_EMA_Lookback must have been stable (not changed by >2) in last 5 bars to avoid signal instability

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — continuous ADX-parameter scaling is novel; most competitors use binary ADX thresholds; the adaptive system adds complexity that deters replication

weaknesses: Adaptive EMA lookback changes every bar as ADX fluctuates, causing EMA value discontinuities — when lookback jumps from 10 to 15, the EMA value can gap, creating false crossover signals
ADX-proportional position sizing increases exposure during strong trends, which is precisely when trend reversals are most damaging — the strategy takes its largest loss on the biggest reversal
The formula ADX_14 * 1.5 for target bps assumes linear relationship between trend strength and expected move magnitude, which is empirically not verified on 1-min NSE data
prior_art: Wilder's ADX (1978); Kaufman's Adaptive Moving Average (KAMA) uses similar efficiency ratio concept; ADX as a parameter modifier discussed in Ehlers 'Cybernetic Analysis for Stocks and Futures'
notes: Consider smoothing the Adaptive_EMA_Lookback by applying an EMA to the lookback value itself: Smoothed_Lookback = EMA(Adaptive_EMA_Lookback, 5). This prevents discontinuous jumps in EMA values when ADX fluctuates.

name: market_state_classifier_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The market operates in three primary intraday states — trending, ranging, and volatile-choppy — each requiring a different strategy. By computing three features (ADX for trend, BB_Width percentile for range, and ATR acceleration for volatility spikes) and classifying the state using a simple rule-based decision tree, we select the optimal sub-strategy. Trending state: trade EMA crossovers. Ranging state: fade BB extremes. Volatile: stay flat. The key insight is that these three states are mutually exclusive and exhaustive — at any moment, the market is doing exactly one of these. The inefficiency is that static strategies blend these states and underperform in 2 of 3 conditions.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; must have enough bars (30+) for classifier inputs

indicators.name: State
indicators.params: TRENDING if ADX_14 > 25 AND ATR_Accel < 0.5; RANGING if ADX_14 < 18 AND BB_Width_Pctile < 40; VOLATILE if ATR_Accel > 0.5

conditions: TRENDING: State == TRENDING AND EMA(close,9) crosses above EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
RANGING: State == RANGING AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap
long.confirmation: TRENDING: volume > SMA(volume, 15); RANGING: RSI(close, 14) < 35

conditions: TRENDING: State == TRENDING AND EMA(close,9) crosses below EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
RANGING: State == RANGING AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap
short.confirmation: TRENDING: volume > SMA(volume, 15); RANGING: RSI(close, 14) > 65

exit.trailing_stop: TRENDING: trail 15 bps after 25 bps profit; RANGING: none
exit.signal_exit: State transitions to VOLATILE or from TRENDING to RANGING (or vice versa) — exit immediately

risk.position_sizing: TRENDING: ₹1L; RANGING: ₹1.25L (smaller moves, need larger size)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; if VIX > 22, classify any ambiguous state as VOLATILE (stay flat)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Volume on signal bar > SMA(volume, 20) for trending entries
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction must agree for TRENDING entries
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: State must have been stable for at least 15 bars (no state transition in last 15 bars)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — state classification is straightforward but the combination of ADX, BB_Width, and ATR acceleration is less common; the decision tree is easily replicable once published

weaknesses: The VOLATILE state (ATR_Accel > 0.5) forces the strategy flat during potentially profitable periods — sharp volatility expansions often coincide with large directional moves
Hard-coded thresholds (ADX > 25, ADX < 18, ATR_Accel > 0.5) are arbitrary and may not be optimal for all stocks — bank stocks have structurally different ADX distributions than IT stocks
State transitions cause immediate exits, which can whipsaw if the classifier oscillates — a stock at ADX = 25.5 can flip between TRENDING and ambiguous on each bar
prior_art: Wilder's ADX for trend identification; Bollinger's squeeze for range detection; decision-tree classifiers for market states discussed in Aronson's 'Evidence-Based Technical Analysis'
notes: Consider using a gradient (soft classification) rather than hard boundaries for state transitions. A weighted average of sub-strategy signals based on classification probabilities would be smoother than discrete switching.

name: vix_bucket_strategy_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: India VIX provides a forward-looking measure of expected market volatility derived from NIFTY option prices. By bucketing VIX into 4 regimes — Calm (VIX < 13), Normal (13-18), Elevated (18-24), and Crisis (> 24) — and assigning a different strategy to each bucket, we adapt to the macroeconomic uncertainty environment. Calm: aggressive mean-reversion (small moves revert quickly). Normal: standard EMA crossover momentum. Elevated: reduced size, wide-stop trend following. Crisis: flat (no edge, too noisy). The inefficiency persists because most retail traders use the same strategy regardless of VIX level, and VIX-conditional strategy selection requires monitoring an external data feed.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; varies by VIX bucket
hold_time: CALM: 10-20 min; NORMAL: 20-45 min; ELEVATED: 30-90 min

indicators.name: VIX_Bucket
indicators.params: CALM if VIX < 13; NORMAL if 13 <= VIX < 18; ELEVATED if 18 <= VIX < 24; CRISIS if VIX >= 24

conditions: CALM: close < BB_lower_calm AND close < vwap AND RSI(close,10) < 30
NORMAL: EMA(close,9) crosses above EMA(close,21) AND close > vwap
ELEVATED: close > Supertrend(10,4.0) AND close > vwap AND volume > 2*SMA(volume,20)
long.confirmation: CALM: uptick (close > close[-1]); NORMAL: volume > SMA(volume,15); ELEVATED: Supertrend hold for 3 bars

conditions: CALM: close > BB_upper_calm AND close > vwap AND RSI(close,10) > 70
NORMAL: EMA(close,9) crosses below EMA(close,21) AND close < vwap
ELEVATED: close < Supertrend(10,4.0) AND close < vwap AND volume > 2*SMA(volume,20)
short.confirmation: CALM: downtick (close < close[-1]); NORMAL: volume > SMA(volume,15); ELEVATED: Supertrend hold for 3 bars

exit.target: CALM: 20 bps; NORMAL: 35 bps; ELEVATED: 60 bps
exit.stop_loss: CALM: 12 bps; NORMAL: 20 bps; ELEVATED: 35 bps
exit.trailing_stop: CALM: none (quick target); NORMAL: 12 bps after 20 bps; ELEVATED: 25 bps after 35 bps
exit.time_stop: CALM: 20 bars; NORMAL: 45 bars; ELEVATED: 90 bars
exit.signal_exit: VIX_Bucket transitions to a different bucket — exit and re-evaluate

risk.position_sizing: CALM: ₹1.5L (large, small moves); NORMAL: ₹1L; ELEVATED: ₹50K (small, large moves); CRISIS: ₹0 (flat)

filters.vix_filter: VIX_Bucket itself is the primary filter — CRISIS bucket = no trading
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 or after 15:10; CALM can trade until 15:15
filters.volume_filter: ELEVATED: strict 2x volume required; CALM/NORMAL: SMA(volume,15) sufficient
filters.trend_filter: NORMAL: NIFTY trend must agree; CALM/ELEVATED: no trend filter
filters.spread_filter: CALM: spread < 3 bps; NORMAL: < 5 bps; ELEVATED: < 8 bps
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day in all buckets; skip all entries on RBI policy day
other_filters: VIX must have been in current bucket for at least 15 min before entry

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — VIX bucket strategy selection is intuitive but requires discipline to switch strategies dynamically; most traders stick with one approach regardless of VIX

weaknesses: VIX bucket boundaries (13, 18, 24) are arbitrary and may not represent true regime shifts — the optimal boundaries likely vary over multi-year cycles as structural volatility changes
India VIX can jump from 14 to 19 within minutes during a shock, causing an immediate regime switch and forced exit from current position at a loss
CRISIS bucket (VIX > 24) has historically offered some of the best mean-reversion opportunities, but the strategy avoids them entirely, missing high-conviction trades
prior_art: VIX-conditional strategies common in US equity options trading; Whaley (2009) on VIX; VIX-based strategy selection discussed in Sinclair's 'Volatility Trading'; India VIX-specific research limited
notes: Consider adding a 5th bucket for 'extremely calm' (VIX < 10) which historically precedes vol spikes — could be used as a warning signal to reduce overall exposure. The CRISIS bucket could allow very selective high-conviction trades with tight stops.

name: autocorrelation_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The sign and magnitude of 1-lag autocorrelation in 1-min returns reveals whether a stock is in a momentum (positive autocorrelation) or mean-reversion (negative autocorrelation) regime. When autocorrelation(returns, lag=1, window=30) > 0.15, returns are serially correlated — trend-follow. When autocorrelation < -0.15, returns are negatively correlated — fade the move. Between -0.15 and 0.15, no edge. The inefficiency exists because autocorrelation is a statistical concept rarely used by retail traders, and it varies significantly across stocks and times of day. Institutional quant desks compute this but at lower frequencies (daily/weekly). Real-time 1-min autocorrelation monitoring is uncommon.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; tick data granularity sufficient for 1-min bar construction

indicators.name: Autocorr_Regime
indicators.params: MOMENTUM if Autocorr_30 > 0.15; REVERSION if Autocorr_30 < -0.15; NEUTRAL otherwise

conditions: MOMENTUM: Autocorr_Regime == MOMENTUM AND ROC(close,3) > 10 bps AND close > EMA(close,5) (follow recent up-move)
REVERSION: Autocorr_Regime == REVERSION AND ROC(close,3) < -15 bps AND VWAP_Distance < -25 (fade recent down-move)
long.confirmation: MOMENTUM: ROC(close,1) > 0 on next bar; REVERSION: ROC(close,1) > 0 on next bar (uptick)

conditions: MOMENTUM: Autocorr_Regime == MOMENTUM AND ROC(close,3) < -10 bps AND close < EMA(close,5)
REVERSION: Autocorr_Regime == REVERSION AND ROC(close,3) > 15 bps AND VWAP_Distance > 25
short.confirmation: MOMENTUM: ROC(close,1) < 0 on next bar; REVERSION: ROC(close,1) < 0 on next bar (downtick)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.trailing_stop: MOMENTUM: trail 10 bps after 20 bps profit; REVERSION: none
exit.signal_exit: Autocorr_Regime transitions to NEUTRAL or opposite regime

risk.position_sizing: Scale with abs(Autocorr_30): ₹75K if abs < 0.20, ₹1L if 0.20-0.30, ₹1.25L if > 0.30

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 31 bars for autocorrelation) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — strategy uses autocorrelation for direction, not trend indicators
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day (autocorrelation structure breaks during event-driven moves)
other_filters: abs(Autocorr_30) must be > 0.15 (must be in a defined regime, not neutral)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — autocorrelation is a well-known statistical concept; the edge is in real-time computation and regime classification at 1-min frequency, not the concept itself

weaknesses: Autocorrelation on 30 1-min returns has very high sampling error — 30 data points give ± 0.18 at 95% confidence, meaning a measured autocorrelation of 0.15 is barely distinguishable from zero
Microstructure noise (bid-ask bounce) introduces negative autocorrelation that is not tradable — the REVERSION signal may be capturing bid-ask bounce rather than genuine mean-reversion
Autocorrelation regime can flip rapidly (every 5-10 bars), causing excessive regime transitions and forced exits before positions have time to reach target
prior_art: Lo & MacKinlay (1988) on stock return autocorrelation; Cont (2001) on empirical properties of asset returns; autocorrelation-based strategies in Aldridge's 'High-Frequency Trading'
notes: Consider using 60-bar window instead of 30 for more stable autocorrelation estimates, at the cost of slower regime detection. The bid-ask bounce issue could be mitigated by using mid-price returns instead of close-to-close returns.

name: hurst_exponent_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The Hurst exponent (H) measures the long-range dependence of a time series. H > 0.5 indicates persistence (trending), H < 0.5 indicates anti-persistence (mean-reverting), and H = 0.5 indicates a random walk. By computing the rolling Hurst exponent on 1-min returns using the rescaled range (R/S) method over 60 bars, we classify the current regime and select the appropriate strategy. H > 0.55: trend-follow with EMA crossover. H < 0.45: mean-revert with Bollinger Bands. 0.45-0.55: random walk, no edge, stay flat. The inefficiency exists because Hurst exponent computation is mathematically sophisticated, and its application to 1-min intraday trading is virtually absent in publicly available strategies.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; at least 60 bars of session data available

indicators.name: Hurst_Regime
indicators.params: PERSISTENT if Hurst_60 > 0.55; ANTI_PERSIST if Hurst_60 < 0.45; RANDOM otherwise

conditions: PERSISTENT: Hurst_Regime == PERSISTENT AND EMA(close,8) > EMA(close,20) AND close > vwap
ANTI_PERSIST: Hurst_Regime == ANTI_PERSIST AND close < BB_lower AND close < vwap
long.confirmation: Hurst_60 has been in current regime for at least 10 bars

conditions: PERSISTENT: Hurst_Regime == PERSISTENT AND EMA(close,8) < EMA(close,20) AND close < vwap
ANTI_PERSIST: Hurst_Regime == ANTI_PERSIST AND close > BB_upper AND close > vwap
short.confirmation: Hurst_60 has been in current regime for at least 10 bars

exit.target: PERSISTENT: 45 bps; ANTI_PERSIST: close reverts to BB_mid
exit.trailing_stop: PERSISTENT: trail 15 bps after 25 bps profit; ANTI_PERSIST: none
exit.signal_exit: Hurst_Regime transitions to RANDOM

risk.position_sizing: Scale with Hurst extremity: ₹75K if abs(Hurst-0.5) < 0.1, ₹1L if 0.1-0.15, ₹1.25L if > 0.15

filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for Hurst computation) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — Hurst exponent serves as the trend/reversion classifier
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: Hurst_60 must not be NaN or inf (sufficient data for computation)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — Hurst exponent computation is mathematically non-trivial; most traders lack the knowledge to implement R/S analysis at 1-min frequency

weaknesses: R/S Hurst exponent on 60 data points is statistically unreliable — the estimator has high variance with small samples, and 60 1-min bars is far below the recommended minimum of 256 for accurate Hurst estimation
Late session start (10:15) due to 60-bar warm-up means missing the morning volatility window where many intraday opportunities occur
The Hurst exponent is a global property of the series within the window — it may not reflect the very recent (last 5-10 bar) dynamics, causing signals that are backward-looking
prior_art: Mandelbrot (1972) on R/S analysis; Peters (1994) 'Fractal Market Analysis'; Di Matteo et al. (2005) on Hurst exponent for financial time series; intraday application is novel but builds on well-established theory
notes: Consider using the Detrended Fluctuation Analysis (DFA) method instead of R/S for more accurate Hurst estimation on short time series. Also consider computing Hurst on overlapping windows for smoother estimates.

name: fractal_dimension_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The fractal dimension (FD) of a price series measures its space-filling complexity on a scale from 1 (smooth trend) to 2 (random noise). When FD approaches 1.0, the price path is trending smoothly — ideal for trend-following. When FD approaches 1.5+, the path is noisy and random. By computing the Higuchi fractal dimension on a rolling 40-bar window and trading only when FD < 1.35 (structured, trending price action), we filter out choppy noise periods and only enter during mechanistically favorable conditions. The inefficiency exists because fractal dimension is a concept from chaos theory, not standard technical analysis, and its real-time computation on 1-min bars is uncommon outside academic research.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; stock must have sufficient tick activity for meaningful 1-min bar construction

indicators.name: FD_Regime
indicators.params: TRENDING if Higuchi_FD < 1.35; NOISY if Higuchi_FD >= 1.35

long.confirmation: Higuchi_FD has been < 1.35 for at least 5 consecutive bars (stable trending regime)

short.confirmation: Higuchi_FD has been < 1.35 for at least 5 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Higuchi_FD rises above 1.45 (price action becoming noisy — edge lost)

risk.position_sizing: Inversely scale with FD: ₹1.25L if FD < 1.20, ₹1L if 1.20-1.30, ₹75K if 1.30-1.35

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:55 (need 40 bars for FD computation) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 fractal dimension should also be < 1.40 (index also trending)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: k_max parameter (8) must have sufficient data points in each scale for robust FD estimate

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — fractal dimension is an obscure indicator rarely used in practice; computational barrier provides moat

weaknesses: Higuchi FD with k_max=8 on 40 data points is at the boundary of statistical reliability — the algorithm requires k_max * N computations and smaller windows reduce accuracy significantly
FD < 1.35 filtering removes the majority of trading time — price is 'noisy' (FD > 1.35) for ~60-70% of the session, leaving a narrow window for entries
The relationship between fractal dimension and future returns is not well-established empirically on 1-min Indian equity data — the theory is from physics, not finance-specific
prior_art: Higuchi (1988) fractal dimension algorithm; Peters (1994) 'Fractal Market Analysis'; Mandelbrot's fractal geometry of markets; Ehlers references fractal concepts in his trading system books
notes: Consider combining FD with the Hurst exponent (strategy 172) for a more robust regime classification. Both measure different aspects of the same underlying fractal structure. The k_max parameter of 8 is a compromise between accuracy and computational speed.

name: entropy_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Shannon entropy of the distribution of 1-min returns measures the randomness/predictability of price action. Low entropy (returns clustered in a few bins) indicates structured, predictable market behavior — ideal for directional trading. High entropy (returns uniformly distributed) indicates random, unpredictable behavior — no edge. By computing the Shannon entropy of binned 1-min returns over a 50-bar rolling window and entering only during low-entropy periods (entropy < 70th percentile of historical distribution), we filter for predictable regimes. The inefficiency exists because entropy is an information-theoretic concept foreign to traditional technical analysis. Most traders have no concept of return distribution entropy.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; sufficient tick activity for 1-min bars

indicators.name: Low_Entropy
indicators.params: True if Entropy_Pctile < 0.30 (bottom 30% of entropy = highly structured)

indicators.name: Dominant_Direction
indicators.params: sign(mean(Returns_1min, 50)) — direction of the structured returns

long.confirmation: Low_Entropy persists for at least 5 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: Low_Entropy persists for at least 5 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 0.8 * ATR(14) profit, trail at 0.4 * ATR(14) from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Entropy_Pctile rises above 0.70 (regime shifting to high entropy / random)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:05 (need 50 bars for entropy computation) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — entropy-based filtering replaces trend filter
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: Number of non-zero bins in histogram must be >= 5 (sufficient diversity for meaningful entropy)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — entropy computation from information theory is uncommon in trading; the concept is academically rigorous but practically obscure

weaknesses: Entropy computed on 50 1-min returns with 10 bins means most bins have 5 or fewer observations — the histogram is sparse, making the entropy estimate unreliable and sensitive to bin width choice
Low-entropy periods can coincide with low-volume lunch hours (12:00-13:00 IST) where returns are clustered near zero not because of structure but because of inactivity — false low-entropy signal
The 20-day historical entropy distribution used for percentile ranking may shift significantly during earnings season or macro events, invalidating the calibration
prior_art: Shannon (1948) information theory; Bandt & Pompe (2002) on permutation entropy for time series; Risso (2008) on entropy and stock market crashes; Hou & Li (2014) on information entropy and stock returns
notes: Consider using permutation entropy instead of Shannon entropy on binned returns — permutation entropy is more robust to small sample sizes and does not require arbitrary binning. Sample entropy (SampEn) is another alternative.

name: rolling_sharpe_adaptive_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: A strategy's real-time performance (measured by rolling Sharpe ratio of its own recent trades) provides information about whether current market conditions are favorable. By computing a rolling Sharpe ratio over the last 20 trade outcomes and scaling position size proportionally, we ride winning streaks with larger size and cut losers with smaller size — a form of adaptive position sizing. The base signal is a simple VWAP + EMA momentum system; the innovation is in the meta-layer that adjusts sizing based on recent strategy performance. The inefficiency exists because most traders use fixed sizing and don't dynamically adapt to their own recent track record. This exploits the regime-clustering phenomenon: winning trades cluster in favorable regimes, and losing trades cluster in unfavorable ones.

conditions: VWAP_Distance > 5 bps (not just barely above vwap)
Rolling_Trade_Sharpe > -1.0 (not in deep drawdown — don't enter when losing badly)
long.confirmation: Volume > SMA(volume, 15) on entry bar

short.confirmation: Volume > SMA(volume, 15) on entry bar

exit.trailing_stop: After 20 bps profit, trail at 12 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: EMA(close,9) crosses EMA(close,21) against position direction

risk.position_sizing: Adaptive: base ₹1L * Size_Multiplier (range ₹50K to ₹2L based on rolling Sharpe)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; if VIX > 20, cap Size_Multiplier at 1.0
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 or after 15:15
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction should agree with trade direction
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: Must have at least 10 completed trades in trade log before adaptive sizing activates (use fixed ₹1L for first 10)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — the adaptive sizing meta-layer adds value independent of the base signal; even a mediocre base strategy benefits from performance-proportional sizing

weaknesses: Rolling Sharpe on 20 trades has very high variance — a single large winner or loser can swing the Sharpe dramatically, causing abrupt position size changes that amplify risk

The adaptive sizing creates a pro-cyclical dynamic: after a winning streak, size increases, so the next loss (which is statistically inevitable) is disproportionately large — can give back streak gains in one trade
Base signal (EMA 9/21 crossover + VWAP) is generic — the adaptive sizing layer cannot compensate for a fundamentally weak entry signal; it only helps during favorable regime clustering
prior_art: Kelly criterion for optimal sizing; Tharp's position sizing concepts in 'Trade Your Way to Financial Freedom'; adaptive position sizing discussed in Vince's 'The Leverage Space Trading Model'
notes: Consider using a geometric Kelly fraction instead of linear Sharpe scaling for mathematically optimal sizing. Also consider capping the Size_Multiplier increase rate (max 10% increase per trade) to smooth the transition.

name: drawdown_adaptive_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: During drawdown periods, reducing position size preserves capital for recovery; during equity growth periods, increasing size compounds gains. By tracking the strategy's intraday equity curve and scaling positions based on current drawdown from session high-water mark, we implement an anti-martingale approach: full size at zero drawdown, 75% at 0.3% drawdown, 50% at 0.6% drawdown, and flat at 1% drawdown (daily loss limit). The base signal is a Supertrend + VWAP trend-following system. The inefficiency exists because most traders use fixed sizing throughout the day regardless of their P&L, or worse, increase size after losses (martingale), which is mathematically suboptimal for finite capital.

indicators.name: Session_PnL
indicators.params: cumulative P&L from all trades since 09:15

long.confirmation: close remains above Supertrend for 2 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: close remains below Supertrend for 2 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Supertrend flips direction against position

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; start at Size_Scale * 0.75 if VIX > 20
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:20 or after 15:15
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 must be above its VWAP for longs, below for shorts
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: If 3 consecutive losses, pause trading for 30 min regardless of DD level

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — drawdown-adaptive sizing is a risk management technique independent of market conditions; its effectiveness is mathematical rather than alpha-dependent

weaknesses: The strategy reduces size after losses, which means if the market regime recovers, it catches the recovery with smaller size — the best trading periods may follow drawdowns, and we're under-positioned
Size_Scale step function creates discontinuities — at 0.29% drawdown the size is ₹1L, at 0.31% it drops to ₹75K; a single additional loss triggers a 25% size cut that may be premature
Starting capital assumption for DD_Pct calculation is ambiguous for intraday — is it session starting capital (₹5L?) or per-trade capital (₹1L)? This affects threshold calibration significantly
prior_art: Anti-martingale position sizing in Jones's 'The Trading Game'; drawdown control in Tharp's position sizing; maximum drawdown constraints in portfolio optimization (Chekhlov et al. 2005)
notes: Consider using a continuous sigmoid function for Size_Scale instead of step function: Size_Scale = 1 / (1 + exp(10 * (DD_Pct - 0.5))). This smooths the transition and avoids cliff effects. Starting capital should be defined as the daily allocated capital (e.g., ₹5L).

name: correlation_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Individual stocks' correlation with their parent index (NIFTY 50 or Bank NIFTY) varies intraday. When a stock's rolling 30-bar correlation with the index drops below 0.3 (decoupled), the stock is driven by idiosyncratic factors — if these are positive (stock up, index flat), the move tends to persist (information-driven). When correlation is high (> 0.7), the stock moves mechanically with the index — better to trade the index directly. We trade only in the decoupled regime, buying stocks that are up while the index is flat (positive alpha) and shorting stocks that are down while the index is flat (negative alpha). The inefficiency exists because most traders don't compute real-time stock-index correlation.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; historical beta to NIFTY between 0.7 and 1.5

indicators.name: Alpha_30
indicators.params: sum(Stock_Returns, 30) - beta * sum(NIFTY_Returns, 30) where beta = historical_beta_60d

conditions: Alpha_30 > 20 bps (stock generating positive alpha while decoupled)
NIFTY_Flat == True (index is flat — confirming idiosyncratic move)
long.confirmation: Alpha_30 has been positive for at least 10 bars (not a transient spike)

conditions: Alpha_30 < -20 bps (stock generating negative alpha while decoupled)
short.confirmation: Alpha_30 has been negative for at least 10 bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Rolling_Corr_30 rises above 0.50 (stock re-coupling with index — idiosyncratic edge gone)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; increase to ₹1.25L if abs(Alpha_30) > 40 bps (strong alpha signal)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 (high VIX = high correlation = fewer decoupled opportunities)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:45 (need 30 bars for correlation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Stock volume > SMA(volume, 20) during decoupled period
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY_Flat must be True (abs NIFTY 30-bar return < 15 bps)
filters.event_filter: Skip if stock has corporate action or earnings — decoupling may be event-driven and ephemeral
other_filters: Historical beta must be between 0.7-1.5 for meaningful correlation measurement

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — real-time correlation monitoring is computationally non-trivial; the concept of trading alpha during decoupled periods is less explored in retail

weaknesses: Correlation computed on 30 1-min returns has very wide confidence intervals — at 30 observations, a measured correlation of 0.30 has a 95% CI of roughly [0.0, 0.55], making the threshold unreliable

NIFTY_Flat requirement (abs return < 15 bps over 30 bars) is very restrictive — during active market hours, NIFTY rarely stays within 15 bps for 30 minutes, limiting opportunities to low-volume periods
Decoupling often occurs during news/events specific to the stock — these are precisely the situations where the stock may gap further in either direction, making the 25 bps stop inadequate
prior_art: Pairs trading (Gatev et al. 2006) uses correlation; stock-index relative value strategies at hedge funds; correlation breakdown discussed in Cont & Wagalath (2013); intraday alpha decomposition less documented
notes: Consider relaxing NIFTY_Flat to abs return < 30 bps for more frequent signals. The beta used for alpha computation should be re-estimated weekly to capture evolving stock-index relationship.

name: momentum_decay_adaptive_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Momentum decays at different rates depending on market conditions. By computing the half-life of momentum (how long it takes for an initial price impulse to lose half its effect, estimated via the AR(1) coefficient on 1-min returns), we adapt the holding period and exit strategy. When half-life is short (< 10 bars), momentum decays quickly — use tight targets, quick exits. When half-life is long (> 30 bars), momentum persists — use wide targets, trailing stops. The inefficiency exists because most momentum traders use fixed holding periods regardless of current momentum persistence. The half-life reveals whether to hold the full move or take quick profits.

indicators.name: AR1_Coeff
indicators.params: OLS regression: Return_t = alpha + phi * Return_{t-1}; phi = AR(1) coefficient on window=60

indicators.name: HL_Regime
indicators.params: FAST_DECAY if Half_Life < 10; SLOW_DECAY if Half_Life > 30; MEDIUM otherwise

conditions: HL_Regime != MEDIUM (must be in a defined half-life regime)
long.confirmation: Momentum_Signal remains positive for 3 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: Momentum_Signal remains negative for 3 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: FAST_DECAY: none (quick exit); SLOW_DECAY: trail 15 bps after 30 bps profit
exit.time_stop: FAST_DECAY: min(20, 2 * Half_Life) bars; SLOW_DECAY: min(90, 2 * Half_Life) bars
exit.signal_exit: AR1_Coeff turns negative (momentum regime shifts to mean-reversion)

risk.position_sizing: FAST_DECAY: ₹1.25L (quick in-out, larger size); SLOW_DECAY: ₹75K (longer hold, smaller size for risk management)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:45 (need 60 bars for AR(1) estimation) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction agrees with trade direction for SLOW_DECAY entries
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: AR1 regression R-squared > 0.05 (minimum explanatory power for the AR model)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — momentum half-life estimation is a quantitative concept rarely applied at 1-min frequency; the adaptive holding period based on half-life is novel

weaknesses: AR(1) coefficient estimated on 60 1-min returns is statistically noisy — the standard error of phi at n=60 is approximately 1/sqrt(60) ≈ 0.13, making the half-life estimate imprecise
Half-life formula assumes AR(1) is a good model for the returns process — in reality, intraday returns may follow GARCH or higher-order AR processes, making the simple AR(1) half-life misleading
MEDIUM regime (HL 10-30) is excluded, losing approximately 40% of potential trading opportunities; the boundary between regimes is arbitrary
prior_art: Momentum half-life concept from Ornstein-Uhlenbeck mean-reversion estimation; AR(1) models in Box & Jenkins; applied to pairs trading by Bertram (2010); intraday momentum decay less studied
notes: Consider using ADF test (Augmented Dickey-Fuller) to check if the price series is stationary before computing half-life — half-life is only meaningful for stationary (mean-reverting) or persistent processes. For non-stationary random walks, the concept doesn't apply.

name: mean_reversion_speed_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The speed at which a stock reverts to its mean (VWAP) can be estimated by fitting an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) process to the VWAP deviation series: dx = theta * (mu - x) * dt + sigma * dW. The theta parameter (mean-reversion speed) tells us how quickly deviations from VWAP are corrected. High theta (> 0.05 per bar): fast reversion, enter on large deviations and expect quick profit. Low theta (< 0.02 per bar): slow reversion, the deviation may persist, so avoid mean-reversion trades. By estimating theta in real-time on a 60-bar rolling window of VWAP deviations, we only trade mean-reversion when the statistical evidence supports it. The inefficiency exists because VWAP mean-reversion traders rarely quantify the reversion speed.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹75 Cr; stock must have stable VWAP (not dominated by single large trade)

indicators.name: VWAP_Dev
indicators.params: close - vwap (absolute deviation in price units)

indicators.name: OU_Theta
indicators.params: OLS regression: delta(VWAP_Dev) = theta * VWAP_Dev + intercept, window=60; theta = -slope

indicators.name: Expected_HL
indicators.params: log(2) / OU_Theta (expected half-life of reversion in bars)

conditions: Z_Score_VWAP < -2.0 (price significantly below VWAP in OU model terms)
long.confirmation: OU_Theta has been > 0.03 for at least 10 bars (stable mean-reverting regime)

short.confirmation: OU_Theta has been > 0.03 for at least 10 bars

exit.target: Z_Score_VWAP crosses zero (full reversion to VWAP)
exit.stop_loss: Z_Score_VWAP reaches -3.0 for longs / +3.0 for shorts (deviation worsens)
exit.trailing_stop: None — pure mean-reversion, target is VWAP
exit.signal_exit: OU_Theta drops below 0.02 (mean-reversion weakening — stop expecting reversion)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with OU_Theta: higher theta = more confidence = larger size. ₹75K if theta 0.05-0.08, ₹1L if 0.08-0.12, ₹1.25L if > 0.12

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 (mean-reversion works best in calm markets)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for OU estimation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Volume > SMA(volume, 20) — sufficient liquidity for VWAP to be meaningful
filters.trend_filter: abs(EMA(NIFTY_50, 30) - EMA(NIFTY_50, 60)) / EMA(NIFTY_50, 60) < 30 bps (index not in strong trend)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day and RBI policy day
other_filters: OU regression R-squared > 0.10 (minimum fit quality for the OU model)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — OU process estimation for mean-reversion speed is a quantitative technique rarely applied to intraday VWAP trading; the statistical rigor provides a moat

weaknesses: OU process assumes constant theta and sigma within the 60-bar window — in reality, both parameters are time-varying (e.g., theta drops as VWAP deviation grows large), violating model assumptions
Z-score based on OU parameters inherits all estimation errors from theta and sigma — a 10% error in theta translates to large errors in Z-score and Expected_HL
The strategy only enters on Z_Score > 2.0, which combined with the high theta requirement, produces very few signals — may generate only 1-2 trades per day across entire universe
prior_art: Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process for mean-reversion (Uhlenbeck & Ornstein 1930); applied to pairs trading in Bertram (2010); VWAP mean-reversion is common but formal OU estimation is rare
notes: Consider using maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) instead of OLS for OU parameters — MLE is more efficient for small samples. The theta threshold of 0.05 corresponds to a half-life of ~14 bars (14 minutes), which is reasonable for intraday mean-reversion.

name: dynamic_stop_regime_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Fixed stop-losses are a primary source of unnecessary losses in intraday trading — too tight in volatile regimes (stopped out by noise before move materializes), too wide in calm regimes (give back too much profit when wrong). By dynamically setting stop-loss distance based on current volatility regime (ATR percentile), we optimize the probability of being stopped out by noise versus genuine reversal. Low-vol regime (ATR_Pctile < 30): stop = 1.0 * ATR(14). Medium-vol (30-70): stop = 1.5 * ATR(14). High-vol (>70): stop = 2.5 * ATR(14). The base signal is EMA(10)/EMA(25) crossover with VWAP confirmation. The inefficiency is that most traders use fixed bps stops that don't adapt to current conditions.

indicators.name: Vol_Regime
indicators.params: LOW if ATR_Pctile < 30; MED if 30-70; HIGH if > 70

indicators.name: Dynamic_Stop_Mult
indicators.params: 1.0 if Vol_Regime == LOW; 1.5 if MED; 2.5 if HIGH

conditions: Stop_Distance / close * 10000 < 60 bps (max allowable stop distance)
long.confirmation: Volume > SMA(volume, 15) on entry bar

short.confirmation: Volume > SMA(volume, 15) on entry bar

exit.stop_loss: Stop_Distance from entry (dynamically sized by regime)
exit.trailing_stop: After 1.0 * Stop_Distance profit, trail at 0.6 * Stop_Distance from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: EMA(close,10) crosses EMA(close,25) against position direction

risk.position_sizing: Risk-normalized: position = capital * max_risk / Stop_Distance. Size automatically shrinks in high-vol (wider stops)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 28; if VIX > 24, use Dynamic_Stop_Mult = 3.0 (even wider stops)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 or after 15:15
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 must be trending in same direction (EMA(NIFTY,10) vs EMA(NIFTY,25))
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day; widen stops by 50% on RBI policy day
other_filters: Stop_Distance must be at least 10 bps (avoid degenerate stops in ultra-low-vol periods)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — dynamic stop sizing is a risk management innovation that improves any base strategy; the edge is structural, not signal-dependent

weaknesses: In HIGH-vol regime, 2.5 * ATR(14) can be very wide (40-60 bps for volatile bank stocks), meaning each loss is large — even with smaller position size, this can hit daily loss limits quickly
The 120-bar lookback for ATR percentile means the strategy misses rapid volatility regime changes that occur within the first 2 hours (e.g., sudden news at 10:00 when percentile is still calibrating)
The 60 bps maximum stop constraint can filter out valid HIGH-vol setups in highly volatile names, reducing the universe during the most volatile (and potentially profitable) sessions
prior_art: ATR-based stops (Wilder, Van Tharp); Keltner Channel stop placement; volatility-scaled position sizing common in CTAs; regime-dependent stop multipliers less standardized
notes: The 1.8:1 reward-to-risk ratio is designed to be profitable at 50% win rate after costs (1.8 * 0.50 - 1.0 * 0.50 = 0.40, minus ~9 bps costs ≈ 31 bps edge). Consider using a continuous function for Stop_Mult instead of discrete regime buckets.

name: kalman_filter_trend_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Traditional moving averages lag price because they weight all observations equally (SMA) or use fixed exponential decay (EMA). A Kalman filter estimates the hidden 'true trend' of price by optimally combining a prediction from a linear state-space model with noisy observations, dynamically adjusting the gain based on the ratio of process noise to observation noise. When the Kalman-estimated trend velocity (the slope state) is strongly positive or negative and the estimation uncertainty is low, we have high-confidence directional signals. The inefficiency exists because Kalman filters require understanding of state-space models and tuning of noise parameters (Q, R matrices), which is beyond most retail traders. The adaptive gain means the filter responds faster to genuine trend changes while smoothing noise.

indicators.name: KF_Level
indicators.params: Kalman filter state[0]: estimated price level; Q=[[0.01,0],[0,0.001]], R=0.1, initialized at first bar

indicators.name: KF_Velocity
indicators.params: Kalman filter state[1]: estimated price velocity (bps per bar)

indicators.name: KF_Uncertainty
indicators.params: sqrt(P[0,0]) where P is Kalman covariance matrix

conditions: KF_Signal_Strength > 2.0 (velocity is statistically significant at ~2 sigma)
close > KF_Level (price above Kalman estimated level)
long.confirmation: KF_Velocity has been positive for at least 5 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: KF_Velocity has been negative for at least 5 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 30 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: KF_Velocity changes sign (Kalman trend reversal)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with KF_Signal_Strength: ₹75K if strength 2.0-3.0, ₹1L if 3.0-4.0, ₹1.25L if > 4.0

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; increase observation noise R by 50% if VIX > 20
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 (Kalman needs ~10 bars to converge from initialization) or after 15:15
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 KF_Velocity should agree with stock KF_Velocity direction
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day; re-initialize Kalman filter on earnings day with higher Q (more process noise)
other_filters: KF_Uncertainty must be below 2x the initial uncertainty (filter has converged)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — Kalman filter implementation requires state-space modeling expertise; noise parameter tuning (Q, R) is the moat — poor tuning gives poor signals

weaknesses: Kalman filter assumes linear dynamics with Gaussian noise — financial returns are heavy-tailed and non-linear, violating both assumptions; large gap moves or jumps cause the filter to lag or overshoot
Noise parameters Q and R must be tuned offline and are assumed constant within the session — misspecification (e.g., Q too small) makes the filter sluggish, while Q too large makes it noisy
The filter is recursive from session start, meaning early-session signals are unreliable because the covariance matrix P hasn't converged — typically need 10-20 bars for convergence
prior_art: Kalman (1960) linear filter; applied to finance in Harvey (1990) 'Forecasting, Structural Time Series and the Kalman Filter'; Wells (1998) and Montana et al. (2009) on Kalman filter for pairs trading
notes: Consider using an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to handle the non-linearities in price dynamics. The Q and R parameters should be estimated from previous session data using expectation maximization. Python's filterpy library provides efficient Kalman filter implementation.

name: wavelet_decomposition_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Financial price series contain information at multiple time scales — noise at the shortest scales, intraday trends at medium scales, and session-level direction at longer scales. Wavelet decomposition (Daubechies db4, 3-level) separates these scales cleanly, unlike moving averages which blur all frequencies together. By reconstructing the price using only the level-2 and level-3 detail coefficients (capturing 4-bar to 16-bar cycles), we extract the 'tradeable frequency' while discarding both noise (level-1) and slow drift (approximation). Trading signals are generated from the denoised price crossover with the original price. The inefficiency exists because wavelet analysis requires signal processing knowledge foreign to most traders.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; sufficient 1-min data for wavelet decomposition (at least 64 bars)

indicators.name: Wavelet_Denoised
indicators.params: pywt.wavedec(close, 'db4', level=3); zero out cD1 coefficients; reconstruct via pywt.waverec

indicators.name: Detail_Energy_L2
indicators.params: sum(cD2^2) / sum(all_coefficients^2) — proportion of energy at level 2

conditions: close crosses above Wavelet_Denoised (raw price emerging above denoised trend)
Detail_Energy_L2 > 0.20 (sufficient energy at tradeable frequency — market is moving)
long.confirmation: close > Wavelet_Denoised for 2 consecutive bars after crossover

short.confirmation: close < Wavelet_Denoised for 2 consecutive bars after crossover

exit.trailing_stop: After 20 bps profit, trail at 12 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Denoised_Slope crosses zero against position direction

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; scale to ₹1.25L if Detail_Energy_L2 > 0.35 (strong cycle at tradeable frequency)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:20 (need 64 bars for wavelet decomposition) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: Denoised_Slope of NIFTY 50 must agree with trade direction
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: Wavelet decomposition must use at least 64 data points for 3-level db4 decomposition

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — wavelet decomposition is from signal processing, not finance; very few traders implement it for real-time trading; the denoising provides genuinely cleaner signals than EMAs

weaknesses: Wavelet decomposition on a rolling window introduces boundary effects — the most recent coefficients are least reliable, which is precisely where trading signals are generated
The 64-bar minimum window means no trading until 10:20 IST, missing the morning session; and each recomputation on the full window adds latency

Choosing db4 wavelet and 3-level decomposition is somewhat arbitrary — different wavelets (Haar, Symlet) and levels produce different decompositions, and there's no principled way to select the 'right' one for financial data
prior_art: Ramsey & Lampart (1998) on wavelets in economics; Gençay et al. (2001) 'An Introduction to Wavelets and Other Filtering Methods in Finance and Economics'; wavelet denoising for trading signals in Addison (2002)
notes: Consider using the stationary wavelet transform (SWT) instead of the discrete wavelet transform (DWT) to avoid boundary effects. The pywt library in Python provides both. Also consider maximal overlap DWT (MODWT) for shift-invariant decomposition.

name: spectral_analysis_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Intraday price action contains periodic components driven by institutional activity cycles (e.g., portfolio rebalancing every 30-60 minutes, lunch lull at 12:00-13:00, closing auction effects). By computing the FFT (Fast Fourier Transform) of 1-min returns over a 128-bar rolling window and identifying the dominant cycle period, we can time entries to coincide with the expected trough of the dominant cycle (buy at cycle low, sell at cycle high).
