The spectral power at the dominant frequency must be significantly above the noise floor (> 3x mean spectral power). The inefficiency exists because FFT cycle detection is a signal processing technique that requires understanding of frequency-domain analysis, unfamiliar to most traders.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; stock must have sufficient intraday periodicity (detectable dominant cycle)
hold_time: half of dominant cycle period (typically 10-30 min)

indicators.name: FFT_Spectrum
indicators.params: abs(fft(detrend(close, 128)))[1:64] — power spectrum of detrended 128-bar close

indicators.name: Spectral_Ratio
indicators.params: max(FFT_Spectrum) / mean(FFT_Spectrum) — how dominant the peak is

indicators.name: Cycle_Phase
indicators.params: current position within dominant cycle (0 = trough, pi = peak)

conditions: Cycle_Phase near 0 (within pi/6 of trough — buy at cycle low)
close < vwap (VWAP confirmation of being at a local low)
long.confirmation: Price starts rising from cycle trough: ROC(close, 2) > 0

conditions: Cycle_Phase near pi (within pi/6 of peak — sell at cycle high)
close > vwap (VWAP confirmation of being at a local high)
short.confirmation: Price starts falling from cycle peak: ROC(close, 2) < 0

exit.target: Hold for approximately half of Dominant_Period (cycle trough to peak or vice versa)
exit.stop_loss: If price moves > 1.5x expected cycle amplitude against position
exit.signal_exit: Spectral_Ratio drops below 2.0 (cycle losing significance — go flat)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with Spectral_Ratio: ₹75K if ratio 3-4, ₹1L if 4-6, ₹1.25L if > 6

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 (cyclical patterns break down in high-volatility environments)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 11:20 (need 128 bars = 2hr 8min for FFT) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: Detrending must remove linear trend before FFT — residual must be stationary
filters.event_filter: Skip on earnings day, budget day, RBI policy day (event-driven moves destroy cycles)
other_filters: Dominant_Period must be stable: same dominant period (± 2 bars) for last 20 bars

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — FFT-based cycle detection is well-known in signal processing but rarely applied correctly to financial data; the edge depends on genuine cyclicality which may be intermittent

weaknesses: Financial returns are not truly periodic — any apparent cyclicality is likely transient and regime-dependent; the FFT may find a 'dominant' frequency that is noise rather than signal
128-bar window is too short for reliable spectral estimation — the frequency resolution is 1/128 = 0.0078 cycles/bar, meaning the algorithm cannot distinguish between, say, 20-bar and 22-bar cycles
Late session start (11:20 IST) misses the first 2+ hours of trading; and the cycle phase estimation has inherent uncertainty that can place entries minutes too early or late
prior_art: Ehlers' 'Rocket Science for Traders' and 'Cybernetic Analysis' extensively cover spectral methods; Granger & Morgenstern (1970) on spectral analysis of economic time series; Fisher Transform discussed in Ehlers' work
notes: Consider using Lomb-Scargle periodogram instead of FFT for unevenly sampled data (when bars are missing). Also consider Hilbert transform for instantaneous phase estimation, which handles non-stationary cycles better than FFT.

name: pca_factor_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Principal Component Analysis on 1-min returns of NIFTY 50 constituents extracts the main factors driving cross-sectional returns: PC1 ≈ market factor (all stocks move together), PC2 ≈ sector rotation factor (e.g., banks vs IT), PC3+ ≈ idiosyncratic signals. By computing rolling PCA on a 60-bar window and identifying stocks whose residual (unexplained by top 3 PCs) is extreme (> 2 sigma), we find stocks with temporary idiosyncratic dislocations that tend to revert as the factor structure reasserts. The inefficiency exists because real-time PCA on 50 stocks at 1-min frequency requires significant computation and linear algebra knowledge. The edge is in identifying factor-adjusted mispricings rather than raw price moves.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents (all 50 used for PCA; trade those with extreme residuals)
stock_filter: All 50 constituents used for PCA computation; trade those with ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr

indicators.name: Returns_Matrix
indicators.params: 50 x 60 matrix of 1-min returns for all NIFTY 50 stocks

indicators.name: Residual
indicators.params: actual_return - factor_return for each stock (current bar)

indicators.name: Variance_Explained
indicators.params: sum of top 3 PC explained variance ratios

conditions: Residual_Zscore < -2.0 (stock significantly underperforming its factor-explained return — idiosyncratic oversold)
Variance_Explained > 0.50 (top 3 PCs explain > 50% of cross-sectional variance — factor structure is strong)
long.confirmation: Residual_Zscore starts improving: Residual_Zscore > Residual_Zscore[2 bars ago]

conditions: Residual_Zscore > 2.0 (stock significantly outperforming its factor-explained return — idiosyncratic overbought)
short.confirmation: Residual_Zscore starts declining: Residual_Zscore < Residual_Zscore[2 bars ago]

exit.target: Residual_Zscore reverts to 0 (stock returns to factor-explained level)
exit.stop_loss: Residual_Zscore reaches -3.5 for longs / +3.5 for shorts (dislocation worsens)
exit.trailing_stop: None — signal-based exit on residual reversion
exit.signal_exit: abs(Residual_Zscore) < 0.5 (residual has substantially reverted)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; increase to ₹1.25L if Variance_Explained > 0.65 (strong factor structure implies more reliable residual signals)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; high VIX disrupts the factor structure
filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for PCA) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: All 50 stocks must have traded in last 10 bars for valid PCA
filters.trend_filter: None — PCA residuals are by construction factor-neutral (market trend removed)
filters.spread_filter: Bid-ask spread < 5 bps on target stock
filters.event_filter: Remove any stock with earnings today from PCA computation (outlier returns corrupt factors)
other_filters: At least 45 of 50 stocks must have complete data for valid PCA

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — real-time PCA on 50 stocks at 1-min frequency is computationally demanding and conceptually sophisticated; statistical arbitrage approach is used by hedge funds but not at this frequency in India

weaknesses: PCA on 60 observations of 50 variables is statistically degenerate (more variables than observations) — the eigenvectors are unstable and can flip sign between windows, causing spurious residual spikes
The residual 'reversion' assumption depends on the factor structure being stable — during sector rotation or macro shocks, the factor structure itself changes, and residuals may not revert
PCA recomputation on each bar for 50 stocks (60x50 matrix eigendecomposition) is O(N³) and may exceed latency budget for real-time 1-min trading without optimized numerical libraries
prior_art: Statistical arbitrage (Avellaneda & Lee 2010); PCA for factor extraction in finance (Connor & Korajczyk 1986); Barra risk model uses PCA; intraday stat-arb discussed in Cont & Kukanov (2017)
notes: Consider using incremental PCA (sklearn.decomposition.IncrementalPCA) for efficient online updates rather than full recomputation. Also consider using only the first 2 PCs and grouping residuals by sector for more interpretable signals.

name: cointegration_residual_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Cointegrated stock pairs (stocks that share a long-run equilibrium despite short-term divergences) provide mean-reversion opportunities when their spread deviates from equilibrium. Unlike correlation, cointegration implies a stable long-run relationship. By applying the Johansen cointegration test to 20-day rolling 1-min data for pre-screened NIFTY 50 pairs (same sector, similar market cap), and trading the spread when the normalized residual exceeds ± 2 sigma, we capture spread reversion. The inefficiency exists because cointegration testing requires econometric expertise, and maintaining a real-time cointegration-adjusted spread across multiple pairs is infrastructure-heavy.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituent pairs within same GICS sector (e.g., HDFCBANK-ICICIBANK, TCS-INFOSYS)
stock_filter: Both pair members: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; Johansen test p-value < 0.05 on 20-day rolling data

indicators.name: Coint_Vector
indicators.params: Johansen cointegration vector (beta) from trace test, estimated on 20-day rolling 1-min data

indicators.name: Coint_PValue
indicators.params: Johansen trace test p-value (re-estimated daily before session)

conditions: Spread_Zscore < -2.0 (spread significantly below equilibrium — long A, short B)
Spread_Zscore is not trending further down: Spread_Zscore > min(Spread_Zscore, last 10 bars)
long.confirmation: Spread_Zscore turns up: Spread_Zscore > Spread_Zscore[2 bars ago]

conditions: Spread_Zscore > 2.0 (spread significantly above equilibrium — short A, long B)
Spread_Zscore is not trending further up: Spread_Zscore < max(Spread_Zscore, last 10 bars)
short.confirmation: Spread_Zscore turns down: Spread_Zscore < Spread_Zscore[2 bars ago]

entry.entry_price: simultaneous market orders on both legs (long A + short B, or vice versa)

exit.target: Spread_Zscore reverts to 0 (spread returns to equilibrium)
exit.stop_loss: Spread_Zscore reaches -3.5 for long spread / +3.5 for short spread
exit.signal_exit: abs(Spread_Zscore) < 0.3 (spread substantially reverted)

risk.position_sizing: Equal notional on both legs: ₹50K long + ₹50K short; scale with abs(Spread_Zscore): larger deviation = larger size, capped at ₹75K per leg

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, cointegration relationships may temporarily break
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 60 bars for spread statistics) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Both stocks must have volume > SMA(volume, 20) on entry bar
filters.trend_filter: None — pairs trade is market-neutral by construction
filters.event_filter: Skip pair if either stock has earnings today or tomorrow
other_filters: Coint_Vector must be re-estimated daily; intraday drift in beta is possible but assumed small

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — pairs trading is well-known; the edge is in the cointegration-based spread construction (vs simple ratio/price difference) and the intraday application with proper Johansen testing

weaknesses: Cointegration is a long-run property (typically tested on daily data over months/years) — testing on 20 days of 1-min data may detect spurious cointegration that is not economically meaningful
Two-legged execution doubles transaction costs (slippage and brokerage on both legs) and creates execution risk — if one leg fills and the other doesn't, you have unhedged directional exposure
Cointegration vectors (beta) estimated on historical data may drift within the session — if beta changes from 0.9 to 1.0, the spread signal is miscalibrated and entries may be premature
prior_art: Johansen (1991) cointegration test; Gatev, Goetzmann & Rouwenhorst (2006) pairs trading; Vidyamurthy (2004) 'Pairs Trading'; intraday cointegration applications in Avellaneda & Lee (2010)
notes: The biggest practical challenge is simultaneous execution of both legs — consider using a smart order router that submits both legs atomically. Pre-screen pairs daily and maintain a watchlist of 5-10 cointegrated pairs to monitor during the session.

name: granger_causality_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Certain stocks lead others in intraday price discovery — large-cap liquid names (RELIANCE, HDFCBANK) tend to move before smaller peers in the same sector (BPCL, FEDERALBNK). By computing rolling Granger causality tests on pairs of stocks (does stock A's lagged return predict stock B's future return?), we identify lead-lag relationships in real-time. When the leader moves but the follower hasn't yet responded, we trade the follower in the expected direction. The inefficiency exists because Granger causality requires econometric testing at each time step and the lead-lag relationships are dynamic (they shift based on which stock has more information flow). Retail traders use vague notions of 'sector leaders' but don't quantify the lead-lag with statistical rigor.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituent pairs where one is likely a price leader (larger, more liquid)
stock_filter: Leader: ADV(20) > ₹200 Cr; Follower: ADV(20) > ₹50 Cr; same GICS sector
hold_time: 5-20 min (short because exploiting a transient lead-lag gap)

indicators.name: GC_F_Stat
indicators.params: Granger causality F-statistic (leader → follower, lag=3, window=60)

indicators.name: Lag_Gap
indicators.params: Leader_Return_5 - Follower_Return_5 (how far follower lags leader)

conditions: Leader_Return_5 > 20 bps (leader has moved up significantly in last 5 bars)
Follower_Return_5 < 5 bps (follower has not yet responded — lag gap > 15 bps)
Follower close < follower vwap OR follower close within 5 bps of vwap (hasn't caught up)
long.confirmation: Leader_Return_5 remains > 15 bps on next bar (leader move is sustained)

conditions: Leader_Return_5 < -20 bps (leader has moved down significantly)
Follower_Return_5 > -5 bps (follower has not yet responded)
Follower close > follower vwap OR follower close within 5 bps of vwap
short.confirmation: Leader_Return_5 remains < -15 bps on next bar

entry.entry_price: market order on follower stock on confirmation

exit.target: Lag_Gap closes to < 5 bps (follower has caught up to leader)
exit.stop_loss: 20 bps from entry (leader move was false signal)
exit.trailing_stop: After 15 bps profit, trail at 8 bps from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: 30 bars (30 min — if follower hasn't responded by then, the gap is structural, not transient)
exit.signal_exit: Leader reverses direction: Leader_Return_5 changes sign

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L on follower; no position on leader (not pairs trading — directional on follower)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, lead-lag relationships become unreliable (correlations spike to 1)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 60+ bars for Granger test) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Both leader and follower must have volume > SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction should agree with leader's move direction
filters.spread_filter: Follower bid-ask spread < 5 bps (follower may be less liquid)
filters.event_filter: Skip if either stock has earnings; the lead-lag relationship is disrupted by idiosyncratic news
other_filters: GC test must use at least 60 observations; re-test every 30 bars

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — lead-lag relationships are well-known among institutional traders; the Granger causality formalization adds rigor but the concept is not novel; speed of execution matters

weaknesses: Granger causality on 60 1-min returns has low statistical power — the test may not detect genuine lead-lag with only 60 observations, leading to false negatives (missed trades) or false positives (spurious causality)
The follower may not respond because the leader's move is idiosyncratic (not sector-wide) — the gap is structural, not a lag, and the follower correctly ignores the leader's move
Short holding period (5-20 min) means the follower's response must happen quickly; in reality, some lead-lag effects take 30-60 minutes to propagate, exceeding the time stop
prior_art: Granger (1969) causality test; Lo & MacKinlay (1990) on cross-autocorrelation and lead-lag; Brennan et al. (1993) on information content; intraday lead-lag in Indian markets studied by Ullah et al.
notes: Consider using Vector Autoregression (VAR) instead of pairwise Granger causality to capture multi-stock lead-lag relationships simultaneously. Pre-screen leader-follower pairs overnight using daily data, then monitor intraday.

name: information_ratio_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The information ratio (IR = alpha / tracking_error relative to NIFTY 50) computed on rolling intraday data identifies which stocks are currently generating the best risk-adjusted alpha. By computing the 60-bar rolling IR for all NIFTY 50 stocks and entering the top 3 by IR (in their current direction), we systematically allocate capital to stocks with the strongest risk-adjusted outperformance. Stocks with high positive IR are generating consistent alpha above the index; stocks with low/negative IR are lagging. The inefficiency exists because IR is a portfolio evaluation metric (monthly/quarterly), not typically used as a real-time stock selection tool at 1-min frequency.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituents — rank by rolling IR, trade top 3
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; all 50 constituents ranked by IR

indicators.name: Alpha_60
indicators.params: mean(stock_return_1min - beta * NIFTY_return_1min, window=60) * 60 (annualized to per-hour)

indicators.name: IR_Rank
indicators.params: cross-sectional rank of Info_Ratio among all NIFTY 50 stocks

indicators.name: IR_Stability
indicators.params: std(Info_Ratio, window=20) — lower = more stable IR

conditions: Info_Ratio > 1.0 (minimum IR threshold for quality signal)
Alpha_60 > 0 (positive alpha, not just low tracking error)
long.confirmation: IR_Rank has been in top 5 for at least 10 bars (stable outperformance, not spike)

short.confirmation: IR_Rank has been in bottom 5 for at least 10 bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: IR_Rank drops out of top 10 (for longs) or rises above bottom 10 (for shorts)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L per position; allocate to top 3 stocks by IR, equal weight

filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for IR computation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Selected stocks must have volume > SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction should be consistent (not whipsawing) for IR to be meaningful
filters.event_filter: Remove stocks with earnings today from ranking (abnormal alpha contaminates IR)
other_filters: IR_Stability must be < 2.0 (IR is relatively stable, not spiking randomly)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — IR as a selection criterion is novel at intraday frequency; however, it is essentially momentum-on-alpha which is a known concept

weaknesses: Information ratio on 60 1-min returns is statistically unreliable — with 60 observations, the estimated IR has a standard error of approximately 1/sqrt(60) ≈ 0.13, making the threshold of 1.0 barely distinguishable from 0.87
Top-3 ranking creates a competitive selection problem — on quiet days, even the top-ranked stock may have IR barely above zero, and we're selecting the 'least bad' rather than 'genuinely good'

The strategy is essentially momentum-on-alpha — stocks that have outperformed recently tend to continue. But at 60-bar lookback on 1-min data, this captures only 1-hour persistence which may not extrapolate
prior_art: Information ratio concept from Grinold & Kahn (2000) 'Active Portfolio Management'; momentum factor (Jegadeesh-Titman); cross-sectional momentum used in Fama-French models; intraday application is novel
notes: Consider using the Treynor ratio (excess return / beta) instead of IR for stocks with different betas. Also consider decay-weighting the 60-bar window (more recent returns get higher weight) using an exponentially weighted version.

name: maximum_entropy_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: The maximum entropy distribution consistent with observed mean and variance of 1-min returns provides the least biased estimate of the true return distribution. When the observed return falls in the extreme tails of this maximum entropy distribution (beyond the 5th or 95th percentile), it is genuinely extreme rather than just 'unusual under a normal assumption.' By calibrating the MaxEnt distribution from rolling moments (mean, variance, skewness) on a 60-bar window and entering when the current return exceeds the MaxEnt 95th percentile (fade) or confirms a MaxEnt breakout (follow), we get statistically rigorous extreme-event signals. The inefficiency is that most traders use normal distribution assumptions (z-scores), which underestimate tail probability and overtrade false extremes.

indicators.name: MaxEnt_P5
indicators.params: 5th percentile of MaxEnt distribution fitted to (Rolling_Mean, Rolling_Var, Rolling_Skew)

indicators.name: MaxEnt_Tail_Event
indicators.params: True if Return_1min < MaxEnt_P5 OR Return_1min > MaxEnt_P95

conditions: Return_1min < MaxEnt_P5 (extreme negative return — genuinely unusual under MaxEnt)
close < vwap (VWAP confirmation of being oversold)
Rolling_Skew > -1.0 (distribution not too negatively skewed — left tail events revert)
long.confirmation: Next bar return > 0 (initial bounce from extreme — uptick confirmation)

conditions: Return_1min > MaxEnt_P95 (extreme positive return — genuinely unusual under MaxEnt)
short.confirmation: Next bar return < 0 (initial fade from extreme — downtick confirmation)

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation bar close

exit.stop_loss: 20 bps from entry (tight — if extreme persists, exit quickly)
exit.trailing_stop: After 20 bps profit, trail at 10 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Return moves back within MaxEnt_P25 to MaxEnt_P75 range (no longer extreme)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; reduce to ₹75K if abs(Rolling_Skew) > 1.5 (highly skewed distributions have unreliable tail estimates)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22 (in high VIX, 'extreme' returns happen frequently, reducing the signal quality)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need 60 bars for moment estimation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Volume on extreme bar > 1.5 * SMA(volume, 20) (volume confirms the extreme move)
filters.trend_filter: abs(EMA(NIFTY_50, 20) slope) < 3 bps/bar (calm market — extremes more likely to revert)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day (extreme returns are information-driven, not noise)
other_filters: Rolling_Var must be > 0 (sufficient price movement for meaningful distribution fitting)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — maximum entropy distribution fitting is an advanced statistical concept; most traders use Gaussian z-scores which are less accurate for heavy-tailed financial returns

weaknesses: MaxEnt distribution fitting with 3 constraints (mean, variance, skewness) on 60 data points is numerically sensitive — the optimization can fail to converge or produce degenerate solutions
Extreme return events on 1-min bars are often driven by single large orders (block trades) that do not revert — the mean-reversion assumption fails for information-driven extremes
The target/stop ratio of 30/20 = 1.5 with 57% win rate gives gross edge of 30*0.57 - 20*0.43 = 8.5 bps per side; after ~9 bps costs, edge is marginal at best
prior_art: Jaynes (1957) maximum entropy principle; Buchen & Kelly (1996) on maximum entropy distributions in finance; application to trading signals is novel but builds on established statistical theory
notes: Consider using the observed empirical distribution (kernel density estimate) instead of parametric MaxEnt — it's simpler and avoids convergence issues. The MaxEnt approach is theoretically cleaner but practically harder. Also consider adding kurtosis as a 4th constraint for better tail estimation.

name: copula_dependence_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Standard correlation measures linear dependence but misses tail dependence — the tendency for stocks to move together during extreme events (crashes, rallies) differently than during normal periods. A Clayton copula captures lower tail dependence (crash co-movements) while a Gumbel copula captures upper tail dependence. By fitting a bivariate copula to rolling 120-bar returns of a stock pair and monitoring the conditional probability of stock B's extreme move given stock A's extreme move, we can identify when tail dependence is abnormally high (expect contagion) or abnormally low (divergence opportunity). The inefficiency exists because copula modeling requires advanced probability theory beyond most market participants.
universe: NIFTY 50 constituent pairs (same sector, high normal-time correlation > 0.6)
stock_filter: Both members: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; rolling correlation(60d daily returns) > 0.6

indicators.name: U_A
indicators.params: empirical_cdf(Return_A, window=120) — uniform marginal for stock A

indicators.name: U_B
indicators.params: empirical_cdf(Return_B, window=120) — uniform marginal for stock B

indicators.name: Copula_Theta
indicators.params: MLE estimate of Clayton copula parameter theta on (U_A, U_B), window=120

indicators.name: Cond_Prob
indicators.params: P(U_B < 0.10 | U_A < 0.10) from fitted copula — conditional crash probability

conditions: Stock A has U_A < 0.10 (extreme negative return for A)
Stock B has U_B > 0.30 (B has NOT crashed despite A crashing)
Cond_Prob > 0.40 (historically, when A crashes, B usually follows — but hasn't yet)
This divergence is unusual: Lower_Tail_Dep is in top quartile (Tail_Dep_Pctile > 0.75) historically, meaning the pair should move together in tails
long.confirmation: LONG stock A (buying the crashed leader expecting bounce) OR SHORT stock B (expecting contagion selloff). Direction determined by Cond_Prob direction

conditions: Stock A has U_A > 0.90 (extreme positive return for A)
Stock B has U_B < 0.70 (B has NOT rallied despite A rallying)
Tail dependence is historically high for this pair
short.confirmation: B starts catching up: ROC(B_close, 3) > 0 and moving toward A's direction

entry.entry_price: market order on confirmation of divergence

exit.target: U_A and U_B converge to within 20 percentile points of each other (tail dependence resolves)
exit.stop_loss: Divergence widens: abs(U_A - U_B) > 0.70 (pair has fully decoupled)
exit.signal_exit: Copula_Theta drops below 0.5 (tail dependence weakening fundamentally)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L on the divergent stock; or ₹50K on each leg if trading both sides

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during genuine crisis (VIX > 25), all stocks crash together (correlation → 1), making copula-based differentiation meaningless
filters.time_filter: No entries before 11:15 (need 120 bars for copula fitting) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Both stocks must have volume > SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: None — strategy trades tail events specifically
filters.event_filter: Skip pair if either stock has earnings (divergence may be fundamental, not transient)
other_filters: Copula fit must have sufficient goodness-of-fit (AIC of Clayton < AIC of independence copula)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — copula modeling is graduate-level probability theory; very few retail or even institutional traders implement real-time copula-based signals at 1-min frequency

weaknesses: Clayton copula MLE on 120 bivariate observations is statistically weak — the theta estimate has high variance, and 120 observations of (U_A, U_B) provide very few joint tail events for reliable tail dependence estimation
The strategy requires U_A < 0.10, which happens only ~12 times per 120-bar window by construction — signal frequency is extremely low (perhaps 1-2 per day across all pairs)

Choosing Clayton copula assumes lower tail dependence is the relevant structure — this may not hold for all stock pairs; some pairs may exhibit upper tail dependence (Gumbel) or symmetric (Frank) dependence instead
prior_art: Nelsen (2006) 'An Introduction to Copulas'; Patton (2006) on copulas for financial time series; copula-based pairs trading in Liew & Wu (2013); tail dependence in Ang & Chen (2002)
notes: Consider using a time-varying copula (e.g., DCC-copula) to capture evolving dependence structure. The copulalib or pyvinecopulib Python libraries provide efficient copula fitting. Pre-screen pairs daily and maintain a watchlist of 5-8 high-tail-dependence pairs.

name: robust_regression_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: OLS linear regression for trend estimation on 1-min bars is heavily influenced by outliers (single large bars from block trades or news). Huber robust regression down-weights outliers and provides a more stable trend estimate. By fitting a Huber regression (y=close, x=bar_index) on a rolling 30-bar window, the slope gives a robust trend estimate less sensitive to price spikes. When the Huber slope is significantly positive (t-stat > 2.0) and the current price is near or below the Huber regression line (buy dip in robust uptrend), we enter long. The inefficiency exists because standard linear regression is used everywhere but robust versions are not — the improvement in signal quality from outlier rejection is underappreciated.

indicators.name: Huber_Line
indicators.params: Huber_Intercept + Huber_Slope * bar_index (regression line value at current bar)

indicators.name: Residual_Std
indicators.params: MAD(Residual, 30) * 1.4826 (robust std from median absolute deviation)

indicators.name: Slope_TScore
indicators.params: Huber_Slope / (Residual_Std / sqrt(sum_x_sq)) — approximate t-statistic for slope

conditions: Residual < 0 (price is below robust trend line — buying dip in uptrend)
Residual / Residual_Std > -2.0 (not too far below — not an outlier itself)
long.confirmation: close starts reverting up: close > close[1 bar ago]

conditions: Residual > 0 (price is above robust trend line — selling rip in downtrend)
short.confirmation: close starts reverting down: close < close[1 bar ago]

exit.target: Residual crosses zero (price returns to robust trend line, capturing the dip/rip)
exit.stop_loss: Residual reaches -2.5 * Residual_Std for longs / +2.5 * Residual_Std for shorts
exit.trailing_stop: None — target is the regression line reversion
exit.signal_exit: Slope_TScore drops below 1.5 (trend weakening)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; scale to ₹1.25L if abs(Slope_TScore) > 3.0 (very strong robust trend)

filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:45 (need 30 bars for regression) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 robust slope (Huber on NIFTY) agrees with stock trend direction
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: HuberRegressor must converge within 100 iterations

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — robust regression is well-known in statistics but rarely applied to 1-min trading; the outlier rejection provides genuinely cleaner trend signals than OLS or EMA

weaknesses: HuberRegressor with epsilon=1.35 is the standard default but may not be optimal for financial data with heavy tails — the epsilon parameter controls the boundary between inliers and outliers
The t-statistic approximation for Huber regression is not exact (Huber regression is not OLS) — the standard errors are asymptotic approximations that may be poor at n=30
Buying dips in an uptrend assumes the trend is genuine and the dip is noise — but some 'dips' are the beginning of a trend reversal, and the 30-bar robust trend takes time to detect the change
prior_art: Huber (1964) robust estimation; robust regression widely used in statistics; application to trading trend estimation less common; linear regression channels in technical analysis use OLS, not robust methods
notes: Consider using RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus) instead of Huber regression for even more aggressive outlier rejection. Also consider Theil-Sen estimator which is a non-parametric alternative to OLS that naturally handles outliers.

name: quantile_regression_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: OLS regression estimates the conditional mean, but traders care about extremes — what is the worst-case (5th percentile) or best-case (95th percentile) return given current conditions? Quantile regression estimates conditional quantiles: for a given set of predictors (VWAP distance, volume ratio, NIFTY return), what is the 10th and 90th percentile of the next 30-bar return? When the 10th percentile is positive (even the worst case is up), we have a high-confidence long signal. When the 90th percentile is negative (even the best case is down), we have a high-confidence short signal. The inefficiency exists because quantile regression is rarely used in trading; most signals estimate expected return, not return distribution quantiles.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; at least 5 days of historical 1-min data for model calibration

indicators.name: QR_P10
indicators.params: QuantileRegression(tau=0.10).predict(X_VWAP_Dist, X_Vol_Ratio, X_NIFTY_Return) — 10th percentile of forward 30-bar return

indicators.name: QR_P90
indicators.params: QuantileRegression(tau=0.90).predict(X_VWAP_Dist, X_Vol_Ratio, X_NIFTY_Return) — 90th percentile of forward 30-bar return

conditions: QR_P10 > 0 (even 10th percentile forward return is positive — very high confidence long)
QR_Median > 10 bps (median expected return exceeds minimum threshold)
long.confirmation: ROC(close, 3) > 0 (short-term momentum agrees with quantile prediction)

conditions: QR_P90 < 0 (even 90th percentile forward return is negative — very high confidence short)
short.confirmation: ROC(close, 3) < 0

exit.target: QR_Median bps from entry (target is the predicted median return)
exit.stop_loss: abs(QR_P10) bps for longs / abs(QR_P90) bps for shorts (stop at predicted worst case)
exit.trailing_stop: After QR_Median * 0.6 profit, trail at QR_Median * 0.3 from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: 45 bars (model predicts 30-bar forward return; allow 50% buffer)
exit.signal_exit: QR_P10 drops below 0 for longs / QR_P90 rises above 0 for shorts (confidence lost)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with confidence spread: ₹75K if QR_P10 barely > 0, ₹1L if QR_P10 > 5bps, ₹1.25L if QR_P10 > 10bps

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; re-fit models daily if VIX regime changes significantly
filters.time_filter: No entries before 10:15 (need predictors computed from 60 bars) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: X_Vol_Ratio must be within training data range (no extrapolation)
filters.trend_filter: None — quantile regression captures trend through NIFTY_Return predictor
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day — model not trained on event-day data
other_filters: All predictors must be within 95th percentile of training data range (avoid extrapolation)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — quantile regression for intraday trading is novel; the conditional distribution approach is more informative than point estimates; model requires periodic re-training

weaknesses: Requiring QR_P10 > 0 for longs (10th percentile positive) is extremely restrictive — this condition may occur only a few times per day across the entire NIFTY 50 universe, severely limiting opportunities
The quantile regression model is fitted on 5 days of historical data and may overfit to recent market conditions — model accuracy degrades as the market regime drifts from the training period

Three predictors (VWAP distance, volume ratio, NIFTY return) may be insufficient to capture the complexity of forward return distributions — important features like volatility, spread, and order flow are omitted
prior_art: Koenker & Bassett (1978) quantile regression; Engle & Manganelli (2004) CAViaR for conditional quantiles; Taylor (2008) on quantile regression for VaR; intraday application to trading signals is novel
notes: Consider using quantile regression forests (random forest that predicts conditional quantiles) for more flexible, nonlinear relationships. The statsmodels.regression.quantile_regression module in Python provides efficient implementation. Re-train models daily at minimum.

name: changepoint_detection_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Intraday price series experience structural breaks — sudden changes in mean return or volatility caused by news, large orders, or sentiment shifts. By detecting these changepoints in real-time using CUSUM (Cumulative Sum) control charts on 1-min returns, we identify the moment a new regime begins. A positive CUSUM break (cumulative returns exceed threshold) signals a new uptrend regime; trade in that direction. A negative CUSUM break signals a new downtrend. The edge comes from entering at the very beginning of a new regime rather than waiting for lagging indicators (like EMA crossovers) to confirm. The inefficiency persists because CUSUM is a quality control technique from manufacturing, rarely applied to finance.

indicators.name: CUSUM_Pos
indicators.params: max(0, CUSUM_Pos[-1] + Return_1min - Rolling_Mean_Return - k) where k = 0.5 * std(Return_1min, 30)

indicators.name: Changepoint_Signal
indicators.params: +1 if CUSUM_Pos > CUSUM_Threshold; -1 if abs(CUSUM_Neg) > CUSUM_Threshold; 0 otherwise

conditions: Changepoint_Signal == +1 (positive CUSUM break — new uptrend regime detected)
CUSUM_Pos just exceeded threshold within last 3 bars (fresh break, not stale)
long.confirmation: ROC(close, 3) > 5 bps (momentum in new regime direction)

conditions: Changepoint_Signal == -1 (negative CUSUM break — new downtrend regime detected)
abs(CUSUM_Neg) just exceeded threshold within last 3 bars
short.confirmation: ROC(close, 3) < -5 bps

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Opposite Changepoint_Signal detected (new regime shift against position) OR CUSUM resets to 0 (regime ended)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; increase to ₹1.25L if CUSUM exceeds 2x threshold (very strong structural break)

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; adjust CUSUM_Threshold (h) proportionally to VIX level
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:25 (need 30 bars for rolling statistics) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Volume on changepoint bar > 1.5 * SMA(volume, 20) (structural breaks should be accompanied by volume)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 must not have a simultaneous opposing changepoint
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day — changepoints are expected and not exploitable
other_filters: CUSUM must have been below threshold for at least 20 bars before break (fresh signal, not continuation)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — CUSUM changepoint detection is from quality control (Page 1954), rarely applied to financial time series in real-time; the early detection provides timing advantage over lagging indicators

weaknesses: The CUSUM parameters k (allowable slack) and h (threshold) critically affect the trade-off between detection speed and false alarm rate — the standard k=0.5*sigma, h=4*sigma may not be optimal for financial data
CUSUM assumes the change is a step-function shift in mean — but financial regime shifts are often gradual (ramping) or volatile (noisy), causing delayed detection or false triggers
The 'fresh break' requirement (CUSUM exceeded threshold within last 3 bars) can miss slow-building changepoints where CUSUM gradually approaches and crosses the threshold over many bars
prior_art: Page (1954) CUSUM test; Basseville & Nikiforov (1993) 'Detection of Abrupt Changes'; Andreou & Ghysels (2002) on structural breaks in financial data; CUSUM applied to trading in some quant research papers
notes: Consider using Bayesian Online Changepoint Detection (Adams & MacKay 2007) for probabilistic changepoint estimation that avoids hard threshold decisions. The ruptures Python library provides multiple changepoint detection algorithms with different computational trade-offs.

name: kernel_density_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Traditional support and resistance levels are drawn subjectively by traders. Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) provides an objective, non-parametric method to identify price levels where trading volume or price visits are concentrated. By computing a Gaussian KDE on the close prices of the last 120 bars, the density peaks (modes) represent natural support/resistance levels. When price approaches a high-density level from above (support), we buy. When price approaches from below (resistance), we sell. The inefficiency exists because KDE is a statistical technique unfamiliar to most traders who rely on subjective line-drawing. KDE-based levels are mathematically defined and reproducible, eliminating confirmation bias.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; intraday price range > 0.5% (sufficient price variation for meaningful KDE)

indicators.name: KDE
indicators.params: GaussianKDE(close[-120:], bandwidth='silverman') — KDE of last 120 bar closes

indicators.name: KDE_Modes
indicators.params: local maxima of KDE — price levels with highest density (support/resistance)

indicators.name: Nearest_Support
indicators.params: highest KDE mode below current close

indicators.name: Nearest_Resistance
indicators.params: lowest KDE mode above current close

indicators.name: KDE_Density_at_Price
indicators.params: KDE.evaluate(close) — density at current price level

indicators.name: Mode_Strength
indicators.params: KDE density at mode / mean KDE density — relative importance of level

conditions: close is within 0.1% of Nearest_Support (approaching support from above)
Mode_Strength(Nearest_Support) > 1.5 (support level is strong — high density)
long.confirmation: Price bounces: close > close[1 bar ago] AND close > close[2 bars ago] (two consecutive upticks at support)

conditions: close is within 0.1% of Nearest_Resistance (approaching resistance from below)
short.confirmation: Price rejects: close < close[1 bar ago] AND close < close[2 bars ago] (two consecutive downticks at resistance)

exit.target: Opposite KDE mode (support → next resistance level above; resistance → next support level below)
exit.stop_loss: 0.15% beyond the KDE mode (support broken by 0.15% = failed support, exit)
exit.trailing_stop: After 20 bps profit, trail at 12 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Price breaks through the KDE mode by > 0.1% (level failed)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; scale with Mode_Strength: ₹1.25L if strength > 2.0

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 22; support/resistance levels are less reliable in high-vol environments
filters.time_filter: No entries before 11:15 (need 120 bars for KDE) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: Volume-weighted KDE preferred; if not, volume on entry bar > SMA(volume, 15)
filters.trend_filter: No strong trend: abs(EMA(close,30) slope) < 2 bps/bar (S/R levels work in ranging markets)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day
other_filters: At least 2 distinct KDE modes must be identified (otherwise price distribution is unimodal and S/R levels are meaningless)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — KDE-based S/R is a rigorous version of subjective S/R trading; the statistical approach is cleaner but the underlying concept (price memory at high-volume levels) is well-known

weaknesses: KDE bandwidth selection (Silverman's rule) assumes Gaussian-like data — financial close prices can have bimodal or irregular distributions that require manual bandwidth tuning
The 120-bar lookback means KDE modes reflect the last 2 hours of price action — if the stock was trending, the modes will be spread widely and may not represent meaningful S/R levels

Support/resistance trading has a negative risk-reward profile (tight targets between modes, wider stops when levels break) — the 0.95 avg winner/loser ratio means the strategy depends heavily on maintaining its 58% win rate
prior_art: KDE in statistics (Rosenblatt 1956, Parzen 1962); volume profile (Market Profile by Steidlmayer); KDE for S/R identification discussed in some quant blogs but not widely in academic literature
notes: Consider using volume-weighted KDE (weighting each close price observation by its bar volume) for more meaningful S/R levels — high-volume price levels are more significant than low-volume ones. The scipy.stats.gaussian_kde module provides efficient implementation.

name: bootstrap_confidence_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Standard technical indicators provide point estimates (e.g., 'RSI is 28') without confidence intervals. Using block bootstrap resampling on rolling 1-min return data, we construct confidence intervals for the expected forward return. If the 90% bootstrap CI for the 30-bar forward return is entirely above zero, we have statistically robust evidence for a long entry. If entirely below zero, a short entry. When the CI straddles zero, no edge — stay flat. This eliminates entries where the point estimate looks good but uncertainty is too high. The inefficiency exists because bootstrap inference requires computational resources (1000 resamples per signal) and statistical knowledge beyond most market participants.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; at least 120 bars of session data for bootstrap base sample

indicators.name: Forward_Return_Proxy
indicators.params: mean(ROC(close,1), window=30) * 30 — estimated 30-bar forward return based on current regime

indicators.name: Block_Bootstrap_CI
indicators.params: 90% CI from 500 block bootstrap samples (block_size=5) of last 120 1-min returns, projected forward 30 bars

indicators.name: CI_Lower
indicators.params: 5th percentile of bootstrap distribution of 30-bar forward returns

indicators.name: Signal_Strength
indicators.params: min(abs(CI_Lower), abs(CI_Upper)) / CI_Width — how far the CI is from zero relative to its width

conditions: CI_Lower > 0 (entire 90% CI is above zero — high confidence in positive forward return)
CI_Lower > 5 bps (minimum expected return even at 5th percentile)
long.confirmation: ROC(close, 5) > 0 (recent momentum agrees with bootstrap prediction)

conditions: CI_Upper < 0 (entire 90% CI is below zero — high confidence in negative forward return)
short.confirmation: ROC(close, 5) < 0

exit.target: Forward_Return_Proxy bps from entry (estimated expected return)
exit.stop_loss: abs(CI_Lower) bps for longs / abs(CI_Upper) bps for shorts (bootstrap worst case)
exit.trailing_stop: After CI_median profit, trail at CI_Width * 0.3 from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: CI shifts to include zero (confidence in direction lost)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with Signal_Strength: ₹75K if strength 0-0.3, ₹1L if 0.3-0.6, ₹1.25L if > 0.6

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; high VIX widens CIs, making it harder to get directional signals
filters.time_filter: No entries before 11:15 (need 120 bars for bootstrap base sample) or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — bootstrap CI inherently captures trend information
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day — bootstrap from non-event data doesn't represent event-day distributions
other_filters: CI_Width must be < 50 bps (uncertainty not too high — otherwise even 'directional' CIs are too wide to be meaningful)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — bootstrap inference for trading signals is novel; the computational requirement (500 resamples per signal evaluation) provides a natural barrier to replication

weaknesses: Block bootstrap with block_size=5 assumes serial dependence structure decays within 5 bars — if the true dependence is longer (e.g., 15-bar cycles), the bootstrap CIs are invalid
Computing 500 bootstrap resamples per signal evaluation per stock adds significant latency — may not complete within the 1-minute bar window for real-time trading across 50 stocks
The 'CI entirely above/below zero' requirement is very restrictive — in noisy 1-min data, bootstrap CIs tend to be wide and straddle zero most of the time, generating very few signals
prior_art: Efron (1979) bootstrap; Politis & Romano (1994) block bootstrap for time series; White (2000) reality check bootstrap for trading strategies; application to real-time entry signals is novel
notes: Consider using the stationary bootstrap (Politis & Romano 1994) with random block lengths instead of fixed block_size=5 for more robust inference. Pre-compute the bootstrap on a slightly lagged window (120 bars ending 5 bars ago) to reduce latency impact. NumPy vectorization can speed up the 500 resamples to under 50ms.

name: lasso_feature_select_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: With dozens of potential indicators (RSI, MACD, BB, VWAP, volume ratios, etc.), overfitting is the primary risk. LASSO (Least Absolute Shrinkage and Selection Operator) regression automatically selects the most predictive features by shrinking unimportant coefficients to zero. By fitting a LASSO model on the last 5 days of 1-min data with the target variable being the 20-bar forward return and 15 potential features, the non-zero coefficients identify which indicators are currently predictive. We trade only when the LASSO-selected features collectively predict a forward return exceeding the cost threshold. The inefficiency exists because most traders either use too few indicators (missing information) or too many (overfitting). LASSO finds the optimal sparse set.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; at least 5 days of complete 1-min data for LASSO training

conditions: LASSO_Prediction > 15 bps (predicted forward return exceeds cost threshold)
Active_Features >= 3 (at least 3 features are predictive — not degenerate model)
Active_Features <= 7 (not too many — prevents overfitting signal)
long.confirmation: LASSO_Prediction has been > 10 bps for 3 consecutive bars (stable prediction)

short.confirmation: LASSO_Prediction has been < -10 bps for 3 consecutive bars

exit.target: abs(LASSO_Prediction) bps from entry (model's expected return as target)
exit.stop_loss: 15 bps from entry (tight — if model is wrong, exit quickly)
exit.trailing_stop: After 15 bps profit, trail at 8 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: LASSO_Prediction sign flips (model now predicts opposite direction)

risk.position_sizing: Scale with abs(LASSO_Prediction): ₹75K if 15-25 bps, ₹1L if 25-40 bps, ₹1.25L if > 40 bps

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; re-train LASSO model if VIX regime changes significantly
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 or after 15:10
filters.trend_filter: None — LASSO model captures trend through F8 (NIFTY return) and F10 (momentum)
filters.event_filter: Skip stock on earnings day; exclude event-day data from LASSO training
other_filters: LASSO model R² on training data must be > 0.02 (model has minimum predictive power)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — LASSO is well-known in ML; the edge is in the specific feature set and real-time application; model requires daily re-training to stay current

weaknesses: LASSO assumes linear relationships between features and forward returns — non-linear interactions (e.g., RSI matters only when VIX is high) are missed, potentially leaving alpha on the table
The alpha regularization parameter (0.001) is fixed but should ideally be cross-validated — too high zeroes out important features, too low loses regularization benefit and overfits
R² > 0.02 threshold for model quality is extremely low — a model that explains only 2% of return variance may not generate reliable predictions despite passing the threshold
prior_art: Tibshirani (1996) LASSO; Gu, Kelly & Xiu (2020) 'Empirical Asset Pricing via Machine Learning'; LASSO for feature selection in trading is increasingly common in quant research; Moritz & Zimmermann (2016) on regularized regression for cross-sectional return prediction
notes: Consider using Elastic Net (L1 + L2 regularization) instead of pure LASSO for better handling of correlated features (many of our features like RSI, BB_Position, Momentum are correlated). Use time-series cross-validation (walk-forward) instead of standard CV to prevent look-ahead bias. Retrain the model at least daily.

name: post_halt_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: When a stock hits its upper or lower circuit limit and trading is halted on NSE/BSE, there is an information asymmetry: the halt indicates extreme demand/supply imbalance, but the price has been artificially frozen. When the halt is lifted (or on the next trading session if the halt persists to close), the first 5-10 minutes show strong momentum continuation in ~65% of cases as the pent-up order flow resolves. The inefficiency exists because retail traders fear post-halt volatility and avoid trading, while institutional participants with faster systems capture the continuation. For partial halts (stock reopens after 45-min cooling period), the reopening bar provides a tradeable momentum signal.
universe: All NSE F&O stocks that hit circuit limits intraday
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹25 Cr; stock must have been halted due to price movement (not regulatory/technical halt); F&O listed

indicators.name: Halt_Direction
indicators.params: +1 if upper circuit hit; -1 if lower circuit hit

indicators.name: Pre_Halt_Momentum
indicators.params: ROC(close, 15) at the time of halt (how fast was the move)

conditions: Halt_Direction == +1 (upper circuit was hit — bullish halt)
Reopen_Gap >= 0 (stock reopens at or above halt price — demand persists)
Reopen_Volume_Ratio > 2.0 (high volume at reopening — genuine interest)
long.confirmation: First 2 bars after reopen close above reopen_price (momentum sustained)

conditions: Halt_Direction == -1 (lower circuit was hit — bearish halt)
Reopen_Gap <= 0 (stock reopens at or below halt price — supply persists)
short.confirmation: First 2 bars after reopen close below reopen_price

exit.target: 50 bps from entry (post-halt moves tend to be large)
exit.stop_loss: 30 bps from entry (quick exit if halt momentum fades)
exit.trailing_stop: After 30 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.time_stop: 30 bars (30 min — post-halt momentum dissipates quickly)
exit.signal_exit: Order_Imbalance flips sign (demand/supply balance reverses)

risk.position_sizing: Reduced size ₹75K due to higher volatility; decrease to ₹50K if VIX > 20

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during market-wide panic (VIX > 25), circuit breaks may be systemic and continuation less reliable
filters.time_filter: Halt reopen must be at least 30 min before market close (reopen after 14:45 IST: skip)
filters.volume_filter: Reopen_Volume_Ratio > 2.0 (sufficient volume to confirm genuine interest, not just market makers)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction should agree with halt direction (bull market + upper circuit = stronger; bear market + upper circuit = weaker signal)
filters.spread_filter: Post-reopen bid-ask spread < 15 bps (wider than normal due to uncertainty)
filters.event_filter: Skip if halt is due to corporate action (bonus, split) rather than market forces
other_filters: Stock must not have hit circuit on previous day (avoid serial circuit hitters where price discovery is impaired)

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low — trading halts are episodic and unpredictable; each event is unique; difficult to build systematic algo around rare events, which reduces competition

weaknesses: Trading halts are rare events (0-3 per day across entire F&O universe) — the strategy may go days without a signal, making it unviable as a standalone strategy
Post-halt spreads are significantly wider (10-20 bps vs normal 3-5 bps), increasing slippage costs and potentially eating the edge

Lower circuit halts in particular can be caused by genuinely bad news (fraud, regulatory action) where the momentum continuation is a trap — the stock may be down for fundamental reasons with further downside
prior_art: Corwin & Lipson (2000) on trading halts; Lee, Ready & Seguin (1994) on volume and volatility around halts; Indian circuit breaker mechanism studied by NSE working papers; post-halt drift documented in various markets
notes: This strategy should be combined with other strategies as part of a portfolio approach given its low frequency. Consider using options instead of equity for post-halt trades to define risk more precisely. The order book data at reopen is critical for assessing demand/supply balance.

name: rights_issue_arb_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: When a company announces a rights issue, the stock price should theoretically drop by the theoretical ex-rights price (TERP) on the ex-date. However, empirical evidence from NSE shows that the actual price adjustment is often incomplete on the ex-date — stocks either overshoot (drop more than TERP implies) or undershoot (drop less). By computing the TERP-implied price and comparing it to the actual opening price on the ex-date, we can identify mispricing. Overshoot = buy (price dropped too much, will recover toward TERP). Undershoot = short (price hasn't fully adjusted, will drop further toward TERP). The inefficiency exists because TERP computation requires understanding of rights issue mechanics, and the ex-date adjustment is confused by retail investors who don't understand dilution.
universe: NSE-listed stocks with active rights issue (ex-date within trading session)
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹25 Cr; rights issue ratio must be at least 1:10 (material dilution); F&O listed preferred

indicators.name: Volume_Ratio
indicators.params: volume / ADV(20) * 375 (normalized for time of day)

conditions: Mispricing_Bps < -30 (stock opened > 30 bps below TERP — overshoot, cheap)
Volume_Ratio > 1.5 in first 15 bars (active trading, not illiquid)
NIFTY_50 not down > 1% (market not in broad selloff)
long.confirmation: Price starts recovering: close > open of ex-date after initial dip AND close > VWAP_ExDate

conditions: Mispricing_Bps > 30 (stock opened > 30 bps above TERP — undershoot, expensive)
short.confirmation: Price starts declining: close < open of ex-date AND close < VWAP_ExDate

entry.entry_price: market order after confirmation (typically within first 30 bars)

exit.target: Close converges to TERP (Mispricing_Bps → 0, abs < 10 bps)

name: bonus_record_date_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Stocks approaching a bonus issue or stock split record date exhibit a consistent pattern: buying pressure increases 2-5 days before the record date as retail investors buy to qualify for 'free' bonus shares (even though the economic value is unchanged post-adjustment). On the ex-date itself, the stock opens at the adjusted price but often overshoots to the downside as retail sellers who received bonus shares dump them. The intraday strategy: on the ex-date, buy the oversold bounce after the initial 30 minutes when selling pressure exhausts. The inefficiency is behavioral — retail investors treat bonus shares as 'free money,' creating predictable buying before and selling after the record date.

weaknesses: Bonus issues and stock splits are infrequent (10-20 material events per year among liquid stocks) — the strategy generates very few trades, unsuitable as a primary trading approach
The 'adjusted previous close' computation may differ from the exchange's official adjustment, causing the Open_Premium_Bps calculation to be slightly off — NSE adjusts using a specific methodology

Retail selling pressure on ex-date may be more persistent than the 30-minute window assumes — if the stock has a large retail holding (>30%), selling can continue for hours, and the 30-bar entry may be premature
prior_art: Grinblatt, Masulis & Titman (1984) on stock splits; Lamoureux & Poon (1987) on bonus issues; Indian market studies on ex-date effects in NSE working papers; behavioral finance literature on 'free shares' illusion

name: fii_dii_flow_signal_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: Foreign Institutional Investor (FII) and Domestic Institutional Investor (DII) net buy/sell data is published by NSE with a T+0 lag (provisional data by 17:00 IST for same-day activity). However, intraday proxies for institutional flow can be estimated from order size distribution: large orders (>₹10L notional) are predominantly institutional. By tracking the ratio of large orders to total orders in real-time, we infer whether institutions are net buying or selling. When large-order flow diverges from small-order flow (institutions buying while retail selling), the institutional direction tends to dominate over the next 30-60 minutes. The inefficiency exists because order-level data analysis requires infrastructure beyond most retail setups.
stock_filter: ADV(20) > ₹100 Cr; F&O listed (institutional participation higher in F&O stocks)

indicators.name: Large_Order_NetBuy
indicators.params: sum(trade_value * sign(trade_side) for trades with value > ₹10L) over last 30 bars

indicators.name: Small_Order_NetBuy
indicators.params: sum(trade_value * sign(trade_side) for trades with value < ₹1L) over last 30 bars

indicators.name: Prev_Day_FII_Flow
indicators.params: sign(FII_net_buy) from previous day's provisional data

conditions: Flow_Divergence > 0 (institutions buying while retail selling — smart money divergence)
Prev_Day_FII_Flow > 0 (FII were net buyers yesterday — momentum in institutional flows)
close >= vwap (price above VWAP confirming institutional buying pressure)
long.confirmation: Institutional_Pressure remains > 0.2 for 5 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: Institutional_Pressure remains < -0.2 for 5 consecutive bars

exit.trailing_stop: After 25 bps profit, trail at 15 bps from high-water mark
exit.signal_exit: Institutional_Pressure crosses zero (institutional flow direction reverses)

risk.position_sizing: Fixed ₹1L; increase to ₹1.25L if Institutional_Pressure > 0.5 and Prev_Day_FII_Flow agrees

filters.vix_filter: India VIX < 25; during high VIX, institutional flows can be erratic (forced selling by leveraged FIIs)
filters.time_filter: No entries before 09:30 (need 30 bars for flow accumulation) or after 15:10
filters.volume_filter: At least 20 large orders (>₹10L) in last 30 bars (sufficient institutional activity to be meaningful)
filters.trend_filter: NIFTY 50 direction should agree with institutional flow direction
filters.event_filter: Avoid F&O expiry days (institutional hedging activity distorts flow signals)
other_filters: FII/DII data must be available from previous day; skip on first trading day after a holiday

edge.edge_decay_risk: Low-Medium — order-level flow analysis requires trade-by-trade data access and real-time processing; the ₹10L threshold for 'large orders' is a reasonable but imperfect proxy for institutional activity

weaknesses: The ₹10L threshold for 'large orders' is arbitrary — wealthy retail traders may place orders above ₹10L, and institutions may use algorithmic slicing to place many small orders, contaminating both categories
Trade-by-trade data is not available on all retail platforms (Zerodha does not provide order-level data) — this strategy requires a data vendor or exchange membership for real-time trade data
Previous day FII/DII data is backward-looking and FII flows can reverse sharply (e.g., RBI policy surprise) — using yesterday's flow to predict today's direction assumes continuity that may not exist
prior_art: FII/DII flow analysis is common in Indian financial media; Sias (2004) on institutional herding; Brunnermeier & Pedersen (2009) on smart money; order flow analysis in Easley & O'Hara (1987); Kyle (1985) on informed trading
notes: Consider using Zerodha Kite's market depth data as a partial proxy for order flow — while it's not trade-by-trade, the bid/ask quantity imbalance at multiple levels can indicate institutional presence. Alternatively, use NSE's tick-by-tick data feed if available.

name: new_listing_momentum_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-agent-4
thesis: IPO listing day offers a unique trading opportunity because of extreme information asymmetry and behavioral biases. Stocks that list at a significant premium (>20% above issue price) and maintain that premium through the first 30 minutes tend to attract further momentum buying from retail FOMO, pushing prices higher. Conversely, IPOs that list at a discount or lose their listing premium within 30 minutes tend to see panic selling. The key signal is the 'listing premium persistence': if the stock holds >80% of its listing premium after 30 bars, momentum is genuine. The inefficiency exists because listing day has no historical OHLCV for the stock, making indicator-based strategies impossible. Most algo traders skip day-1 entirely, leaving the field to retail traders and IPO flippers.

weaknesses: IPO listing days are infrequent (20-40 material IPOs per year in India) — this is a very low-frequency strategy, unsuitable as a primary trading approach
Listing day spreads are 10-20 bps (vs normal 3-5 bps), and slippage can be 5-10 bps per side — total round-trip costs of 20-30 bps can erase much of the edge

No historical price data exists for the stock on listing day — all indicators must be computed from scratch, with no backtesting possible for the specific stock; backtesting relies on out-of-sample IPO events
prior_art: Ritter (1991) IPO underpricing; Loughran & Ritter (2004) on long-run IPO performance; Indian IPO listing day studies in NSE Working Papers; retail FOMO and flipping behavior documented in Aggarwal, Prabhala & Puri (2002)
notes: The grey market premium (GMP) available through informal dealer networks provides a strong pre-listing signal — IPOs with GMP > 30% tend to list strong. Consider tracking GMP on the morning of listing as a pre-trade filter. This strategy has the highest per-trade edge but lowest frequency of all strategies in this batch; best used as an overlay to a higher-frequency core strategy.

This inefficiency exists because index movements (often driven by institutional flows or macro announcements) are not always fully anticipated by individual stock prices. It persists due to market friction and the broad-based nature of moves.

The pattern persists due to friction (trading costs) and the difficulty of front-running large players.

This inefficiency arises from short-term overreactions and institutional VWAP-centric execution. It persists because many traders under-utilize VWAP and because reverting trades require precise timing amid noise.

The idea is early volatility (reflecting overnight news and institutional orders) sets a directional bias, so breaking out signals continuation【10†L137-L145】. For example, RSI<30 in an oversold dip often precedes a bounce, and RSI>70 an overbought top. The inefficiency stems from behavioral overreaction: traders oversell/overbuy in short term, then price reverts. It persists due to noise and the difficulty of timing quick reversals.

name: momentum_ignition_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When a stock breaks a multi-hour range (30+ bars) on a volume surge (> 3x average), stop-loss cascades from trapped range traders amplify the move for 10-30 bars. This is a microstructure phenomenon: range traders accumulate positions near the range boundaries, and their stops cluster just outside. The breakout triggers these stops, creating artificial but tradeable momentum. Edge persists because the stop cascade effect is structural to how leveraged intraday traders manage risk.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO stocks by avg daily turnover

indicators.name: bars_in_range
indicators.formula: count of consecutive bars where high < range_high_30 AND low > range_low_30
indicators.purpose: how long the range has held

long.confirmation: breakout bar closes in top 25% of its range (strong close)

short.confirmation: breakout bar closes in bottom 25% of its range (weak close)

exit.stop_loss: 0.5 * range_width back inside the range (midpoint of range)

filters.time_filter: no entries after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: vol_surge > 3.0 is the core entry condition
filters.trend_filter: for long: nifty50_return_30bar > 0; for short: < 0
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day (too much noise)
other_filters: range_width must be between 0.2% and 0.8% — too tight is noise, too wide means risk is too large

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural but crowding risk from other breakout systems

weaknesses: False breakouts are frequent — 55% of trades lose, requiring strong risk:reward to compensate
Slippage on breakout bars is higher than normal (4+ bps) due to momentum and competing algos
The 30-bar range lookback is somewhat arbitrary — different stocks consolidate on different timeframes
prior_art: Range breakout with volume confirmation — Toby Crabel, Linda Raschke, and countless others
notes: Consider adaptive range lookback based on stock's typical consolidation period.

name: intraday_trend_following_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Strong intraday trends in Nifty50 stocks persist due to herding behavior and information cascades. When price is above both EMA(20) and EMA(50) on 1-min, and the 20 is above the 50, pullbacks to the EMA(20) offer high-probability continuation entries. Institutional order flow that initiated the trend continues to provide bids/offers during pullbacks. Edge persists because most retail traders either chase momentum too late or fade it too early.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover, avg daily range > 1%

long.confirmation: bar closes above ema_20 after touching it

short.confirmation: bar closes below ema_20 after touching it

exit.stop_loss: 1.0 * atr_20 from entry or close below ema_50 (whichever is tighter)
exit.trailing_stop: trail by 1.0 * atr_20 after +1.0 * atr_20 profit
exit.signal_exit: close below ema_50 (for longs) or above ema_50 (for shorts)

filters.time_filter: no entries in first 30 min (need trend to establish) or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: adx_14 > 25 is the trend filter
filters.event_filter: skip on stock results day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — trend following is structural; herding behavior is persistent

weaknesses: Sub-50% win rate means long drawdown periods; need strong conviction to keep trading through losses
ADX > 25 filter on 1-min bars is slow to react — trend may reverse before ADX catches up
On choppy days, false trends form and collapse, generating multiple small losses
prior_art: EMA pullback trend following — standard trend-following concept adapted for 1-min intraday
notes: Consider Supertrend indicator as an alternative trend filter for faster adaptation.

name: relative_strength_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks showing the strongest intraday returns relative to their sector peers in the first 60 minutes tend to continue outperforming for the next 2-3 hours. This is driven by information asymmetry — when one stock in a sector moves first, institutional flow follows into that specific name. The leader-follower dynamic creates persistent momentum in the relative outperformer. Edge persists because computing real-time sector-relative strength across 200+ stocks requires infrastructure most retail traders don't have.
stock_filter: FnO stocks, grouped by GICS sector, top 3 per sector by first-hour return

indicators.name: sector_avg_return_60
indicators.formula: mean(return_60bar for all stocks in same sector)

short.confirmation: stock still in bottom 10% after 75 bars from open

filters.trend_filter: for longs: nifty50 return from open > -0.3% (not a crash day)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, expiry day
other_filters: minimum 5 stocks in the sector for valid ranking

weaknesses: First-hour leaders can be driven by one-off news that doesn't persist — mean reversion takes over
Sector classification matters a lot — misclassified stocks corrupt the ranking
On days when entire market is range-bound, relative strength rankings are noise
prior_art: Intraday momentum (Gao, Han, Li, Zhou 2018) — academic evidence for first-hour return persistence
notes: Test with Fama-French sector definitions vs NSE sector indices for classification.

name: previous_day_high_low_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Previous day's high and low are the most-watched support/resistance levels by both retail and institutional traders. When price breaks these levels with conviction (volume + close beyond level), stop-loss triggers from the prior day's trapped traders create momentum. The inefficiency exists because PDH/PDL are anchoring points for human decision-making — behavioral finance research confirms that round levels and recent extremes attract disproportionate order clustering.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

conditions: dist_from_pdh > 5 AND dist_from_pdh < 30 (clean break, not overextended)
long.confirmation: two consecutive bars closing above pdh

short.confirmation: two consecutive bars closing below pdl

entry.entry_price: market on second confirmation bar close

exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside PDH/PDL

filters.trend_filter: nifty50 trending in same direction as the trade
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day, stock results day
other_filters: skip if prior day range was < 50% of 20-day avg range (dead day = unreliable levels)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — PDH/PDL is a universal anchoring bias that won't disappear

weaknesses: False breakouts at PDH/PDL are extremely common — 50% win rate means half the time it fails
On inside days (today's range inside yesterday's), PDH/PDL may never be tested
If many stocks break PDH/PDL simultaneously, it's a macro-driven day and edge comes from market direction, not the level
prior_art: Previous Day High/Low breakout — Linda Raschke, Mark Fisher. Ancient setup.
notes: Consider combining with pre-market auction data for better breakout conviction.

name: first_pullback_after_trend_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: The first pullback in a new intraday trend (defined as 0.5%+ move from open in the first 45 min) is the highest-probability continuation entry. Early institutional flow that initiated the trend creates a 'base' of positioned traders. The first pullback attracts profit-takers, but the remaining institutional flow absorbs the selling, creating a continuation. Second and third pullbacks are progressively weaker. Edge persists because timing the 'first' pullback requires real-time structural analysis that's hard to do manually.
stock_filter: top 20 by avg daily turnover

indicators.name: pullback_count
indicators.formula: number of times close has touched ema_9 from the trend side since open

long.confirmation: bar closes above ema_9 after touching it

short.confirmation: bar closes below ema_9 after touching it

exit.trailing_stop: trail by 1.0 * atr_20 after target is hit (let winners run)
exit.time_stop: exit after 90 bars or by 13:00 (post-lunch trend is different)
exit.signal_exit: close below vwap for longs, above vwap for shorts

filters.time_filter: entry only 09:45-13:00 (morning trend)
filters.volume_filter: pullback bar volume < avg volume (light selling = healthy pullback)
filters.trend_filter: return_from_open > 0.5% is the trend filter
filters.event_filter: skip on stock results day
other_filters: skip if nifty50 is gapped > 1% (macro-driven, not stock-specific)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — first pullback is a structural pattern in trending markets

weaknesses: Defining 'first pullback' algorithmically is tricky — small wiggles may count as pullbacks falsely
On V-shaped reversal days, the 'first pullback' is actually the start of a full reversal
Limited to morning session (before lunch), reducing total opportunity set significantly
prior_art: First pullback (Al Brooks, Lance Beggs) — price action concept systematized
notes: Test with different pullback definitions: EMA touch, Fibonacci retracement, or fixed % pullback.

name: narrow_range_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: NR7 bars (narrowest range in 7 bars) on 1-min data indicate energy coiling before an expansion. When a stock prints an NR7 bar in the context of declining ATR and above-average volume, the next breakout direction tends to be the prevailing trend direction. This is a volatility-expansion trade: low-vol periods are followed by high-vol periods (mean reversion of volatility). Edge persists because most traders use NR7 on daily bars; on 1-min it's underexplored and more frequent.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: next bar breaks above NR7 bar high with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

short.confirmation: next bar breaks below NR7 bar low with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

exit.stop_loss: opposite end of NR7 bar (full NR7 range as risk)
exit.trailing_stop: trail by 1.0 * NR7 range after +1.5 * NR7 range
exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside NR7 range

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: trade in direction of ema_20 only
filters.event_filter: none
other_filters: NR7 bar range must be > 0.02% (not zero range / halted stock)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volatility clustering is a structural market property

weaknesses: NR7 on 1-min is frequent but many signals are in low-volume dead zones (lunch hour)
False breakouts: tight range breaks, reverses, and stops you out on the opposite side
Using NR7 bar range as stop can be extremely tight (< 5 bps), leading to noise-triggered stops
prior_art: NR7 (Tony Crabel) — originally daily; adapted here for 1-min intraday
notes: Consider NR4 or NR10 variants. Also test inside bar as alternative contraction pattern.

name: three_bar_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Three consecutive same-direction bars with expanding volume and range indicate a micro-momentum burst that persists for 5-15 more bars. This pattern captures institutional order flow that executes over multiple minutes. The first bar initiates, the second confirms, the third signals that the flow hasn't been fully absorbed yet. Edge persists because the pattern is too fast for most retail traders to act on and too small for most institutional systems to bother with.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: enter on next bar open

short.confirmation: enter on next bar open

exit.signal_exit: first bar that closes opposite to trade direction

filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none — pure momentum play
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread > 0.06% (tight spreads needed for small edge)
filters.event_filter: none
other_filters: minimum 3rd bar range > 0.05% (not a doji pattern)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — simple pattern, easily crowded by other systems

weaknesses: Very tight target (20 bps) and stop (15 bps) means costs are a huge % of gross edge — slippage kills
High trade frequency (up to 12/day) amplifies brokerage costs — ₹40 * 12 = ₹480/day fixed cost
Three green/red bars with expanding volume is common during the open — many false signals in noisy periods
prior_art: Three soldiers / three crows candlestick pattern with quantitative volume/range filters
notes: Consider a 5-min timeframe version for cleaner signals and lower cost impact.

name: sector_pair_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Highly correlated stocks within the same sector (e.g., HDFCBANK/ICICIBANK, TCS/INFY) temporarily diverge due to asynchronous order flow, then converge as sector-level information equilibrates. The spread between normalized prices of two co-integrated stocks reverts to its mean within 30-90 minutes during normal trading hours. This inefficiency exists because different institutional desks execute on different timing, creating temporary price discrepancies. Edge persists because monitoring and trading spread dynamics in real-time requires dedicated infrastructure.
stock_filter: pre-defined pairs with rolling 20-day correlation > 0.85 and co-integration p-value < 0.05

indicators.name: spread_halflife
indicators.formula: estimated halflife from ADF regression on rolling 500 bars

conditions: spread_zscore < -2.0 (spread is 2 SD below mean — stock A is cheap vs B)
spread_halflife < 60 (mean reversion is expected within 60 bars)
long.confirmation: spread_zscore starts reverting (spread_zscore[1] < spread_zscore, i.e., z-score turning up)

conditions: spread_zscore > 2.0 (spread is 2 SD above mean — stock A is rich vs B)
short.confirmation: spread_zscore starts reverting (spread_zscore[1] > spread_zscore, i.e., z-score turning down)

exit.stop_loss: spread_zscore reaches ±3.0 (spread widens further — cut loss)
exit.trailing_stop: move stop to breakeven when z-score crosses ±1.0 (halfway back)
exit.signal_exit: spread_zscore crosses 0
