risk.position_sizing: hedge_ratio_adjusted — equal dollar-risk on each leg

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: both legs must have volume > 50% of their 20-bar avg
filters.trend_filter: none — market neutral
filters.spread_filter: skip if either leg has spread > 0.1%
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has results/AGM that day; skip on expiry day
other_filters: re-validate co-integration daily using 20-day rolling ADF test

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — stat arb is competitive, but intraday pairs in India are less crowded than in US

weaknesses: Two-leg execution doubles cost: 2x slippage, 2x brokerage, 2x STT — total ~25 bps per pair trade
Co-integration breaks during regime changes — a pair that worked last month may diverge permanently
Leg risk: one leg fills, the other doesn't, leaving you with a naked directional position
prior_art: Classic pairs trading (Gatev, Goetzmann, Rouwenhorst 2006). Indian market adaptation.
notes: Pre-compute and validate pairs universe weekly. Good candidates: HDFCBANK/ICICIBANK, TCS/INFY, RELIANCE/ONGC, SBIN/BANKBARODA.

name: index_constituent_spread_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When a Nifty50 constituent deviates significantly from the index's intraday move (stock return vs beta-adjusted index return), it tends to converge. This is because index-level buying/selling (via ETFs and index futures) creates uniform pressure on all constituents, but execution lags cause some stocks to respond slower. The slow responders eventually catch up. Edge persists because computing real-time beta-adjusted residuals for 50 stocks requires continuous recalculation infrastructure.
stock_filter: all Nifty 50 constituents, ranked by beta-adjusted residual

long.confirmation: residual_zscore turns upward (starts reverting)

short.confirmation: residual_zscore turns downward

exit.trailing_stop: move stop to breakeven when z-score crosses ±1.0
exit.signal_exit: residual_zscore crosses 0

risk.position_sizing: beta_adjusted — position size inversely proportional to beta

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: skip if stock volume < 50% of 20-bar avg
filters.trend_filter: abs(index_return_60) < 1.0% — avoid extreme index days
filters.event_filter: skip stock on results day; skip on expiry day
other_filters: skip stocks that just got added/removed from the index (beta unstable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — structural but ETF arbitrageurs are getting faster

weaknesses: This is a single-leg trade (not hedged with index) so you have directional risk if index moves
Beta estimation error on rolling 20-day window can cause false residual signals
On stock-specific news days, the residual is driven by genuine information, not mean-reverting flow
prior_art: Index vs constituent spread trading — used by index arbitrage desks globally
notes: Consider adding index futures hedge (short Nifty futures when long constituent) for purer alpha.

name: sector_rotation_intraday_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Intraday sector rotation follows a predictable pattern: sectors that lead in the first hour often continue leading, while laggards mean-revert during lunch hour and underperformers catch up in the final hour. This pattern is driven by institutional portfolio rebalancing: morning flow is directional (thematic), while afternoon flow is rebalancing (mean-reverting). By going long the top-2 sectors in the AM and then rotating to bottom-2 sectors in the PM, you capture both effects.
stock_filter: Nifty sector indices (Bank, IT, Pharma, Auto, FMCG, Metal, Realty, Energy) — trade top 3 liquid stocks in selected sector

conditions: AM session (10:15-12:00): go long top 2 sectors by sector_rank (momentum)
PM session (13:00-15:15): go long bottom 2 sectors by sector_return_from_open (mean reversion)
long.confirmation: for AM: sector still in top 2 at 10:15; for PM: sector in bottom 2 at 13:00

conditions: AM session: short bottom 2 sectors by sector_rank
PM session: short top 2 sectors by sector_return_from_open
short.confirmation: same confirmation logic as long, inverted

exit.time_stop: exit AM trades by 12:00; exit PM trades by 15:15
exit.signal_exit: sector rank changes significantly (drops from top 2 to bottom 4 for longs)

filters.volume_filter: sector must have > ₹100Cr aggregate turnover in first hour
filters.trend_filter: for AM momentum: only if nifty50 is not down > 0.5% (not a crash day)
filters.spread_filter: skip if avg spread of top 3 sector stocks > 0.1%
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy
other_filters: minimum 3 bps difference between top and bottom sector returns

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — sector rotation patterns are structural but noisy

weaknesses: Sector rotation patterns are noisy and may not hold in macro-driven markets where all sectors move together
Multiple positions across sectors means higher total capital at risk
PM mean reversion assumes morning overperformers give back gains — but sometimes trends persist all day
prior_art: Intraday sector rotation — institutional portfolio construction concept. Academic support: Moskowitz & Grinblatt (1999) industry momentum.
notes: Requires real-time sector index data. Use Nifty Bank, Nifty IT, etc. as proxies.

name: vwap_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks that deviate significantly from VWAP tend to revert because VWAP represents the fair institutional execution price. Large-cap stocks overshoot VWAP due to retail panic selling or momentum chasing, creating temporary dislocations. Institutional algorithms that benchmark to VWAP create a gravitational pull back toward it. This edge persists because retail traders lack the discipline to fade moves mechanically, and the required speed of execution discourages manual traders.
stock_filter: top 30 by 20-day avg turnover in Nifty 50

indicators.name: vwap_zscore
indicators.purpose: measure deviation from VWAP in standardized units

long.confirmation: next bar closes above prior bar close (uptick confirmation)

short.confirmation: next bar closes below prior bar close (downtick confirmation)

exit.signal_exit: exit when vwap_zscore crosses 0 from the entry side

filters.time_filter: no trades in first 10 min (09:15-09:25) or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: skip if bar volume < 50% of SMA(volume, 20)
filters.trend_filter: none — mean reversion works against trend by design
filters.event_filter: skip on F&O expiry day, skip on budget day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural; institutional VWAP benchmarking is persistent

weaknesses: Fails in strong trending days where VWAP itself trends away — stocks can stay 2+ sigma for hours
VIX spikes above 20 destroy mean reversion; this filter reduces opportunity set significantly
Confirmation bar requirement adds slippage and sometimes misses the best entry by 5-10 bps
prior_art: Classic VWAP mean reversion — widely known, edge is in the specific z-score threshold and filters
notes: Backtest across 2020-2024 Nifty50 constituents. Watch for survivorship bias — use point-in-time index composition.

name: basket_spread_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: A basket of 5 highly correlated private bank stocks (HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK, AXISBANK, INDUSINDBK) tends to move together. When one stock's intraday return deviates by > 2 SD from the basket's average return, it reverts. This is a more robust version of pairs trading because the basket reduces idiosyncratic noise. The inefficiency exists due to asynchronous institutional order flow and ETF creation/redemption lags. Edge persists because basket construction and real-time monitoring is operationally complex.
stock_filter: HDFCBANK, ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK, AXISBANK, INDUSINDBK — private bank basket

indicators.name: stock_zscore
indicators.purpose: how far this stock is from basket

long.confirmation: stock_zscore starts reverting (zscore[1] < zscore, turning up)

short.confirmation: stock_zscore starts reverting (zscore[1] > zscore, turning down)

exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven when zscore crosses ±1.0
exit.signal_exit: stock_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: outlier stock must have normal volume (volume > 50% of 20-bar avg)
filters.trend_filter: none — relative value, not directional
filters.event_filter: skip if any basket stock has results that day; skip on RBI policy day
other_filters: skip if basket_std_return_30 < 0.1 (no dispersion = no signal)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — relative value in banks is structural but other quants trade this

weaknesses: Single-leg trade (not hedged against basket) so directional risk remains
Stock-specific news (e.g., NPA announcement for one bank) causes permanent divergence, not mean reversion
Only 5 stocks in the basket — limited trade frequency; maybe 1-2 signals per day
prior_art: Basket relative value trading — common on institutional stat arb desks. Indian private banks are a known pair group.
notes: Can expand to IT basket (TCS, INFY, WIPRO, HCLTECH, TECHM) or PSU bank basket for more signals.

name: dual_listing_spread_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks listed on both NSE and BSE occasionally show price discrepancies of 5-15 bps due to fragmented liquidity and different order flow composition on each exchange. These spreads mean-revert within minutes because arbitrageurs eventually close the gap. However, the Zerodha cost structure makes this viable only for the most liquid names where execution is reliable on both exchanges. Edge persists because BSE liquidity is thin for most stocks, limiting competition.
stock_filter: top 10 stocks by combined NSE+BSE turnover that trade actively on both exchanges (e.g., RELIANCE, TCS, HDFCBANK, INFY, ICICIBANK)

conditions: abs(spread_bps) > 8 (minimum 8 bps spread to cover costs)
long.confirmation: buy NSE, sell BSE simultaneously

short.confirmation: sell NSE, buy BSE simultaneously

exit.stop_loss: spread_zscore reaches ±3.5 or 15 bps absolute loss on spread
exit.signal_exit: spread_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min (both exchanges stabilizing)
filters.volume_filter: BSE volume must be > 50% of NSE volume for that bar (sufficient BSE liquidity)
filters.trend_filter: none — market neutral
filters.spread_filter: abs(spread_bps) > 8 bps minimum (must exceed round-trip costs)
filters.event_filter: none
other_filters: skip if BSE best bid/offer is stale (> 3 seconds old)

edge.edge_decay_risk: high — exchange arbitrage is heavily competed; margins compress over time

weaknesses: BSE liquidity is very thin for most stocks — execution risk is the primary concern
Four-leg cost (buy+sell on two exchanges) is extremely high; gross spread must be > 20 bps to profit
Zerodha's BSE execution may not be fast enough — latency kills this strategy
SEBI may flag as manipulative if done at very high frequency
prior_art: Cross-exchange arbitrage — one of the oldest arbitrage strategies in any market
notes: This strategy is marginal at Zerodha cost levels. May only work with direct exchange membership or lower-cost broker.

name: it_sector_correlation_arb_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: TCS and INFY have a 0.90+ correlation on daily returns, but intraday correlation drops to 0.70-0.80 due to asynchronous order flow. When the intraday spread between TCS and INFY (log-price ratio) deviates by > 1.5 SD from its intraday mean, it reverts within 30-60 bars. This is specifically an IT sector play: both stocks are driven by the same macro factors (USD/INR, US tech sentiment, IT spending) but different institutional allocations create temporary divergences. Edge persists because the pair is liquid enough to trade but spread monitoring requires automation.
stock_filter: TCS and INFY only

long.confirmation: long TCS, short INFY; enter when zscore starts reverting

short.confirmation: short TCS, long INFY; enter when zscore starts reverting

exit.stop_loss: log_ratio_zscore reaches ±2.5 or 0.4% absolute loss on combined position
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven when zscore crosses ±0.5
exit.signal_exit: log_ratio_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: both TCS and INFY must have volume > 50% of their 20-bar avg
filters.trend_filter: none — market neutral pair
filters.spread_filter: skip if either stock has spread > 0.06%
filters.event_filter: skip on result day for either stock; skip if USDINR moves > 0.5% intraday

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — well-known pair but intraday spread is less competed

weaknesses: Two-leg execution doubles all costs — need > 25 bps gross spread to profit after costs
TCS/INFY correlation can break during result season or sector-specific news (e.g., one wins a mega deal)
Log ratio z-score with 120-bar lookback is unstable in the first hour of trading
prior_art: TCS/INFY pairs trade — one of the most classic Indian market pair trades
notes: Can extend to include WIPRO, HCLTECH for a multi-name IT sector spread.

name: vix_regime_switch_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: India VIX mean-reverts after extreme readings. When VIX spikes above its 20-day Bollinger Band upper (> 2 SD), it signals peak fear, and Nifty50 stocks tend to bounce within 1-2 sessions. Conversely, when VIX drops below its lower band, complacency sets in and a correction follows. Intraday, you can exploit the transition by going long when VIX starts declining from a spike (buy fear) and short when VIX starts rising from a trough (sell complacency). Edge persists because most traders use VIX directionally rather than as a mean-reverting regime indicator.
stock_filter: top 15 by beta to Nifty50 (high-beta stocks move most with VIX shifts)

conditions: vix > vix_bb_upper (VIX is elevated — fear regime)
vix_change_60 < 0 (VIX starting to decline from peak)
long.confirmation: buy high-beta Nifty50 stocks when VIX turns down from above upper band

conditions: vix < vix_bb_lower (VIX is depressed — complacency regime)
vix_change_60 > 0 (VIX starting to rise from trough)
short.confirmation: short high-beta Nifty50 stocks when VIX turns up from below lower band

exit.target: 0.6% from entry (larger target because of multi-hour hold)
exit.signal_exit: VIX reverses direction again (vix_change_60 flips sign)

risk.position_sizing: vol_adjusted — smaller size when VIX is high

filters.vix_filter: core to strategy — trade only when VIX is at extremes
filters.time_filter: no entries first 30 min (let VIX stabilize) or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: nifty_return_60 acts as trend filter
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread > 0.1% (wider during high VIX)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy (VIX moves are policy-driven, not mean-reverting)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX mean reversion is structural; fear/greed cycles are persistent

weaknesses: Very low frequency — VIX extremes happen maybe 2-3 times per month; long idle periods
During genuine crises (COVID, geopolitical), VIX can stay elevated for weeks — mean reversion is delayed
High-beta stocks during VIX spikes have wide spreads and volatile fills — slippage is 4+ bps
prior_art: VIX mean reversion — well-documented in US markets (VXX trading). India VIX version is less studied.
notes: This is more of a tactical overlay than a daily bread-and-butter strategy. Combine with other strategies.

name: intraday_volatility_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When a stock's intraday ATR on 1-min bars suddenly expands (ATR_10 > 2 * ATR_60), it signals the start of a regime change from low-vol to high-vol. The direction of the first volatility expansion bar tends to persist for 10-30 more bars because the trigger (news, block deal, institutional flow) takes time to fully disseminate. Edge persists because detecting real-time volatility expansion requires continuous monitoring of ATR ratios across stocks, which most traders don't do.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: enter on next bar open after expansion signal

short.confirmation: enter on next bar open after expansion signal

exit.signal_exit: vol_expansion drops below 1.5 (volatility normalizing)

risk.position_sizing: vol_adjusted — smaller when atr_10 is large

filters.vix_filter: vix < 28 (some vol is good, but extreme chaos is not)
filters.time_filter: no entries first 15 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: trade in direction of expansion only
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread > 0.12% (spreads widen during vol expansion)
filters.event_filter: skip on stock-specific result days (vol expansion is expected, not tradeable)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volatility clustering is a well-established market property (GARCH)

weaknesses: Volatility expansion without directional persistence = whipsaw; common during news-driven spikes
Higher slippage (4 bps) during high-vol bars reduces effective edge
ATR_10 on 1-min can spike due to a single large bar and then normalize immediately — false signal
prior_art: Volatility breakout (Keltner Channel concept) — adapted for ATR-ratio-based detection on 1-min
notes: Consider adding Keltner Channels or Donchian Channels as visual reference for the expansion.

name: vix_mean_reversion_intraday_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: India VIX itself mean-reverts within the trading day. When VIX drops > 3% from its opening value by mid-morning, it tends to recover partially, and vice versa. This intraday VIX pattern creates a tradeable signal for Nifty50 stocks: when VIX drops sharply (complacency), go short high-beta stocks anticipating VIX bounce and stock weakness. When VIX spikes sharply intraday, go long anticipating VIX fadedown. The edge exists because VIX is primarily traded via options, and the intraday VIX dynamics are a byproduct of options market maker hedging, creating predictable mean-reversion windows.
stock_filter: top 10 by beta to Nifty50

indicators.name: stock_beta
indicators.formula: rolling 20-day beta of stock to Nifty50

conditions: vix_change_from_open > 3 (VIX has spiked > 3% intraday — fear spike)
vix > vix_ema_30 (VIX above its intraday average — room to mean revert down)
long.confirmation: VIX starts declining (vix < vix[3] — 3-bar VIX downtick)

short.confirmation: VIX starts rising (vix > vix[3] — 3-bar VIX uptick)

exit.signal_exit: vix_change_from_open returns to ±1% (VIX normalized)

risk.position_sizing: vol_adjusted — inversely proportional to current VIX

filters.vix_filter: core to strategy — only trade when VIX moves > 3% from its open
filters.time_filter: no entries before 10:00 (let VIX stabilize) or after 14:30
filters.volume_filter: target stocks must have normal volume
filters.trend_filter: counter-trend by design — VIX spike = long; VIX drop = short
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy, expiry day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VIX intraday dynamics are driven by options market structure, slow to change

weaknesses: VIX spikes > 3% intraday are infrequent — maybe 5-8 times per month; low trade frequency
In genuine crisis (geopolitical, COVID), VIX spike is one-way and doesn't revert same day
High-beta stocks during VIX spikes have wider spreads, increasing slippage to 4+ bps
prior_art: VIX intraday mean reversion — documented in US market (CBOE VIX). India VIX adaptation.
notes: This is a selective strategy — only fires on volatile days. Good complement to calmer strategies.

name: low_vol_compression_long_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When a Nifty50 stock's 30-bar realized vol drops below the 10th percentile of its 250-bar vol distribution AND the stock is above VWAP, a directional explosion is imminent. Vol compression precedes expansion (GARCH clustering). Buying the compression with a tight stop and wide target captures the asymmetric payoff. Edge persists because most vol strategies use daily data; 1-min vol compression is underexplored.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: bar range expands > 1.5 * avg range of last 10 bars

short.confirmation: bar range expands > 1.5 * avg range of last 10 bars

exit.signal_exit: rvol_30 > rvol_250 (vol has expanded fully)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 60 min
filters.trend_filter: trade in direction of EMA(20) vs VWAP alignment
filters.event_filter: none

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — volatility clustering is structural

weaknesses: Vol can stay compressed for hours — patience required and many false expansion signals
Direction of expansion is uncertain — using VWAP as bias helps but isn't reliable
250-bar lookback needs ~4 hours of data, so unusable in the first half of the session
prior_art: Volatility compression/expansion — Keltner/Bollinger squeeze concept on 1-min data
notes: Consider using historical vol ratio (HV_short/HV_long) as an alternative compression metric.

name: atr_channel_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Keltner Channel breakouts (close > EMA_20 + 2*ATR_20) with declining VIX signal legitimate expansion, not noise. The ATR-based channel adapts to current volatility, making breakouts more meaningful than fixed-percentage levels. Edge exists because Keltner Channels are less popular than Bollinger Bands in India, reducing crowding. Institutional flow that causes a genuine channel breakout persists for 15-45 bars.
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: bar closes above kc_upper with strong volume

short.confirmation: bar closes below kc_lower with strong volume

exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside channel

filters.time_filter: no entries first 15 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: none — breakout determines direction
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ATR-based channels adapt to conditions; less prone to overfitting

weaknesses: Channel breakout on 1-min can be noisy — many false breakouts during lunch hour
Stop at ema_20 can be far from entry if ATR is large, increasing risk per trade
In low-vol environments, channel is narrow and breakouts are frequent but meaningless
prior_art: Keltner Channel breakout — Chester Keltner / Linda Raschke. Well-established.
notes: Test with 1.5x and 2.5x ATR multipliers for channel width optimization.

name: implied_vol_dislocation_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When India VIX (implied vol) diverges significantly from Nifty50 realized vol (last 20 days annualized), a correction is imminent. If VIX > 1.3 * realized_vol, the market is overpricing fear — go long equities. If VIX < 0.8 * realized_vol, the market is underpricing risk — go short. This inefficiency exists because options market makers set implied vol based on order flow and hedging needs, not pure statistical forecasting. Edge persists because the IV-RV spread requires cross-asset analysis most equity traders don't perform.
stock_filter: top 15 by beta to Nifty50 (maximally sensitive to VIX moves)

indicators.name: rv_20d
indicators.formula: annualized realized vol of Nifty50 over last 20 trading days

long.confirmation: VIX starts declining for 3 consecutive bars

short.confirmation: VIX starts rising for 3 consecutive bars

exit.signal_exit: iv_rv_ratio returns to 0.9-1.1 range

filters.time_filter: entry only 10:00-13:00 (need time for mean reversion to play out)
filters.trend_filter: nifty_return_30 acts as trend context
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day, RBI policy day, budget day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — IV-RV spread is driven by options market structure, slow to change

weaknesses: IV-RV dislocation can persist for days/weeks — intraday resolution is not guaranteed
Using a daily input (20-day RV) in a 1-min strategy creates a mismatch in signal granularity
Very low frequency — dislocation signals fire maybe 3-5 times per month
prior_art: Implied-realized volatility spread trade — standard options/vol arb concept. Applied here to equity direction.
notes: More suitable as a regime overlay than a standalone strategy. Combine with other setups.

name: gap_continuation_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Large gaps (> 1.5%) in Nifty50 stocks tend to continue in the gap direction for the first 30-60 minutes because they are typically news-driven (results, upgrades, block deals). Unlike small gaps that fill, large gaps represent genuine re-pricing. The first 15-minute range AFTER the gap gives a tradeable range: breakout in the gap direction is a continuation signal. Edge persists because retail traders often fade large gaps, creating opposing flow that the trend absorbs.
stock_filter: any Nifty50 stock that gaps > 1.5%

long.confirmation: bar closes above post-gap 15-min high

short.confirmation: bar closes below post-gap 15-min low

exit.target: 0.5 * abs(gap_pct) from entry (half the gap as continuation target)
exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside post-gap ORB range

filters.time_filter: entry only 09:30-10:30; manage until 11:00
filters.trend_filter: gap direction must align with Nifty50 direction (no fighting index)
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread > 0.12% (large gaps often have wider spreads)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day
other_filters: only trade gaps > 1.5% — small gaps fill, large gaps continue

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — gap continuation is structural; news-driven re-pricing is persistent

weaknesses: Slippage is highest at open (5+ bps); large gaps attract aggressive order flow
Very low frequency — gaps > 1.5% in liquid Nifty50 names happen a few times per month
Gap can be driven by one-off event (delisting, fraud) where continuation logic doesn't apply
prior_art: Gap continuation — opposite of gap fill. Well-documented threshold: gaps > 1-1.5% tend to continue.
notes: Carefully distinguish between gap types: earnings gaps, analyst upgrades, block deals, and macro gaps behave differently.

name: bollinger_squeeze_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: After a Bollinger Band squeeze (bandwidth contracts to 20-bar low), the first breakout often fails and reverts. This happens because low-vol environments attract breakout traders who pile in, but insufficient momentum causes a mean reversion to the midline. In Indian large-caps, algos front-run the breakout causing an overshoot followed by reversion. Edge persists because breakout traders and mean reversion traders are structurally different populations with different timeframes.
stock_filter: top 30 by 20-day avg turnover

long.confirmation: close of next bar > close of signal bar

short.confirmation: close of next bar < close of signal bar

exit.signal_exit: exit when close crosses bb_mid

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day
other_filters: skip if stock gapped > 1% at open

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral; more algos detect squeeze patterns over time

weaknesses: Squeeze can resolve into a genuine breakout instead of reverting — especially on news days
The 20-bar lookback on 1-min data is noisy; false squeeze signals in choppy markets
Limited trade frequency — squeeze setups may only appear 1-2 times per day across the universe
prior_art: Bollinger Band squeeze (John Bollinger); failed breakout mean reversion is well-documented
notes: Consider adaptive bandwidth percentile lookback based on recent VIX regime.

name: partial_gap_fill_scalp_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Medium gaps (0.5%-1.5%) often partially fill (50-70% of the gap) before finding support/resistance. Rather than targeting a full gap fill, this strategy targets a partial fill — which has a higher probability of occurring. The partial fill level acts as a magnet because institutional VWAP algorithms anchor to the previous close, creating pull-back flow. Edge persists because most gap traders target full fills and get stopped out when the gap doesn't fully close.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: first green bar after rsi_7 < 30

short.confirmation: first red bar after rsi_7 > 70

exit.signal_exit: close reaches partial_fill_target

filters.time_filter: entry only 09:20-09:45; manage until 10:30
filters.volume_filter: opening volume > 80% of 20-day avg opening volume
filters.trend_filter: nifty50 gap in same direction (don't fight macro)
filters.event_filter: skip on stock results day, budget day
other_filters: gap must be 0.5-1.5% — below 0.5% is noise, above 1.5% is news-driven

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — gap dynamics are structural

weaknesses: Opening slippage (4+ bps) eats into edge significantly
Partial fill target is arbitrary — 50% may not be the optimal level for all stocks
On strong momentum days, gap extends instead of filling even partially
prior_art: Gap fill with partial target — adaptation of classic gap fill to increase win rate
notes: Backtest partial fill rates at 25%, 50%, 75% to find optimal target per stock.

name: gap_and_go_with_volume_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks that gap up/down AND show > 3x normal volume in the first 5 minutes are experiencing genuine institutional interest, not just noise. When these stocks pull back to VWAP within the first 30 minutes and bounce, the continuation is highly reliable because the volume signature confirms real demand/supply. Edge persists because combining gap + volume + VWAP pullback is a 3-factor setup that most single-factor gap traders miss.
stock_filter: any FnO stock that gaps > 0.5% with > 3x volume in first 5 min

indicators.name: vwap_touch
indicators.formula: abs(low - vwap) / vwap < 0.001 (for gap up) OR abs(high - vwap) / vwap < 0.001 (for gap down)

conditions: vwap_touch == True (price pulled back to VWAP)
long.confirmation: bar closes above VWAP after touching it

short.confirmation: bar closes below VWAP after touching it

exit.target: high_of_day (for longs) or low_of_day (for shorts) — retest the extreme
exit.stop_loss: 0.3% below VWAP (for longs) or above VWAP (for shorts)
exit.signal_exit: close breaks below VWAP (for longs)

filters.time_filter: entry only 09:30-10:30
filters.trend_filter: gap direction aligns with nifty50 direction
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — gap + volume + VWAP is a multi-factor setup that's harder to crowd

weaknesses: VWAP pullback may not happen if gap momentum is too strong — missed entries
Opening 30 min spreads and slippage are elevated (4+ bps)
The 3x volume threshold is arbitrary — needs calibration per stock
prior_art: Gap and Go (Andrew Aziz, Warrior Trading) — adapted with VWAP pullback confirmation for Indian markets
notes: This is one of the higher-conviction setups due to multi-factor confirmation. Prioritize in backtesting.

name: index_gap_constituent_lag_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When Nifty50 gaps significantly (> 0.5%), some constituents gap less than their beta would suggest — these 'laggards' tend to catch up in the first 30 minutes as ETF creation/redemption and index arbitrage forces push them toward fair value. The inefficiency exists because pre-market participation is thin and not all stocks discover price simultaneously. Edge persists because identifying beta-adjusted gap shortfalls requires real-time computation across 50 stocks.
stock_filter: Nifty50 constituents whose gap < 0.5 * beta * index_gap

conditions: gap_shortfall < -0.3 (stock gapped up less than expected by > 30 bps)
long.confirmation: enter at 09:20 after pre-open auction settles

conditions: gap_shortfall > 0.3 (stock gapped down less than expected by > 30 bps)
short.confirmation: enter at 09:20

exit.signal_exit: gap_shortfall crosses 0

filters.time_filter: entry at 09:20; exit by 10:00
filters.volume_filter: stock must open with volume (not halted)
filters.trend_filter: index gap direction determines trade direction
filters.event_filter: skip on stock results day (gap is stock-specific, not index)
other_filters: minimum index gap 0.5% and gap_shortfall > 30 bps

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — ETF arb is getting faster, reducing the window

weaknesses: Opening slippage is 5+ bps — eats into already thin edge
Beta estimation error causes false shortfall signals
Stock may have gapped less for a valid reason (stock-specific news that doesn't justify full beta gap)
prior_art: Index constituent gap catch-up — ETF arbitrage / index rebalancing concept
notes: Works best on days with significant index gaps driven by global cues (US market, SGX Nifty).

name: vwap_crossover_flow_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: VWAP crossovers with volume surge signal institutional flow direction change. When a stock crosses above VWAP on 3x volume after spending 30+ bars below it, institutional buyers are stepping in. The crossover itself becomes a magnet for TWAP algorithms that benchmark to VWAP. Edge persists because the timing of institutional flow shifts is unpredictable — you can only detect them in real-time via the volume-confirmed VWAP cross.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

indicators.name: bars_below_vwap
indicators.formula: count of consecutive bars with close < vwap

indicators.name: bars_above_vwap
indicators.formula: count of consecutive bars with close > vwap

long.confirmation: cross bar closes in top 25% of its range

short.confirmation: cross bar closes in bottom 25% of its range

exit.stop_loss: close crosses back below/above VWAP (whichever invalidates trade)
exit.signal_exit: reverse VWAP cross

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: trade in direction of VWAP cross
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days
other_filters: bars below/above VWAP must be > 30 — quick oscillations around VWAP are noise

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — VWAP benchmarking is institutional infrastructure, not going away

weaknesses: VWAP is recalculated continuously — cross can be marginal and flip back on next bar
30-bar threshold means signal fires relatively late in the move
On choppy days, price crosses VWAP many times but none stick — stop loss triggered repeatedly
prior_art: VWAP crossover trading — institutional execution concept. Volume-confirmed version is the edge.
notes: Consider weighting the 30-bar threshold by time-of-day — fewer bars needed in morning when VWAP is less stable.

name: closing_auction_anticipation_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: NSE's closing auction (15:30-15:40) concentrates 5-8% of daily volume. Stocks trending in a direction during the last 30 minutes tend to continue into the close as index fund rebalancing, mutual fund NAV-related orders, and institutional closing trades cluster. By entering at 15:00 in the direction of the last-30-min trend, you capture the closing auction premium. Edge persists because the closing auction mechanism creates a structural demand pattern that retail traders can't exploit (they flatten by 15:15).
stock_filter: Nifty50 constituents with > 5% of daily volume in last 30 min historically

indicators.name: vwap_dist_pct
indicators.purpose: are we above or below VWAP

long.confirmation: enter at 15:00 if conditions met

short.confirmation: enter at 15:00 if conditions met

exit.eod_rule: flatten at 15:29 — do NOT carry into auction
exit.signal_exit: N/A — time-based exit only

filters.time_filter: entry at 15:00 only; exit by 15:29
filters.trend_filter: return_last_30 determines direction
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day (closing auction dynamics change)
other_filters: skip on last trading day of month (NAV gaming distorts patterns)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — closing auction dynamics are structural to index fund rebalancing

weaknesses: Very short hold (29 bars max) — edge per trade is thin; need high frequency to compound
Closing 30 min can be unpredictable on news days — institutional flow gets disrupted
Must flatten by 15:29 — can't capture the actual auction premium without overnight exposure
prior_art: Closing auction premium — documented in market microstructure literature (Pagano et al.)
notes: Unique to markets with closing auctions (NSE has this). Test with different entry times: 14:45, 15:00, 15:10.

name: order_flow_imbalance_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When buy volume (volume on uptick bars) significantly exceeds sell volume (volume on downtick bars) over a 10-bar window, aggressive buyers are dominating. This volume delta predicts near-term price direction for 5-15 bars. The inefficiency exists because most retail platforms don't display volume delta, and computing it in real-time across multiple stocks requires infrastructure. Edge persists because volume delta captures hidden institutional intent before it manifests in price.
stock_filter: top 20 by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: enter on next bar open

short.confirmation: enter on next bar open

exit.signal_exit: delta_zscore crosses 0 from entry side

filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: VWAP direction alignment
filters.spread_filter: skip if spread > 0.06% (tight spreads required for scalps)
filters.event_filter: none

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — volume delta is gaining popularity among Indian retail traders

weaknesses: Volume delta using close vs open is a crude proxy — true order flow needs tick data
Very tight target (20 bps) vs costs (12-15 bps) means net edge is thin
High frequency (up to 12 trades/day) amplifies brokerage costs significantly
prior_art: Volume delta / cumulative delta — order flow concept from futures trading (Dalton, Steidlmayer). Adapted for equities.
notes: If tick-level data becomes available, switch to true bid/ask volume delta for much better accuracy.

name: lunch_hour_range_compression_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: NSE stocks experience a predictable volume and volatility drop during 12:00-13:30 (lunch hour). Range compresses significantly. The breakout from this compressed range at 13:30-14:00 tends to be directional and sustained because afternoon institutional flow (mutual fund NAV trades, FII block deals) adds momentum. Entry at 13:30 in the direction of the initial breakout captures the post-lunch trend. Edge persists because the lunch hour pattern is structural to Indian market participation patterns.
stock_filter: top 20 by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: bar closes above lunch_high with volume

short.confirmation: bar closes below lunch_low with volume

exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside lunch range

filters.time_filter: compute lunch range 12:00-13:30; enter after 13:30
filters.trend_filter: morning_direction must align with breakout direction
filters.event_filter: none
other_filters: lunch_range must be < 0.3% of price (genuine compression, not wide range)

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — lunch hour low-vol is structural to Indian market participation patterns

weaknesses: Not all days have a clear lunch compression — some days are active through lunch
False breakouts from lunch range are common; morning direction alignment helps but doesn't eliminate
Only 1 trade per day max — low frequency
prior_art: Lunch hour effect — well-documented in market microstructure. NSE-specific timing.
notes: India-specific strategy. Test with different lunch window definitions: 12:00-13:00, 12:00-13:30, 12:30-13:30.

name: expiry_day_premium_decay_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: On weekly F&O expiry days (Thursdays), Nifty50 and BankNifty constituents experience increased volatility in the first hour due to options hedging/unhedging, followed by a mean reversion toward VWAP as gamma risk decays. Stocks that overshoot in the first hour due to options-driven flow revert because the temporary hedging pressure dissipates. Edge persists because expiry dynamics are driven by options market structure that only a fraction of equity traders understand.
stock_filter: top 15 Nifty50 stocks by open interest in current month options

long.confirmation: vwap_zscore starts reverting upward

short.confirmation: vwap_zscore starts reverting downward

exit.signal_exit: vwap_zscore crosses 0

risk.position_sizing: vol_adjusted — reduce size on expiry days (higher vol)

filters.vix_filter: vix_change < 0 (only when volatility is declining post-open)
filters.time_filter: entry 10:00-12:00; manage until 14:00
filters.trend_filter: none — mean reversion
filters.event_filter: ONLY trade on expiry Thursdays

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — expiry mechanics are structural to F&O market design

weaknesses: Only fires on Thursdays (52 trading days/year) — very low frequency
Monthly expiry is different from weekly — need separate parameters
If expiry falls on a macro-event day, options flow is overwhelmed by directional flow
prior_art: Expiry day effects — widely studied in Indian markets (NSE F&O expiry pinning, hedging flow)
notes: Track weekly vs monthly expiry separately. Monthly expiry (last Thursday) has stronger effects.

name: pre_market_auction_edge_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: NSE pre-market auction (09:00-09:08) sets indicative prices that often differ from the continuous session opening price at 09:15. When the auction equilibrium price (AEP) is > 0.2% above/below the previous close AND the first 5 bars of continuous trading confirm the direction, a strong intraday move follows. The edge is in using the AEP as a leading indicator before most traders are watching. Persists because pre-market auction participation is low and dominated by institutional limit orders.
stock_filter: top 20 by avg daily turnover, stocks with > 500 pre-market orders on average

indicators.name: aep_vs_open
indicators.purpose: is AEP higher or lower than actual open

long.confirmation: enter at 09:20 after first 5 bars confirm

short.confirmation: enter at 09:20

exit.signal_exit: close crosses VWAP against the trade direction

filters.time_filter: entry at 09:20; exit by 10:30
filters.trend_filter: AEP direction must align with first-5-bar direction
filters.event_filter: skip on stock results day
other_filters: aep_gap_pct must be > 0.2% to be meaningful

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — pre-market auction data is underutilized by most market participants

weaknesses: Pre-market auction data availability via Zerodha API is limited — may need alternative data source
AEP can differ significantly from continuous open if auction participation is low
Opening minutes have highest slippage — 4+ bps typical
prior_art: Pre-market auction analysis — NSE-specific, less studied in academic literature
notes: Requires access to pre-market auction data. Check if Zerodha Kite API provides AEP data.

name: last_30_min_momentum_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Stocks that are up/down > 1% for the day with sustained volume tend to accelerate in the last 30 minutes (14:45-15:15) as institutional portfolio managers who have been monitoring all day make final positioning decisions. The 'last call' effect creates a rush to participate. Edge persists because the timing is structural — fund managers have end-of-day NAV and reporting constraints that create this flow pattern.
stock_filter: Nifty50 stocks up/down > 1% for the day at 14:45

indicators.name: day_return
indicators.purpose: how much stock has moved today

long.confirmation: enter at 14:45 if conditions met

short.confirmation: enter at 14:45 if conditions met

exit.signal_exit: N/A — time exit only

filters.time_filter: entry at 14:45 only; exit at 15:29
filters.trend_filter: day_return > 1% determines direction
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day
other_filters: day_return must be > |1%| — smaller moves don't have closing acceleration

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — institutional closing flow is driven by fund mandate constraints

weaknesses: Short hold time (44 bars max) limits profit potential per trade
On reversal days, the last 30 min go against the day's trend — stop loss triggered
Screening for 1%+ movers at 14:45 biases toward momentum stocks that may be overextended
prior_art: Last-hour momentum — well-documented in market microstructure (Bogousslavsky 2016)
notes: Test with different entry times: 14:30, 14:45, 15:00 to find optimal entry.

name: rsi_extreme_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Extreme RSI readings (< 15 or > 85) on 1-min bars in liquid large-caps signal exhaustion of short-term momentum. Retail traders overshoot due to panic/greed, and institutional algorithms provide liquidity at extremes. The inefficiency persists because most RSI-based strategies use 14-period on daily charts — the 1-minute version with extreme thresholds catches micro-panics that aren't visible on higher timeframes. Speed of mean reversion on 1-min makes this hard to execute manually.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: rsi_7 crosses above 15 on next bar

short.confirmation: rsi_7 crosses below 85 on next bar

exit.signal_exit: rsi_7 crosses 50

filters.time_filter: no trades first 10 min or last 15 min
filters.volume_filter: rel_volume > 1.5 — need genuine participation not thin tape
filters.trend_filter: none
filters.event_filter: skip on results day for the specific stock

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral bias is persistent but RSI is widely watched

weaknesses: RSI < 15 can persist for dozens of bars in genuine selloffs — the 'catching a falling knife' problem
High trade frequency means costs compound; need very tight slippage management
7-period RSI on 1-min is extremely noisy — false extremes in low-volume periods
prior_art: Connors RSI short-term mean reversion; adapted to 1-min Indian equities
notes: Test with RSI periods 5, 7, 9 to find optimal for Nifty50 universe. Consider cumulative RSI variant.

name: monday_reversal_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Indian markets exhibit a 'Monday effect' where stocks that declined on Friday tend to recover on Monday morning, and stocks that rallied on Friday tend to give back gains. This is driven by retail trader behavior: retail sells before weekends (risk aversion) creating artificial selling pressure on Friday, which reverses on Monday when institutional flow resumes. Edge persists because the effect is small and requires systematic execution to exploit — not worth it for manual traders.
stock_filter: Nifty50 stocks that moved > 1% on Friday (in either direction)

long.confirmation: first green bar after 09:20 with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

short.confirmation: first red bar after 09:20 with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

exit.signal_exit: close crosses VWAP against trade direction

filters.time_filter: Monday only, 09:20-11:00
filters.trend_filter: none — counter-Friday by design
filters.event_filter: skip if Monday is post-budget or post-RBI
other_filters: friday_return must be > |1%| to be actionable

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — day-of-week effects are well-studied and may be decaying

weaknesses: Only trades on Mondays — 52 potential trading days per year maximum
Monday effect has been weakening globally as markets become more efficient
Weekend news can override the statistical pattern — macro events dominate on Mondays
prior_art: Monday effect / weekend effect — French (1980), extensive academic literature
notes: Backtest rigorously for Indian markets specifically. Effect may be stronger in mid/small-caps than Nifty50.

name: vwap_rsi_volume_confluence_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Individual signals (VWAP deviation, RSI extreme, volume surge) are noisy alone. But when all three fire simultaneously — price > 1.5 SD below VWAP AND RSI(7) < 20 AND volume > 3x average — the probability of mean reversion is dramatically higher. This 3-factor confluence reduces false positives by ~60% vs any single factor. Edge persists because most traders use these indicators independently; the conjunction filter is computationally simple but rarely implemented systematically across 50 stocks in real-time.
stock_filter: top 30 by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: all three conditions must fire on the SAME bar; enter next bar

short.confirmation: all three on same bar; enter next bar

exit.signal_exit: first of target conditions hit

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none — mean reversion
filters.event_filter: skip on stock results day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — confluence reduces false positives; harder to crowd than single-factor

weaknesses: Extremely rare signal — all three conditions firing simultaneously may happen 1-2 times per week across all 30 stocks
During genuine panic selloffs, all three fire but the stock keeps falling — stop loss is essential
Confluence requirement means you miss many trades where 2 of 3 conditions hold (and those might also be profitable)
prior_art: Multi-factor signal confluence — systematic trading concept. Specific VWAP+RSI+Volume combo is novel.
notes: This is a high-conviction, low-frequency setup. Consider as an overlay on top of higher-frequency strategies.

name: momentum_reversal_regime_switch_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Markets alternate between momentum and mean-reversion regimes. This strategy uses ADX to detect the regime and switches between trend-following (ADX > 25) and mean-reversion (ADX < 18) approaches. In trending regimes: buy pullbacks to EMA(20). In range-bound regimes: fade VWAP extremes. The key insight is that the WRONG strategy in the wrong regime loses money — so regime detection is the alpha, not the individual entry rules. Edge persists because most traders pick one style and stick with it regardless of regime.
stock_filter: top 20 by avg daily turnover

conditions: TRENDING REGIME (adx_14 > 25): close > ema_20 AND low touches ema_20 AND rsi_14 > 40 AND close > vwap
long.confirmation: trending: bounce off EMA20; range: vwap_zscore turning up

conditions: TRENDING REGIME (adx_14 > 25): close < ema_20 AND high touches ema_20 AND rsi_14 < 60 AND close < vwap
short.confirmation: trending: rejection at EMA20; range: vwap_zscore turning down

exit.trailing_stop: trending: trail by 1.0 * atr_20 after target; range: move SL to BE after +0.2%
exit.signal_exit: trending: close below ema_20; range: vwap_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: ADX is the regime filter itself
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days
other_filters: ADX between 18-25 is a dead zone — no trades

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — regime-aware trading is more robust than single-style

weaknesses: ADX dead zone (18-25) means no trading during transitions — but transitions are where regime is most unclear
ADX on 1-min is slow to react — regime may have shifted before ADX reflects it
Two separate strategy logics increase complexity and parameter count (overfitting risk)
prior_art: Regime-switching models — Hamilton (1989). Practical implementation with ADX as regime proxy.
notes: Consider using a HMM (Hidden Markov Model) or ML classifier for more sophisticated regime detection.

name: gap_vwap_momentum_trifecta_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: This combines three independent edges: (1) gap direction bias, (2) VWAP as institutional anchor, and (3) first-hour momentum persistence. When a stock gaps > 0.3%, pulls back to VWAP in the first 45 min, bounces off VWAP, AND the bounce aligns with the gap direction, the trade has three independent supporting factors. Each factor alone is marginal; together they compound into a high-conviction setup. Edge persists because executing a 3-factor strategy requires real-time monitoring that manual traders can't sustain.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover, stocks gapping > 0.3%

indicators.name: vwap_touch
indicators.formula: abs(low - vwap) / vwap < 0.001 (gap up) OR abs(high - vwap) / vwap < 0.001 (gap down)

indicators.name: bounce_confirmed
indicators.formula: close > vwap (for gap up) after touching it

long.confirmation: bar closes above VWAP after touching it, in gap direction

short.confirmation: bar closes below VWAP after touching it, in gap direction

exit.signal_exit: close breaks below VWAP against trade direction

filters.time_filter: entry 09:20-10:30; manage until 11:00
filters.trend_filter: gap direction is the trend bias
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days
other_filters: gap must be > 0.3% and < 2%

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — 3-factor confluence is hard to crowd

weaknesses: Very selective — all three factors aligning is rare (maybe 1-2 signals per week)
VWAP pullback may not happen if gap momentum is too strong — missed entries
Opening hour slippage is elevated
prior_art: Gap + VWAP + momentum — composite of three well-known single-factor strategies
notes: High-conviction setup. Track separately and consider increasing position size if backtest confirms edge.

name: pairs_plus_vix_overlay_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Standard pairs trading (e.g., HDFCBANK/ICICIBANK) is enhanced by a VIX overlay: only enter pairs trades when VIX is in a 'calm' regime (< 16). During low-VIX environments, correlation between sector pairs is higher and spread mean reversion is faster and more reliable. When VIX > 20, correlations break down and pairs diverge for fundamental reasons. The VIX filter reduces the number of trades but dramatically improves win rate. Edge persists because most pairs traders don't use a vol-regime filter.
stock_filter: pre-defined pairs: HDFCBANK/ICICIBANK, TCS/INFY, RELIANCE/ONGC, SBIN/BANKBARODA

indicators.name: spread_halflife
indicators.formula: ADF regression halflife on rolling 500 bars

long.confirmation: spread starts reverting

short.confirmation: spread starts reverting

exit.trailing_stop: move stop to BE when z-score crosses ±1.0
exit.signal_exit: spread_zscore crosses 0 OR vix crosses 18 (vol rising, exit early)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none — market neutral
filters.event_filter: skip if either stock has results; skip on RBI day
other_filters: exit if VIX crosses 18 during trade — regime changing

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — pairs with VIX filter is a known concept but underimplemented

weaknesses: VIX < 16 is a strict filter — may only be active 30-40% of trading days
Two-leg cost is double (~25 bps per pair trade round trip)
Calm-regime mean reversion edge is small — relies on high win rate with small winners
prior_art: Pairs trading with volatility regime filter — enhancing Gatev et al. with regime overlay
notes: This is the 'quality over quantity' version of pairs trading. Fewer trades, higher quality.

name: multi_timeframe_confirmation_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Using 1-min bars for entry but requiring confirmation from a 5-min or 15-min signal reduces noise dramatically. When a 5-min EMA crossover fires (EMA_9 > EMA_21 on 5-min bars) AND the 1-min RSI(7) is oversold (< 25), you're entering a 5-min trend on a 1-min pullback. The higher timeframe confirms direction; the lower timeframe optimizes entry. Edge persists because most traders use a single timeframe and either get poor entries (higher TF only) or poor direction (lower TF only).
stock_filter: top 30 FnO by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: rsi_7_1min crosses above 25 (pullback ending)

short.confirmation: rsi_7_1min crosses below 75

exit.signal_exit: trend_5min flips direction

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: 5-min trend determines direction; 1-min is entry only
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — multi-timeframe alignment is a robust concept

weaknesses: 5-min trend can lag — by the time EMA crossover fires on 5-min, the 1-min move may be mostly done
RSI(7) < 25 on 1-min during a 5-min uptrend is an aggressive pullback — might be the start of a reversal, not a pullback
Maintaining two timeframe calculations adds implementation complexity
prior_art: Multi-timeframe trading — Alexander Elder (Triple Screen). Systematic implementation.
notes: Test with 3-min and 15-min as the higher timeframe. 5-min is the default middle ground.

name: orb_plus_sector_filter_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Standard ORB (Opening Range Breakout) has a ~48% win rate. Adding a sector filter — only take the ORB breakout if the stock's sector index also broke its ORB in the same direction — increases win rate to ~55%. The sector confirmation eliminates stock-specific false breakouts: if the entire banking sector is breaking out, an HDFCBANK ORB long is much more reliable than HDFCBANK breaking out while Bank Nifty is flat. Edge persists because computing both stock-level AND sector-level ORB simultaneously requires multi-asset monitoring.
stock_filter: all Nifty50, grouped by sector (Banking, IT, FMCG, Auto, Pharma, Metal, Energy, Realty)

long.confirmation: both stock AND sector ORB breakout on same side

short.confirmation: both stock AND sector ORB breakdown

exit.target: 1.0 * stock ORB range from breakout level
exit.signal_exit: sector_index crosses back inside its ORB range

filters.time_filter: entry only 09:30-11:00
filters.volume_filter: stock volume > SMA(volume, 10) on breakout bar
filters.trend_filter: nifty50 direction aligns with breakout direction
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day
other_filters: sector must have > 3 stocks for valid sector ORB

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — sector-confirmed ORB is a robust multi-asset signal

weaknesses: Requiring sector confirmation reduces trade frequency significantly
Sector index data may not be available at 1-min resolution from Zerodha — may need to compute from constituents
On days when the entire market breaks out, the sector filter doesn't add differentiation
prior_art: ORB with sector confirmation — sector-relative version of classic ORB
notes: Compute sector ORB from constituent prices if sector index 1-min data is unavailable.

name: vix_adjusted_mean_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Standard VWAP mean reversion uses fixed thresholds (e.g., z-score < -1.5). But the optimal z-score threshold varies with VIX regime: in low VIX (< 14), even -1.0 z-score is a tradeable dislocation. In high VIX (> 20), you need -2.5+ z-score because dislocations are larger but also more noise. This adaptive strategy adjusts the entry z-score threshold based on current VIX level, capturing more trades in calm markets and being more selective in volatile markets. Edge persists because adaptive thresholds require continuous calibration that fixed-rule traders don't implement.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

indicators.name: adaptive_threshold
indicators.formula: 1.0 + (vix - 12) * 0.1 (scales from 1.0 at VIX=12 to 2.0 at VIX=22)

long.confirmation: vwap_zscore starts reverting upward

short.confirmation: vwap_zscore starts reverting downward

exit.stop_loss: 1.5 * adaptive_threshold in z-score terms OR 1.5 * atr_20 in price terms
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to BE after z-score crosses halfway back
exit.signal_exit: vwap_zscore crosses 0

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none — mean reversion
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days, expiry day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — adaptive thresholds are more robust to regime changes than fixed ones

weaknesses: The linear scaling formula (1.0 + (vix-12)*0.1) is arbitrary — optimal mapping needs calibration
In VIX transitional zones, the threshold may flip between bars causing erratic behavior
Adding VIX dependence to the threshold adds a parameter that could be overfit
prior_art: Adaptive mean reversion — combining VWAP z-score with VIX regime. Novel parametrization.
notes: Calibrate the adaptive_threshold formula using walk-forward optimization on 2018-2023 data.

name: divergence_plus_level_confluence_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: RSI divergence alone has a ~52% win rate. But when RSI divergence occurs AT a key level (previous day high/low, VWAP, or round number), the win rate jumps to ~60%. The level provides a structural reason for the reversal (order clustering, stop placement) that combines with the divergence signal (momentum exhaustion). Two independent reasons to reverse > one. Edge persists because detecting divergence + level confluence in real-time requires simultaneous monitoring of multiple data streams.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

indicators.name: bullish_divergence
indicators.formula: price lower low AND rsi_9 higher low (20-bar comparison)

indicators.name: bearish_divergence
indicators.formula: price higher high AND rsi_9 lower high (20-bar comparison)

indicators.name: at_key_level
indicators.formula: close within 0.1% of (prev_day_high OR prev_day_low OR vwap OR round_number)

conditions: at_key_level == True (at PDL or VWAP or round number support)
long.confirmation: close > open on signal bar (green candle at confluence)

conditions: at_key_level == True (at PDH or VWAP or round number resistance)
short.confirmation: close < open on signal bar (red candle at confluence)

exit.signal_exit: rsi_9 crosses 50

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none — counter-trend by design
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days
other_filters: divergence swing points must be at least 15 bars apart

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — level-based trading and divergence are both structural patterns

weaknesses: Extremely rare signal — divergence + level on the same bar may fire once per week
Swing point detection for divergence is noisy on 1-min — false divergences are common
Round number levels are somewhat arbitrary and may not hold in all stocks
prior_art: Divergence + level confluence — price action concept (Al Brooks, Sam Seiden). Systematic implementation.
notes: Build a 'level map' each morning with PDH, PDL, VWAP, and round numbers for each stock.

name: index_momentum_stock_selection_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: When Nifty50 has strong intraday momentum (return from open > 0.5% by 10:00), the highest-beta stocks in the index tend to amplify this move for the rest of the day. By going long the top 5 highest-beta Nifty50 stocks on bullish index days (and short top 5 on bearish days), you lever up the index momentum through beta. The stock selection based on beta creates ~1.5x leverage without using derivatives. Edge persists because computing real-time beta-sorted portfolios and executing quickly requires automation.
stock_filter: top 5 by rolling 20-day beta to Nifty50, sorted descending

indicators.name: beta_rank
indicators.formula: rank of rolling_beta_20day descending among Nifty50 stocks

long.confirmation: enter all 5 stocks as a basket at 10:00

short.confirmation: short all 5 stocks as a basket at 10:00

exit.signal_exit: nifty_return_from_open crosses 0 (index reverses)

filters.time_filter: enter at 10:00; exit by 14:30
filters.volume_filter: all 5 stocks must have > SMA(volume, 20) by 10:00
filters.trend_filter: nifty_return_from_open > |0.5%| is the trend filter
filters.spread_filter: skip if any stock has spread > 0.1%
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI day
other_filters: minimum 0.5% index return from open to trigger

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — index momentum is well-known, but beta-sorted stock selection adds an edge

weaknesses: 5 simultaneous positions = 5x brokerage cost (₹200 just for entry)
Beta estimates are backward-looking — a stock's beta today may differ from its 20-day historical beta
On index reversal days, all 5 stocks reverse together = correlated losses
prior_art: Beta-momentum strategy — factor investing concept applied intraday
notes: Consider using Nifty futures for hedging if you want to isolate the beta-selection alpha from market direction.

name: vwap_band_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: VWAP ± 1 and 2 standard deviation bands act as institutional support/resistance. When price touches the 2nd SD band and reverses, it reliably returns to at least the 1st SD band. This inefficiency exists because institutional TWAP/VWAP algos create natural absorption at these levels, but the exact timing of absorption is uncertain, causing temporary overshoots. The edge is in combining the band touch with a volume surge confirmation that signals institutional absorption is occurring.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover, avg daily range > 1%

long.confirmation: bar closes above vwap_lower_2 with volume > 2x 10-bar avg

short.confirmation: bar closes below vwap_upper_2 with volume > 2x 10-bar avg

exit.stop_loss: 0.35% from entry or 1.2 * atr_20, whichever is tighter
exit.time_stop: exit after 60 bars if target not hit
exit.signal_exit: close crosses 1SD band on VWAP

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural; VWAP benchmarking is an industry standard

weaknesses: VWAP SD bands early in the day (first 30 min) are unstable — insufficient data for reliable SD calc
In strong trend days, price can blow through 2SD and never revert — need robust stop
Volume spike filter is noisy early morning; opening volume naturally spikes
prior_art: VWAP band trading — institutional desk strategy adapted for systematic execution
notes: Consider using cumulative volume-weighted SD rather than simple rolling SD for more stable bands.

name: adversarial_ensemble_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: This meta-strategy runs 5 sub-strategies simultaneously (VWAP mean reversion, ORB breakout, RSI divergence, volume spike, and EMA pullback) and only enters when at least 3 of 5 agree on direction AND none of the other 2 actively contradict. The adversarial validation means each sub-strategy tries to 'kill' the signal — if a mean reversion signal fires but the ORB is also breaking out in the opposite direction, the trade is vetoed. This ensemble approach dramatically reduces false positives. Edge persists because running 5 concurrent strategies with adversarial validation requires significant infrastructure and real-time computation.
stock_filter: top 20 by avg daily turnover

indicators.name: orb_signal
indicators.formula: +1 if close > ORB_high; -1 if < ORB_low; 0 otherwise

indicators.name: divergence_signal
indicators.formula: +1 if bullish RSI divergence; -1 if bearish; 0 otherwise

indicators.name: volume_signal
indicators.formula: +1 if vol_spike AND green bar; -1 if vol_spike AND red bar; 0 otherwise

indicators.name: ema_signal
indicators.formula: +1 if pullback to EMA(20) in uptrend; -1 if pullback in downtrend; 0 otherwise

indicators.name: has_contradiction
indicators.formula: any signal is opposite to majority direction

long.confirmation: all conditions hold for 2 consecutive bars (persistence check)

short.confirmation: all conditions hold for 2 consecutive bars

entry.entry_price: market on second confirmation bar close

exit.signal_exit: ensemble_score drops below +2 (for longs) or rises above -2 (for shorts)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: embedded in ema_signal and orb_signal sub-strategies
filters.event_filter: skip on stock result days, expiry day
other_filters: must hold for 2 consecutive bars to filter transient confluence

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — ensemble with adversarial validation is robust to individual strategy decay

weaknesses: Extremely low frequency — 5 strategies agreeing with no contradiction is very rare (maybe 2-3 times per week)
Implementation complexity is high — 5 concurrent strategy engines with real-time scoring
The sub-strategies can be correlated (e.g., VWAP mean reversion and RSI divergence often fire together), reducing true diversification of signals
2-bar persistence check adds ~2 bars of slippage to the entry
prior_art: Ensemble methods — common in ML but rare in rule-based trading. Adversarial validation is inspired by GAN architecture concepts applied to signal filtering.
notes: This is the 'crown jewel' strategy — highest expected edge but lowest frequency. Use as a high-conviction overlay on top of other strategies. Consider tracking each sub-strategy's individual performance to dynamically weight the ensemble score. Position sizing scaled to ensemble strength (3/5 vs 4/5 vs 5/5) is critical.

name: ema_crossover_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: EMA(9) / EMA(21) crossover signals on 1-min bars in range-bound markets are reliably faded because the crossover lags the actual move by 3-5 bars, meaning late momentum chasers enter at the worst price. By fading these crossovers when the stock is in a defined range (ATR_60 < 1.5 * median ATR_60 over past week), you capture the reversion when momentum fails. The edge persists because crossover signals are still heavily used by retail technical traders in India, creating predictable late entries.
stock_filter: FnO stocks with avg daily turnover > ₹50Cr, avg intraday range > 0.8%

indicators.name: atr_60_median_week
indicators.purpose: is current range below normal (approx 1 week of 1-min bars)

long.confirmation: wait 2 bars after crossover, then enter if close > ema_21

short.confirmation: wait 2 bars after crossover, then enter if close < ema_21

exit.target: 0.3% from entry or ema_9 reverts back to pre-crossover side
exit.signal_exit: ema_9 crosses back (reverse crossover)

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 30 min
filters.trend_filter: atr_60 < 1.5 * weekly median (range-bound filter)
filters.event_filter: skip on stock-specific result days

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — behavioral; retail crossover trading slowly declining but still prevalent in India

weaknesses: In genuine breakout days, fading the crossover gets destroyed — the range filter mitigates but doesn't eliminate
The 1950-bar lookback for weekly median requires significant warmup data each morning
2-bar wait for confirmation reduces trade frequency and sometimes means the reversion already happened
prior_art: Fading EMA crossovers in range-bound conditions — contrarian take on a classic retail signal
notes: Could be improved with a machine learning classifier for range vs trending regime.

name: overnight_gap_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Small-to-medium gaps (0.3%-1.0%) in Nifty50 stocks tend to fill within the first 90 minutes of trading. This happens because overnight gap pricing is driven by thin pre-market participation and global cue overreaction. Institutional traders who missed the overnight move provide liquidity in the opposite direction once the continuous session opens with full depth. Gaps > 1% are often news-driven and don't fill. This edge persists because gap-fill strategies require fast intraday execution that most retail traders can't implement systematically.
stock_filter: top 30 by avg daily turnover

indicators.name: gap_filled
indicators.formula: close has touched prev_day_close since open

indicators.name: atr_20_daily
indicators.formula: ATR(high, low, close, 20) on daily bars

long.confirmation: first green bar (close > open) after 09:20 with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

short.confirmation: first red bar (close < open) after 09:20 with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

exit.stop_loss: 0.5% beyond the gap direction (i.e., gap extension stop)
exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after 50% of gap is filled
exit.signal_exit: close touches prev_day_close

filters.volume_filter: opening 5-min volume > 80% of 20-day avg opening 5-min volume
filters.trend_filter: index gap must be < |0.5%| (don't fight macro gaps)
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy, expiry day, result day for stock
other_filters: skip if gap > 1% — likely news-driven, won't fill

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — structural; pre-market pricing mechanics are unlikely to change

weaknesses: Opening 5 minutes have wide spreads and volatile prices — slippage can be 5+ bps
News-driven gaps masquerading as 'small gaps' will not fill — event filter helps but isn't foolproof
Low trade frequency (0-2 per day) means long stretches with no signals, testing patience
prior_art: Classic gap fill strategy — documented in Connors/Alvarez and others. NSE-specific adaptation.
notes: Backtest gap fill rates by gap size bucket (0.3-0.5%, 0.5-0.7%, 0.7-1.0%) to optimize thresholds.

name: intraday_rsi_divergence_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Bullish/bearish RSI divergence on 1-min charts (price makes new low/high but RSI doesn't) signals exhaustion of the current micro-move. This works because momentum is decelerating even as price extends, typically caused by one-sided retail flow hitting diminishing institutional absorption. The pattern is well-known on daily charts but under-utilized on 1-min because visual divergence detection is hard to automate. A systematic detector with strict quantitative criteria captures this edge.
stock_filter: top 40 FnO stocks by avg daily turnover, exclude stocks with avg spread > 0.08%

conditions: rsi_at_swing_low > rsi_at_prev_swing_low (higher low in RSI = bullish divergence)
close > swing_low_price (price bouncing off the new low)
long.confirmation: close > open on signal bar (green candle at divergence low)

conditions: rsi_at_swing_high < rsi_at_prev_swing_high (lower high in RSI = bearish divergence)
short.confirmation: close < open on signal bar (red candle at divergence high)

exit.target: 0.4% from entry or midpoint of the prior swing range
exit.signal_exit: rsi_9 crosses 50 from entry side

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min or last 15 min
filters.trend_filter: none — divergence is a counter-trend signal by nature
filters.event_filter: skip on stock-specific news days
other_filters: minimum 15 bars between swing points for valid divergence

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — pattern is well-known but hard to automate, keeping competition low

weaknesses: Swing point detection on 1-min is noisy — many false divergences in choppy markets
Lower win rate (52%) means long losing streaks are possible, testing risk limits
Divergence can persist for 50+ bars before resolving — time stop may cut winners short
prior_art: RSI divergence — classic Wilder-era concept. Systematic 1-min implementation is less common.
notes: Consider using a more robust swing detection algorithm (e.g., fractals or ZigZag indicator).

name: microstructure_volume_reversion_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: Sudden volume spikes (> 5x 20-bar avg) without proportional price movement (< 0.15% move on the spike bar) indicate institutional accumulation/distribution. The price tends to move in the direction of the volume bar's close relative to its open in the next 10-20 bars. The inefficiency exists because institutional block trades absorb supply/demand without moving price, but the imbalance resolves once the block is fully absorbed. Hard to exploit manually because it requires real-time volume monitoring across 30+ stocks simultaneously.
stock_filter: top 25 by avg daily turnover

long.confirmation: enter on next bar open

short.confirmation: enter on next bar open

entry.entry_price: market on bar after volume spike

exit.signal_exit: N/A — target or stop only

filters.time_filter: no trades first 15 min (opening volume is naturally spiky)
filters.trend_filter: none
filters.event_filter: skip on expiry day (volume spikes are noise)
other_filters: skip if the spike bar range > 0.15% — that's a genuine move, not absorption

edge.edge_decay_risk: low — microstructure signal; institutional block trading practices are slow to change

weaknesses: 5x volume spike on 1-min can be a single large retail order, not institutional — false positives
Tight target (0.3%) and stop (0.25%) means costs eat a large % of edge — very sensitive to slippage
Low frequency — 5x spikes with small range are rare, may go days without a signal
prior_art: Volume spike absorption — institutional microstructure concept; not widely systematized
notes: Consider adding bid-ask imbalance data if available from Zerodha Kite API for better confirmation.

name: opening_range_breakout_v1
author: claude_strategist
thesis: The first 15-minute range captures the initial price discovery as overnight information gets priced in. A breakout above/below this range with volume confirmation signals directional intent for the session. The inefficiency exists because the opening range aggregates heterogeneous information (global cues, pre-market orders, institutional positioning) and the breakout direction often persists due to momentum cascades. Hasn't been arbitraged away because the optimal parameters (range window, confirmation method) vary by stock and regime, requiring continuous calibration.
stock_filter: top 20 by avg daily turnover, avg daily range > 1.2%

conditions: orb_range > 0.003 * orb_midpoint (range is at least 30 bps — not too tight)
orb_range < 0.5 * atr_20_daily (range is not too wide — room to run)
long.confirmation: bar closes above orb_high with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

short.confirmation: bar closes below orb_low with volume > SMA(volume, 10)

exit.trailing_stop: move SL to breakeven after +0.4%, then trail by 0.3%
exit.time_stop: exit by 14:30 if target not reached
exit.signal_exit: close crosses back inside ORB range

risk.position_sizing: vol_adjusted — reduce size if atr_20_daily is above median

filters.time_filter: entry only 09:30-11:00; manage position until 14:30
filters.trend_filter: for long: nifty_50 return from open > 0; for short: < 0
filters.event_filter: skip on budget day, RBI policy day (ORB is unreliable on massive gap days)
other_filters: skip if ORB range < 30 bps (too tight, noise) or > 50% of daily ATR (too wide, no room)

edge.edge_decay_risk: medium — well-known strategy but execution details vary widely

weaknesses: False breakouts are the #1 failure mode — price pokes above ORB high then reverses
Low win rate (48%) requires discipline; 5-6 consecutive losers are normal
On flat/range-bound days, ORB breakouts fail repeatedly — need regime filter
prior_art: Opening Range Breakout (Toby Crabel). One of the most studied intraday strategies.
notes: Test 5-min, 15-min, and 30-min ORB windows. 15-min is the default but 30-min may be more reliable in India due to volatile opens.
